questions.solution: DNA ligase is the enzyme responsible for joining the foreign DNA fragment (like an antibiotic resistance gene) with the plasmid vector by forming phosphodiester bonds.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
In genetic engineering, a DNA segment (gene) of interest, is transferred to the host cell through a vector. Consider the following four agents (i- iv) in this regard and select the correct option about which one or more of these can be used as a vector / vectors.
(i) Bacterium
(ii) Plasmid
(iii) Plasmodium
(iv) Bacteriophage
questions.solution: Plasmids (ii) and bacteriophages (iv) are commonly used as cloning vectors to transfer foreign DNA into host cells. A bacterium (i) is typically the host cell, and Plasmodium (iii) is a parasite.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Restriction endonucleases are enzymes which
options: make cuts at specific positions within the DNA molecule
recognize a specific nucleotide sequence for binding of DNA ligase
restrict the action of the enzyme DNA polymerase
remove nucleotides from the ends of the DNA molecule
questions.answer: Option (A): make cuts at specific positions within the DNA molecule
questions.solution: Restriction endonucleases are molecular scissors that recognize and cut DNA at specific palindromic recognition sequences, not randomly or at ends.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: DNA or RNA segment tagged with a radioactive molecule is called
questions.solution: A probe is a single-stranded DNA or RNA molecule that is complementary to the target sequence and is labeled with a radioactive isotope or fluorescent dye for detection.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following palindromic base sequences in DNA can be easily cut at about the middle by some particular restriction enzyme?
questions.solution: A palindromic sequence reads the same on both DNA strands when read in the $5'\to 3'$ direction. The sequence $5'\text{GAATTC}3'$ and $3'\text{CTTAAG}5'$ is a classic palindromic site recognized by EcoRI, which cuts it to produce sticky ends.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Agarose extracted from sea weeds is used in
questions.solution: Agarose, a polysaccharide derived from seaweeds, is the primary matrix material used for gel electrophoresis, particularly for separating nucleic acids like DNA and RNA.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: There is a restriction endonuclease called EcoRI. What does "co" part in it stand for?
questions.solution: The nomenclature of restriction enzymes follows a specific system: E (Escherichia) for the genus, co (coli) for the species, R for the strain (RY13), and I for the order of discovery.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: For transformation, micro-particles coated with DNA to be bombarded with gene gun are made up of
questions.solution: The gene gun (biolistic method) uses microscopic particles of heavy metals like gold or tungsten, coated with foreign DNA, to deliver genes into plant cells by bombardment.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A single strand of nucleic acid tagged with a radioactive molecule is called
questions.solution: A probe is a single-stranded nucleic acid (DNA or RNA) molecule that is labeled with a radioactive isotope or fluorescent tag, used to detect specific complementary sequences.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The colonies of recombinant bacteria appear white in contrast to blue colonies of non-recombinant bacteria because of
options: insertional inactivation of alpha galactosidase in recombinant bacteria
inactivation of glycosidase enzyme in recombinant bacteria
insertional inactivation of alpha galactosidase in non-recombinant bacteria
questions.answer: Option (C): non-recombinant bacteria containing beta galactosidase
questions.solution: In blue-white screening, non-recombinant bacteria have an intact $\beta$-galactosidase gene, express the enzyme, and cleave the chromogenic substrate X-gal to produce a blue color. Recombinant bacteria have the gene inactivated by the insert, so they cannot produce $\beta$-galactosidase and remain white.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Commonly used vectors for human genome sequencing are
questions.solution: Bacterial Artificial Chromosomes (BACs) and Yeast Artificial Chromosomes (YACs) are cloning vectors capable of carrying very large DNA fragments, making them suitable for whole-genome sequencing projects.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which vector can clone only a small fragment of DNA?
questions.solution: Plasmids typically have a limited cloning capacity, usually up to 10-15 kb, which is considered a small fragment compared to cosmids (30-45 kb), BACs (up to 300 kb), or YACs (up to 1000 kb or more).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The introduction of T-DNA into plants involves
options: exposing the plants to cold for a brief period
allowing the plant roots to stand in water
infection of the plant by Agrobacterium tumefaciens
altering the pH of the soil, then heat-shocking the plants
questions.answer: Option (C): infection of the plant by Agrobacterium tumefaciens
questions.solution: Agrobacterium tumefaciens naturally infects plants and transfers a segment of its Ti plasmid, called T-DNA, into the plant genome. This natural process is exploited in plant genetic engineering.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A gene whose expression helps to identify transformed cell is known as
questions.solution: A selectable marker gene allows transformed cells to be identified and preferentially grown, often by conferring resistance to an antibiotic or by producing a detectable color.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: DNA fragments are
options: either positively or negatively charged depending on their size
questions.solution: DNA molecules are negatively charged due to the phosphate groups in their sugar-phosphate backbone, which allows them to migrate towards the positive electrode (anode) during gel electrophoresis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The DNA fragments separated on an agarose gel can be visualised after staining with
questions.solution: Ethidium bromide is a fluorescent dye that intercalates between the base pairs of DNA. When exposed to UV radiation, the DNA-ethidium bromide complex fluoresces a bright orange, making the DNA bands visible.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is commonly used as a vector for introducing a DNA fragment in human lymphocytes?
questions.solution: Retroviruses are frequently used as gene therapy vectors due to their ability to integrate their genetic material into the host cell's genome, including human lymphocytes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Given below are four statements pertaining to separation of DNA fragments using gel electrophoresis. Identify the incorrect statements.
(i) DNA is negatively charged molecule and so it is loaded on gel towards the anode terminal.
(ii) DNA fragments travel along the surface of the gel whose concentration does not affect movement of DNA.
(iii) Smaller the size of DNA fragment larger is the distance it travels through it.
(iv) Pure DNA can be visualized directly by exposing UV radiation.
Choose correct answer from the options given below.
questions.solution: Statement (i) is incorrect: DNA is loaded at the cathode (negative) end of the gel and migrates towards the anode (positive) terminal, not loaded towards the anode terminal. Statement (ii) is incorrect: DNA fragments travel through the gel matrix, and the concentration of the gel significantly affects the movement of DNA fragments. Statement (iv) is incorrect: Pure DNA is not visible under UV radiation; it must be stained with ethidium bromide for visualization. Statement (iii) is correct.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A selectable marker is used to
options: help in eliminating the non-transformants, so that the transformants can be regenerated
identify the gene for a desired trait in an alien organism
select a suitable vector for transformation in a specific crop
mark a gene on a chromosome for isolation using restriction enzyme
questions.answer: Option (A): help in eliminating the non-transformants, so that the transformants can be regenerated
questions.solution: A selectable marker allows for the identification and selection of cells that have successfully taken up the foreign DNA (transformants) by providing them with a growth advantage or a distinguishable phenotype, while eliminating non-transformants.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Identify the wrong statement with regard to restriction enzymes.
options: Each restriction enzyme functions by inspecting the length of a DNA sequence
They cut the strand of DNA at palindromic sites
They are useful in genetic engineering
Sticky ends can be joined by using DNA ligases
questions.answer: Option (A): Each restriction enzyme functions by inspecting the length of a DNA sequence
questions.solution: Restriction enzymes recognize and bind to specific nucleotide sequences (palindromic sites), not by inspecting the overall length of a DNA sequence. They then cleave the DNA at these sites.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A specific recognition sequence identified by endonucleases to make cuts at specific positions within the DNA is
questions.solution: Restriction endonucleases recognize specific palindromic nucleotide sequences in DNA, which read the same on both strands when the orientation of reading is kept the same ($5'\to 3'$).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Plasmid pBR322 has PstI restriction enzyme site within gene ampR that confers ampicillin resistance. If this enzyme is used for inserting a gene for $\beta$-galactosidase production and the recombinant plasmid is inserted in an E. coli strain.
options: It will be able to produce a novel protein with dual ability.
It will not be able to confer ampicillin resistance to the host cell.
The transformed cells will have the ability to resist ampicillin as well as produce $\beta$-galactoside.
It will lead to lysis of host cell
questions.answer: Option (B): It will not be able to confer ampicillin resistance to the host cell.
questions.solution: If a foreign gene is inserted into the PstI site, which is located within the ampR gene, the ampR gene will be inactivated. This phenomenon is called insertional inactivation. Consequently, the host E. coli cells transformed with this recombinant plasmid will lose their resistance to ampicillin.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: DNA strands on a gel stained with ethidium bromide when viewed under UV radiation, appear as
questions.solution: Ethidium bromide is an intercalating agent that binds to DNA. When DNA stained with ethidium bromide is exposed to UV light, it emits a bright orange fluorescence.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Restriction endonucleases recognise specific sequence to cut DNA known as palindromic nucleotide sequence.
Statement II: Restriction endonucleases cut the DNA strand a little away from the centre of the palindromic site.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.answer: Option (A): Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.solution: Statement I is correct: Restriction endonucleases recognize specific palindromic sequences. Statement II is also correct: Many restriction enzymes make staggered cuts, which are slightly away from the center of the palindromic site, generating 'sticky ends'.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In the following palindromic base sequences of DNA, which one can be cut easily by particular restriction enzyme?
questions.solution: A palindromic sequence reads the same on both DNA strands when read in the $5'\to 3'$ direction. Option (b) $5'\text{GAATTC}3'$ is a perfect palindrome and is the recognition site for the restriction enzyme EcoRI.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is not a cloning vector?
questions.solution: pBR322 (a plasmid), BAC (Bacterial Artificial Chromosome), and YAC (Yeast Artificial Chromosome) are all types of cloning vectors used to carry foreign DNA. A probe (b) is a labeled nucleic acid used for detecting specific DNA or RNA sequences, not for carrying or transferring DNA.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In gene gun method used to introduce alien DNA into host cells, microparticles of ______ metal are used.
questions.solution: The gene gun (biolistics) method utilizes microscopic particles of gold or tungsten coated with the desired DNA to bombard and introduce it into host cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Upon exposure to UV radiation, DNA stained with ethidium bromide will show
questions.solution: Ethidium bromide is a fluorescent dye that intercalates into the DNA helix. When stained DNA is exposed to UV light, the ethidium bromide fluoresces a characteristic bright orange color.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statement is incorrect about Agrobacterium tumefaciens?
options: It is used to deliver gene of interest in both prokaryotic as well as eukaryotic host cells.
'Ti' plasmid from Agrobacterium tumefaciens used for gene transfer is not pathogenic to plant cell.
It transforms normal plant cells into tumor cells.
questions.answer: Option (A): It is used to deliver gene of interest in both prokaryotic as well as eukaryotic host cells.
questions.solution: Agrobacterium tumefaciens is primarily used as a vector for gene transfer into eukaryotic plant cells, not prokaryotic host cells. Statements (c) and (d) describe its natural pathogenic ability and T-DNA transfer, while (b) describes the disarmed Ti plasmid used in genetic engineering.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Ligation of foreign DNA at which of the following site will result in loss of tetracycline resistance of pBR322?
questions.solution: In the pBR322 plasmid, the tetracycline resistance gene (tetR) contains restriction sites for BamHI and SalI. Insertion of foreign DNA at either of these sites will disrupt the tetR gene, leading to insertional inactivation and loss of tetracycline resistance.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Hind II always cuts DNA molecules at a particular point called recognition sequence and it consists of
questions.solution: HindII was the first restriction endonuclease discovered and characterized. It recognizes a specific palindromic sequence of 6 base pairs (5'-GTPyPuAC-3').

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The 'Ti plasmid" of Agrobacterium tumefaciens stands for
questions.solution: The 'Ti' in Ti plasmid refers to 'Tumor inducing', as this plasmid naturally causes crown gall tumors in dicot plants by transferring a segment of its DNA (T-DNA) into the plant genome.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In the below represented plasmid, an alien piece of DNA is inserted at EcoRI site. Which of the following strategies will be chosen to select the recombinant colonies?
options: Blue color colonies grown on ampicillin plates can be selected.
Using ampicillin & tetracycline containing medium plate.
Blue color colonies will be selected.
White color colonies will be selected.
questions.answer: Option (D): White color colonies will be selected.
questions.solution: The diagram shows that the EcoRI site is located within the $\beta$-galactosidase gene. Insertion of an alien DNA fragment at this site will disrupt the $\beta$-galactosidase gene (insertional inactivation). In blue-white screening, non-recombinant colonies produce active $\beta$-galactosidase and turn blue, while recombinant colonies (with the inactivated gene) cannot produce the enzyme and remain white. Thus, white colonies are selected as recombinants.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: PCR and restriction fragment length polymorphism are the methods for
questions.solution: Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) and Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism (RFLP) are key molecular techniques used in genetic fingerprinting (DNA profiling) for individual identification, paternity testing, and forensic analysis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: During the process of isolation of DNA, chilled ethanol is added to
options: break open the cell to release DNA
questions.solution: Chilled ethanol is added to an aqueous solution containing DNA to cause the DNA to precipitate out of the solution, allowing it to be collected (spooled).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In vitro clonal propagation in plants is characterized by
questions.solution: In vitro clonal propagation produces genetically identical plants. Techniques like Random Amplified Polymorphic DNA (RAPD), which is PCR-based, are used to characterize the genetic uniformity or detect variations within these clones.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: An analysis of chromosomal DNA using the Southern hybridization technique does not use
questions.solution: Southern hybridization involves DNA separation by electrophoresis, transfer to a membrane (blotting), hybridization with a labeled probe, and detection (e.g., autoradiography). PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) is used for DNA amplification, not as a direct step in Southern hybridization.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is not a component of downstream processing?
questions.solution: Downstream processing involves separation, purification, and preservation (formulation) of the product. Expression (gene expression, protein synthesis) is part of the upstream processing (fermentation/bioreactor stage) where the product is actually made.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Stirred-tank bioreactors have been designed for
options: addition of preservatives to the product
availability of oxygen throughout the process
ensuring anaerobic conditions in the culture vessel
questions.answer: Option (C): availability of oxygen throughout the process
questions.solution: Stirred-tank bioreactors are equipped with an agitator system to ensure thorough mixing of the culture broth and a sparger to introduce oxygen, thereby ensuring optimal oxygen availability for aerobic processes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The process of separation and purification of expressed protein before marketing is called
questions.solution: Downstream processing encompasses all the steps required to recover, separate, purify, and formulate a biotechnological product (like an expressed protein) after the initial production phase (fermentation or cell culture), making it ready for market.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The correct order of steps in Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) is
questions.solution: Each cycle of PCR consists of three main steps: 1. Denaturation (separation of DNA strands at high temperature), 2. Annealing (primers bind to complementary DNA sequences at a lower temperature), and 3. Extension (DNA polymerase synthesizes new DNA strands at an intermediate temperature).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: During the purification process for recombinant DNA technology, addition of chilled ethanol precipitates out
questions.solution: Chilled ethanol is commonly used in DNA purification protocols to precipitate DNA from aqueous solutions, allowing it to be easily collected.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is a correct sequence of steps in a PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction)?
questions.solution: The three sequential steps in each cycle of PCR are denaturation (melting of DNA), annealing (primer binding), and extension (DNA synthesis).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): Polymerase chain reaction is used in DNA amplification.
Reason (R): The ampicillin resistant gene is used as a selectable marker to check transformation.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.answer: Option (B): Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.solution: Assertion (A) is correct: PCR is a molecular technique used to amplify specific DNA sequences. Reason (R) is correct: The ampicillin resistance gene serves as a selectable marker to identify bacterial cells that have taken up the plasmid (transformants). However, the reason (R) does not explain the assertion (A); they are two independent correct statements.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Main steps in the formation of recombinant DNA are given below. Arrange these steps in a correct sequence.
A. Insertion of recombinant DNA into the host cell.
B. Cutting of DNA at specific location by restriction enzyme.
C. Isolation of desired DNA fragment.
D. Amplification of gene of interest using PCR.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: The typical main steps in recombinant DNA technology are: Isolation of the desired DNA fragment (C), cutting of DNA at specific locations by restriction enzyme (B) to create fragments for insertion into a vector, formation of recombinant DNA (ligation, an implicit step), insertion of recombinant DNA into the host cell (A), and amplification of the gene of interest using PCR (D), which can be done at various stages for preparation or screening.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Thermostable DNA polymerase used in PCR was isolated from
questions.solution: Taq polymerase, a crucial enzyme for PCR due to its thermostability, was isolated from the thermophilic bacterium *Thermus aquaticus*, which thrives in hot springs.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: A bio-reactor provides optimal growth conditions for achieving the desired product
Most commonly used bio-reactors are of stirring type
Bio-reactors are used to produce small scale bacterial cultures
Bio-reactors have an agitator system, an oxygen delivery system and foam control system
questions.answer: Option (C): Bio-reactors are used to produce small scale bacterial cultures
questions.solution: Bioreactors are large vessels designed for large-scale culturing of cells or microorganisms to produce significant quantities of products. Small-scale cultures are typically performed in laboratory flasks or Petri dishes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The DNA fragments extracted from gel electrophoresis can be used in construction of recombinant DNA.
Statement II: Smaller size DNA fragments are observed near anode while larger fragments are found near the wells in an agarose gel.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct
Both statement I and statement II are correct
Both statement I and statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
questions.answer: Option (B): Both statement I and statement II are correct
questions.solution: Statement I is correct: DNA fragments separated and isolated from an agarose gel (via gel elution) are routinely used as inserts for constructing recombinant DNA. Statement II is correct: In gel electrophoresis, smaller DNA fragments migrate faster and further towards the positive electrode (anode), while larger fragments move slower and remain closer to the wells (negative electrode/cathode end).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) amplifies DNA following the equation.
questions.solution: In PCR, the number of DNA copies doubles with each cycle. Therefore, after 'n' cycles, the initial number of DNA molecules will be amplified $2^n$ times.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
The blue and white selectable markers have been developed which differentiate recombinant colonies from nonrecombinant colonies on the basis of their ability to produce colour in the presence of a chromogenic substrate.
Given below are two statements about this method:
Statement I: The blue coloured colonies have DNA insert in the plasmid and they are identified as recombinant colonies.
Statement II: The colonies without blue colour have DNA insert in the plasmid and are identified as recombinant colonies.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
questions.answer: Option (A): Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution: In blue-white screening, blue colonies are non-recombinant (intact $\beta$-galactosidase gene), while white colonies are recombinant (insertional inactivation of $\beta$-galactosidase gene due to DNA insert). Therefore, Statement I is incorrect, and Statement II is correct.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: With the help of given pedigree, find out the probability for the birth of a child having no disease and being a carrier (has the disease mutation in one allele of the gene) in F3 generation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: According to Mendelism, which character shows dominance?
questions.solution: According to Mendel's experiments, green pod colour is dominant over yellow pod colour.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following can be explained on the basis of Mendel's Law of Dominance? A. Out of one pair of factors one is dominant and the other is recessive. B. Alleles do not show any expression and both the characters appear as such in F2 generation. C. Factors occur in pairs in normal diploid plants. D. The discrete unit controlling a particular character is called factor. E. The expression of only one of the parental characters is found in a monohybrid cross. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: A, C, D and E only
A, B, C, D and E
questions.answer: Option (B): A, C, D and E only
questions.solution: Mendel's Law of Dominance explains that in a pair of contrasting characters, one factor (allele) expresses itself (dominant) and the other is masked (recessive) (A). In a monohybrid cross, only the dominant parental character is expressed in F1 (E). Factors (genes) occur in pairs (C) and are discrete units (D) are fundamental principles that underpin Mendel's work. B describes non-dominance scenarios like incomplete or co-dominance.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What is the pattern of inheritance for polygenic trait?
questions.solution: Polygenic inheritance involves multiple genes contributing to a single trait, often showing continuous variation, which is considered a non-Mendelian inheritance pattern.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: When dominant and recessive alleles express itself together it is called
questions.solution: The phrasing 'dominant and recessive alleles express itself together' typically describes co-dominance. However, the provided answer key states (b) 'dominance'. This might imply the question is poorly worded and refers to the expression of the dominant allele in the heterozygous state.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A gene is said to be dominant if
options: it expresses its effect only in homozygous state
it expresses its effect only in heterozygous condition
it expresses its effect both in homozygous and heterozygous condition
it never expresses its effect in any condition
questions.answer: Option (A): it expresses its effect only in homozygous state
questions.solution: A dominant gene expresses its effect both in homozygous and heterozygous conditions. The provided answer key states (a) 'it expresses its effect only in homozygous state', which is incorrect as this describes a recessive gene.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Phenotype of an organism is the result of
questions.solution: Phenotype is the observable characteristics of an organism, which are a result of the interaction between its genotype and the environment.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Test cross involves
options: crossing between two genotypes with dominant trait
crossing between two genotypes with recessive trait
crossing the F₁ hybrid with a double recessive genotype
questions.answer: Option (D): crossing the F₁ hybrid with a double recessive genotype
questions.solution: A test cross involves crossing an individual with a dominant phenotype (and unknown genotype) with an individual that is homozygous recessive for the trait(s) in question.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A common test to find the genotype of a hybrid is by
options: crossing of one F2 progeny with female parent
studying the sexual behaviour of F1 progenies
crossing of one F1 progeny with male parent
crossing of one F2 progeny with male parent
questions.answer: Option (B): studying the sexual behaviour of F1 progenies
questions.solution: The common test to find the genotype of a hybrid is a test cross, which involves crossing the hybrid with a homozygous recessive parent. The provided answer key states (b) 'studying the sexual behaviour of F1 progenies', which is irrelevant for genotype determination.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In pea plants, yellow seeds are dominant to green. If a heterozygous yellow seeded plant is crossed with a green seeded plant, what ratio of yellow and green seeded plants would you expect in F1 generation?
questions.solution: Cross: Yy (heterozygous yellow) $\times$ yy (green). The progeny genotypes would be 1 Yy (yellow) : 1 yy (green), resulting in a 1:1 ratio (50% yellow, 50% green). The provided answer key states (b) 1:3, which is incorrect.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In Antirrhinum two plants with pink flowers were hybridized. The F1 plants produced red, pink and white flowers in the proportion of 1 red, 2 pink and 1 white. What could be the genotype of the two plants used for hybridisation? Red flower colour is determined by RR and white by rr genes.
questions.solution: This is a case of incomplete dominance. Pink flowers have genotype Rr. A cross between two pink flowered plants (Rr $\times$ Rr) produces progeny in a 1 RR (red) : 2 Rr (pink) : 1 rr (white) ratio.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A cross in which an organism showing a dominant phenotype is crossed with the recessive parent in order to know its genotype is called
questions.solution: The described cross is a test cross, which is used to determine the genotype of an individual with a dominant phenotype. The provided answer key states (d) 'dihybrid cross', which is incorrect.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following traits of garden pea studied by Mendel was a recessive feature?
questions.solution: Green seed colour is a recessive trait in garden pea; yellow seed colour is dominant.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: ABO blood grouping is controlled by gene I which has three alleles and show co-dominance. There are six genotypes. How many phenotypes in all are possible?
questions.solution: The three alleles ($I^A, I^B, i$) result in four blood group phenotypes: A, B, AB, and O. The provided answer key states (d) five, which is incorrect.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Test cross in plants or in Drosophila involves crossing
options: between two genotypes with recessive trait
the F1 hybrid with a double recessive genotype
between two genotypes with dominant trait.
questions.solution: A test cross involves crossing the F1 hybrid with a homozygous recessive parent. Option (c) describes this concept more accurately. The provided answer key states (b) 'between two F₁ hybrids', which is incorrect for a test cross.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A test cross is carried out to
options: determine the genotype of a plant at F2
predict whether two traits are linked
assess the number of alleles of a gene
determine whether two species or varieties will breed successfully
questions.answer: Option (C): assess the number of alleles of a gene
questions.solution: A test cross is primarily used to determine the genotype of an individual expressing a dominant phenotype. Option (a) 'determine the genotype of a plant at F2' is a more accurate description of its purpose than (c) 'assess the number of alleles of a gene', which is stated in the answer key.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: F2 generation in a Mendelian cross showed that both genotypic and phenotypic ratios are same as 1:2:1. It represents a case of
questions.answer: Option (D): monohybrid cross with incomplete dominance
questions.solution: Incomplete dominance is characterized by identical genotypic and phenotypic ratios (1:2:1) in the F2 generation, where the heterozygote shows an intermediate phenotype.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which idea is depicted by a cross in which the F1 generation resembles both the parents?
questions.solution: When the F1 generation resembles both parents simultaneously, it's a case of co-dominance. For example, in ABO blood groups, AB phenotype shows characteristics of both A and B parents. The provided answer key states (a) 'Inheritance of one gene', which is a broader concept, not the specific phenomenon described.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: If two persons with 'AB' blood group marry and have sufficiently large number of children, these children could be classified as 'A' blood group: 'AB' blood group: 'B' blood group in 1:2:1 ratio. Modern technique of protein electrophoresis reveals presence of both 'A' and 'B' type proteins in 'AB' blood group individuals. This in an example of
questions.solution: The presence of both 'A' and 'B' type proteins in 'AB' blood group individuals and their co-expression is a classic example of co-dominance. The provided answer key states (d) 'incomplete dominance', which is incorrect.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A man with blood group 'A' marries a woman with blood group 'B'. What are all the possible blood groups of their offspring?
questions.solution: If both parents are heterozygous ($I^A i \times I^B i$), all four blood groups (A, B, AB, O) are possible. If at least one parent is homozygous, the possibilities are more restricted. Option (b) 'O only' is impossible for A and B parents. The provided answer key states (b), which is incorrect.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Multiple alleles are present
options: at the same locus of the chromosome
at different loci on the same chromosome
questions.solution: Multiple alleles are different forms of a gene that occupy the same locus on homologous chromosomes. The provided answer key states (c) 'on different chromosomes', which is incorrect.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A tall true breeding garden pea plant is crossed with a dwarf true breeding garden pea plant. When the F1 plants were selfed the resulting genotypes were in the ratio of
questions.solution: Cross: TT $\times$ tt $\rightarrow$ F1: Tt. Selfing F1: Tt $\times$ Tt $\rightarrow$ F2 genotypes: 1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt. The genotypic ratio is 1:2:1 (1 Tall homozygous : 2 Tall heterozygous : 1 Dwarf). The provided answer key states (a) '3:1:: Tall : Dwarf', which is the phenotypic ratio, not the genotypic ratio.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The genotypes of a husband and wife are $I^A I^B$ and $I^A i$. Among the blood types of their children, how many different genotypes and phenotypes are possible?
questions.solution: Cross: $I^A I^B \times I^A i$. Possible genotypes: $I^A I^A$, $I^A I^B$, $I^B i$. (3 genotypes). Possible phenotypes: A, AB, B. (3 phenotypes). Thus, 3 genotypes; 3 phenotypes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The genes controlling the seven pea characters studied by Mendel are now known to be located on how many different chromosomes?
questions.solution: The seven characters studied by Mendel are located on four different chromosomes (1, 4, 5, 7).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In Antirrhinum (Snapdragon), a red flower was crossed with a white flower and in F1 generation all pink flowers were obtained. When pink flowers were selfed, the F2 generation showed white, red and pink flowers. Choose the incorrect statements from the following.
options: Law of segregation does not apply in this experiment.
This experiment does not follow the Principle of Dominance.
Pink colour in F1 is due to incomplete dominance
questions.answer: Option (B): This experiment does not follow the Principle of Dominance.
questions.solution: This is a case of incomplete dominance. The Law of Segregation always applies (a is incorrect). The experiment does not follow the Principle of Dominance (b is correct). Pink in F1 is due to incomplete dominance (c is correct). The F2 ratio is 1:2:1 (d is correct). The question asks for the incorrect statement. Statement (a) 'Law of segregation does not apply in this experiment' is factually incorrect. Statement (b) 'This experiment does not follow the Principle of Dominance' is factually correct as it is incomplete dominance. However, the provided answer key states (b) as the incorrect statement.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Identify the wrong statement with reference to the
options: A person will have only two of the three alleles.
When $I^A$ and $I^B$ are present together, they express same type of sugar.
Allele i does not produce any sugar
questions.answer: Option (D): Allele i does not produce any sugar
questions.solution: Statement (a) 'The gene (I) has three alleles' is correct. Statement (b) 'A person will have only two of the three alleles' is correct. Statement (d) 'Allele i does not produce any sugar' is correct. Therefore, statement (c) 'When $I^A$ and $I^B$ are present together, they express same type of sugar' is the wrong statement as $I^A$ and $I^B$ produce different sugars (antigens). The provided answer key states (d) as the wrong statement, which is incorrect.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In a cross between a male and female, both heterozygous for sickle cell anaemia gene, what percentage of the progeny will be diseased?
questions.solution: Sickle cell anemia is an autosomal recessive disorder. A cross between two heterozygotes (Hh x Hh) results in 1 HH : 2 Hh : 1 hh. The percentage of diseased progeny (hh) is 25%. The provided answer key states (b) 50%, which is incorrect.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A heterozygous pea plant with violet flowers was crossed with homozygous pea plant with white flower. Violet is dominant over white. Which one of the following represents the expected combinations among 40 progenies formed?
options: 30 produced violet and 10 produced white flowers
20 produced violet and 20 produced white flowers
questions.answer: Option (B): 20 produced violet and 20 produced white flowers
questions.solution: Cross: Vv (heterozygous violet) $\times$ vv (homozygous white). This is a test cross, yielding Vv (violet) and vv (white) progeny in a 1:1 ratio. For 40 progenies, 20 will be violet and 20 will be white.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Match List I with List II. List I: A. Two or more alternative forms of a gene B. Cross of F1 progeny with homozygous recessive parent C. Cross of F1 progeny with any of the parents D. Number of chromosome sets in plant List II: I. Back cross II. Ploidy III. Allele IV. Test cross Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.solution: The correct matches are: A-III (Allele), B-IV (Test cross), C-I (Back cross), D-II (Ploidy). This corresponds to option (c). However, the provided answer key states (b) as the correct answer, which gives incorrect pairings for all items.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In a plant, black seed color (BB/Bb) is dominant over white seed color (bb). In order to find out the genotype of the black seed plant, with which of the following genotype will you cross it?
questions.solution: To determine the genotype of a plant with a dominant phenotype (black seed, which could be BB or Bb), a test cross is performed by crossing it with a homozygous recessive individual (white seed, bb).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A pink flowered snapdragon plant was crossed with a red flowered snapdragon plant. What type of phenotype/s is/are expected in the progeny?
options: Red flowered as well as pink flowered plants
Red, pink as well as white flowered plants
questions.answer: Option (B): Red flowered as well as pink flowered plants
questions.solution: In snapdragons, red (RR), white (rr), and pink (Rr) show incomplete dominance. A cross between a pink (Rr) and a red (RR) plant results in progeny with genotypes RR (red) and Rr (pink) in a 1:1 ratio. Thus, both red and pink flowered plants are expected.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: As per ABO blood grouping system, the blood group of father is B+, mother is A+ and child is O+. Their respective genotype can be A. $I^B i/Rr$, $I^A i/Rr$, $ii/Rr$ B. $I^B I^B/RR$, $I^A I^A/RR$, $ii/RR$ C. $I^A I^B / i I^A / I^B i$ D. $I^A i / I^B i / i i$ E. $i I^B / i I^A / I^A I^B$ Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
questions.solution: Child is O+ ($ii Rr$). For the child to be $ii$, both parents must carry the $i$ allele. For the child to be $Rr$, both Rh+ parents must be heterozygous ($Rr$). So, Father ($I^B i Rr$), Mother ($I^A i Rr$), Child ($ii Rr$). Option A correctly represents these genotypes. Options D and E are incompletely specified or inconsistent.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Due to the cross between TTRr $\times$ ttrr the resultant progenies show what percent of tall, red flowered plants?
questions.solution: For height (T/t): TT $\times$ tt $\rightarrow$ all Tt (Tall). For flower color (R/r): Rr $\times$ rr $\rightarrow$ 1 Rr (Red) : 1 rr (white). Therefore, 100% Tall $\times$ 50% Red = 50% Tall, Red flowered plants.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: How many pairs of contrasting characters in pea plants were studied by Mendel in his experiments?
questions.solution: Mendel studied seven pairs of contrasting characters in pea plants.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Two non-allelic genes produce the new phenotype when present together but fail to do so independently then it is called
questions.solution: Complementary genes are non-allelic genes that interact such that the dominant allele of both genes is required to produce a specific phenotype. Neither gene expresses the phenotype independently.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A and B genes are linked. What shall be genotype of progeny in a cross between AB/ab and ab/ab?
questions.solution: If genes A and B are linked, in a cross AB/ab $\times$ ab/ab (a test cross), the gametes from AB/ab will be AB and ab (assuming no crossing over or parental combinations are predominant). The gamete from ab/ab is ab. Thus, the progeny genotypes will be AB/ab (AaBb) and ab/ab (aabb).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Ratio of complementary genes is
questions.solution: The typical phenotypic ratio for complementary genes in a dihybrid cross is 9:7. The ratio 9:3:4 is characteristic of recessive epistasis. The provided answer key states (a) 9:3:4 for complementary genes, which is generally incorrect.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: There are three genes a, b, c. Percentage of crossing over between a and b is 20%, b and c is 28% and a and c is 8%. What is the sequence of genes on chromosome?
questions.solution: Map distances: d(a,b) = 20, d(b,c) = 28, d(a,c) = 8. The smallest distance (8) is between a and c. The sum of the two smaller distances should equal the largest distance if the genes are in sequence. Here, 20 (a,b) + 8 (a,c) does not equal 28 (b,c). However, if the order is b-a-c, then d(b,a) + d(a,c) = 20 + 8 = 28, which fits d(b,c). So the sequence is b-a-c. The provided answer key states (c) 'a, c, b'. If the sequence is a-c-b, then d(a,c) + d(c,b) = 8 + 28 = 36, but d(a,b) is given as 20, so 'a, c, b' is incorrect.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Two crosses between the same pair of genotypes or phenotypes in which the sources of the gametes are reversed in one cross, is known as
questions.solution: The description defines a reciprocal cross. A test cross is different. The provided answer key states (a) 'test cross', which is incorrect.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Lack of independent assortment of two genes A and B in fruit fly Drosophila sp. is due to
questions.solution: Lack of independent assortment is due to linkage, meaning the genes are located on the same chromosome. Crossing over (d) is a mechanism that can break linkage and allow for recombination, thus it's not the cause of lack of independent assortment. The provided answer key states (d) 'crossing over', which is incorrect.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In a plant, red fruit (R) is dominant over yellow fruit (r) and tallness (T) is dominant over shortness (t). If a plant with RRTt genotype is crossed with a plant that is rrtt,
options: 25% will be tall with red fruit
50% will be tall with red fruit
75% will be tall with red fruit
all the offspring will be tall with red fruit
questions.answer: Option (B): 50% will be tall with red fruit
questions.solution: Cross: RRTt $\times$ rrtt. For fruit color: RR $\times$ rr $\rightarrow$ all Rr (red). For height: Tt $\times$ tt $\rightarrow$ 1 Tt (tall) : 1 tt (short). Thus, 100% red $\times$ 50% tall = 50% tall with red fruit.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Select the correct statement from the ones given below with respect to dihybrid cross.
options: Tightly linked genes on the same chromosomes show higher recombinations.
Genes far apart on the same chromosome show very few recombinations
Genes loosely linked on the same chromosome show similar recombinations
Tightly linked genes on the same chromosome show very few recombinations
questions.answer: Option (D): Tightly linked genes on the same chromosome show very few recombinations
questions.solution: Tightly linked genes on the same chromosome are inherited together more often, resulting in very few recombinations (low recombination frequency).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: When two unrelated individuals or lines are crossed, the performance of F1 hybrid is often superior to both its parents. This phenomenon is called
questions.solution: Heterosis, or hybrid vigor, is the phenomenon where the F1 hybrid shows superior performance compared to its parents.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements is not true of two genes that show 50% recombination frequency?
options: If the genes are present on the same chromosome, they undergo more than one crossover in every meiosis
The genes may be on different chromosomes.
questions.answer: Option (D): The genes are tightly linked
questions.solution: A 50% recombination frequency means genes assort independently. This occurs if genes are on different chromosomes or are very far apart on the same chromosome. Tightly linked genes (d) show significantly less than 50% recombination frequency.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In his classic experiments on pea plants, Mendel did not use
questions.solution: Mendel used 'flower position' (axial/terminal) as one of his seven contrasting traits. However, the provided answer key states (b) as the correct answer, implying it was not used.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Fruit colour in squash is an example of
questions.solution: Fruit color in squash is a classic example of dominant epistasis, where a dominant allele at one locus masks the expression of alleles at another locus.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The movement of a gene from one linkage group to another is called
questions.solution: Translocation is a chromosomal rearrangement where a segment of a chromosome moves to a different, non-homologous chromosome, effectively moving genes between linkage groups.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The term “linkage” was coined by
questions.solution: T.H. Morgan coined the term 'linkage' and extensively studied it in Drosophila melanogaster.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In a test cross involving F1 dihybrid flies, more parental-type offspring were produced than the recombinant-type offspring. This indicates
options: the two genes are linked and present on the same chromosome
both of the characters are controlled by more than one gene
the two genes are located on two different chromosomes
chromosomes failed to separate during meiosis
questions.answer: Option (A): the two genes are linked and present on the same chromosome
questions.solution: When parental combinations are more frequent than recombinant types in a test cross, it indicates that the genes are linked and located on the same chromosome, as linkage tends to keep parental allele combinations together.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one from those given below is the period for Mendel's hybridisation experiments?

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Ethylene oxide when treated with Grignard reagent yields
questions.solution: Ethylene oxide reacts with a Grignard reagent ($RMgX$) to form an adduct. Upon subsequent hydrolysis ($H_3O^+$), this adduct yields a primary alcohol ($R-CH_2CH_2OH$). For example, $CH_3MgBr + \text{ethylene oxide} \rightarrow CH_3CH_2CH_2OMgBr \xrightarrow{H_3O^+} CH_3CH_2CH_2OH$ (primary alcohol).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Consider the following reaction:
Phenol $ \xrightarrow{\text{Zn dust}} $ X $ \xrightarrow{\text{CH}_3\text{Cl}} $ Y $ \xrightarrow{\text{Anhyd. AlCl}_3} $ Z $ \xrightarrow{\text{Alkaline KMnO}_4} $ Z'
the product Z is
questions.solution: Phenol reacts with Zn dust to form Benzene (X). Benzene (X) reacts with $CH_3Cl$ in the presence of Anhydrous $AlCl_3$ (Friedel-Crafts alkylation) to yield Toluene (Z). Toluene (Z) upon oxidation with alkaline $KMnO_4$ would form Benzoic acid (Z'). The question asks for product Z, which is Toluene.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: HOCH$_2$CH$_2$OH on heating with periodic acid gives
questions.solution: Vicinal diols (1,2-diols) undergo oxidative cleavage when treated with periodic acid ($HIO_4$). Ethane-1,2-diol (HOCH$_2$CH$_2$OH) is cleaved to produce two molecules of formaldehyde (HCHO). The formula shown in option (c) represents two molecules of formaldehyde, $2\ H_2C=O$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Consider the following reaction :
Ethanol $ \xrightarrow{\text{PBr}_3} $ X $ \xrightarrow{\text{alc.KOH}} $ Y $ \xrightarrow{\text{(i)H}_2\text{SO}_4\text{, room temperature}} $ Z $ \xrightarrow{\text{(ii)H}_3\text{O}^{+}\text{, heat}} $ 
the product Z is
questions.solution: Ethanol ($CH_3CH_2OH$) reacts with $PBr_3$ to form Bromoethane ($CH_3CH_2Br$) (X). Bromoethane (X) undergoes elimination with alcoholic KOH to produce Ethene ($CH_2=CH_2$) (Y). Ethene (Y) reacts with $H_2SO_4$ at room temperature to form Ethyl hydrogen sulfate ($CH_3CH_2OSO_3H$) (Z). Subsequent hydrolysis of Z with $H_3O^+$ and heat would yield Ethanol ($CH_3CH_2OH$). The question asks for product Z.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: When glycerol is treated with excess of HI, it produces
questions.solution: Glycerol ($CH_2(OH)CH(OH)CH_2(OH)$) reacts with excess HI to first form glycerol triiodide ($CH_2ICHICH_2I$), which is unstable and immediately loses two molecules of $I_2$ to form allyl iodide ($CH_2=CH-CH_2I$). Allyl iodide further reacts with HI to form 2-iodopropane ($CH_3CHICH_3$). Under heating and with excess HI, 2-iodopropane undergoes dehydrohalogenation to form propene ($CH_3CH=CH_2$). Thus, propene is the final product.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Among the following four compounds
(i) Phenol
(ii) Methyl phenol
(iii) Meta-nitrophenol
(iv) Para-nitrophenol
The acidity order is
questions.solution:
Electron-withdrawing groups increase acidity, while electron-donating groups decrease it. Nitro groups ($-NO_2$) are electron-withdrawing, and methyl groups ($-CH_3$) are electron-donating.
- Para-nitrophenol (iv) has a strong electron-withdrawing nitro group at the para position, which stabilizes the phenoxide ion through resonance and inductive effects, making it most acidic.
- Meta-nitrophenol (iii) has a nitro group at the meta position, exhibiting only an inductive electron-withdrawing effect (no direct resonance stabilization for meta), making it less acidic than para-nitrophenol but more acidic than phenol.
- Phenol (i) is less acidic than nitrophenols.
- Methyl phenol (ii) (cresol) has an electron-donating methyl group, which destabilizes the phenoxide ion, making it least acidic.
Therefore, the order of decreasing acidity is (iv) > (iii) > (i) > (ii).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following compounds has the most acidic nature?
questions.solution:
The acidity of organic compounds depends on the stability of their conjugate base. Electron-withdrawing groups stabilize the conjugate base, increasing acidity.
(a) Benzyl alcohol (primary alcohol): Less acidic than phenol.
(b) Phenol: More acidic than aliphatic alcohols due to resonance stabilization of the phenoxide ion.
(c) Cyclohexanol (aliphatic alcohol): Least acidic among the given options with an -OH group.
(d) p-Nitrophenol: The nitro group ($NO_2$) is a strong electron-withdrawing group at the para position, which highly stabilizes the p-nitrophenoxide ion through resonance and inductive effects, making it significantly more acidic than phenol and alcohols. Thus, p-nitrophenol is the most acidic.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Given are cyclohexanol(I), acetic acid(II), 2,4,6-trinitrophenol (III) and phenol (IV). In these the order of decreasing acidic character will be
questions.solution:
The acidic strength generally follows the order: Sulfonic acids > Carboxylic acids > Picric acid (2,4,6-trinitrophenol) > other Nitrophenols > Phenols > Water > Alcohols. 
- 2,4,6-Trinitrophenol (III) is picric acid, which is extremely acidic due to the strong electron-withdrawing effect of three nitro groups, making it even more acidic than most carboxylic acids.
- Acetic acid (II) is a carboxylic acid, generally more acidic than phenols.
- Phenol (IV) is more acidic than alcohols due to resonance stabilization of the phenoxide ion.
- Cyclohexanol (I) is an aliphatic alcohol, the least acidic among the given compounds.
Thus, the order of decreasing acidic character is: (III) 2,4,6-trinitrophenol > (II) acetic acid > (IV) phenol > (I) cyclohexanol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
In the following reactions,
$ \substack{\mathrm{CH}_3 \\ \mathrm{(i)}\ \mathrm{CH}_3\text{-CH-CH-CH}_3 \ \xrightarrow{\text{H}^{+}/\text{heat}} \ \mathrm{OH}} \ \text{A Major product} + \text{B Minor product} $
$ \substack{\quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \text{HBr, dark} \\ \mathrm{(ii)} \ \text{in absence of peroxide} \ \mathrm{C} + \mathrm{D} \\ \quad \quad \quad \text{Major product} \quad \quad \text{Minor product}} $
the major products (A) and (C) are respectively
questions.solution:
Reaction (i): Dehydration of 3-methylbutan-2-ol ($CH_3CH(CH_3)CH(OH)CH_3$) in the presence of $H^+$/heat. This reaction proceeds via a carbocation intermediate. The initial secondary carbocation ($CH_3CH(CH_3)CH^+CH_3$) rearranges via a 1,2-hydride shift to form a more stable tertiary carbocation ($CH_3C^+(CH_3)CH_2CH_3$). Subsequent elimination of a proton yields the most substituted alkene (Saytzeff's product), which is 2-methylbut-2-ene ($CH_3C(CH_3)=CHCH_3$) as the major product (A).
Reaction (ii): Addition of HBr to 2-methylbut-2-ene ($CH_3C(CH_3)=CHCH_3$) in the absence of peroxide follows Markovnikov's rule. The H adds to the carbon with more hydrogens (less substituted), and Br adds to the carbon with fewer hydrogens (more substituted). This yields 2-bromo-2-methylbutane ($CH_3C(Br)(CH_3)CH_2CH_3$) as the major product (C).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
In the following sequence of reactions, $ \mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{Br} \xrightarrow{\text{KCN}} \text{A} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{O}^{+}} \text{B} \xrightarrow{\text{LiAlH}_4/\text{ether}} \text{C} $
the end product (C) is
questions.solution:
1. $CH_3Br + KCN \rightarrow CH_3CN$ (A, acetonitrile) via $S_N2$ reaction.
2. $CH_3CN \xrightarrow{H_3O^+} CH_3COOH$ (B, acetic acid) via hydrolysis of nitrile.
3. $CH_3COOH \xrightarrow{LiAlH_4/ether} CH_3CH_2OH$ (C, ethyl alcohol) via reduction of carboxylic acid.
Thus, the end product (C) is ethyl alcohol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Number of isomeric alcohols of molecular formula $ C_6H_{14}O $ which give positive iodoform test is
questions.solution:
Alcohols that give a positive iodoform test contain the $CH_3CH(OH)-$ group. For $C_6H_{14}O$, the following structural isomers possess this group:
1. Hexan-2-ol ($CH_3CH(OH)CH_2CH_2CH_2CH_3$)
2. 3-Methylpentan-2-ol ($CH_3CH(OH)CH(CH_3)CH_2CH_3$)
3. 4-Methylpentan-2-ol ($CH_3CH(OH)CH_2CH(CH_3)CH_3$)
4. 3,3-Dimethylbutan-2-ol ($CH_3CH(OH)C(CH_3)_2CH_3$)
There are 4 such structural isomers.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following will not be soluble in sodium hydrogen carbonate?
questions.solution:
A compound is soluble in sodium hydrogen carbonate ($NaHCO_3$) if it is more acidic than carbonic acid ($H_2CO_3$).
- 2,4,6-Trinitrophenol (Picric acid) is exceptionally acidic (more acidic than carbonic acid).
- Benzoic acid is a carboxylic acid, more acidic than carbonic acid.
- Benzenesulphonic acid is a strong acid, much more acidic than carbonic acid.
- o-Nitrophenol is less acidic than carbonic acid. Therefore, it will not react with or dissolve in sodium hydrogen carbonate.
The approximate order of acidity: Benzenesulphonic acid > 2,4,6-Trinitrophenol > Benzoic acid > Carbonic acid > o-Nitrophenol > Phenol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Which of the following reaction(s) can be used for the preparation of alkyl halides?
(I) CH$_3$CH$_2$OH + HCl$ \xrightarrow{\text{Anh.ZnCl}_2} $
(II) CH$_3$CH$_2$OH + HCl $ \rightarrow $
(III) (CH$_3$)$_3$COH + HCl $ \rightarrow $
(IV) (CH$_3$)$_2$CHOH + HCl $ \xrightarrow{\text{Anh.ZnCl}_2} $
questions.solution:
Alkyl halides can be prepared from alcohols by reaction with hydrogen halides, often catalyzed by $ZnCl_2$ (Lucas reagent).
(I) Primary alcohol ($CH_3CH_2OH$) with Lucas reagent ($HCl/ZnCl_2$). Reaction is slow, but possible, especially with heating. So, it can be used.
(II) Primary alcohol ($CH_3CH_2OH$) with HCl alone. Very slow or no reaction under normal conditions. Not suitable for preparation.
(III) Tertiary alcohol ($(CH_3)_3COH$) with HCl. Tertiary alcohols are highly reactive and react immediately with HCl even without $ZnCl_2$. So, it can be used.
(IV) Secondary alcohol ($(CH_3)_2CHOH$) with Lucas reagent ($HCl/ZnCl_2$). Reacts within 5-10 minutes. So, it can be used.
Therefore, reactions (I), (III), and (IV) can be used for the preparation of alkyl halides.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Reaction of phenol with chloroform in presence of dilute sodium hydroxide finally introduces which one of the following functional group?
questions.solution: This is the Reimer-Tiemann reaction. Phenol reacts with chloroform ($CHCl_3$) in the presence of dilute sodium hydroxide (NaOH) to form salicylaldehyde (o-hydroxybenzaldehyde), introducing an aldehyde ($-CHO$) functional group predominantly at the ortho position.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which one is the most acidic compound?
questions.solution:
The acidity of phenols increases with the presence of electron-withdrawing groups (like $NO_2$) especially at ortho and para positions, due to resonance and inductive effects stabilizing the phenoxide ion. Electron-donating groups (like $CH_3$) decrease acidity.
(a) Phenol.
(b) p-Nitrophenol: One electron-withdrawing nitro group.
(c) 2,4-Dinitrophenol: Two electron-withdrawing nitro groups, significantly increasing acidity.
(d) 2-Nitro-4-methylphenol: Contains one electron-withdrawing nitro group and one electron-donating methyl group. The methyl group will reduce acidity compared to 2,4-dinitrophenol.
Comparing the options, 2,4-dinitrophenol (c) has two strong electron-withdrawing nitro groups that provide the greatest stabilization to its conjugate base, making it the most acidic among the given options.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Identify the major products P, Q and R in the following sequence of reactions :
$ \text{Cumene} \xrightarrow{\text{anhyd. AlCl}_3} P \xrightarrow{\text{(i) O}_2 \quad \text{(ii) H}_3\mathrm{O}^{+}/\Delta} Q+R $
questions.solution:
The reaction sequence describes the Cumene process for the industrial preparation of phenol. The starting material is Cumene (isopropylbenzene, $C_6H_5CH(CH_3)_2$).
1. Cumene reacts with oxygen ($O_2$) via auto-oxidation to form Cumene hydroperoxide (P). The label "anhyd. $AlCl_3$" in the diagram is incorrect for this step; it is a catalyst for Friedel-Crafts alkylation, which could be used to form Cumene from benzene and propene, but not for the conversion of Cumene to P.
2. Cumene hydroperoxide (P) then undergoes acid-catalyzed hydrolysis ($H_3O^+ / \Delta$) to yield Phenol (Q) and Acetone (R).
Thus, P = Cumene hydroperoxide, Q = Phenol, and R = Acetone.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Compound A, $ C_8H_{10}O $, is found to react with NaOI (produced by reacting Y with NaOH) and yields a yellow precipitate with characteristic smell. A and Y are respectively
questions.solution:
The reaction producing a yellow precipitate with NaOI (formed from $I_2$ and NaOH) is characteristic of a positive iodoform test. This test is given by compounds containing a $CH_3CH(OH)-$ group or a $CH_3CO-$ group. The molecular formula $C_8H_{10}O$ suggests an aromatic alcohol.
Let's analyze the options for A:
(a) and (b) represent 2-phenylethanol ($C_6H_5-CH_2-CH_2-OH$). This compound does not have the $CH_3CH(OH)-$ group, so it won't give a positive iodoform test.
(c) Represents 1-phenylethanol ($C_6H_5-CH(OH)-CH_3$). This compound contains the $CH_3CH(OH)-$ group, which gives a positive iodoform test.
(d) Represents 4-methylphenol (p-cresol). This is a phenol, not an alcohol with the required group.
Therefore, A is 1-phenylethanol. Y is $I_2$, which reacts with NaOH to produce NaOI.

questions.question:

$ \substack{\mathrm{OH} \\ \mathrm{ONa}^{+} \\ + \mathrm{CHCl}_3 + \mathrm{NaOH} \rightarrow \mathrm{CHO}} $

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: When vapours of a secondary alcohol is passed over heated copper at 573 K, the product formed is
questions.solution:
When alcohol vapours are passed over heated copper (Cu) at 573 K (300°C):
- Primary alcohols ($1^\circ$) are dehydrogenated to aldehydes.
- Secondary alcohols ($2^\circ$) are dehydrogenated to ketones.
- Tertiary alcohols ($3^\circ$) undergo dehydration to form alkenes.
Since the reactant is a secondary alcohol, the product formed will be a ketone.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Reaction between acetone and methyl magnesium chloride followed by hydrolysis will give
questions.solution:
Acetone ($CH_3COCH_3$) is a ketone. Ketones react with Grignard reagents ($RMgX$) to form tertiary alcohols after hydrolysis.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Given below are two statements : Statement I: In Lucas test, primary, secondary and tertiary alcohols are distinguished on the basis of their reactivity with conc. $ \mathrm{HCl} + \mathrm{ZnCl}_2 $, known as Lucas Reagent. Statement II : Primary alcohols are most reactive and immediately produced turbidity at room temperature on reaction with Lucas Reagent. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both statement I and statement II are correct.
Both statement I and statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct.
questions.answer: Option (C): Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect.
questions.solution:
Statement I: Lucas test uses Lucas reagent ($conc. HCl + ZnCl_2$) to distinguish primary, secondary, and tertiary alcohols based on the rate of formation of alkyl chlorides (turbidity). This statement is correct.
Statement II: Tertiary alcohols are the most reactive towards Lucas reagent and produce immediate turbidity at room temperature. Primary alcohols are the least reactive and show turbidity only upon heating, if at all. This statement is incorrect.
Therefore, Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Given below are two statements : Statement-I : The acidic strength of monosubstituted nitrophenol is higher than phenol because of electron withdrawing nitro group. Statement-II: o-Nitrophenol, m-Nitrophenol and p-Nitrophenol will have same acidic strength as they have one nitro group attached to the phenolic ring. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both statement-I and statement-II are correct.
Both statement-I and statement-II are incorrect.
Statement-I is correct but statement-II is incorrect.
Statement-I is incorrect but statement-II is correct.
questions.answer: Option (C): Statement-I is correct but statement-II is incorrect.
questions.solution:
Statement-I: Nitro groups ($-NO_2$) are electron-withdrawing groups. Their presence stabilizes the phenoxide ion, thereby increasing the acidic strength of nitrophenols compared to phenol. This statement is correct.
Statement-II: The acidic strengths of o-, m-, and p-nitrophenols are not the same. The electron-withdrawing effect of the nitro group varies with its position. p-Nitrophenol is generally more acidic than o-nitrophenol (due to intramolecular hydrogen bonding in o-nitrophenol reducing its ability to donate a proton, and stronger resonance stabilization for p-nitro). m-Nitrophenol is less acidic than both o- and p-nitrophenol because the nitro group at the meta position primarily exerts an inductive effect and does not directly stabilize the phenoxide ion through resonance. Thus, this statement is incorrect.
Therefore, Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which amongst the following will be most readily dehydrated under acidic conditions?
questions.solution:
Dehydration of alcohols in acidic conditions proceeds via the formation of a carbocation. The ease of dehydration is directly related to the stability of the carbocation intermediate. Alkyl groups (electron-donating) stabilize carbocations, while electron-withdrawing groups (like $NO_2$) destabilize them.
(a) 2-Nitrocyclohexanol: The nitro group is electron-withdrawing, destabilizing the carbocation formed at the carbon where OH is located, making dehydration less favorable.
(b) Cyclohexanol: Forms a secondary carbocation.
(c) 4-Nitrocyclohexanol: Similar to (a), the nitro group's electron-withdrawing inductive effect destabilizes the carbocation, making dehydration less favorable than for cyclohexanol.
(d) 2-Methylcyclohexanol: The methyl group is electron-donating, stabilizing the carbocation formed (via hyperconjugation and inductive effect) more than in plain cyclohexanol. Therefore,…

questions.question:
Consider the following reaction and identify the product (P).
$ \substack{\mathrm{CH}_3\text{-CH-CH-CH}_3 \\ \mathrm{CH}_3 \ \mathrm{OH} \\ \text{3-Methylbutan-2-ol}} \ \xrightarrow{\text{HBr}} \text{Product (P)} $
questions.solution:
The reaction of an alcohol with HBr proceeds via an $S_N1$ mechanism for secondary alcohols, which involves the formation of a carbocation followed by possible rearrangement to a more stable carbocation.
Starting alcohol: 3-Methylbutan-2-ol ($CH_3-CH(OH)-CH(CH_3)-CH_3$).
1. Protonation of the hydroxyl group: $CH_3-CH(OH_2^+)-CH(CH_3)-CH_3$.
2. Loss of water ($H_2O$) to form a secondary carbocation: $CH_3-CH^+-CH(CH_3)-CH_3$.
3. Carbocation rearrangement: A 1,2-hydride shift from the adjacent tertiary carbon ($C_3$) to the secondary carbocation ($C_2$) will result in a more stable tertiary carbocation: $CH_3-CH_2-C^+(CH_3)-CH_3$.
4. Nucleophilic attack by bromide ion ($Br^-$) on the tertiary carbocation to form the final product: 2-bromo-2-methylbutane ($CH_3-CH_2-C(Br)(CH_3)-CH_3$).
This product matches option (c).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which one of the following alcohols reacts instantaneously with Lucas reagent?
questions.solution:
The Lucas test is used to distinguish between primary, secondary, and tertiary alcohols based on their reactivity with Lucas reagent ($conc. HCl + ZnCl_2$). The reactivity order is: Tertiary alcohols > Secondary alcohols > Primary alcohols.
- Tertiary alcohols react instantaneously at room temperature, producing immediate turbidity.
- Secondary alcohols react within 5-10 minutes, producing turbidity.
- Primary alcohols react very slowly or only upon heating.
Let's classify the given alcohols:
(a) Butan-1-ol ($CH_3CH_2CH_2CH_2OH$) is a primary alcohol.
(b) Butan-2-ol ($CH_3CH_2CH(OH)CH_3$) is a secondary alcohol.
(c) 2-Methylpropan-1-ol ($CH_3CH(CH_3)CH_2OH$) is a primary alcohol.
(d) 2-Methylpropan-2-ol ($(CH_3)_3COH$) is a tertiary alcohol.
Therefore, 2-methylpropan-2-ol, being a tertiary alcohol, will react instantaneously with Lucas reagent.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Methanol is industrially prepared by
options: reaction of HCHO with a solution of NaOH
questions.answer: Option (D): reduction of CO using $ \mathrm{H}_2 $ and $ \mathrm{ZnO-Cr_2O_3} $.
questions.solution:
Industrially, methanol ($CH_3OH$) is synthesized by the catalytic reduction of carbon monoxide (CO) with hydrogen ($H_2$) at high temperature and pressure (typically $500-1000$ atm, $300-400^\circ C$) using catalysts such as $ZnO-Cr_2O_3$. This process is known as the synthesis gas ($CO/H_2$) process.
$CO(g) + 2H_2(g) \xrightarrow{ZnO/Cr_2O_3 \quad 300-400^\circ C} CH_3OH(l)$

questions.question: The compound which does not react with sodium is
questions.solution:
Sodium is an active metal that reacts with compounds containing acidic hydrogen atoms (e.g., in -OH or -COOH groups) to produce hydrogen gas and a corresponding sodium salt.
(a) Acetic acid ($CH_3COOH$) has an acidic proton in its carboxyl group.
(b) Propan-2-ol ($CH_3CHOHCH_3$) has an acidic proton in its hydroxyl group.
(c) Ethanol ($C_2H_5OH$) has an acidic proton in its hydroxyl group.
(d) Dimethyl ether ($CH_3OCH_3$) is an ether. The hydrogen atoms are bonded to carbon, and the oxygen atom does not have an acidic proton directly attached. Ethers are generally unreactive with active metals like sodium.
Thus, dimethyl ether does not react with sodium.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Identify Z in the sequence of reactions :
$ \mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{CH}\text{=CH}_2 \xrightarrow{\mathrm{HBr}/\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_2} \text{Y} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{ONa}} \text{Z} $
questions.solution:
1. But-1-ene ($CH_3CH_2CH=CH_2$) reacts with $HBr$ in the presence of peroxide ($H_2O_2$). This is an anti-Markovnikov addition of HBr, where the bromine atom adds to the less substituted carbon atom. The product Y is 1-bromobutane ($CH_3CH_2CH_2CH_2Br$).
2. 1-Bromobutane (Y) reacts with sodium ethoxide ($C_2H_5ONa$). This is a Williamson ether synthesis, an $S_N2$ reaction where the ethoxide ion displaces the bromide ion.
 The product Z is 1-ethoxybutane (butyl ethyl ether, $CH_3CH_2CH_2CH_2OCH_2CH_3$).
 Option (a) shows $CH_3(CH_2)_3OCH_2CH_3$, which is 1-ethoxybutane.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Among the following sets of reactants which one produces anisole?
questions.solution:
Anisole is methyl phenyl ether ($C_6H_5OCH_3$).
(a) Acetaldehyde and Grignard reagent produce alcohols (secondary alcohol with $CH_3MgX$).
(b) Phenol ($C_6H_5OH$) reacts with NaOH to form sodium phenoxide ($C_6H_5ONa$). Sodium phenoxide then reacts with methyl iodide ($CH_3I$) via Williamson ether synthesis to yield anisole. This is a common and effective method.
(c) Phenol with neutral $FeCl_3$ gives a characteristic violet coloration, a test for phenols, not a preparation method for anisole.
(d) Toluene ($C_6H_5CH_3$) with acetyl chloride and $AlCl_3$ undergoes Friedel-Crafts acylation to produce a methyl phenyl ketone, not anisole.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The reaction $ \mathrm{OH} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{NaH}} \mathrm{ONa}^{+} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{Me-I}} \mathrm{OMe} $ can be classified as
questions.solution: The reaction sequence shows phenol reacting with sodium hydride (NaH) to form sodium phenoxide ($C_6H_5ONa$). The phenoxide then reacts with methyl iodide (Me-I) via an $S_N2$ mechanism to produce methyl phenyl ether (anisole, $C_6H_5OCH_3$). This entire process is a prime example of the Williamson ether synthesis.

Among the given options, if dibromination occurs, 2,4-dibromoaniline (d) is a possible product if conditions are not strictly controlled for monobromination.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is more basic than aniline?
questions.solution: Benzylamine is an aliphatic amine whose lone pair is not delocalized by the benzene ring, making it more basic than aniline, an aromatic amine where the lone pair is delocalized by resonance.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following statements about primary amines is false?
options: Alkyl amines are stronger bases than aryl amines.
Alkyl amines react with nitrous acid to produce alcohols.
Aryl amines react with nitrous acid to produce phenols.
Alkyl amines are stronger bases than ammonia.
questions.answer: Option (C): Aryl amines react with nitrous acid to produce phenols.
questions.solution: Aryl amines react with nitrous acid to form diazonium salts, which then hydrolyze to produce phenols. The direct statement 'react...to produce phenols' skips the stable diazonium salt intermediate.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following compounds is most basic?
questions.solution: Benzylamine is an aliphatic amine; its nitrogen lone pair is not delocalized by the benzene ring, making it more basic than aniline derivatives or amides.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: An organic compound ($C_3H_9N$) (A), when treated with nitrous acid, gave an alcohol and $N_2$ gas was evolved. (A) on warming with $CHCl_3$ and caustic potash gave (C) which on reduction gave isopropylmethylamine. Predict the structure of (A).
questions.solution: The formation of alcohol and $N_2$ with nitrous acid indicates A is a primary aliphatic amine. The formula $C_3H_9N$ implies propan-1-amine or propan-2-amine. However, if 'isopropylmethylamine' is the reduction product of C, it points to propan-2-amine (isopropylamine). But propan-2-amine is not an option. Given the options, propan-1-amine (d) is the only primary amine matching the formula, despite the inconsistency with the final product name.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: On hydrolysis of a "compound", two compounds are obtained. One of which on treatment with sodium nitrite and hydrochloric acid gives a product which does not respond to iodoform test. The second one reduces Tollens' reagent and Fehling's solution. The "compound" is
questions.solution: Hydrolysis of propyl isocyanide ($CH_3CH_2CH_2NC$) yields propan-1-amine ($CH_3CH_2CH_2NH_2$) and formic acid ($HCOOH$). Propan-1-amine, upon diazotization, gives propan-1-ol, which does not give the iodoform test. Formic acid reduces Tollens' and Fehling's reagents.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The correct statement regarding the basicity of arylamines is
options: arylamines are generally more basic than alkylamines because of aryl group
arylamines are generally more basic than alkylamines, because the nitrogen atom in arylamines is sp-hybridised
arylamines are generally less basic than alkylamines because the nitrogen lone-pair electrons are delocalised by interaction with the aromatic ring electron system
arylamines are generally more basic than alkylamines because the nitrogen lone-pair electrons are not delocalised by interaction with the aromatic ring electron system.
questions.answer: Option (C): arylamines are generally less basic than alkylamines because the nitrogen lone-pair electrons are delocalised by interaction with the aromatic ring electron system
questions.solution: The resonance delocalization of the nitrogen lone pair into the aromatic ring reduces its availability for protonation, thereby decreasing the basicity of arylamines compared to alkylamines.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The correct increasing order of basic strength for the following compounds is
questions.solution: p-Nitroaniline (II) is weakest due to electron-withdrawing $NO_2$ group. Aniline (I) is next. p-Toluidine (III) is strongest due to electron-donating $CH_3$ group.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Nitration of aniline in strong acidic medium also gives m-nitroaniline because
options: inspite of substituents nitro group always goes to only m-position
in electrophilic substitution reactions amino group is meta directive
in absence of substituents nitro group always goes to m-position
in acidic (strong) medium aniline is present as anilinium ion.
questions.answer: Option (D): in acidic (strong) medium aniline is present as anilinium ion.
questions.solution: In strong acidic medium, aniline is protonated to form anilinium ion ($C_6H_5NH_3^+$), which is a meta-directing and deactivating group, leading to m-nitroaniline.
