(a) In roots, xylem and phloem in a vascular bundle are arranged in an alternate manner along the different radii.
(b) Conjoint closed vascular bundles do not possess cambium
(c) In open vascular bundles, cambium is present in between xylem and phloem
(d) The vascular bundles of dicotyledonous stem possess endarch protoxylem
(e) In monocotyledonous root, usually there are more than six xylem bundles present
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.answer: Option (D): All the options are correct
questions.solution:
All the given statements are correct:
• When xylem and phloem within a vascular bundle are arranged in an alternate manner along the different radii, the arrangement is called radial such as in roots.
• Conjoint, closed vascular bundles enclose both xylem and phloem. Xylem is found towards the inner surface and phloem towards the outer surface. Cambium is absent.
• Open vascular bundles are vascular bundles in which secondary growth is possible. This type of vascular bundle has cambium present in between the xylem and phloem.
• Vascular bundles of dicot stem are eight in number, arranged in the form of a broken ring. The vascular bundles are conjoint, collateral and open. Xylem is on the inner surface and phloem on the outer surface. Xylem is described as endarch.
• Vascular bundles in monocot roots are radial, polyarch and exarch. Large number (more than 6) of xylem and phloem groups al…

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Read the different components from (a) to (d) in the list given below and tell the correct order of the components with reference to their arrangement from outer side to inner side in a woody dicot stem:
(1) Secondary cortex (2) Wood
(3) Secondary phloem (4) Phellem The correct order is:
questions.solution: The correct order of the components with reference to their arrangement from outer side to inner side in a woody dicot stem is phellem – secondary cortex – secondary phloem – wood.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is made up of dead cells?
questions.solution: Cork cambium undergoes periclinal division and cuts off thick-walled suberized dead cells toward outside i.e., phellem (cork) and it cuts off thin-walled living cells i.e., phelloderm on the inner side. Parenchyma is living tissue and helps in support and storing food. Collenchyma is also living tissue that provides tensile strength to plants.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Find the statement that is NOT correct with regard to the structure of monocot stem.
options: Vascular bundles are conjoint and closed
questions.solution: The monocot stem has a sclerenchymatous hypodermis, a large number of scattered vascular bundles, Vascular bundles are conjoint and closed & phloem parenchyma is absent.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Bulliform cells are responsible for
options: Protecting the plant from salt stress.
Providing large spaces for storage of sugars.
Inward curling of leaves in monocots.
questions.answer: Option (D): Inward curling of leaves in monocots.
questions.solution: In grasses, certain adaxial epidermal cells along the veins modify themselves into large, empty, colourless cells. These are called bulliform cells. When the bulliform cells in the leaves have absorbed water and are turgid, the leaf surface is exposed. When they are flaccid due to water stress, they make the leaves curl inwards to minimise water loss Bulliform cells are therefore responsible for inward curling of leaves in the monocots.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Identify the correct statements:
A. Lenticels are the lens-shaped openings permitting the exchange of gases.
B. Bark formed early in the season is called hard bark.
C. Bark is a technical term that refers to all tissues exterior to vascular cambium.
D. Bark refers to periderm and secondary phloem.
E. Phellogen is single layered in thickness.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: A and D only

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Casparian strips occur in
options: <!-StartFragment->Epidermis of both monocot and dicot root<!-EndFragment->
questions.answer: Option (D): Endodermis cell of dicot root
questions.solution: Endodermis of the root contains a Casparian strip on the radial and inner tangential wall. It is formed by the deposition of suberin. Casparian strips are impermeable for water and it is a characteristic feature of roots.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The balloon- shaped structures called tyloses
options: Are extensions of xylem parenchyma cells into vessels
Are linked to the ascent to sap through xylem vessels
Originate in the lumen of vessels
questions.answer: Option (B): Are extensions of xylem parenchyma cells into vessels
questions.solution: The balloon shaped structures, formed in the vessels of heart wood, due to the extension of parenchyma are called tyloses. They block the vessels. They contain the depositions of bio-chemicals like tannins, resins, gums, etc. Due to the presence of tyloses, heart wood cannot conduct water and heart wood shows resistance to pathogens to insects. So it is highly durable. So, the correct option is ‘are extensions of xylem parenchyma cells into vessels’.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Plant having little or no secondary growth are
questions.solution:
Secondary growth occurs in dicot and gymnosperms. Grasses are monocots hence they do not perform secondary growth.
Palm like monocots shows anomalous secondary growth.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II :
List-IList-II
A.Conjunctive tissueI.Specialised cells in the vicinity of guard cells
B.Casparian stripsII.Endodermal cells rich in starch
C.Subsidiary cellsIII.Tissue between xylem and phloem
D.Starch sheathIV.Endodermal cells with suberin deposition

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
(A) Conjunctive tissue is the tissue between xylem and phloem.
(B) Casparian strips are found in endodermal cells, they are suberin depositions in the cell wall.
(C) Subsidiary cells are specialised cells in the vicinity of guard cells.
(D) Starch sheath is another name for endodermal cells rich in starch.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Lenticels are involved in
questions.solution: Lenticels are involved in gaseous exchange between the plant stem and the surrounding.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Cortex is the region found between
questions.solution:
Cortex is the ground tissue present below the epidermis. It surrounds the central cylinder and endodermis lines the outermost layer of the cylinder. So, the region between epidermis and stele is cortex. Pericycle is present between the endodermis and vascular bundle. The whole ground tissue system (cortex, endodermis and pericycle) is present between epidermis and stele. 
Therefore, the correct answer is option d.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Identify the wrong statement in the context of heartwood.
options: It conducts water and minerals efficiently
It comprises dead elements with highly lignified walls
Organic compounds are deposited in it
questions.answer: Option (A): It conducts water and minerals efficiently
questions.solution: Heartwood is physiologically inactive due to the deposition of organic compounds and tyloses formation, so this will not conduct water and minerals.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Phloem of gymnosperms lacks
options: Both sieve tubes and companion cells
questions.answer: Option (C): Both sieve tubes and companion cells
questions.solution: Phloem in gymnosperms lacks both sieve tube and companion cells, whereas they contain albuminous cells and sieve cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
The transverse section of a plant shows following anatomical features:
(i) Large number of scattered vascular bundles surrounded by bundle sheath.
(ii) Large conspicuous parenchymatous ground tissue.
(iii) Vascular bundles conjoint and closed.
(iv) Phloem parenchyma absent.
Identify the category of plant and its part:
questions.solution:
All anatomical features mentioned is shown by monocotyledonous stem so option 
(c) is correct. In monocots vascular bundles are scattered between parenchymatous ground tissue. There is no pith region in monocots. The vascular bundles are closed as they do not have cambium in it.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Grass leaves curl inwards during very dry weather. Select the most appropriate reason from the following:
options: Shrinkage of air spaces in spongy mesophyll
questions.solution: Bulliform cells are the modified epidermal cell present in the leaves of grasses. Bulliform cells become flaccid due to water loss. This makes the leaves curl inward to minimise water loss.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Tracheids differ from other tracheary elements in
questions.solution: Tracheids and vessels together are called tracheary elements as both take part in transport of sap. Tracheids differ from other tracheary elements in being imperforate and their wall is more thickened. The wall of vessels is perforated.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Stomata in grass leaves are
questions.solution: Monocots contain dumb-bell shaped stomata. Grass being a monocot, has dumb-bell shaped stomata in its leaves. Kidney shaped stomata are present in dicot leaves.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Secondary xylem and phloem in dicot stem are produced by
questions.solution:
Vascular cambium is partially primary and partially secondary meristem.
It forms the secondary xylem towards the inside and the secondary phloem towards the outsides.
4-10 times more secondary xylem is produced than secondary phloem due to differential activity of cambium.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Endarch and exarch are the terms often used for describing the position of secondary xylem in the plant body.
Statement II: Exarch condition is the most common feature of the root system.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is false.
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
questions.answer: Option (C): Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is true.
questions.solution: Endarch and exarch are the terms often used for describing the position of primary xylem in the plant body.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Given below are two statements.
Statement 1: Parenchyma is living but collenchyma is dead tissue
Statement 2: Gymnosperms lack xylem vessels but presence of xylem vessels is the characteristic of angiosperms.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
questions.answer: Option (C): Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.solution:
Both Parenchyma and Collenchyma are living simple permanent tissue, while sclerenchyma is a dead tissue.
Phloem in Angiosperms is composed of sieve tube elements, companion cells. Gymnosperms have albuminous cells and sieve cells. They lack sieve tubes and companion cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: You are given a fairly old piece of dicot stem and a dicot root. Which of the following anatomical structures will you use to distinguish between the two?
questions.solution: In stems, the protoxylem lies towards the centre (pith) and the metaxylem lies towards the periphery of the organ. This type of primary xylem is called endarch. In roots, the protoxylem lies towards the periphery and the metaxylem lies towards the centre. Such arrangement of primary xylem is called exarch.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Age of a tree can be estimated by
questions.solution: The number of annual rings tells the age of the tree. The number of annual rings suggests the number of years. The annual rings of a tree are made each year when a new layer of wood is added to the trunk and branches of the tree. The study of the rings of trees is called dendrochronology.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Identify the basic amino acid from the following.
questions.solution: Lysine is the basic amino acid. Valine is neutral amino acid. Tyrosine is an aromatic amino acid. Glutamic acid is acidic amino acid.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
The anatomy of springwood shows some peculiar features. Identify the correct set of statements about springwood.
(a) It is also called early wood.
(b) In the spring season cambium produces xylem elements with narrow vessels.
(c) It is lighter in colour.
(d) The springwood along with autumnwood shows alternate concentric rings forming annual rings.
(e) It has lower density
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
In the spring season, cambium is very active. The wood formed during this season is called spring wood or early wood.
- In spring season, cambium produces a large number of xylary elements having vessels
with wider cavities and not narrow cavities.
-The spring wood is lighter in colour.
-The two kinds of woods (spring and autumnwood) appear as alternate concentric rings that constitute an annual ring. Annual rings seen in a cut stem give an estimate of the age of the tree.
-Springwood has a lower density.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Select the correct pair.
options: Cells of medullary rays that form part of cambial ring - Interfascicular cambium
Loose parenchyma cells rupturing the epidermis and forming a lens-shaped opening in bark - Spongy parenchyma
Large colorless empty cells in the epidermis of grass leaves – Subsidiary cells
In dicot leaves, vascular bundles are surrounded by large thick-walled cells– Conjunctive tissue
questions.answer: Option (A): Cells of medullary rays that form part of cambial ring - Interfascicular cambium
questions.solution: When the cells of medullary rays are differentiated, they give rise to the new cambium called interfascicular cambium. Loose parenchyma cells rupturing the epidermis and forming a lens-shaped opening in the bark are called complementary cells. Large colourless empty cells in the epidermis of grass leaves are called bulliform cells. In the dicot leaf, vascular bundles are surrounded by large thick-walled cells called bundle sheath cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Consider the following features:
(1) Organ system level of organisation
(2) Bilateral symmetry
(3) True coelomates with segmentation on body
Select the correct option of animal groups which possess all the above characteristics:
questions.solution: True segmentation is present in Annelida, Arthropoda and Chordata. They also have organ system level of organisation, bilateral symmetry and are true coelomates.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which among these is the correct combination of aquatic mammals?
questions.solution: Sharks and Trygon (stingray) are the members of Chondrichthyes (cartilaginous fish) while whales, dolphins, and seals are aquatic mammals that belong to class Mammalia.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Select the incorrect statements from the following:
A. Digestive system in Platyhelminthes is incomplete.
B. Bilateral symmetry is a characteristic feature of adult Echinoderms.
C. Pseudocoelom is possessed by Aschelminthes.
D. Notochord is persistent throughout life in the class Chondrichthyes.
E. Members of class Reptilia maintain a constant body temperature.

Choose the answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
$(\mathrm{A}) \rightarrow$ correct → Platyhelminthes have an incomplete digestive system.
(B) → incorrect → Bilateral symmetry is a characteristic feature of larvae of echinoderms. In adult echinoderms, radial symmetry is seen.
(C) → correct → Aschelminthes are characterised by the presence of pseudocoelom.
(D) → correct → Notochord is persistent throughout life in the Chondrichthyes.
(E) → incorrect → Reptiles are cold-blooded organisms and thus, they cannot maintain a constant body temperature.

Warm-blooded organisms like birds and mammals can maintain a constant body temperature.
Thus, as the incorrect statements are indicated by ( B ) and ( E ) only, the correct answer is option (a)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The unique mammalian characteristics are
options: Pinna, monocondylic skull and mammary glands
Hairs, tympanic membrane and mammary glands
questions.answer: Option (A): Hairs, pinna and mammary glands
questions.solution: Hairs, pinna and mammary glands

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Infection of Ascaris usually occurs by
questions.answer: Option (A): Drinking water containing eggs of Ascaris
questions.solution: Infection of Ascaris occurs because of the consumption of food and water contaminated with eggs of Ascaris.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Consider the following statement:
A. Annelids are true coelomates
B. Poriferans are pseudocoelomates
C. Aschelminthes are acoelomates
D. Platyhelminthes are pseudocoelomates
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Poriferans are Acoelomates
Aschelminthes are Pseudocoelomate
Platyhelminthes are Acoelomates

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List I with List II.
List IList II
A.Taenia I.Nephridia
B.Paramoecium II.Contractile vacuole
C.Periplaneta III.Flame cells
D.Pheretima IV.Uricose gland

Choose the correct answer from the options give below:
questions.solution: List IList IIA.Taenia III.Flame cellsB.Paramoecium II.Contractile vacuoleC.Periplaneta IV.Uricose glandD.Pheretima I.Nephridia

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match the following columns and select the correct option.
Column IColumn II
(a) 6-15 pairs of gill slits(i) Trygon
(b) Heterocercal caudal fin(ii) Cyclostomes
(c) Air bladder(iii) Chondrichthyes
(d) Poison sting(iv) Osteichthyes
options: a – iv; b – ii; c – iii; d – i
a – i; b – iv; c – iii; d – ii
a – ii; b – iii; c – iv; d – i
a – iii; b – iv; c – i; d – ii
questions.answer: Option (C): a – ii; b – iii; c – iv; d – i
questions.solution:
(a) Cyclostomata that belongs to agnatha which comprises the living jawless 
vertebrates.
(b) Chondrichthyes consists of the cartilaginous fishes (eg. shark), a typical member of which has heterocercal (two unequal lobes) caudal fins.
(c) Osteichthyes consists of the bony fishes in which air bladder is present which 
regulates buoyancy.
(d) Chondrichthyes poison sting (e.g., Trygon, whose common name is sting ray).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Genus represents
options: a population of plants and animals
a group of closely related species
a group of closely related families
questions.answer: Option (B): a group of closely related species
questions.solution: Genus comprises a group of related species which has more characters in common in comparison to species of other genera.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Radial symmetry is NOT found in adults of phylum ______.
questions.solution: Adults of phylum Hemichordata exhibit Bilateral symmetry.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: All living members of the class Cyclostomata are:
questions.solution: All living members of class cyclostomata are ectoparasites.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: When any plane passing through the central axis of the body divides the organism into two identical halves, it is called radial symmetry.
Statement II: In phylum Echinodermata, both adults and larvae are radially symmetrical.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.answer: Option (B): Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
questions.solution: When any plane passing through the central axis of the body divides the organism into two identical halves, it is called radial symmetry. Adult echinoderms are radially symmetrical while larval echinoderms are bilaterally symmetrical.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of these animals is not a homeotherm?
questions.solution:
Homeotherm is animals that maintain constant body temperature, irrespective of surrounding temperature. Birds and mammals are homeotherms. Camelus and Macropus are mammals whereas Psittacula is a bird.
Chelone (Turtle) belongs to class reptilia which are Poikilotherm or cold blood.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following characteristics is not shared by birds and mammals?
questions.solution: Both mammals and birds can regulate body temperature and have warm-blooded nature. They have lungs and hence use them for breathing. Both the groups have ossified endoskeletons (formation of bones by adding osteoblasts - osteogenesis, results in an ossified endoskeleton.) But birds lay eggs and show oviparity whereas mammals give birth to live young and show Vivipary (except Monotremes or egg-laying mammals).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
A group of researchers procured some fish like animals and upon investigation the following characters were observed:
A. Endoskeleton was made of cartilage.
B. Ectoparasitic; as they were found attached on fish skin with their circular sucking mouth.
C. Paired fins and scales were absent, but 7 pairs of gill slits were present.

Which of the following species of animals did they consider to fit best with these characters?
questions.solution:
Petromyzon sp. have cartilaginous endoskeleton. They have circular sucking mouth. They are ectoparasites on some fishes. Their body is devoid of scales and paired fins. They have 7 pairs (6-15 pairs) of gill slits.
Scoliodon and Exocoetus are not parasites.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following living organisms completely lacks a cell wall?
questions.solution: Sea-fan (Gorgonia) belongs to kingdom Animalia and phylum Cnidaria, which completely lacks a cell wall. Saccharomyces is a fungus which has a cell wall majorly composed of chitin. Blue-green algae or cyanobacteria are the eubacteria which are covered by cell wall.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Select the correct statements with reference to chordates.
A. Presence of mid-dorsal, solid and double nerve cord.
B. Presence of closed circulatory system
C. Presence of paired pharyngeal gill slits
D. Presence of dorsal heart
E. Triploblastic pseudocoelomate animals
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
A. Presence of dorsal, hollow nerve cord.
D. Presence of ventral heart
E. Triploblastic coelomate animals

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as
Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): All vertebrates are chordates but all chordates are not vertebrates
Reason (R): Notochord is replaced by the vertebral column in the adult vertebrates.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.answer: Option (A): Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.solution: All vertebrates are chordates but all chordates are not vertebrates. This statement is true because all the features of chordates are present in all the vertebrates in some stage of life. In adult vertebrates, the notochord is replaced by the vertebral column and this is not the case for all chordates, hence the assertion is correct and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Following are the statements about the prostomium of earthworms.
(a) It serves as a covering for the mouth
(b) It helps to open cracks in the soil into which it can crawl
(c) It is one of the sensory structures
(d) It is the first body segment
Choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: (a), (b), (c) and (d) are correct
(b), (c) are correct
(a), (b) and (c) are correct
(a), (b) and (d) are correct
questions.solution: The anterior end of the earthworm has a mouth that has a covering called prostomium. Prostomium acts as a wedge to force open cracks in the soil. Prostomium has receptors, so it is sensory in function. The first body segment of earthworms is the peristomium.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Select the taxon mentioned that represents both marine and freshwater species.
questions.solution: Phylum Cnidaria includes both marine and freshwater species. However, most of them are marine, only a few are freshwater species. Ctenophora, Cephalochordata, Echinoderms are found exclusively in the marine environment.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Exoskeleton of arthropods is composed of:
questions.solution: All arthropods have a hard exoskeleton made of chitin, a type of protein. This shell provides protection for the animals, and gives support for the attachment of the arthropod's muscles. Although arthropods grow, their exoskeletons do not grow with them.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following characteristic features always holds true for the corresponding group of animals?
options: Possess a mouth with an upper and a lower jaw – Chordata
questions.solution: Chondrichthyes is a class that contains the cartilaginous fishes: they are jawed vertebrates with paired fins, paired nares, scales, a heart with its chambers in series, and skeletons made of cartilage rather than bone. Viviparous - Giving birth to living young that develop within the mother's body rather than hatching from eggs. Not all mammals are viviparous like platypus. All chordates do not possess a mouth with an upper and lower jaw. All reptiles have three-chambered hearts, except crocodiles, which have four-chambered hearts (2 atria, 2 ventricles), like mammals and birds.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Select the set of fishes which belong to the class Osteichthyes:
options: Flying fish, Angel fish and Fighting fish
Saw fish, Fighting fish and Dog fish
questions.answer: Option (C): Flying fish, Angel fish and Fighting fish
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option (3).
Flying fish (Exocoetus) is a marine bony fish. Angel fish (Pterophyllum) and fighting fish (Betta) are aquarium bony fishes.
Option (1) is incorrect as:-
Devil fish (Octopus) and cuttlefish (Sepia) are molluscs.
Hag fish (Myxine) is a cyclostome.
Option (4) is incorrect as:-
Saw fish (Pristis) and dog fish (Scoliodon) are cartilaginous fishes.
Option (2) is incorrect as:-
Starfish (Asterias) is an echinoderm.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following features is not present in the phylum Arthropoda?
questions.solution: Arthropods have a rigid chitinous exoskeleton that covers their complete body. They are characterized by a segmented body with repetitions of organs and tissues at intervals i.e. metameric segmentation and have paired, jointed appendages to perform different functions. Parapodia are lateral appendages of annelids and are characteristic features of Nereis (Phylum Annelida), not Arthropoda.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Planaria possess high capacity of:
questions.solution: Planaria is a flatworm which possesses a high capacity of regeneration. They have a high capacity of the generation due to the neoplastic cells which are found in them. If an individual is cut transversely into two parts, the anterior segment will generate a new tail and posterior end will develop a new head.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Read the following statements.
(a) Metagenesis is observed in Helminths.
(b) Echinoderms are triploblastic and coelomate animals.
(c) Roundworms have organ-system level of body organization.
(d) Comb plates present in ctenophores help in digestion.
(e) Water vascular system is characteristic of Echinoderms.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: (a), (d) and (e) are correct
(b), (c) and (e) are correct
(c), (d) and (e) are correct
(a), (b) and (c) are correct
questions.solution: Metagenesis is the characteristic of cnidarians. Those cnidarians which exist in both forms exhibit alternation of generation (Metagenesis), i.e., polyps produce medusae asexually and medusae form the polyps sexually (e.g., Obelia). Ctenophores, commonly known as sea walnuts or comb jellies are exclusively marine, radially symmetrical, diploblastic organisms with tissue level of organization. The body bears eight external rows of ciliated comb plates, which help in locomotion.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is not a characteristic of chordates?
questions.solution: The members of phylum Chordata show following features: (1) Presence of notochord (2) Pharynx perforated by gill slits (3) Dorsal, hollow and single central nervous system (4) Ventral heart (5) A post-anal tail. Gill slits are absent in non-chordates.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List I with List II:
List IList II
A. PterophyllumI. Hag fish
B. MyxineII. Saw fish
C. PristisIII. Angel fish
D. ExocoetusIV. Flying fish

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Pterophyllum - Angel fish
Myxine - Hag fish
Pristis - saw fish
Exocoetus - Flying fish

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which group of animals belongs to the same phylum?
questions.solution:
Prawns, scorpions and locusts belong to the phylum Arthropoda. Hence, the (c) option is correct.Whereas malarial parasite is a sporozoan, Amoeba is an amoeboid protozoan and mosquito belongs to Arthropoda. Hence, the (a) option is wrong.
Earthworm belongs to Annelida, Pinworm belongs to Ascheminthes, Tapeworm belongs to Platyhelminthes. Hence, the (b) option is incorrect.

Sponge belongs to Porifera, Sea anemone belongs to Cnidaria, Starﬁsh belongs to Echinodermata. Hence, the (d) option is also incorrect.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: An important characteristic that Hemichordates share with Chordates is
questions.solution: Pharyngeal gill slits are present in hemichordates as well as in chordates. The notochord is present in chordates only. The ventral tubular nerve cord is a characteristic feature of non-chordates.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following organisms bears hollow and pneumatic long bones?
questions.solution: The scientific name of Vulture is Neophron. Vultures belong to the class Aves. Aves possess an endoskeleton that is fully ossified (bony) and the long bones are hollow with air cavities (pneumatic). Macropus is the scientific name of kangaroo. questions.subject: Biology

questions.solution:
Oily fishes store omega-3 fatty acids (oil) in their tissues and body cavity and are the richest source of omega-3 fatty acid. Fish oils contain the omega-3 fatty acids eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA). The most widely available dietary source of EPA and DHA is oily fish, such as salmon, herring, mackerel, anchovies, menhaden, and sardines. questions.solution: A species facing extremely high risk of extinction in the immediate future is called critically endangered species. A species is vulnerable when it is not critically endangered or endangered but is facing a high risk of extinction in the medium-term future.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: An example of ex situ conservation is:
questions.solution: Ex-situ conservation is the preservation of samples of biological origin outside their natural habitats. This involves conservation of genetic resources as well as wild and cultivated species. A seed bank stores seeds as a source for planting in case seed reserves elsewhere are destroyed. It is a type of gene bank. The seeds stored may be food crops or those of rare species to protect biodiversity. Whereas in-situ conservation is the conservation and maintenance of samples of living organisms in their natural habitat. Wildlife sanctuary, sacred groves and national parks are examples of in-situ conservation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Alexander Von Humbolt described for the first time
questions.solution: Alexander Von Humbolt discovered species-area relationships. Species area relationships are the relationship between the area and the particular habitat. It is dependent on immigration, extinction, and clustering, etc. This relation can be graphically expressed as a rectangular hyperbola.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Habitat loss and fragmentation, over exploitation, alien species invasion and co-extinction are causes for:
questions.solution: 'The Evil Quartet' of biodiversity loss is a concept that describes the reason that causes extinction of species. These main four reasons are overexploitation, loss of habitat, extinction of species continuously and introduction of the exotic species.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following represents the maximum number of species among global biodiversity?
questions.solution: Fungi represent the maximum number of species among global biodiversity.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following regions of the globe exhibits highest species diversity?
questions.solution: Species diversity is the number of different species that are present in a given community. Amazon forest is the richest ecosystem on earth. It contains millions of species of plants, insects, birds and other forms of life, many are still unrecorded by scientists.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The type of conservation in which the threatened species are taken out from their natural habitat and placed in special setting when they can he protected and given special care is called
questions.solution: Ex situ Conservation – In this approach, threatened animals and plants are taken out from their natural habitat and placed in special setting where they can be protected and given special care.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Following are the statements with reference to 'lipids'.
(a) Lipids having only single bonds are called unsaturated fatty acids.
(b) Lecithin is a phospholipid
(c) Trihydroxy propane is glycerol.
(d) Palmitic acid has 20 carbon atoms including carboxyl carbon
(e) Arachidonic acid has 16 carbon atoms
Choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: (b) and (c) only
(b) and (e) only
(a) and (b) only
(c) and (d) only
questions.solution: The correct option is (a) because lipids having only single bonds are called saturated fatty acids and lipids having one or more C = C double bonds are called unsaturated fatty acids. Palmitic acid has 16 carbon atoms including carboxyl carbon. Arachidonic acid has 20 carbon atoms including carboxyl carbon. Lecithin is a phospholipid found in the cell membrane. Glycerol has 3 carbons, each bearing a hydroxyl (–OH) group.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following organisms are known as chief producers in the oceans?
questions.solution: Phytoplankton is the producer in the ocean. Diatoms belong to the class of phytoplankton which are known as chief producers in the ocean.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Select the wrong statement.
options: Pseudopodia are locomotory and feeding structures in Sporozoans
Cell wall is present in members of Fungi and Plantae
Mitochondria are the powerhouse of the cell in all kingdoms except monera
questions.answer: Option (B): Pseudopodia are locomotory and feeding structures in Sporozoans
questions.solution:
Pseudopodia are the finger-like projections and are the locomotory organs of the protozoan protists. For example, Amoeba.
The cell wall is present in the members of both the kingdom Fungi and Plantae. Fungi have a cell wall made up of chitin and polysaccharides while plants' cell wall is made up of cellulose and hemicellulose.
Mitochondria are called the powerhouse of the cell because these are associated with cellular respiration. Mitochondria is present only in eukaryotes and absent in prokaryotes i.e. in members of kingdom Monera.
Mushrooms belong to the class Basidiomycetes of kingdom Fungi. For example, Agaricus.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Identify the asexual reproductive structure associated with Penicillium:
questions.solution: In Penicillium, asexual spores called conidia produced exogenously on the special mycelium called conidiophores. Conidia, upon germination, produce mycelium.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Thiobacillus is a group of bacteria helpful in carrying out
questions.solution: Thiobacillus denitrificans cause denitrification i.e., conversion of oxides of nitrogen to free N2.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Floridean starch has structure similar to
questions.solution: Floridean starch is the storage substance found in red algae (Rhodophyta). The structure of this compound is similar to amylopectin and glycogen.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Pigment-containing membranous extensions in some cyanobacteria are
questions.solution: In cyanobacteria, chromatophores are the photosynthetic pigments containing membranous extensions. These pigments are mainly chlorophylls and impart their peculiar bluish green colour.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-IList-II
A. Fusion of protoplasms between gametesI. Meiosis
B. Fusion of two nucleiII. Plasmogamy
C. Generation of haploid sporesIII. Karyogamy

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Karyogamy involve fusion of two nuclei. Plasmogamy is fusion of protoplasm. Meiosis leads to the production of haploid spores.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: After karyogamy followed by meiosis, spores are produced exogenously in
questions.solution:
In Agaricus (a genus of basidiomycetes), basidiospores are produced exogenously on a basidium.
Neurospora (a genus of ascomycetes) produces ascospores but endogenously inside the ascus.
Alternaria (a genus of Deuteromycetes) does not produce sexual spores.
Saccharomyces (Unicellular ascomycetes) produces ascospores endogenously.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following fungi contains hallucinogens?
questions.solution: Hallucinogen is the psychoactive agent that causes hallucination. It can be found in some plants and mushrooms. Amanita muscaria or fly amanita is a mushroom and psychoactive basidiomycete fungus, in the genus Amanita produces muscimol which has hallucinogenic properties.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match the following
Column IColumn II
(a) Inhibitor of catalytic Activity(i) Ricin
(b) Possess peptide bonds(ii) Malonate
(c) Cell wall material in fungi(iii) Chitin
(d) Secondary metabolite(iv) Collagen
options: a – iii; b – iv; c – i; d – ii
a – ii; b – iii; c – i; d – iv
a – ii; b – iv; c – iii; d – i
a – iii; b – i; c – iv; d – ii
questions.answer: Option (C): a – ii; b – iv; c – iii; d – i
questions.solution: Malonate resembles succinate in structure. Succinate is the substrate of the enzyme succinate dehydrogenase. Hence malonate acts as a competitive inhibitor of this enzyme. Collagen is a protein, and hence contains peptide bonds. Cell wall of fungi is made of chitin. Ricin, a toxin, is a secondary metabolite.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is correct about viroids?
options: They have DNA with a protein coat
They have free DNA without a protein coat
They have RNA with a protein coat
They have free RNA without a protein coat
questions.answer: Option (D): They have free RNA without a protein coat
questions.solution: Viroids have free RNA without a protein coat. Potato spindle tuber disease is a disease caused by viroids.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Select the WRONG statement.
options: ‘Diatomaceous earth’ is formed by the cell walls of diatoms
Diatoms are chief producers in the oceans
Diatoms are microscopic and float passively in water
The walls of diatoms are easily destructible
questions.answer: Option (D): The walls of diatoms are easily destructible
questions.solution: Diatoms are unicellular eukaryotes placed under the kingdom Protista and serve as main producers in oceans. The cell of diatoms is surrounded by the cell wall, deposited with silica, called as frustules which are composed of two overlapping halves (the epitheca and the hypotheca). Shells of diatoms are highly resistant to decomposition due to the presence of silica and are deposited in ocean beds leading to the formation of the diatomaceous earth. The gliding movement of floating diatoms is a passive process, facilitated by secretion of slimy material. Therefore, the correct answer is option d.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Each of the following characteristics represent a Kingdom proposed by Whittaker. Arrange the following in increasing order of complexity of body organization.
A. Multicellular heterotrophs with cell wall made of chitin.
B. Heterotrophs with tissue/organ/organ system level of body organization.
C. Prokaryotes with cell wall made of polysaccharides and amino acids.
D. Eukaryotic autotrophs with tissue/organ level of body organization.
E. Eukaryotes with cellular body organization.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.answer: Option (D): C, E, A, D, B
questions.solution:
According to the R.H. Whittaker (1969) 
1. Monera - Prokaryotic cell which cell wall made up of Non-cellulosic (Polysaccharide + amino acid)
2. Protista - Eukaryotic with cellular body organisation
3. Fungi - Eukaryotic multicelluar heterotrophs with cell wall made of chitin 
4. Plantae - Eukaryotic autotrophs with tissue/ organ level of organisation. 
5. Animalia - Heterotrophs with Tissue/organ/ organ system level of organisation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Select the WRONG statement.
options: Pili and fimbriae are mainly involved in motility of bacterial cells
Bacterial cell wall is made up of peptidoglycan
questions.answer: Option (A): Pili and fimbriae are mainly involved in motility of bacterial cells
questions.solution:
Fimbriae and pili are hair-like appendages present on the bacterial cell wall similar to flagella. They are shorter than flagella and more in number. They are involved in the bacterial conjugation, attachment to the surface and motility. They are present in both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria but more prevalent in Gram-negative bacteria.
Fimbriae and pili are extensions of the cytoplasmic membrane and are made up of an oligomeric protein known as pilin.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Pick out the wrong statement.
options: Cell wall is absent in Animalia.
Protista have photosynthetic and heterotrophic modes of nutrition.
Nuclear membrane is present in Monera.
questions.answer: Option (D): Nuclear membrane is present in Monera.
questions.solution: Kingdom Monera includes prokaryotes in which nuclear membrane is absent. Hence, the (d) statement is wrong.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which among the following is not a prokaryote?
questions.solution:
Saccharomyces i.e. yeast is a eukaryote (unicellular fungi).
Mycobacterium is a bacteria i.e. prokaryote.
Anabaena and Nostoc are cyanobacteria; they are also prokaryotes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: An example of colonial alga is
questions.solution: Volvox is a motile colonial freshwater alga with a definite number of vegetative cells. It is a unicellular green alga found in freshwater bodies. It is photosynthetic in nature.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following are the most suitable indicators of SO<sub>2</sub> pollution in the environment?
questions.solution: Lichens are useful bioindicators for air pollution, especially sulphur dioxide pollution since they derive essential nutrients from sulphur dioxide. If air is badly polluted with SO2, there may be no lichens present.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
options: Organisms that depend on living plants are called saprophytes
Some of the organisms can fix atmospheric nitrogen in specialized cells called sheath cells
Fusion of two cells is called Karyogamy
Fusion of protoplasms between two motile or non-motile gametes is called plasmogamy
questions.answer: Option (D): Fusion of protoplasms between two motile or non-motile gametes is called plasmogamy
questions.solution: Saprophytes are plants and animals which live on dead material and obtain all their nutrients. Some of these organisms can fix atmospheric nitrogen in specialized cells called heterocysts, e.g., Nostoc and Anabaena. The fusion of two nuclei is called karyogamy.Hence, the (d) option is correct as fusion of protoplasms between two motile or non-motile gametes is called plasmogamy.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Ciliates differ from all other protozoans in
options: Having a contractile vacuole for removing excess water
questions.answer: Option (D): Having two types of nuclei
questions.solution:
Ciliates differ from other protozoans in having two types of nuclei.
eg. Paramoecium has two types of nuclei i.e. macronucleus and micronucleus.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Viroids differ from viruses having
options: RNA molecules with a protein coat
RNA molecules without a protein coat
DNA molecules with a protein coat
DNA molecules without a protein coat
questions.answer: Option (B): RNA molecules without a protein coat
questions.solution: Viroids are sub-viral agents as infectious RNA particles, without a protein coat. The virus is made up of protein and has a protein coat as an outer covering. Viroid is the smallest particle that contains RNA as a genetic material but does not contain protein as an outer covering.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Five kingdom system of classification suggested by R.H. Whittaker is not based on
questions.solution: Five kingdom system of classification suggested by R.H. Whittaker is based on cell structure, thallus organisation, mode of nutrition, reproduction and phylogenetic relationships. It is not based on the habitat of the organisms because a single organism can inhabit one or more habitat.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is a correct statement?
options: Cyanobacteria are a group of autotrophic organisms classified under Kingdom Monera.
Slime moulds are saprophytic organisms classified under Kingdom Monera.
Mycoplasma have DNA, Ribosome and cell wall
questions.answer: Option (A): Cyanobacteria are a group of autotrophic organisms classified under Kingdom Monera.
questions.solution: The nutrition in bacteria is mainly autotrophic and heterotrophic. Phototrophic bacteria contain various pigments to synthesise their own food, while heterotrophic bacteria are dependent on other organisms for food. Parasitic bacteria fulfil their nutrition needs or requirements from the host cell. Slime moulds are saprophytes belonging to Kingdom Protista. Mycoplasma are prokaryotic organisms which do not possess a cell wall.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
The main criteria used for Five Kingdom Classification proposed By R.H. Whittaker (1969) included :
A. Cell structure
B. Body organization
C. Presence of flagellum
D. Reproduction
E. Phylogenetic relationships

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: A, B, D and E only
A, B, C, D and E
questions.answer: Option (A): A, B, D and E only
questions.solution: The main criteria for five kingdom classification used by (R.H. Whittaker) includes cell structure, body organization, mode of nutrition, reproduction and phylogenetic relationships.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Besides paddy ﬁelds, cyanobacteria are also found inside vegetative part of
questions.solution: Cyanobacteria are found in the coralloid root of the Cycas plant.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Choose the wrong statement.
options: Neurospora is used in the study of biochemical genetics.
Morels and truffles are poisonous mushrooms.
Yeast is unicellular and useful in fermentation.
questions.answer: Option (C): Morels and truffles are poisonous mushrooms.
questions.solution: Morels and truffles are edible mushrooms. They are not poisonous.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Select the wrong statement.
options: The viroids were discovered by D.J. Ivanowski.
W.M. Stanley showed that viruses could be crystallised.
The term 'contagium vivum fluidum' was coined by M.W. Beijerinck.
Mosaic disease in tobacco and AIDS in human beings are caused by viruses.
questions.answer: Option (A): The viroids were discovered by D.J. Ivanowski.
questions.solution: In 1971 T.O. Diener discovered viroids.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The imperfect fungi which are decomposers of litter and help in mineral cycling belong to
questions.solution: Deuteromycetes are commonly known as imperfect fungi because only the asexual or vegetative phases of these fungi are known. They are decomposers of litter and help in mineral cycling.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Methanogens belong to
questions.solution:
Carl Woese proposed the classification of the organisms in three kingdoms, Archaebacteria, Eubacteria and Eukarya, which were later called the domains. The archaebacteria are the group which comprises the primitive prokaryotic organisms like methanogens. These are unicellular, anaerobic and autotrophic prokaryotes. The cell wall lacks peptidoglycan and can convert carbon dioxide and hydrogen into methane gas. The hydrogen serves as an electron donor for the reduction of carbon dioxide. 
Therefore, the correct answer is option a.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following shows coiled RNA strand and capsomeres?
questions.solution: Tobacco mosaic virus shows coiled RNA strand and a protein coat called capsid made of small subunits or capsomeres.The coat protein self-assembles into the rod-like helical structure around the RNA which forms a hairpin loop structure. Inside the core helix, a coiled RNA molecule is present. Coiled RNA is absent in measles, retrovirus and poliovirus.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following are found in extreme saline conditions?
questions.solution:
Archaebacteria are able to survive in harsh conditions because of the branched lipid chain in the cell membrane which reduces fluidity of the cell membrane.
Halophiles are exclusively found in saline habitats.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following pairs is of unicellular algae?
questions.solution: Chlorella and Spirulina are unicellular algae. Chlorella comes under chlorophyceae and Spirulina comes under cyanobacteria. They are rich in proteins and are used as food supplements even by space travellers. These algae also produce a nutritional biomass that astronauts can eat.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements is wrong for viroids?
options: Their RNA is of high molecular weight
questions.answer: Option (D): Their RNA is of high molecular weight
questions.solution: Viroids are infectious, non protein‐coding, highly structured small circular low-molecular-weight ribonucleic acids (RNAs) able to replicate autonomously and induce diseases in higher plants. Viroids are single-stranded covalently closed circular RNA molecules existing as highly base-paired rod-like structures.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Cell wall is absent in:
questions.solution: Mycoplasmas are organisms that completely lack a cell wall.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In which group of organisms, the cell walls form two thin overlapping shells which fit together?
questions.solution: In diatoms (Chrysophytes), the cell walls form two thin overlapping shells, which fit together as in a soap box. Hence, the (a) option is correct.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following is WRONG for fungi?
options: All fungi possess a purely cellulosic cell wall
They are both unicellular and multicellular
questions.answer: Option (A): All fungi possess a purely cellulosic cell wall
questions.solution: The fungal cell wall is mainly composed of chitin, not cellulose. All the fungi are eukaryotic, heterotrophic (saprophytic) and may be unicellular or multicellular.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following is not a criterion for classification of fungi?
questions.solution:
The morphology of the mycelium, mode of spore formation and fruiting bodies form the basis for the division of the kingdom into various classes.
Mode of nutrition is not the criterion for classification of fungi.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following statements is wrong?
options: Golden algae are also called desmids.
Eubacteria are also called false bacteria.
Phycomycetes are also called algal fungi.
questions.answer: Option (C): Eubacteria are also called false bacteria.
questions.solution: Phycomycetes are also called algal fungi. They have characteristic aseptate coenocytic hyphae. Cyanobacteria are also called blue-green algae. They are photosynthetic bacteria. Golden algae are also called desmids. It is referred to as a single species, Prymnesium parvum. It is found in freshwater. Bacteria has two domains, namely eubacteria and archaea. Eubacteria are also called true bacteria. They have rigid cell walls and flagella.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is incorrectly matched?
questions.solution: Brown algae or Phaeophyceae contain mannitol as stored food material. Ulothrix belongs to Chlorophyceae (green algae) and they contain starch as the reserve food material.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The motile bacteria are able to move by:
questions.solution: Flagella is a whip-like appendage present on the surface of the bacteria. It is helically shaped and contains the protein flagellin. Its main function is the locomotion. It helps motile bacteria to move.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-IList-II
A. SphericalI. Vibrio
B. RodII. Cocci
C. CommaIII. Spirilla
D. SpirillumIV. Bacilli

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Bacteria are grouped under four categories based on their shape: Spherical → Coccus, Rod-shaped → Bacillus, Comma-shaped → Vibrium, Spiral → Spirillum.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: Claviceps is a source of many alkaloids and LSD
Conidia are produced exogenously and ascospores endogenously
Yeasts have filamentous bodies with long thread-like hyphae
Morels and truffles are edible delicacies
questions.answer: Option (C): Yeasts have filamentous bodies with long thread-like hyphae
questions.solution: Yeast is a unicellular sac fungus. It lacks a filamentous structure or hyphae. It comes under the group ascomycetes due to the formation of ascus and ascospore during sexual reproduction.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Which among the following are the smallest living cells, known without a definite
cell wall, pathogenic to plants as well as animals and can survive without oxygen?
questions.solution: Mycoplasmas are the smallest, wall-less prokaryotes, pleomorphic in nature. It does not possess a cell wall but has a cell membrane as an outer covering. These are pathogenic to both plants and animals as they do not have a cell wall and hence do not get affected by the antibiotics.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Select the option which is not correct with respect to enzyme action:
options: Addition of lot of succinate does not reverse the inhibition of succinic dehydrogenase by malonate
A noncompetitive inhibitor binds the enzyme at a site distinct from that which binds the substrate
Malonate is a competitive inhibitor of succinic dehydrogenase
Substrate binds with the enzyme at its active site
questions.answer: Option (A): Addition of lot of succinate does not reverse the inhibition of succinic dehydrogenase by malonate
questions.solution: Substrate binds with enzyme at its active site. A non competitive inhibitor binds the enzyme at a site distinct from the active site, the site which binds the substrate. Hence, it does not have any effect on the substrate concentration. This type of inhibition cannot be reversed by addition of more substrate. A competitive inhibitor binds to the enzyme at the active site, the site which binds the substrate. This type of inhibition can be reversed by addition of more substrate. For example, malonate is a competitive inhibitor of succinic dehydrogenase. Succinate and malonate both bind to the same active site of the enzyme succinic dehydrogenase. Addition of a lot of succinate reverses inhibition of succinic dehydrogenase by malonate.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Oxygen is not produced during photosynthesis by
questions.solution: Green sulphur bacteria do not use H2O as the source of electrons - they use H2, H2S, and S instead. Therefore, they do not evolve O2. This type of photosynthesis is known as anoxygenic photosynthesis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match list I with list II.
List IList II
A. RhizopusI. Mushroom
B. UstilagoII. Smut fungus
C. PucciniaIII. Bread mould
D. AgaricusIV. Rust fungus

Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.solution:
Rhizopus (the bread mould mentioned earlier) and Albugo (the parasitic fungi on mustard).
Some common members are Agaricus (mushroom), Ustilago (smut) and Puccinia (rust fungus).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Mycoplasma can pass through less than 1 micron filter size.
Statement II: Mycoplasma are bacteria with a cell wall.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.answer: Option (C): Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
questions.solution: Mycoplasmas are the smallest cells which are only 0.3 µm in length hence they can pass through less than 1 micron filter. All prokaryotes have a cell wall surrounding the cell membrane except in mycoplasma. So, statement I is correct and statement II is incorrect.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Chrysophytes, Euglenoids, Dinoflagellates and Slime moulds are included in the kingdom
questions.solution: R.H. Whittaker proposed a five kingdom classification in which Protista is a kingdom that comprises organisms which are unicellular but eukaryotic organisms. Its members may be autotrophic or heterotrophic. Primarily these are aquatic. The Protista kingdom has been divided into chrysophytes, euglenoids, dinoflagellates, protozoans, and slime moulds.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following are likely to be present in deep seawater?
questions.solution: Archaebacteria ﬂourish in deep-sea hydrothermal vents and hot springs where sunlight is scarce. They obtain nutrition through chemosynthesis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Symbiotic association between fungi and algae are called
questions.solution: Lichens are symbiotic associations i.e. mutually useful associations, between algae and fungi. Mycorrhiza are associations between fungi and roots of higher plants.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The structures that help some bacteria to attach to rock and/or host tissues are:
questions.solution: Fimbriae are small bristle-like fibres found in bacteria that help them to attach to the rock or host tissues.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following produces nitrogen fixing nodules on the roots of Alnus?
questions.solution: Frankia is a genus of nitrogen-fixing, filamentous bacteria that live in symbiosis with actinorhizal plants but this is non-leguminous. Hence nitrogen fixation in root nodules of Alnus is brought about by Frankia.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: Infective constituent in viruses is the protein coat
Prions consist of abnormally folded proteins
questions.answer: Option (B): Infective constituent in viruses is the protein coat
questions.solution: Infective constituent in viruses is either DNA or RNA, not protein.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Archaebacteria differ from other bacteria in:
questions.solution: Archaebacteria differ from other bacteria in having a different cell wall structure and this feature is responsible for their survival in extreme conditions.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Anoxygenic photosynthesis is characteristic of
questions.solution: Anoxygenic photosynthesis is the phototrophic process, where cellular energy i.e., ATP is produced without producing oxygen. Water is therefore not used as an electron donor. There are several groups of bacteria, that undergo anoxygenic photosynthesis such as green sulfur bacteria, green and red filamentous anoxygenic phototrophs (FAPs), phototrophic purple bacteria, Rhodospirillum because they do not produce oxygen as a by-product of photosynthesis. This bacterium is used in nitrogen fixation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Mad cow disease is caused by
questions.solution: Mad cow disease is caused by prions.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is not a prokaryote?
questions.solution: The prokaryotic cells are represented by bacteria, blue-green algae, Mycoplasma and PPLO. Fungi are eukaryotic organisms.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The primitive prokaryotes responsible for the production of biogas from the dung of ruminant animals, include the:
questions.solution: Methanogens are present in the gut of several ruminant animals such as cows and buffaloes and they are responsible for the production of methane (biogas) from the dung of these animals.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: One of the major components of cell wall of most fungi is
questions.solution: The fungal cell wall is predominantly composed of carbohydrate polymers called chitin. Chitin is thought to mostly add structural strength to the cell wall.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The incorrect statement regarding enzymes is :
options: Like chemical catalysts enzymes reduce the activation energy of bio processes .
Enzymes are very specific for a particular reaction and substrate.
questions.solution: Enzymes are globular proteins and not polysaccharides

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Phytochrome is a
questions.solution: Phytochromes are light-sensitive chromoproteins (a type of photoreceptor) in plants, bacteria, and fungi which are used to detect light. They are sensitive to light in the red and far-red region of the visible spectrum and can be classified as either Type I, which is activated by far-red light, or Type II which is activated by red light. They are responsible for photoperiodism in plants.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which statement regarding polymers is not correct?
options: Elastomers have polymer chains held together by weak intermolecular forces.
Thermoplastic polymers are capable of repeatedly softening and hardening on heating and cooling respectively.
questions.solution: Thermosetting polymers cannot be reshaped and reused.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The biodegradable polymer is:
questions.solution: Biodegradable polymers are a special class of polymer that breaks down after its intended purpose by bacterial decomposition process to result in natural byproducts such as gases (CO2, N2), water, biomass, and inorganic salts.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
options: Adenine pairs with thymine through three H-bonds.
Adenine does not pair with thymine.
Adenine pairs with thymine through two H-bonds.
Adenine pairs with thymine through one H-bond.
questions.answer: Option (C): Adenine pairs with thymine through two H-bonds.
questions.solution: In the double helix of DNA adenine pairs with thymine through two hydrogen bonds and guanine pair with cytosine through three hydrogen bonds.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Concanavalin A is
questions.solution: Concanavalin A is a secondary metabolite, a type of lectin. It has the property to agglutinate RBCs.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following is the most abundant protein in the animals?
questions.solution: Collagen is the most abundant protein in the animal world and Ribulose bisphosphate Carboxylase-Oxygenase (RUBisCO) is the most abundant protein in the whole of the biosphere. Lectins are carbohydrate-binding proteins. Insulin is the hormone that helps in controlling the level of sugar(glucose) in the blood. Haemoglobin is the iron bound protein molecule (pigment) in the blood that helps to transport oxygen.

questions.subject: Biology

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Regarding catalytic cycle of an enzyme action, select the correct sequential steps :
A. Substrate enzyme complex formation.
B. Free enzyme ready to bind with another substrate.
C. Release of products.
D. Chemical bonds of the substrate broken.
E. Substrate binding to active site.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.answer: Option (D): E, A, D, C, B
questions.solution:
The catalytic cycle of an enzyme action can be described in the following steps:
1. First, the substrate binds to the active site of the enzyme, fitting into the active site.
2. The binding of the substrate induces the enzyme to alter its shape, fitting more tightly around the substrate.
3. The active site of the enzyme, now in close proximity of the substrate breaks the chemical bonds of the substrate and the new enzyme- product complex is formed.
4. The enzyme releases the products of the reaction and the free enzyme is ready to bind to another molecule of the substrate and run through the catalytic cycle once again.

questions.question: A molecule that can act as a genetic material must fulfill the traits given below, except.
options: It should be able to generate its replica.

questions.answer: Option (B): It should be unstable structurally and chemically.

So, the correct answer is option B.

Colour blindness is an autosomal recessive disorder present on the X chromosome. Thus, a man whose father was colour blind will be normal (XY), marries a woman who had a colour blind mother and a normal father, i.e. the woman will be a carrier (XXC).
When the carrier woman marries a normal man then 50% of their son will be colour blind as
Parents….. Husband × Wife
Genes…. XY × XcX
Gametes…. X, Y × Xc, X
XYXCXCXXCYXXXXY

Hence, the probability of the male child being colour blind would be 50%.

questions.solution: In nucleic acids, the phosphate group at the 5′ position of the sugar molecule is joined to the sugar molecule of the next nucleotide at 3′ position by a phosphodiester bond.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A dehydration reaction links two glucose molecules to produce maltose. If the formula for glucose is C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>12</sub>O<sub>6</sub> then what is the formula for maltose?
questions.solution: In a dehydration reaction, two molecules of the sugar glucose (monomers) combine to form a single molecule of the sugar maltose. Two glucose molecules should combine to form a disaccharide C12H24O12 . However, due to dehydration, one H2O molecule is eliminated and the final product is C12H22O11.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What triggers activation of protoxin to active Bt toxin of Bacillus thuringiensis in bollworm?
questions.solution: Bacillus thuringiensis forms protein crystals during a particular phase of their growth. These crystals contain a toxic insecticidal protein. These proteins exist as inactive protoxins but once an insect ingest the inactive toxin, it is converted into an active form of toxin due to alkaline pH of the gut which solubilize the crystals. The activated toxin binds to the surface of midgut epithelial cells and creates pores that cause cell swelling and lysis and eventually cause death of insects.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: To obtain virus-free healthy plants from a diseased one by tissue culture technique, which part/parts of the diseased plant will be taken?
questions.answer: Option (B): Both apical and axillary meristems
questions.solution: The meristem is the tissue in plants that contain undifferentiated cells or meristematic cells which are rapidly dividing cells and thus are the virus-free part of the diseased plant. The culture with meristem has enabled the production of disease-free varieties including virus-free healthy plants.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The inactive form of Bt toxin is converted to the active form in the insect gut
questions.solution: Bt toxin protein exists as inactive protoxins, but once an insect ingests the inactive toxin, it is converted into an active form of toxin due to the alkaline pH of the gut which solubilises the crystals.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Nowadays it is possible to detect the mutated gene causing cancer by allowing radioactive probe to hybridize its complementary DNA in a clone of cells, followed by its detection using autoradiography because:
options: Mutated gene does not appear on a Photographic film as the probe has no complementarity with it
Mutated gene does not appear on Photographic film as the probe has complementarity with it
Mutated gene partially appears on a photographic film
Mutated gene completely and clearly appears on a photographic film
questions.answer: Option (A): Mutated gene does not appear on a Photographic film as the probe has no complementarity with it
questions.solution: It is possible to detect the mutated gene causing cancer by allowing a radioactive probe to hybridize its complementary DNA in a clone of cells, followed by its detection using autoradiography because a single-stranded DNA or RNA, tagged with a radioactive molecule (probe) is allowed to hybridize to its complementary DNA in a clone of cells followed by detection using autoradiography. The clone having the mutated gene will hence not appear on the photographic film, because the probe will not have complementarity with the mutated gene.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In-vitro clonal propagation in plants is characterised by
questions.solution: Molecular techniques are at present powerful and valuable tools for assessing the genetic stability among in vitro micropropagated plants. Random amplified polymorphic DNA (RAPD) is polymerase chain reaction (PCR) based techniques widely used for the determination of the genetic fidelity of in vitro regenerated plantlets. RAPD does not require prior sequence information, uses a small amount of DNA and is easy to use, thus considered to be suitable techniques for assessment of genetic fidelity of in vitro regenerated plantlets.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following statements is not valid for aerosols?
options: They have a negative impact on agricultural land
They are harmful to human health
They alter rainfall and monsoon patterns
questions.answer: Option (A): They cause increased agricultural productivity
questions.solution: Aerosols can be defined as the colloid of fine solid particles in the air such as fog. Aerosols can cause various problems to agriculture through their direct or indirect effects on plants. However, continuously increasing air pollution may represent a persistent and largely irreversible threat to agriculture in the future. Aerosols are a type of pollutant that hinders the sunlight to reach the plants and thus, plants are not able to trap light for photosynthesis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements is not correct?
options: The functional insulin has A and B chains linked together by hydrogen bonds
Genetically engineered insulin is produced in E. coli
In man insulin is synthesised as a proinsulin
The proinsulin has an extra peptide called C-peptide
questions.answer: Option (A): The functional insulin has A and B chains linked together by hydrogen bonds
questions.solution: The functional insulin molecule has two chains A and chain B, that are linked together by disulphide bridges, not by hydrogen bonds.While the remaining statements are correct.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Exploring molecular, genetic and species-level diversity for products of economic importance is called
questions.solution: Exploring molecular, genetic and species - level diversity for products of economic importance is called as bioprospecting.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statements related to human insulin are given below:
Which statement(s) is/are correct about genetically engineered Insulin?
(a) Pro-hormone insulin contain extra stretch of C-peptide
(b) A-peptide and B-peptide chains of insulin were produced separately in E. coli, extracted and combined by creating a disulphide bond between them.
(c) Insulin used for treating Diabetes was extracted from Cattles and Pigs.
(d) Pro-hormone insulin needs to be processed for converting into a mature and functional hormone.
(e) Some patients develop allergic reactions to the foreign insulin.
Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: In mammals, including humans, insulin is synthesised as a pro-hormone which contains an extra stretch called the C peptide. The pro-hormone needs to be processed before it becomes fully mature and functional. However, in case of genetically engineered insulin, there is no C-peptide, hence no proinsulin is formed. Genetically engineered insulin that is used for diabetes is produced using yeast and bacteria, unlike natural insulin which was earlier extracted from pancreas of slaughtered cattle and pigs.

questions.subject: Biology

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
questions.answer: Option (B): Statement I is true but Statement II is false
questions.solution:
Specific Bt toxin genes were isolated from Bacillus thuringiensis and incorporated into the several crop plants such as cotton. The choice of genes depends upon the crop and the targeted pest, as most Bt toxins are insect-group specific. The toxin is coded by a gene cryIAc named cry

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The human protein named $\alpha-1$-antitrypsin, obtained from transgenic animals, is used for the treatment of _____.
questions.solution:
The human protein named $\alpha-1$-antitrypsin, obtained from transgenic animals, is used for the treatment of emphysema.

Transgenic models exist for the study of other diseases, such as Alzheimer's disease, rheumatoid arthritis and cystic fibrosis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: For effective treatment of the disease, early diagnosis and understanding its pathophysiology is very important. Which of the following molecular diagnostic techniques is very useful for early detection?
questions.solution: ELISA can be used for early detection of infection either by detecting the presence of pathogenic antigen or by detecting the antibodies synthesized against the pathogen. In the hybridization technique, an ssDNA/ssRNA tagged with a radioactive molecule (probe) is allowed to hybridize its complementary DNA in a clone of cells followed by detection using autoradiography. It is used to find a mutated gene. The western blotting technique is used to detect a specific protein molecule among a mixture of proteins. Southern blotting is used to detect a specific DNA sequence in the given sample and can be detected prior to antibody formation. One can detect the presence of pathogenic DNA/RNA.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Golden rice is a genetically modified crop plant where the incorporated gene is meant for biosynthesis of
questions.solution: Golden rice is a rice designed to produce beta-carotene, a precursor of vitamin A, in the edible part called endosperm of rice. Hence, golden rice is a genetically modified crop plant where the incorporated gene is meant for biosynthesis of Vitamin A.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In India, the organisation responsible for assessing the safety of introducing genetically modified organisms for public use is
options: Council for Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR)
questions.solution: The GEAC is the apex biotech regulatory body in India. It is a statutory body. It is responsible for the appraisal of activities involving large-scale use of hazardous microorganisms and recombinants in research and industrial production from the environmental angle. The committee is also responsible for the appraisal of proposals relating to the release of genetically engineered (GE) organisms and products into the environment including experimental field trials.
