(a bacteria).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which part of the tobacco plant is infected by Meloidogyne incognitia?
questions.solution: A nematode Meloidegyne incognitia infects the roots of tobacco plant. They exist in soil in areas with hot climates or short winters. Root-knot nematode larvae infect plant roots, causing the development of root-knot galls that drain the plant's nutrients.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: When gene targeting involving gene amplification is attempted in an individual's tissue to treat disease, it is known as
questions.solution: Gene therapy is a collection of methods that allows the correction of a gene defect that has been diagnosed in a child/embryo. Here genes are inserted into a person’s cells and tissues to treat a disease. Correction of a genetic defect involves the delivery of a normal gene into the individual or embryo to take over the function of and compensate for the non-functional gene. The first clinical gene therapy was given in 1990 to a 4-year old girl with adenosine deaminase (ADA) deficiency. Molecular diagnosis refers to the act or process of determining the nature and cause of a disease. Biopiracy is the term used to refer to the use of bio-resources by multinational companies and other organizations without proper authorization from the countries and people concerned without compensatory payment.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following Bt crops is being grown in India by the farmers?
questions.solution: Bt cotton is grown by Indian farmers. Other than this no other transgenic crop is permitted for cultivation in India.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The Adenosine deaminase deficiency results into
options: Dysfunction of Immune system
questions.solution: The adenosine deaminase (ADA) enzyme is crucial for the immune system to function. Hence, its deficiency results in the dysfunction of the immune system. Hyposecretion of hormones of the adrenal cortex causes Addison's disease. Parkinson's disease is a long-term degenerative disorder of the central nervous system. Disorders that affect GIT & associated glands are called digestive disorders.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The first human hormone produced by recombinant DNA technology is
questions.solution: Insulin is the first human hormone produced by recombinant DNA. In 1983, Eli Lilly, an American company, prepared two DNA sequences corresponding to A and B chains of human insulin and introduced them in plasmids of E. coli to produce insulin chains.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following are fused in somatic hybridization involving two varieties of plants?
questions.solution: Isolated protoplasts from two different varieties of plants – each having a desirable character – can be fused to get hybrid protoplasts, which can be further grown to form a new plant. These hybrids are called somatic hybrids while the process is called somatic hybridisation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
With regard to insulin choose correct options.
(a) C-peptide is not present in mature insulin.
(b) The insulin produced by rDNA technology has C-peptide.
(c) The pro-insulin has C-peptide.
(d) A-peptide and B-peptide of insulin are interconnected by disulphide bridges
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: (a), (c) and (d) only
(a) and (d) only
(b) and (d) only
(b) and (c) only
questions.solution: In mammals, including humans, insulin is synthesized as a prohormone (like a pro-enzyme, the pro-hormone also needs to be processed before it becomes a fully mature and functional hormone) which contains an extra stretch called the C peptide. This C peptide is not present in the mature insulin and is removed during maturation into insulin. A and B chain of insulin are connected by disulphide bridges.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The introduction of t-DNA into plates involves:
options: Infection of the plant by Agrobacterium tumefaciens
Altering the pH of the soil, then heat shocking the plants
Exposing the plates to cold for a brief period
Allowing the plant roots to stand in water
questions.answer: Option (A): Infection of the plant by Agrobacterium tumefaciens
questions.solution:
The part of Ti plasmid transferred into plant cell DNA is called t-DNA. Ti plasmid (tumour inducing) from the soil bacterium Agrobacterium tumefaciens .Agrobacterium tumefaciens a plant pathogenic bacterium that carries Ti plasmid.
It can transfer a particular segment of the tumor-inducing (Ti) plasmid into the nucleus of infected cells.
The transferred T-DNA is then integrated into the host genome and transcribed with it.
This ability of Agrobacterium tumefaciens to transfer the T-DNA in the host genome is explored in genetic engineering to transfer the desired DNA segment, carrying the gene of the interest, into the genome of selected organisms.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which kind of therapy was given in 1990 to a four-year- old girl with adenosine deaminase (ADA) deficiency?
questions.solution: Adenosine deaminase (ADA) deficiency is a genetically inherited disorder that will damage the immune system. It causes SCID (Severe combined Immunodeficiency). 1st successful gene transfer in humans was performed by F. Anderson. A 4-year girl was treated by replacing ADA gene (Adenosine deaminase) deficiency in lymphocytes.

questions.question: The capacity to generate a whole plant from any cell of the plant is called
questions.solution: It was learnt by scientists, during 1950s, that whole plants could be regenerated from explants, i.e., any part of a plant taken out and grown in a test tube, under sterile conditions in special nutrient media. This capacity to generate a whole plant from any cell/explant is called totipotency

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Silencing of specific mRNA is possible via RNAi because of -
questions.solution:
RNA interference (RNAi) is a gene-silencing mechanism used by cells to regulate gene expression or defend against viral RNA. It works through double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) that is complementary to the target mRNA.
This is how it works:
Introduction of complementary dsRNA into the cell.
The dsRNA is recognized and cleaved by an enzyme called Dicer into small fragments called siRNA (small interfering RNA).
These siRNAs bind to a protein complex called RISC (RNA-induced silencing complex).
The siRNA guides RISC to the complementary mRNA, leading to its cleavage and silencing (i.e., preventing translation).
Therefore, complementary double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) is crucial for initiating RNAi.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is true for Golden rice?
options: It is pest resistant, with a gene from Bacillus thuringiensis
It is drought tolerant developed using Agrobacterium vector
It has yellow grains because of a gene introduced from a primitive variety of rice
It is Vitamin A enriched with a gene from daffodil

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The “Ti plasmid” of Agrobacterium tumefaciens stands for
questions.solution: A better understanding of the art of delivering genes by pathogens in their eukaryotic hosts has generated knowledge to transform these tools of pathogens into useful vectors for delivering genes of interest to humans. The tumor inducing (Ti) plasmid of Agrobacterium tumifaciens has now been modified into a cloning vector which is no more pathogenic to the plants but is still able to use the mechanisms to deliver genes of our interest into a variety of plants.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: DNA fragments generated by the restriction endonucleases in a chemical reaction can be separated by
questions.solution: DNA fragments generated by restriction endonuclease are separated using gel electrophoresis. It separates DNA fragments according to their size. The rate of migration is proportional to size, i.e., smaller fragments move more quickly, and wind up at the bottom of the gel.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Commonly used vector for human genome sequencing are:
questions.solution: Commonly used vectors for human genome sequencing are BAC (Bacterial Artificial Chromosome) and YAC. BAC is a DNA construct, based on a functional fertility plasmid (F plasmid) used for transforming and cloning in bacteria ( E.coli ). Yeast artificial chromosomes (YACs) are genetically engineered chromosomes derived from the DNA of the yeast, Saccharomyces cerevisiae, which is then ligated into a bacterial plasmid. By inserting large fragments of DNA, from 100–1000 kb, the inserted sequences can be cloned and physically mapped using a process called chromosome walking.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In gel electrophoresis, separated DNA fragments can be visualized with the help of:
questions.answer: Option (D): Ethidium bromide in UV radiation
questions.solution: The separated DNA fragments can be visualised only after staining the DNA with a compound known as ethidium bromide followed by exposure to UV radiation (you cannot see pure DNA fragments in the visible light and without staining). You can see bright orange coloured bands of DNA in a ethidium bromide stained gel exposed to UV light.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Hind II always cuts DNA molecules at a particular point called recognition sequence and it consists of
questions.solution: Recognition sequence of Hind II consists of 6 bp.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Choose the correct pair from the following.
options: Nucleases - Separate the two strands of DNA
Exonucleases - Make cuts at specific positions within DNA
Ligases - Join the two DNA molecules
Polymerases - Break the DNA into fragments
questions.answer: Option (C): Ligases - Join the two DNA molecules
questions.solution: DNA ligase is an enzyme that can connect two DNA molecules together by forming a phosphodiester bond between them. Nucleases cleave the phosphodiester bonds of nucleic acids and can be endo- or exo-nuclease based on the position where it makes the cut. Exonucleases make cuts at the ends of the DNA strand. Polymerases help in the polymerization of a DNA or RNA molecule. DNA polymerases and RNA polymerases are the enzymes that perform this function respectively.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A gene whose expression helps to identify transformed cell is known as
questions.solution: In recombinant DNA technology, selectable markers helps in identifying and eliminating non-transformants and selectively permitting the growth of the transformants after the process of recombination. These marker genes are resistant to various antibiotics and are used in cloning vectors.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : The DNA fragments extracted from gel electrophoresis can be used in construction of recombinant DNA.
Statement II : Smaller size DNA fragments are observed near anode while larger fragments are found near the wells in an agarose gel.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct
Both statement I and statement II are correct
Both statement I and statement II are incorrect
questions.answer: Option (C): Both statement I and statement II are correct
questions.solution:
Statement I - The separated bands of DNA are cut out from the agarose gel and extracted from the gel piece. This step is known as elution. The DNA fragments purified in this way are used in constructing recombinant DNA by joining them with cloning vectors.
Statement II - The DNA fragments separate (resolve) according to their size through sieving effect provided by the agarose gel. Hence, the smaller the fragment size, the farther it
 moves towards anode while larger fragments are move slowly so found near wells in an agrose gel.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is not correctly matched for the organism and its cell wall degrading enzyme?
questions.solution: In algae, the cell wall is made up of cellulose, and thus, cellulase is used for its degradation. Methylase is used for the process of methylation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The process of separation and purification of expressed protein before marketing is  called
questions.solution: Biosynthetic stage for the synthesis of products in recombinant DNA technology is called the upstreaming process while after completion of the biosynthetic stage, the product has to be subjected to a series of processes which include separation and purification are collectively referred to as downstream processing.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Following statements describe the characteristics of the enzyme Restriction Endonuclease. Identify the incorrect statement.
options: The enzyme binds DNA at specific sites and cuts only one of the two strands
The enzyme cuts the sugar-phosphate backbone at specific sites on each strand
The enzyme recognizes a specific palindromic nucleotide sequence in the DNA
The enzyme cuts DNA molecule at identified positions within the DNA
questions.answer: Option (A): The enzyme binds DNA at specific sites and cuts only one of the two strands
questions.solution: Restriction enzymes cut DNA molecules at a particular point (restriction site) by recognising a specific sequence known as recognition site. Each restriction endonuclease functions by inspecting the length of a DNA sequence. Once it finds its specific recognition sequence, it binds to the DNA and cuts each of the two strands of the double helix at specific points in their sugar-phosphate backbone.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following statements is not true regarding gel electrophoresis technique?
options: The process of extraction of separated DNA strands from gel is called elution
The separated DNA fragments are stained by using ethidium bromide
The presence of chromogenic substrate gives blue coloured DNA bands on the gel
Bright orange coloured bands of DNA can be observed in the gel when exposed to UV light
questions.answer: Option (C): The presence of chromogenic substrate gives blue coloured DNA bands on the gel
questions.solution: No chromogenic substrates are used during gel electrophoresis. Instead EtBr is used which intercalates between the DNA and it becomes visible under UV light. DNA bands are not visible in the gel unless they are illuminated by UV light.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In gene gun method, used to introduce alien DNA into host cells, microparticles of _______ metal are used.
questions.solution: In a method, suitable for plants, cells are bombarded with high velocity micro-particles of gold or tungsten coated with DNA in a method known as biolistics or gene gun.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The thermostable DNA polymerase enzyme is obtained from
questions.solution: Taq polymerase is a thermostable DNA polymerase named after the thermophilic bacterium Thermus aquaticus from which it was originally isolated. It is frequently used in the polymerase chain reaction (PCR), a method for greatly amplifying the quantity of short segments of DNA. T. aquaticus is a bacterium that lives in hot springs and hydrothermal vents, and Taq polymerase was identified as an enzyme able to withstand the protein-denaturing conditions (high temperature) required during PCR.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: An analysis of chromosomal DNA using the southern hybridisation technique does not use:
questions.solution: The steps of southern hybridization includes the digestion of DNA or genomic source with a restriction enzyme and its separation by electrophoresis. The DNA is denatured into single strands by incubation with NaOH. The DNA is transferred to a membrane which is a sheet of special blotting paper. The DNA fragments retain the same pattern of the separation as on the gel (blotting). The blot is incubated with many copies of a probe which is single-stranded DNA. This probe will form base pairs with its complementary DNA sequence and bind to form a ds DNA molecule. The probe is radioactive. The location of the probe is revealed when it is exposed to X-ray film (autoradiography). It does not involve PCR (polymerase chain reaction).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is commonly used as a vector for introducing a DNA fragment in human lymphocytes?
questions.solution: Retrovirus is commonly used as a vector for introducing a DNA fragment in human lymphocytes. This technique is known as gene therapy. In this technique, lymphocytes from the blood of the patient are grown in the culture outside the body. A functional gene is introduced by using a retroviral vector into these lymphocytes, which then subsequently returned to the patient's body.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Stirred-tank bioreactors have been designed for ____.
options: Addition of preservatives to the product
Availability of oxygen throughout the process
Ensuring anaerobic conditions in the culture vessel
questions.answer: Option (B): Availability of oxygen throughout the process
questions.solution: Stirred-tank bioreactor is usually cylindrical or with a curved base to facilitate the mixing of the reaction contents. The stirrer facilitates even mixing and oxygen availability throughout the bioreactor.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following equipment is essentially required for growing microbes on a large scale, for industrial production of enzymes?
questions.solution: To produce enzymes in large quantities for the commercial purpose required equipment is bioreactors.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is a restriction endonuclease?
questions.solution: Restriction enzymes are traditionally classified into four types on the basis of subunit composition, cleavage position, sequence specificity and cofactor requirements. There are four classes of restriction endonucleases: types I, II,III and IV. HindII is a type II restriction enzyme found in Haemophilus influenzae.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I

List-II

(a) Cells with active cell division capacity

(i) Vascular Tissues

(b) Tissue having all cells similar in structure and function

(ii) Meristematic tissues

(c) Tissue having different type of cells

(iii) Sclereids

(d) Dead cells with highly thickened walls and narrow lumen

(iv) Simple Tissue
questions.solution: Growth in plants is largely restricted to specialized regions of active cell division called meristems. Meristematic tissues are those tissues that have cells with active cell division capacity. Permanent tissues having all cells similar in structure and function are called simple tissues. Vascular tissue is a complex conducting tissue, formed of more than one cell type, found in vascular plants. The sclereids are spherical, oval, or cylindrical, highly thickened dead cells with very narrow cavities (lumen). These are commonly found in the fruit walls of nuts; pulp of fruits like guava, pear, and sapota; seed coats of legumes and leaves of tea.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: During the purification process for recombinant DNA technology, the addition of chilled ethanol precipitates out:
questions.solution: During the purification process for recombinant DNA technology, the addition of chilled ethanol precipitates out DNA. This can be seen as a collection of fine threads in the suspension. The RNA can be removed by treatment with ribonuclease whereas proteins can be removed by treatment with protease. Histones are basic proteins that help condense DNA in a cell.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Arrange the following steps of DNA fingerprinting in a correct sequence.
A. Isolation of DNA and its digestion by restriction endonucleases.
B. Hybridisation using a labelled VNTR probe.
C. Transferring of separated DNA fragments to synthetic membranes.
D. Detection of hybridised DNA fragments by autoradiography.
E. Separation of DNA fragments by electrophoresis.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.answer: Option (A): A, E, C, B, D
questions.solution:
The following is the correct sequence of steps of DNA fingerprinting.
A. Isolation of DNA and its digestion by restriction endonuclease.
B. Probes made complementary to the VNTR locus are allowed to hybridise with the DNA fragments.
C. The separated DNA fragments are transferred to synthetic membranes made of nylon or nitrocellulose.
D. Finally, the hybridised DNA fragments are detected under X-rays in a technique called autoradiography.
E. DNA fragments are separated based on their size by the technique of gel electrophoresis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Restriction endonucleases recognise specific sequences to cut DNA known as palindromic nucleotide sequences.
Statement II: Restriction endonucleases cut the DNA strand a little away from the centre of the palindromic site.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.answer: Option (A): Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.solution: Restriction endonucleases recognise specific sequences to cut DNA known as palindromic nucleotide sequences. However, the restriction enzymes cut the strand of DNA a little away from the centre of the palindrome site, but between the same two bases on the opposite strands.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is a correct sequence of steps in a PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction)?
questions.solution:
Polymerase chain reaction or PCR consists of the following three steps:
i)Denaturation- The two DNA strands of template DNA separate from each other when heated to 92℃. ii) Annealing- The primers anneal to the 3’ end of single strands of DNA. iii)Extension- The primers are extended by DNA polymerase by the addition of nucleotides to form complete strands of DNA. Hence the sequence of steps is denaturation, annealing, extension.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In the following palindromic base sequence of DNA, which one can be cut easily by a particular restriction enzyme?
questions.solution: The sequence 5’ GAATTC 3’ ; 3’ CTTAAG 5’ is a palindromic sequence and therefore can be cut easily by a restriction endonuclease. The rest of the sequences are not palindromic. 5’ GAATTC 3’ ; 3’ CTTAAG 5’ is, in fact, the recognition sequence of the restriction enzyme EcoRI.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is not required for any of the techniques of DNA fingerprinting available at present?
questions.solution: Polymerase chain reaction is used to amplify DNA into large amounts. Zinc finger is a kind of structural motif that is characterized by coordination between zinc ions to stabilize the tertiary structure of proteins. Restriction enzymes are the endonucleases that make a cut at specific positions within the DNA. DNA-DNA hybridisation is a technique of molecular biology which is used to measure the similarity between DNA sequences. Hence, zinc finger analysis which is related to proteins, is not required for DNA.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is not an application of PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction)?
questions.solution:
PCR is Polymerase Chain Reaction. It is used for making multiple copies of the gene. Hence PCR is used for:
• Gene amplification.
• PCR-based assays have been developed that detect the presence of gene sequences of the infectious agents.
• It is also used in detecting mutations.
• Protein is not the target of PCR. Hence, plays no role in its purification.
Majorly the PCR is used in analyzing and determining purposes only.

questions.subject: Biology

questions.solution: During the isolation of desired genes, chilled ethanol is used for the precipitation of DNA. Due to which DNA form pallets and other biomolecules are present in the supernatant.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which or the following statements is incorrect?
options: Most commonly used bio-reactors are of stirring type.
Bio-reactors are used to produce small scale bacterial cultures.
Bio-reactors have an agitator system, an oxygen delivery system and foam control system.
A bio-reactor provides optimal growth conditions for achieving the desired product.
questions.answer: Option (B): Bio-reactors are used to produce small scale bacterial cultures.
questions.solution: After having cloned the gene of interest and having optimised the conditions to induce the expression of the target protein, one has to consider producing it on a large scale. Small volume cultures cannot yield appreciable quantities of products. To produce in large quantities, the development of bioreactors, where large volumes (100-1000 litres) of culture can be processed, was required

questions.solution: After the bands are stained, they are viewed in UV light. The bands appear bright orange in color. Ethidium bromide is the intercalating agent that stacks in between the nitrogenous bases of DNA.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is not a feature of the plasmids?
questions.solution: Plasmids are extrachromosomal genetic material present in bacteria. They are capable of independent replication. They are a separate entity present in the cytoplasm. They are circular double stranded DNA molecules and contain some specialized genes like antibiotic resistant genes. They are transferable.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is not a cloning vector?
questions.solution: A probe is a single-stranded sequence of DNA or RNA used to search for its complementary sequence in a sample genome.

questions.solution: Vector is an intermediate carrier, a phage, plasmid or virus DNA into which another DNA is inserted for introduction into bacterial or other cells for amplification.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following restriction enzymes produces blunt ends?
questions.solution:
SalI is a restriction endonuclease isolated from Streptomyces albus. It produces sticky ends by making the cut in the nucleotide sequence G/TCGAC
EcoRV is type II restriction endonuclease isolated from Escherichia coli which produces blunt ends by making a cut in the center of the nucleotide sequence GAT/ATC.
XhoI is a restriction endonuclease isolated from Xanthomonas campestris. It produces sticky ends by making a cut in the recognition sequence C/TCGAG.
HindIII is a type II restriction enzyme isolated from Haemophilus influenzae. It produces sticky ends by making a cut in the nucleotide sequence A/AGCTT.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is not a desirable feature of a cloning vector ?
options: Presence of single restriction enzyme site
Presence of two or more recognition sites
questions.answer: Option (D): Presence of two or more recognition sites
questions.solution: In order to link the alien DNA, the cloning vector needs to have very few, preferably single recognition sites for the commonly used restriction enzymes. Presence of more than one recognition sites within the vector will generate several fragments, which will complicate the gene cloning.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A foreign DNA and plasmid cut by the same restriction endonuclease can be joined to form a recombinant plasmid using
questions.solution:
Polymerase III and Taq polymerase are enzymes of DNA polymerization and add deoxyribonucleotides to the primer in 5' to 3' direction. EcoRI is a restriction enzyme from E. coli that digest DNA at specific recognition sites. DNA ligase enzyme joins two DNA fragments together by a phosphodiester bond between 3’ hydroxyl at the end of one fragment and a 5’ phosphate at the end of another fragment. Foreign DNA and a plasmid having complementary ends can be ligated using DNA ligase. 
Therefore, the correct answer is option c.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Which of the following statements are correct with respect to DNA separation, isolation and visualization?
A. The cutting of DNA is done by molecular scissors.
B. The DNA fragments separate according to their size in an agarose gel, upon electrophoresis.
C. The separated DNA fragments can be seen without staining when exposed to UV light.
D. The separated DNA fragments, when stained with ethidium bromide, can be seen in visible light.

questions.solution:

- The DNA fragments separate (resolve) according to their size through sieving effect provided by the agarose gel.
- The separated DNA fragments can be visualised only after staining the DNA with a compound known as ethidium bromide followed by exposure to UV radiation.

questions.subject: Biology

questions.solution: If one ligate a foreign DNA at the BamHI site of tetracycline resistance gene in the vector pBR322, the recombinant plasmid will lose tetracycline resistance due to insertion of foreign DNA.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Identify the wrong statement with regard to restriction enzymes.
options: They are useful in genetic engineering
Sticky ends can be joined by using endonucleases
Each restriction enzyme functions by inspecting the length of a DNA sequence
They cut the strand of DNA at palindromic sites
questions.answer: Option (B): Sticky ends can be joined by using endonucleases
questions.solution:
(a) Genetic engineering or recombinant DNA technology can be accomplished only if we have the key tools, i.e., restriction enzymes, polymerase enzymes, ligases, vectors and the host organism.
(b) The sticky ends in DNA that result from the action of restriction endonucleases cannot be joined by the restriction enzymes, but by DNA ligases. 
(c) Restriction enzymes begin their action by first scanning the length of the DNA sequence and then recognising a specific sequence. This specific base sequence is known as the recognition sequence.
(d) Each restriction endonuclease recognises a specific palindromic nucleotide sequence in the DNA.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): Polymerase chain reaction is used in DNA amplification.
Reason (R): The ampicillin resistant gene is used as a selectable marker to check transformation.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.answer: Option (B): Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.solution: Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) is used in DNA amplification. Selectable markers are not used in PCR. Selectable markers like the antibiotic resistance genes are useful during transformation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match list I with list II.

List-I

List-II

(a) Lenticels

(i) Phellogen

(b) Cork cambium

(ii) Suberin deposition

(c) Secondary cortex

(iii) Exchange of gases

(d) Cork

(iv) Phelloderm
questions.solution: Lenticels permit the exchange of gases between the outer atmosphere and the internal tissue of the stem. With the continuous increase in girth due to the activity of vascular cambium, the outer cortical and epidermis layers get broken and need to be replaced to provide new protective cell layers. Hence, sooner or later, another meristematic tissue called cork cambium or phellogen develops, usually in the cortex region. Phellogen is a couple of layers thick. It is made of narrow, thin-walled, and nearly rectangular cells. Phellogen cuts off cells on both sides. The outer cells differentiate into cork or phellem while the inner cells differentiate into secondary cortex or phelloderm. The cork is impervious to water due to suberin deposition in the cell wall.

(b) Thermus aquaticus(ii) Construction of first rDNA Molecule

questions.subject: Biology

questions.solution:
Downstream processing is the recovery of biological products which includes following stages:
Extraction, separation, purification and preservation of the biotechnological products.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:

questions.solution: Statements C and D are incorrect. Restriction endonucleases usually cut the DNA slightly away from the centre of palindrome sites. They cannot remove nucleotides from the ends of the DNA fragment, which is function of restriction exonuclease.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: During the process of gene amplification using PCR, if a very high temperature is not maintained in the beginning, then which of the following steps of PCR will be affected first?
questions.solution: PCR stands for Polymerase Chain Reaction. In this reaction, multiple copies of the gene (or DNA) of interest are synthesized in vitro using two sets of primers (small chemically synthesized oligonucleotides that are complementary to the regions of DNA) and the enzyme DNA polymerase. The first step of PCR is denaturation in which the two DNA strands of template DNA separate from each other when heated to 92℃. This step requires a high temperature, and if a high temperature is not maintained at the beginning of PCR amplification, denaturation wouldn't take place.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Plasmid pBR322 has a PstI restriction enzyme site within gene ampR that confers ampicillin resistance. If this enzyme is used for inserting a gene for β-galactoside production and the recombinant plasmid is inserted in an E.coli strain
options: It will lead to lysis of the host cell
It will be able to produce a novel protein with dual ability
It will not be able to confer ampicillin resistance to the host cell
The transformed cells will have the ability to resist ampicillin as well as produce β-galactoside
questions.answer: Option (C): It will not be able to confer ampicillin resistance to the host cell
questions.solution: pBR322 is a commonly used cloning vector. When the gene for β-galactoside is inserted in the ampicillin resistance gene by using Pst I, the recombinant E.coli will lose ampicillin resistance due to insertional inactivation of the antibiotic resistance gene. The host (recombinant) cell will produce β-galactoside which is not a novel protein nor does it have the dual ability. The transformed cells cannot resist ampicillin as they have lost ampicillin resistance. A recombinant E. coli is produced and the host cell will not undergo lysis due to the insertion of the β-galactoside gene.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
The blue and white selectable markers have been developed which differentiate recombinant colonies from non-recombinant colonies on the basis of their ability to produce colour in the presence of a chromogenic substrate.
Given below are two statements about this method:
Statement I : The blue coloured colonies have DNA insert in the plasmid and they are identified as recombinant colonies.
Statement II : The colonies without blue colour have DNA insert in the plasmid and are identified as recombinant colonies.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.answer: Option (B): Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution:
Statement I: The blue coloured colonies have DNA insert in the plasmid and they are identified as recombinant colonies.
Incorrect. In blue-white screening, non-recombinant colonies (those without the gene insert) turn blue because they can produce a functional β-galactosidase enzyme, which breaks down the chromogenic substrate (X-gal) and produces the blue color. The presence of an insert in the plasmid disrupts the β-galactosidase gene, leading to a white color.
Statement II: The colonies without blue colour have DNA insert in the plasmid and are identified as recombinant colonies.
Correct. The white colonies are recombinant because the insertion of foreign DNA disrupts the β-galactosidase gene, preventing the formation of the blue color.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A specific recognition sequence identified by endonucleases to make cuts at specific positions within the DNA is:
questions.solution: Each restriction endonuclease recognizes a specific palindromic nucleotide sequence in the DNA. Once it finds its specific recognition sequence it binds to DNA and cuts each of the two strands of DNA. During post-transcriptional modification in eukaryotes, poly(A) tail (200–300 adenylate residues) are added at the 3' end of hnRNA. questions.subject: Biology

GAATTCCTTAAG

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
What is the criterion for DNA fragments movement on agarose gel during gel
electrophoresis?
options: Positively charged fragments move to the farther end
Negatively charged fragments do not move
The larger the fragment size, the farther it moves
The smaller the fragment size, the farther it moves
questions.answer: Option (D): The smaller the fragment size, the farther it moves
questions.solution: Gel electrophoresis is used to segregate DNA fragments according to size. During gel electrophoresis, DNA fragments separate (resolve) according to their size through the sieving effect provided by agarose gel. DNA is negatively charged and hence it travel towards the positive electrode. The mobility of DNA fragments is directly proportional to the size. Smaller the fragment, farther it moves, and vice versa. Hence, the (d) option is correct.

questions.subject: Biology

questions.solution: Origin of replication (ori): This is a sequence from where replication starts and any piece of DNA when linked to this sequence can be made to replicate within the host cells. This sequence is also responsible for controlling the copy number of the linked DNA.

questions.solution: The separated DNA fragments can be visualised only after staining the DNA with a compound known as ethidium bromide followed by exposure to UV radiation. Bright orange coloured bands of DNA are visible in a ethidium bromide stained gel exposed to UV light.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: If you suspect major deficiency of antibodies in a person, to which of the following would you look for confirmatory evidence?
questions.solution: Globulin is one of the proteins found in serum. So, if a major deficiency of antibodies is suspected in a person, the serum globulin is tested for a confirmatory evidence.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Select the incorrect statement with reference to Rh grouping.
A. Erythroblastosis foetalis is a condition observed having foetus with $\mathrm{Rh}^{-\mathrm{ve}}$ blood and mother with $\mathrm{Rh}^{+\mathrm{ve}}$ blood.
B. Rh antigen is observed on RBCs in the majority of human beings.
C. Before blood transfusion, Rh group should also be matched.
D. Rh incompatibility is observed when a pregnant mother is $\mathrm{Rh}^{-\mathrm{ve}}$ and the foetus is $\mathrm{Rh}^{+\mathrm{ve}}$.
E. Erythroblastosis foetalis can be avoided by administering anti-Rh antibodies to the mother immediately after the delivery of the second child.
Choose the answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
(A) Incorrect → A special case of Rh incompatibility has been observed between the Rh-ve blood of a pregnant mother with $\mathrm{Rh}^{+\mathrm{ve}}$ blood of the foetus.
(B) Correct → Rh antigen is observed on the surface of RBCs of majority (nearly 80 percent) of humans.
(C) Correct → Before blood transfusion, Rh group should also be matched to avoid severe problems of destruction of RBCs.
(D) Correct → Rh incompatibility (Erythroblastosis foetalis) is observed when a pregnant mother is $\mathrm{Rh}^{-\mathrm{ve}}$ and the foetus is $\mathrm{Rh}^{+v e}$.
(E) Incorrect → Erythroblastosis foetalis can be avoided by administering anti-Rh antibodies to the mother immediately after the delivery of the first child.
Thus, the incorrect statements are (A) and (E).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:

A. IBi/IAi/ii

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Blood pressure in the pulmonary artery is:
options: Same as that in the aorta
More than that in the carotid
More than that in the pulmonary vein
Less than that in the venae cavae.
questions.answer: Option (C): More than that in the pulmonary vein
questions.solution: The blood pressure in the arteries is greater than that in the veins. Artery > Arteriole > Capillary > Venule > Vein (Vena Cava). The pulmonary artery is a short and stout (wide) structure which branches into two parts. On the other hand the pulmonary veins are large blood vessels. Hence, the pressure of blood is greater in the pulmonary artery as compared to that in the pulmonary vein.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Persons with “AB” blood group are called “Universal recipients”. This is due to
options: Presence of antibodies, anti-A and anti-B, on RBCs
Absence of antibodies, anti-A and anti-B, in plasma
Absence of antigens A and B on the surface of RBCs
Absence of antigens A and B in plasma
questions.answer: Option (B): Absence of antibodies, anti-A and anti-B, in plasma
questions.solution: Persons with the 'AB' blood group contain antigens 'A' and 'B' but lack antibodies anti-A and anti-B in plasma. So, persons with the 'AB' blood group can accept blood from persons with AB as well as the other groups of blood due to the lack of antibodies in their blood. Therefore, such persons are called "Universal recipients".

questions.solution: In the hepatic portal system, the hepatic portal vein carries the maximum amount of nutrients from the intestine to the liver. The hepatic portal vein carries the deoxygenated blood from the gastrointestinal tract, gallbladder, pancreas, and spleen to the liver.

Both heart rate and cardiac output increase
Heart rate decreases but cardiac output increases
Reduces both heart rate and cardiac output

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The WBC count of a person's blood sample is $8000 / \mathrm{cu} \mathrm{mm}$. How many eosinophils and lymphocytes would be in the same blood sample approximately?
questions.solution:
Eosinophils constitute $2-3 \%$ of total WBCs. Hence its value is approximately 2 to $3 \%$ of $8000 / \mathrm{cu} \mathrm{mm}= 160-240 / \mathrm{cu} \mathrm{mm}$

Lymphocytes constitute $20-25 \%$ of total WBCs. Hence its value is approximately 20 to $25 \%$ of $8000 / \mathrm{cu} \mathrm{mm}=1600-2000 / \mathrm{cu} \mathrm{mm}$

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The QRS complex in a standard ECG represents
questions.solution: The QRS complex represents the depolarisation of the ventricles, which initiates the ventricular contraction. The contraction starts shortly after Q and marks the beginning of ventricular systole.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Cardiac activities of the heart are regulated by :
A. Nodal tissue
B. A special neural centre in the medulla oblongata
C. Adrenal medullary hormones
D. Adrenal cortical hormones
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.answer: Option (C): A, B and C Only
questions.solution:
Heart are regulated intrinsically, i.e., auto regulated by specialised muscles (nodal tissue), 
A special neural centre in the medulla oblongata can moderate the cardiac function through autonomic nervous system (ANS), Adrenal medullary hormones can also increase the cardiac output. 
(the adrenal cortex, which produces cortisol and aldosterone, does not directly increase heart rate in the same way. These hormones from the adrenal cortex primarily regulate blood pressure and blood volume, indirectly impacting the heart.)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Adult human RBCs are enucleated. Which of the following statement(s) is/are the most appropriate explanation for this feature?
(a) They do not need to reproduce
(b) They are somatic cells
(c) They do not metabolize
(d) All their internal space is available for oxygen transport
questions.solution: In human RBCs, the nucleus degenerates during maturation which provides more space for oxygen-carrying pigment (Haemoglobin). It lacks most of the cell organelles including mitochondria so respires anaerobically and does not show any metabolic activity and multiplication.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Doctors use stethoscopes to hear the sounds produced during each cardiac cycle. The second sound is heard when
options: Ventricular walls vibrate due to gushing in of blood from atria.
Semilunar valves close down after the blood flows into vessels from ventricles.
AV node receives signal from SA node.
questions.answer: Option (C): Semilunar valves close down after the blood flows into vessels from ventricles.
questions.solution: During each cardiac cycle, two prominent sounds are produced which can be easily heard through a stethoscope. The first heart sound (lub) is associated with the closure of the tricuspid and bicuspid valves whereas the second heart sound (dub) is associated with the closure of the semilunar valves.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Name the blood cells, whose reduction in number can cause clotting disorder, leading to excessive loss of blood from the body.
questions.solution:
Thrombocytes are also called platelets. They are the vital component of blood. It's basic function is to stop bleeding from injured blood vessels by clumping and clotting blood vessels. Reduction in the number of platelets causes clotting disorder and thus loss of blood from the body.
Hence, the correct option is c.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Following are the stages of pathway for conduction of an action potential through the heart
A. AV bundle
B. Purkinje fibres
C. AV node
D. Bundle branches
E. SA node
Choose the correct sequence of pathway from the options given below
questions.solution: A specialised cardiac musculature called the nodal tissue is also distributed in the heart. A patch of this tissue is present in the right upper corner of the right atrium called the sino-atrial node (SAN). Another mass of this tissue is seen in the lower left corner of the right atrium close to the atrio-ventricular septum called the atrio-ventricular node (AVN). A bundle of nodal fibres, atrioventricular bundle (AV bundle) continues from the AVN which passes through the atrio-ventricular septa to emerge on the top of the interventricular septum and immediately divides into a right and left bundle. These branches give rise to minute fibres throughout the ventricular musculature of the respective sides and are called Purkinje fibres. These fibres alongwith right and left bundles are known as bundle of His. The nodal musculature has the ability to generate action potentials without any ex…

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
The frog’s heart when taken out of the body continues to beat for some time. Select the best option from the following statements.
(a) Frog is a poikilotherm
(b) Frog does not have any coronary circulation
(c) Heart is "myogenic" in nature.
(d) Heart is autoexcitable.
questions.solution: Frog or the vertebrates have myogenic heart, i.e., they are self contractile or are autoexcitable. They do not require external stimuli. When a frog’s heart is taken out of the body, it continues to beat for some time because till then ATP is available. It is not dependent on the nervous system and does not require external stimuli as the SA node can generate action potential on its own.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Erythropoietin hormone which stimulates RBC formation is produced by
options: The cells of bone marrow
Juxtaglomerular cells of the kidney
Alpha cells of pancreas
The cells of rostral adenohypophysis
questions.answer: Option (B): Juxtaglomerular cells of the kidney
questions.solution: Juxtaglomerular cells of the kidney secrete erythropoietin hormone which stimulates RBC formation. Alpha cells of the pancreas produce the hormone glucagon. The cells of rostral adenohypophysis synthesize hormones of the anterior lobe of the pituitary. The cells of bone marrow are responsible for the formation of formed elements.

questions.answer: Option (C): Father: IAIB and Mother: IAi
questions.solution: This combination (Father: IAIB) of parent blood group is not possible for a person with blood group 'O'. For a child to have type 'O' blood, both biological parents must carry the recessive 'i' allele and pass it down.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The coagulum is formed of a network of threads called thrombins.
Statement II: Spleen is the graveyard of erythrocytes.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.answer: Option (D): Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution: Blood clot or coagulum is formed mainly of a network of threads called fibrins in which dead and damaged formed elements of blood are trapped, so the statement, coagulum is formed of a network of threads called thrombins is incorrect. RBCs have an average life span of 120 days after which they are destroyed in the spleen, hence the spleen is called the graveyard of RBCs.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What would be the heart rate of a person if the cardiac output is 5L, blood volume in the ventricles at the end of diastole is 100 mL and at the end of ventricular systole is 50 mL.
questions.solution:
Cardiac output = stroke volume x Heart rate
⇒ Cardiac output = 5L or 5000 ml
⇒ Blood volume in ventricles at the end of diastole = 100 ml
⇒ Blood volume in ventricles at the end of systole = 50 ml
Stroke volume = 100 - 50= 50 ml.
So,
5000 ml = 50 ml x Heart rate
So, Heart rate = 100 beats per minute.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following statements is correct ?
options: The atrioventricular node (AVN) generates an action potential to stimulate atrial contraction
The tricuspid and the bicuspid valves open due to the pressure exerted by the simultaneous contraction of the atria
Blood moves freely from atrium to the ventricle during joint diastole
Increased ventricular pressure causes closing of the semilunar valves
questions.answer: Option (C): Blood moves freely from atrium to the ventricle during joint diastole
questions.solution: The Sino-atrial node generates new action potential. With the decline of ventricular pressure, the tricuspid and bicuspid valves are pushed open by the pressure in the atria exerted by the blood which was being emptied into them by the veins. Joint diastole refers to the phase in the cardiac cycle of the heart when both atria and ventricles are relaxed. During joint diastole, blood is poured into the left and right atria. Due to this filling of blood, atrioventricular valves (Bicuspid and Tricuspid valves) open and allow blood to flow from atria to ventricles. During ventricular diastole, the ventricular pressure falls causing the closure of semilunar valves and this prevents the backflow of blood into the ventricles.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Serum differs from blood in
questions.solution: Blood is composed of a clear, straw-colored, watery fluid called plasma in which different types of blood cells are suspended. The serum is that part of blood that is similar in composition with plasma but does not contain clotting factors of blood. It includes all proteins (except protein involved in blood clotting) and all the electrolytes, antibodies, antigens, hormones, etc. So, the correct option is b.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:

Statement I : Bone marrow is the main lymphoid organ where all blood cells including lymphocytes are produced.
Statement II : Both Bone marrow and thymus provide micro environments for the development and maturation of T-lymphocytes.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is Correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
questions.answer: Option (D): Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
questions.solution: The bone marrow is the main lymphoid organ where all blood cells including lymphocytes are produced. The thymus is a lobed organ located near the heart and beneath the breastbone. The thymus is quite large at the time of birth but keeps reducing in size with age and by the time puberty is attained it reduces to a very small size. Both bone-marrow and thymus provide micro-environments for the development and maturation of T-lymphocytes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What is the name of the blood vessel that carries deoxygenated blood from the body to the heart in a frog ?
questions.solution: In a frog, the vena cava is the blood vessel that carries deoxygenated blood from the body to the heart. The deoxygenated blood from various parts of the body enters the right atrium of the heart through the anterior and posterior vena cava.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which enzyme is responsible for the conversion of inactive fibrinogens to fibrins?
questions.solution: Fibrins are formed by the conversion of inactive fibrinogens in the plasma by the enzyme thrombin. Thrombins, in turn, are formed from another inactive substance present in the plasma called prothrombin. An enzyme complex, thrombokinase, is required for the above reaction. This complex is formed by a series of linked enzymatic reactions (cascade process) involving a number of factors present in the plasma in an inactive state. Epinephrine also known as adrenaline is rapidly secreted in response to stress of any kind and during emergency situations and is called emergency hormones or hormones of Fight or Flight. Renin enzyme secreted by the kidney (and also, possibly, by the placenta) that is part of a physiological system that regulates blood pressure. In the blood, renin acts on a protein known as angiotensinogen, resulting in the release of angiotensin I.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): A person goes to high altitude and experiences 'altitude sickness' with symptoms like breathing difficulty and heart palpitations.
Reason (R): Due to low atmospheric pressure at high altitudes, the body does not get sufficient oxygen.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: (A) is true but (R) is false
(A) is false but (R) is true
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.answer: Option (C): Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.solution: Altitude sickness can be experienced at high altitudes where the body does not get enough oxygen due to low atmospheric pressure and causes nausea, fatigue, and heart palpitations.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
In humans, respiration occurs in the following steps. Arrange these steps in the correct order.
A. Diffusion of $\mathrm{O}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{CO}_{2}$ between blood and tissues
B. Diffusion of $\mathrm{O}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{CO}_{2}$ across alveolar membrane
C. Pulmonary ventilation by which atmospheric air is drawn in and $\mathrm{CO}_{2}$ rich alveolar air is released out
D. Cellular respiration
E. Transport of gases by the blood

Choose the correct answer from the options given below
questions.answer: Option (D): C, B, E, A, D
questions.solution:
Respiration involves the following steps:
(i) Breathing or pulmonary ventilation by which atmospheric air is drawn in and $\mathrm{CO}_{2}$ rich alveolar air is released out.
(ii) Diffusion of gases across alveolar membrane.
(iii) Transport of gases by the blood
(iv) Diffusion of $\mathrm{O}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{CO}_{2}$ between blood and tissues
(v) Utilisation of $\mathrm{O}_{2}$ by the cells for catabolic reactions and resultant release of $\mathrm{CO}_{2}$

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: It is much easier for a small animal to run uphill than for a large animal because:
options: It is easier to carry a small body weight
Smaller animals have a higher metabolic rate
Small animals have a lower O<sub>2</sub><sub> </sub>requirement
The efficiency of muscles in large animals is less than in the small animals
questions.answer: Option (B): Smaller animals have a higher metabolic rate
questions.solution: Metabolic rate is directly proportional to the size of an animal. Larger the animal, lower is the metabolic rate.Small animals can run uphill than a large animal because of their fast metabolic rate.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Select the correct events that occur during inspiration.
(i) Contraction of diaphragm
(ii) Contraction of external inter-costal muscles
(iii) Pulmonary volume decreases
(iv) Intra pulmonary pressure increases
questions.solution: Inspiration is initiated by the contraction of diaphragm which increases the volume of thoracic chamber in antero-posterior axis and contraction of external inter-costal muscles which lifts up the ribs and sternum causing increases in the volume of thoracic chamber in dorsoventral axis. This increase in thoracic volume causes an increase in pulmonary volume. It decreases the intra-pulmonary pressure to less than atmospheric pressure which allows the entry of air from outside to the lungs i.e., inspiration.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Occupational respiratory disorder leads to:
questions.solution:
Silicosis is due to excess inhalation of silica dust in the workers involved in grinding or stone breaking industries. A long exposure gives rise to inflammation leading to fibrosis and thus causing serious lung damage. 
Anthrax is a serious infectious disease caused by Bacillus anthracis. It commonly affects domestic and wild animals. 
Emphysema is a chronic disorder in which alveolar walls are damaged due to which respiratory surface is decreased.
Botulism is a form of food poisoning caused by Clostridium botulinum.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following options correctly represents the lung conditions in asthma and emphysema, respectively?
options: Increased respiratory surface; Inflammation of bronchioles
Increased number of bronchioles; Increased respiratory surface
Inflammation of bronchioles; Decreased respiratory surface
Decreased respiratory surface; Inflammation of bronchioles

questions.solution: Asthma is an allergy in which difficulty in breathing causes wheezing due to inflammation of bronchi and bronchioles. Emphysema is a chronic disorder in which alveolar walls are damaged due to which respiratory surface is decreased.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Select the favourable conditions required for the formation of oxyhaemoglobin at the alveoli.
options: High pO2, high pCO2, less H+, higher temperature
Low pO2, low pCO2, more H+, higher temperature
High pO2, low pCO2, less H+, lower temperature
Low pO2, high pCO2, more H+, higher temperature
questions.answer: Option (C): High pO2, low pCO2, less H+, lower temperature
questions.solution: In the alveoli, where there is high pO2, low pCO2, lesser H+ concentration, and lower temperature, the factors are all favourable for the formation of oxyhaemoglobin, whereas, in the tissues, where low pO2, high pCO2, high H+ concentration, and higher temperature exist, the conditions are favourable for dissociation of oxygen from the oxyhaemoglobin.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Asthma may be attributed to
options: Allergic reaction of the mast cells in the lungs
Accumulation of fluid in the lungs
questions.answer: Option (B): Allergic reaction of the mast cells in the lungs
questions.solution: Bronchial asthma is due to allergic reactions (release of histamine from mast cells)  to foreign substances that affect respiratory tract. Excess amount of mucus is secreted on the wall of respiratory tract which may clog bronchi and bronchioles.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Approximately seventy percent of carbon dioxide absorbed by the blood will be transported to the lungs
options: In the form of dissolved gas molecules
questions.solution: Nearly 20-25 percent of CO2 is transported by RBCs whereas 70 percent of it is carried as bicarbonate to the lungs. About 7 percent of CO2 is carried in a dissolved state through plasma.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The partial pressures (in mmHg) of oxygen (O2) and carbon dioxide (CO2) at alveoli (the site of diffusion) are:
options: pO2 = 95 and pCO2 = 40
pO2 = 159 and pCO2 = 0.3
pO2 = 104 and pCO2 = 40
pO2 = 40 and pCO2 = 45
questions.solution: Pressure contributed by an individual gas in a mixture of gases is called partial pressure and is represented as pO2 for oxygen and pCO2 for carbon dioxide. The partial pressures (in mmHg) of oxygen (O2) and carbon dioxide (CO2) at alveoli (the site of diffusion) are 104 and 40 respectively. In the atmosphere, pO2 is 159 mm Hg and pCO2 is 0.3 mm Hg. In deoxygenated blood, pO2 is 40 mmHg and pCO2 is 45 mmHg. In oxygenated blood, pO2 is 95 mmHg and pCO2 is 40 mmHg.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The partial pressure of oxygen in the alveoli of the lungs is
options: More than that in the blood
Less than that in the blood
Less than that of carbon dioxide
Equal to that in the blood
questions.answer: Option (A): More than that in the blood
questions.solution:
Alveoli are the site of gaseous exchange and have the higher partial pressure of oxygen than that of blood. Blood is rich in carbon dioxide at cell and tissue level due to cellular respiration. The higher partial pressure of oxygen in alveoli allows diffusion of oxygen from alveoli into the blood. 
Therefore, the correct answer is option a.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Reduction in pH of blood will:
options: Reduce the rate of heart beat.
Reduce the blood supply to the brain.
Decrease the affinity of hemoglobin with oxygen.
Increase the affinity of hemoglobin with oxygen.
questions.answer: Option (C): Decrease the affinity of hemoglobin with oxygen.
questions.solution: A lower pH in the blood increases carbon dioxide concentration which in turn, is suggestive of a more active tissue that requires more oxygen. According to Bohr, the lower pH will cause hemoglobin to deliver more oxygen. This manifests as a right-ward shift in the Oxygen-Hemoglobin Dissociation Curve described in oxygen transport and yields enhanced unloading of oxygen by hemoglobin.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Under normal physical conditions in human beings every 100 ml oxygenated blood can deliver____ml of O<sub>2</sub> to the tissues.
questions.solution: Every 100 ml of oxygenated blood can deliver around 5 ml of O2 to the tissues under normal physiological conditions.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following factors are favourable for the formation of oxyhaemoglobin in alveoli?
options: High pO<sub>2</sub> and lesser H<sup>+</sup> concentration
Low pCO<sub>2</sub> and high H<sup>+</sup> concentration
questions.answer: Option (A): High pO2 and lesser H+ concentration
questions.solution: Binding of oxygen with haemoglobin is primarily related to partial pressure of O2. Partial pressure of CO2, hydrogen ion concentration and temperature are the other factors which can interfere with this binding. A sigmoid curve is obtained when percentage saturation of haemoglobin with O2 is plotted against the pO2. This curve is called the Oxygen dissociation curve (Figure 17.5) and is highly useful in studying the effect of factors like pCO2, H+ concentration, etc., on binding of O2 with haemoglobin. In the alveoli, where there is high pO2, low pCO2, lesser H+ concentration and lower temperature, the factors are all favourable for the formation of oxyhaemoglobin, whereas in the tissues, where low pO2, high pCO2, high H+ concentration and higher temperature exist, the conditions are favourable for dissociation of oxygen from the oxyhaemoglobin. This clearly indicates that O2 gets bound …

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is not the function of the conducting part of the respiratory system?
options: It clears inhaled air from foreign particles
Temperature of inhaled air is brought to body temperature
Provides surface for diffusion of O<sub>2</sub> and CO<sub>2</sub>
questions.answer: Option (D): Provides surface for diffusion of O2 and CO2
questions.solution: The part starting with the external nostrils up to the terminal bronchioles constitute the conducting part whereas the alveoli and their ducts form the respiratory or exchange part of the respiratory system. The conducting part transports the atmospheric air to the alveoli, clears it from foreign particles, humidifies and also brings the air to body temperature. Exchange part is the site of actual diffusion of O2 and CO2 between blood and atmospheric air.

questions.question: Name the pulmonary disease in which alveolar surface area involved in gas exchange is drastically reduced due to damage in the alveolar walls.

Pleurisy- Inflammation of pleura that lines the lungs and chest cavity.
