questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Frogs respire in water by skin and buccal cavity and on land by skin, buccal cavity and lungs.
Choose the correct answer from the following:
options: The statement is false for water and but true for land
The statement is false for both the environment
The statement is true for water but false for land
The statement is true for both the environment
questions.answer: Option (A): The statement is false for water and but true for land
questions.solution: In water, frogs respires only through skin and not buccal cavity, thus, the statement is wrong, whereas on land it can respire through skin, buccal cavity and lungs, thus, this statement is correct.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In which one of the following processes CO<sub>2 </sub>is not released?
questions.solution: End products of aerobic respiration in animals, alcoholic fermentation and aerobic respiration in plants release CO2. However, lactate fermentation does not release CO2. Lactate fermentation is a type of anaerobic respiration in which the respiratory substrate is converted into lactate along with the production of ATP. It takes place in muscles during strenuous physical work.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Lungs are made up of air-filled sacs, the alveoli. They do not collapse even after
forceful expiration, because of
questions.solution: The volume of air present in the lungs after forceful expiration is called the residual volume which prevents the collapsing of alveoli even after forceful expiration. This averages around 1100 mL to 1200 mL. Inspiratory Reserve Volume (IRV) is the extra volume of air inspired by a forcible inspiration. Expiratory Reserve Volume is the additional volume of air, a person can expire by a forcible expiration. The volume of air inspired or expired during normal respiration is called tidal volume.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Due to increasing air-borne allergens and pollutants, many people in urban areas are suffering from respiratory disorder causing wheezing due to
options: Proliferation of fibrous tissues and damage of the alveolar walls
Reduction in the secretion of surfactants by pneumocytes
Benign growth on mucous lining of nasal cavity
questions.answer: Option (A): Inflammation of bronchi and bronchioles
questions.solution: Asthma is a difficulty in breathing which causes wheezing due to inflammation of bronchi and bronchioles. It can be due to increasing air-borne allergens and pollutants. Asthma is an allergic condition. Many people in urban areas are suffering from this respiratory disorder.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Lungs do not collapse between breaths and some air always remains in the lungs which can never be expelled that volume of air is due to
options: There is a positive intrapleural pressure
Pressure in the lungs is higher than the atmospheric pressure
There is a negative pressure in the lungs
questions.solution: Lungs do not collapse between breaths as some air always remains in the lung which can never be expelled because the negative intrapleural pressure is created by two opposing elastic forces pulling in the intrapleural space. The elastic lungs tend to collapse while the elastic chest wall tends to thrust outward. These two opposite forces create a negative intrapleural pressure which in turn opposes the natural tendency of lungs to collapse.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Identify the wrong statement with reference to transport of oxygen.
options: Higher H<sup>+ </sup>conc. in alveoli favours the formation of oxyhaemoglobin
Low pCO<sub>2</sub> in alveoli favours the formation of oxyhaemoglobin
Binding of oxygen with haemoglobin is mainly related to partial pressure of O<sub>2</sub>
Partial pressure of CO<sub>2 </sub>can interfere with<sub> </sub>O<sub>2 </sub>binding with haemoglobin
questions.answer: Option (A): Higher H+ conc. in alveoli favours the formation of oxyhaemoglobin
questions.solution:
The Oxygen dissociation curve is highly useful in studying the effect of factors like pCO2, H+ concentration, etc., on binding of O2 with haemoglobin. In the alveoli, where there is high pO2, low pCO2, lesser H+ concentration and lower temperature, favour the formation of oxyhaemoglobin.
In the tissues, where low pO2, high pCO2, high H+ concentration and higher temperature exist, are favourable conditions for dissociation of oxygen from the oxyhaemoglobin.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Sponges exchange O2 with CO2 by
options: simple diffusion over their entire body surfaces
questions.answer: Option (D): simple diffusion over their entire body surfaces
questions.solution: Lower invertebrates like sponges, coelenterates, flatworms, etc., exchange O2 with CO2 by simple diffusion over their entire body surfaces.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Name the chronic respiratory disorder caused mainly by cigarette smoking.
questions.solution:
Emphysema is a destructive disease of the lung in which the alveoli (small sacs) that promote oxygen exchange between the air and the bloodstream are destroyed. Smoking is the primary cause of emphysema, which makes it a preventable illness. While asthma is a respiratory disorder in which there is difficulty in breathing due to inflammation of the bronchi and bronchioles. 

Respiratory alkalosis- It is characterized by a low level of carbon dioxide in the blood due to breathing excessively.

Respiratory acidosis- It occurs when the body cannot remove enough carbon dioxide that the body produces and hence, making the body fluid and blood acidic.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List - I with List – II
List - IList - II
A.EmphysemaI.Rapid spasms in muscle due to low Ca++ in body fluid
B.Angina PectorisII.Damaged alveolar walls and decreased respiratory surface
C.Glomerulo-nephritisIII.Acute chest pain when not enough oxygen is reaching to heart muscle
D.TetanyIV.Inflammation of glomeruli of kidney

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Emphysema is a chronic disorder in which alveolar walls are damaged due to which respiratory surface is decreased. One of the major causes of this is cigarette smoking
Angina: It is also called ‘angina pectoris’. A symptom of acute chest pain appears when no enough oxygen is reaching the heart muscle. Angina can occur in men and women of any age but it is more common among the middle-aged and elderly. It occurs due to conditions that affect the blood flow.
Glomerulonephritis: Inflammation of glomeruli of kidney, 
Tetany: Rapid spasms (wild contractions) in muscle due to low Ca++ in body fluid.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In water, frogs respire using
questions.solution: Frogs respire on land and in water by different methods. In water, skin acts as aquatic respiratory organ (cutaneous respiration). Dissolved oxygen in the water is exchanged through the skin by diffusion. On land, the buccal cavity, skin and lungs act as the respiratory organs.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Vital capacity of lung is______.
questions.solution: Vital Capacity (VC) refers to the maximum volume of air a person can breathe in after a forced expiration. This includes ERV, TV and IRV or the maximum volume of air a person can breathe out after a forced inspiration.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List I with List II:
List IList II
A. Expiratory capacityI. Expiratory reserve volume + Tidal volume + Inspiratory reserve volume
B. Functional residual capacityII. Tidal volume + Expiratory reserve volume
C. Vital capacityIII. Tidal volume + Inspiratory reserve volume
D. Inspiratory capacityIV. Expiratory reserve volume + Residual volume

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Inspiratory Capacity (IC): Total volume of air a person can inspire after a normal expiration. This includes tidal volume and inspiratory reserve volume (TV+IRV). 
Expiratory Capacity (EC): Total volume of air a person can expire after a normal inspiration. This includes tidal volume and expiratory reserve volume (TV+ERV). 
Functional Residual Capacity (FRC): Volume of air that will remain in the lungs after a normal expiration. This includes ERV+RV. 
Vital Capacity (VC): The maximum volume of air a person can breathe in after a forced expiration. This includes ERV, TV and IRV or the maximum volume of air a person can breathe out after a forced inspiration.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Dissolution of the synaptonemal complex occurs during:
questions.solution: Dissolution of the synaptonemal complex occurs at the diplotene phase of prophase I in meiosis. It occurs after the completion of crossing over which takes place in the pachytene stage.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match the plant with the kind of life cycle it exhibits. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
List - IList - II
(a) Spirogyra(i)Dominant diploid sporophyte vascular plant, with highly reduced male or female gametophyte
(b)Fern(ii)Dominant haploid free-living gametophyte
(c)Funaria(iii)Dominant diploid sporophyte alternating with reduced gametophyte called prothallus
(d)Cycas(iv)Dominant haploid leafy gametophyte alternating with partially dependent multicellular sporophyte
questions.solution:
Spirogyra: Sporophytic generation is represented only by the one-celled zygote. There are no free-living sporophytes. The dominant, photosynthetic phase in such plants is the free-living gametophyte. 
Fern: The diploid sporophyte is represented by a dominant, independent, photosynthetic, vascular plant body. It alternates with multicellular, saprophytic/autotrophic, independent but short-lived haploid gametophyte. 
Funaria: Dominant haploid leafy gametophyte alternating with partially dependent multicellular sporophyte. 
Cycas: Dominant diploid sporophyte vascular plant, with highly reduced male or female gametophyte. This is found in all gymnosperms (Cycas) and angiosperms.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What is the main function of the spindle fiber during mitosis?
questions.solution: Spindle fibers help in separating sister chromatids of the chromosome during the anaphase of Mitosis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The stage during which separation of the paired homologous chromosomes begins is
questions.solution: Synaptonemal complex disintegrates and terminalisation begins during the diplotene stage, i.e. chiasmata start to shift towards the end.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Spindle fibres attach to kinetochores of chromosomes during
questions.solution: At metaphase stage, metaphase chromosome is made up of two sister chromatids, which are held together by the centromere. Small disc-shaped structures at the surface of the centromeres are called kinetochores. These structures serve as the sites of attachment of spindle fibres (formed by the spindle fibres) to the chromosomes that are moved into position at the centre of the cell.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The complex formed by a pair of synapsed homologous chromosomes is called
questions.solution: The complex formed by a pair of synapsed homologous chromosomes is known as a bivalent. The homologous chromosomes start pairing in the zygotene subphase of prophase I (meiosis I), and this process of association is called synapsis. Complex formed by a pair of synapsed homologous chromosomes is called bivalent or tetrad.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List I with List II :
List-I(Phase of cell cycle)List-II(Activity)
A.G1 phaseI.Actual cell division occurs
B.S phaseII.Cell is metabolically active and continuously grows but does not replicate its DNA
C.G2 PhaseIII.Synthesis of DNA occurs and the amount of DNA per cell doubles
D.M phaseIV.Proteins are synthesized while cell growth continues

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
During G1 phase the cell is metabolically active and continuously grows but does not replicate its DNA. S-phase marks the phase during which DNA synthesis or replication takes place and amount of DNA per cell doubles.
During the G2 phase, proteins are synthesised in preparation for mitosis while cell growth continues. During M phase the actual cell division takes place.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List I with List II:
List I(Sub Phases of Prophase I)List II(Specific characters)
A. DiakinesisI. Synaptonemal complex formation
B. PachyteneII. Completion of terminalisation of chiasmata
C. ZygoteneIII. Chromosomes look like thin threads
D. LeptoteneIV. Appearance of recombination nodules

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
(b) A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III
Diakinesis - Completion of terminalisation
Pachytene - Appearance of recombination nodule
Zygotene - Synaptonemal complex forms
Leptotene - Chromosomes look like thin threads

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Among eukaryotes, replication of DNA takes place in
questions.solution: G1 phase

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Spindle fibre attach on to
questions.solution: In prophase of mitosis, specialized regions on centromeres called kinetochores attach chromosomes to spindle fibers. The centromere is the part of a chromosome that links sister chromatids. During mitosis, spindle fibers attach to the chromosomes via the kinetochore. Kinetochores generate kinetochore fibers, which attach sister chromatids to spindle fibers. Kinetochore fibers and spindle polar fibers work together to manipulate and separate chromosomes during mitosis and meiosis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Anaphase Promoting Complex (APC) is a protein degradation machinery necessary for proper mitosis of animal cells. If APC is defective in a human cell, which of the following is expected to occur?
options: Recombination of chromosome arms will occur
questions.solution: Anaphase Promoting Complex (APC) is a protein necessary for the separation of daughter chromosomes during anaphase. If APC is defective then the chromosomes will fail to segregate during anaphase.

questions.question:

B.G2 Phase II.Inactive phase
C.Quiescent stage III.Interval between mitosis and initiation of DNA replication
D.G1 Phase IV. Equational division

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: List IList IIA.M Phase IV.Equational divisionB.G2 Phase I.Proteins are synthesizedC.Quiescent stage II.Inactive phase D.G1 Phase III. Interval between mitosis and initiation of DNA replication

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Zygotic meiosis is characteristic of
questions.solution: Zygotic meiosis is defined as a meiotic division that results in the formation of haploid individuals. It occurs in the zygote. It is to be noted that thallophytes have dominant gametophytic generation, i.e., the presence of haploid individuals. Chlamydomonas has a haplontic life cycle as they belong to the kingdom Plantae and division thallophyta, hence show zygotic meiosis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The enzyme recombinase is required at which stage of meiosis
questions.solution: During pachytene, crossing over occurs which is an enzyme-mediated process that requires the enzyme recombinase. Recombination nodules are formed during the pachytene stage of meiosis which helps to exchange the genetic segments between two non-sister chromatids. Recombinase enzymes play a prominent role in the formation of recombination nodules.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following stages of meiosis involves the division of centromere?
questions.solution: In anaphase II, the centromeres separate, and the sister chromatids—now individual chromosomes—move toward the opposite poles of the cell. The centromeres separate, and the two chromatids of each chromosome move to opposite poles on the spindle. The separated chromatids are now called chromosomes in their own right.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The appearance of recombination nodules on homologous chromosomes during meiosis characterizes:
options: Sites at which crossing over occurs
questions.answer: Option (C): Sites at which crossing over occurs
questions.solution: In the pachytene stage of prophase I, the non-sister chromatids of the homologous chromosomes cross-over and exchange of genetic material takes place. Recombination nodules are the sites at which the non-sister chromatids cross-over.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The process of appearance of recombination nodules occurs at which substage of prophase I in meiosis?
questions.solution: During pachytene, the four chromatids of each bivalent chromosomes becomes distinct and clearly appears as tetrads. This stage is characterised by the appearance of recombination nodules, the sites at which crossing over occurs between non-sister chromatids of the homologous chromosomes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: During which phase(s) of cell cycle, amount of DNA in a cell remains at 4C level if the initial amount is denoted as 2C?
questions.solution: In the G1 phase, the initial amount of DNA was 2C. In the S phase, DNA replicates and the amount of DNA doubles. So the amount of DNA becomes 4C. In the G2 phase, there will be no change in the amount of DNA, so it remains 4C. In M phase, cell division occurs. Before dividing into two daughter cells, the amount of DNA was 4C. After cytokinesis, each daughter cell will have 2C amount of DNA. Thus, in the S phase, 2C becomes 4C and at the end of the M phase, 4C becomes 2C. Hence, the amount of DNA remains at 4C during G2 .

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In meiosis, crossing over is initiated at
questions.solution: The pachytene stage is characterized by the formation of recombination nodules which allows the exchange of genetic material between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes by a process known as crossing over. This also helps in the generation of recombinants.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Given below are two statements.
Statement 1: Chromosomes become gradually visible under light microscope during leptotene stage.
Statement 2: The beginning of diplotene stage is recognized by dissolution of synaptonemal complex.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
questions.answer: Option (D): Both Statement I and Statement II are true
questions.solution:
During leptotene stage the chromosomes become gradually visible under the light microscope
The beginning of diplotene is recognised by the dissolution of the synaptonemal complex and the tendency of the recombined homologous chromosomes of the bivalents to separate from each other except at the sites of crossovers.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: During G0 phase of cell cycle, the cell is metabolically inactive.
Statement II: The centrosome undergoes duplication during S phase of interphase.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
questions.answer: Option (C): Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct.
questions.solution: Statement I: During G0 phase of cell cycle, the cell remain metabolically active but no longer proliferate unless called on to do so depending on the requirement of the organism.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A cell at telophase stage is observed by a student in a plant brought from the field. He tells his teacher that these cells are not like other cells at telophase stage. There is no formation of a cell plate and thus the cell contains more number of chromosomes as compared to other dividing cells. This would result in:
questions.solution: After the division of the nucleus, the division of cytoplasm takes place which is known as cytokinesis. This involves the formation of a cell plate to divide two daughter nuclei. If the cytoplasmic division is not proper and there is no formation of a cell wall then two daughter nuclei cannot be separated and it will result in the formation of a single cell with double genetic material. This condition is known as polyploidy.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Life cycle of Ectocarpus and Fucus respectively are:
questions.solution: Haplodiplontic cycle is the life cycle which is intermediate between haplontic and diplontic. In this both the haplontic and diplontic are free living and multicellular. In the diplontic life cycle the diploid sporophyte is dominant. Ectocarpus and Fucus are algae which have both haplodiplontic and diplontic life cycles.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List -I with LIst – II
List IList II
(a) S phase(i)Proteins are synthesized
(b) G2 phase(ii)Inactive phase
(c) Quiescent stage(iii)Interval between mitosis and initiation of DNA replication
(d) G1 phase(iv)DNA replication
questions.solution: S or synthesis phase marks the period during which DNA synthesis or replication takes place. During this time the amount of DNA per cell doubles. During the G2 phase, proteins are synthesized in preparation for mitosis while cell growth continues. These cells that do not divide further exit the G1 phase to enter an inactive stage called the quiescent stage (G0) of the cell cycle. G1 phase corresponds to the interval between mitosis and initiation of DNA replication. During the G1 phase, the cell is metabolically active and continuously grows but does not replicate its DNA.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is not a characteristic feature during mitosis in somatic cells?
questions.solution: Synapsis, as it's a pairing of the homologous chromosomes. It occurs during the zygotene stage of the meiosis. The homologous chromosomes come closer leading to cross-over in the stage called pachytene. These features are hereby not observed during mitosis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Cells in G<sub>0 </sub>phase
questions.solution: Cells in G0 phase are said to exit cell cycle. These are at the quiescent stage where they are metabolically active but do not proliferate unless called upon to do so. Some cells in animals do not show cell division (e.g. nerve cells), and some cells divide occasionally to replace the damaged/injured cells. These cells do not divide further and exit the G1 phase of cell cycle and enter into an inactive stage called G0 phase.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Select the correct statements:
A. Tetrad formation is seen during Leptotene.
B. During Anaphase, the centromeres split and chromatids separate.
C. Terminalization takes place during Pachytene.
D. Nucleolus, Golgi complex and ER are reformed during Telophase.
E. Crossing over takes place between sister chromatids of homologous chromosome.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
A. Tetrad formation is seen during Zygotene.
C. Crossing over takes place during Pachytene.
E. Crossing over takes place between non - sister chromatids of homologous chromosome.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: During cell growth, DNA synthesis takes place in
questions.solution: The cell cycle is a four-stage process in which the cell increases in size (gap 1 stage or G1 phase), copies its DNA (synthesis or S phase), prepares to divide (gap 2 stage or G2 phase), and divides (mitosis or M phase). The stages G1 , S, and G2 make up interphase, which accounts for the span between cell divisions.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In ‘S’ phase of the cell cycle
options: The amount of DNA remains same in each cell
The amount of DNA is reduced to half in each cell
The amount of DNA doubles in each cell
questions.answer: Option (D): The amount of DNA doubles in each cell
questions.solution: Interphase of the cell cycle involves G1, S and G2 phases. S or synthesis phase marks the period during which DNA synthesis or replication takes place. Hence, the amount of DNA doubles in each cell during the S phase of the cell cycle.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The correct sequence of phases of cell cycle is
questions.solution:
The correct sequence of phases of cell cycle is
G1 → S → G2 → M

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which stage of meiotic prophase shows terminalisation of chiasmata as its distinctive feature?
questions.solution: In meiosis, I, chiasmata (X-shaped structure) is formed in the diplotene stage while it terminalizes in the diakinesis stage. Bivalents are formed in the zygotene stage and crossing over takes place in the pachytene stage. Compaction of chromosomal material occurs in the leptotene stage.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Meiosis takes place in
questions.solution: The cells in which meiosis occurs are called meiocytes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Arrange the following events of meiosis in correct sequence.
a. Crossing over
b. Synapsis
c. Terminalisation of chiasmata
d. Disappearance of nucleolus
questions.solution: During zygotene stage of meiosis, chromosomes start pairing together and this process of association is called synapsis. Crossing over occurs at pachytene stage. Diakinesis is marked by terminalisation of chiasmata. By the end of diakinesis, the nucleolus disappears and the nuclear envelope also breaks down.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The correct sequence of adult cell cycle phases is
questions.solution: Gap 1 phase is the first phase of interphase. After Gap 1 phase, synthesis phase starts in which DNA replicates, then Gap 2 phase occur and finally cell cycle ends with M phase (mitosis).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Some dividing cells exit the cell cycle and enter vegetative inactive stage. This is called quiescent stage (G<sub>0</sub>). This process occurs at the end of :
questions.solution:
Some cells in the adult animals do not appear to exhibit division (e.g., heart cells) and many other cells divide only occasionally, as needed to replace cells that have been lost because of injury or cell death. These cells that do not divide further exit G1 phase to enter an inactive stage
called quiescent stage (G0) of the cell cycle. Cells in this stage remain metabolically active but no longer proliferate unless called on to do so depending on the requirement of the organism.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The concept of “Omnis Cellula-e-cellula” regarding cell division was first proposed by:
questions.solution: Concept of "Omnis cellula-e cellula" regarding cell division was proposed by Rudolf Virchow. It means new cells arise from pre-existing cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Chromosomes are fully condensed at the end of prophase I.
Statement II: Meiosis I resembles mitosis.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is false
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
questions.answer: Option (B): Statement I is correct, but Statement II is false
questions.solution: The final stage of meiotic prophase-I is diakinesis. So, at the end of prophase-I the chromosomes are fully condensed and the meiotic spindle is assembled to prepare the homologous chromosomes for separation. So, Statement I is correct. Meiosis II resembles mitosis as it is an equational division.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following stages of meiosis involves division of centromere?
questions.solution: Anaphase II begins with the simultaneous splitting of the centromere of each chromosome (which was holding the sister chromatids together), allowing them to move toward opposite poles of the cell by shortening of microtubules attached to kinetochores.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Regarding Meiosis, which of the statement(s) is incorrect?
options: There are two stages in Meiosis, Meiosis-I and II
DNA replication occurs in S phase of Meiosis-II
Pairing of homologous chromosomes and recombination occurs in Meiosis-I
Four haploid cells are formed at the end of Meiosis-II
questions.answer: Option (B): DNA replication occurs in S phase of Meiosis-II
questions.solution: In meiosis, a cell undergoes two divisions, i.e. meiosis I and II. Meiosis I is reduction division and meiosis II is equational division (similar to mitosis). However, DNA replicates only once during meiosis, i.e. before meiosis I in S phase.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: DNA replication in bacteria occurs
questions.solution: DNA replication in bacteria occurs prior to fission. The formation of new DNA from parent DNA is called DNA replication. In bacteria, DNA replication prior to fission. It occurs with the help of mesosomes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following options gives the correct sequence of events during mitosis?
options: Condensation → crossing over → nuclear membrane disassembly → segregation → telophase
Condensation → arrangement at equator → centromere division → segregation → telophase
Condensation → nuclear membrane disassembly → crossing over → segregation → telophase
Condensation → nuclear membrane disassembly → arrangement at equator → centromere division → segregation → telophase
questions.answer: Option (D): Condensation → nuclear membrane disassembly → arrangement at equator → centromere division → segregation → telophase
questions.solution:
The correct sequence of events during mitosis would be as follows:
(i) Condensation of DNA so that chromosomes become visible occurs during early to mid-prophase.
(ii) Nuclear membrane disassembly begins at late prophase or transition to metaphase.
(iii) Arrangement of chromosomes at the equator occurs during metaphase, called congression.
(iv) Centromere division or splitting occurs during anaphase forming daughter chromosomes.
(v) Segregation also occurs during anaphase as daughter chromosomes separate and move to opposite poles.
(vi) Telophase leads to the formation of two daughter nuclei.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The fruit fly has 8 chromosomes (2n) in each cell. During the interphase of Mitosis if the number of chromosomes at the G1 phase is 8, what would be the number of chromosomes after the S phase?
questions.solution: S or synthesis phase marks the period during which DNA synthesis or replication takes place. During this time the amount of DNA per cell doubles. If the initial amount of DNA is denoted as 2C then it increases to 4C. However, there is no increase in the chromosome number; if the cell had diploid or 2n number of chromosomes at G1, even after the S phase the number of chromosomes remains the same, i.e., 2n. Therefore, the correct option is c.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
<!-StartFragment->The number of autosomes in human primary 
spermatocyte is<!-EndFragment->
questions.solution:
The human primary spermatocyte is a diploid cell 
that is about to undergo meiosis. Since it is diploid, it contains 44 autosomes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The centriole undergoes duplication during:
questions.solution: In animal cells, during the S phase, DNA replication begins in the nucleus, and the centriole duplicates in the cytoplasm. In the G2 phase there is duplication of mitochondria, chloroplast, and Golgi bodies. Tubulin protein is also synthesized during this phase. During prophase, condensation of chromatin starts. During metaphase, chromosomes get aligned at the equator to form a metaphasic plate.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Identify the correct statement with regard to G<sub>1</sub> phase (Gap I) of interphase.
options: Cell is metabolically active, grows but does not replicate its DNA
DNA synthesis or replication takes place
questions.answer: Option (A): Cell is metabolically active, grows but does not replicate its DNA
questions.solution: G1 phase is a metabolically active stage of the cell cycle. Different types of amino acid, RNA and protein synthesis take place in the G1 phase but DNA replication does not take place. (Note:- DNA replication occur in S phase).

C. Synthesis phase

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: When a cell has stalled DNA replication, which checkpoint should be predominantly activated?
questions.solution: Stalled forks activate checkpoint signaling and pause replication. Since, G1/S checkpoint checks DNA damage, cells size prior to S-phase (i.e. DNA replication phase). This checkpoint would be activated by a stalled DNA replication fork.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Select the incorrect match:
questions.answer: Option (D): Polytene chromosomes – Oocytes of amphibians
questions.solution: Polytene chromosomes are found in salivary glands of insects of order Diptera whereas oocytes of amphibians contain lampbrush chromosomes which are diplotene bivalent chromosomes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The solid linear cytoskeletal elements having a diameter of 6 nm and made up of a single type of monomer are known as
questions.solution: The primary types of fibers comprising the cytoskeleton are microfilaments, microtubules, and intermediate filaments. Microfilaments are fine, thread-like protein fibers, 3-6 nm in diameter. They are composed predominantly of a contractile protein called actin. Microtubules are cylindrical tubes, 20-25 nm in diameter. They are composed of subunits of the protein tubulin. Intermediate filaments are about 10 nm diameter and provide tensile strength for the cell. Lamin is the protein present in intermediate filaments.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A protoplast is a cell:
questions.solution: A protoplast is a cell whose cell wall is removed by digestion with enzymes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is true for nucleolus?
options: It takes part in spindle formation
Larger nucleoli are present in dividing cells
It is a site for active ribosomal RNA synthesis
questions.answer: Option (D): It is a site for active ribosomal RNA synthesis
questions.solution: Nucleolus is a non-membranous structure and is a site of rRNA synthesis. Centromere takes part in spindle formation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Smooth endoplasmic reticulum
options: is the major site for the synthesis of lipids
is actively involved in protein synthesis
is a site for the synthesis of carbohydrates
has ribosomes attached to its surface
questions.answer: Option (A): is the major site for the synthesis of lipids
questions.solution: The Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum (SER) is responsible for synthesis of lipids as well as steroidal hormones. It is not associated with ribosomes and hence appears smooth. Rough endoplasmic reticulum is actively involved in protein synthesis. Carbohydrate synthesis occurs in chloroplasts.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Which of the following cell organelles is responsible for extracting energy from
carbohydrates to form ATP?
questions.solution: Mitochondria are the site of aerobic oxidation of carbohydrates to generate ATP. It oxidizes the pyruvic acid and produces energy in the form of ATP. It also stores the energy for future use.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A cell organelle containing hydrolytic enzymes is
questions.solution: Lysosomes are membranous organelles whose specific function is to breakdown cellular wastes and debris by engulfing it with hydrolytic enzymes. Due to their peculiar function, they are also known as the “suicide bags” of the cell.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements is not correct?
options: The hydrolytic enzymes of lysosomes are active under acidic pH
Lysosomes are formed by the process of packaging in the endoplasmic reticulum
questions.answer: Option (C): Lysosomes are formed by the process of packaging in the endoplasmic reticulum
questions.solution: Lysosomes bud off from trans face of Golgi bodies. Precursors of lysosomal enzymes are synthesised by RER and then sent to Golgi bodies for further processing.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The plastid that stores xanthophyll is known as
questions.solution: The plastid that stores xanthophyll is known as chromoplast.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: In prokaryotes, the positively charged DNA is held with some negatively charged proteins in a region called nucleoid.
Statement II: In eukaryotes, the negatively charged DNA is wrapped around the positively charged histone octamer to form nucleosome.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is false.
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
questions.answer: Option (C): Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is true.
questions.solution: Statement I: In prokaryotes, the negatively charged DNA is held with some positively charged proteins in a region called nucleoid.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Cellular organelles with membranes are
questions.answer: Option (D): Lysosomes, Golgi apparatus and mitochondria
questions.solution: Besides the nucleus, the eukaryotic cells have other membrane-bound cell organelles like lysosomes, Golgi apparatus, and mitochondria. Ribosomes are non-membrane bound organelles present in all cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Chromatophores take part in
questions.solution: Chromatophores are pigments that take part in photosynthesis. Hence, (a) option is correct.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following functions is carried out by cytoskeleton in a cell?
questions.solution: The cytoskeleton in a cell are involved in many functions such as mechanical support, motility, maintenance of the shape of the cell.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Balbiani rings are sites of:
questions.solution: Balbiani rings are large uncoiled regions of polytene chromosomes where RNA transcription and protein synthesis occurs.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The shorter and longer arms of a submetacentric chromosome are referred to as:
questions.solution:
• Sub metacentric chromosome is Heterobrachial.
• Short arm designated as 'p' arm
(p = petite i.e. short)
• Long arm designated as 'q' arm

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Microtubules are the constituents of:
questions.answer: Option (B): Spindle fibres, centrioles and cilia
questions.solution: The microtubules are found in the cytoplasmic matrix of all eukaryotic cells. They also occur in cilia, flagella, centrioles, basal bodies, and mitotic apparatus. Spindle fibers form the protein structure which helps in mitosis and meiosis. Centrioles are the two cylindrical structures of a cell organelle called centrosome. Cilia and flagella are fine hair-like outgrowths of the membrane while peroxisomes are the microbodies.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The organelles that are included in the endomembrane system are
options: Golgi complex, Mitochondria, Ribosomes and Lysosomes
Golgi complex, Endoplasmic reticulum, Mitochondria and Lysosomes
Endoplasmic reticulum, Mitochondria, Ribosomes and Lysosomes
Endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi complex, Lysosomes and Vacuoles
questions.answer: Option (D): Endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi complex, Lysosomes and Vacuoles
questions.solution:
The endomembrane system consists of the endoplasmic
reticulum, Golgi complex, vacuoles, and
lysosomes. Mitochondria is a semi-autonomous cell organelle. The ribosome is a non-membranous cell organelle.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The function of gap junction is to:
options: Perform cementing to keep neighbouring cells together.
Facilitate communication between adjoining cells by connecting the cytoplasm for rapid transfer of ions, small molecules and some large molecules.
Separate two cells from each other.
Stop substance from leaking across a tissue.
questions.answer: Option (B): Facilitate communication between adjoining cells by connecting the cytoplasm for rapid transfer of ions, small molecules and some large molecules.
questions.solution: The gap junction facilitates communication between adjoining cells by connecting the cytoplasm for rapid transfer of ions, small molecules and some large molecules.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The DNA present in chloroplast is
questions.solution: The stroma of the chloroplast contains small, double stranded circular DNA molecules.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following events does not occur in rough endoplasmic reticulum?
questions.solution: Phospholipid synthesis does not take place in RER. The smooth endoplasmic reticulum is involved in lipid synthesis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following structures is not found in a prokaryotic cell?
questions.solution: Nuclear envelope is a double layered membrane surrounding the nucleus in eukaryotes. However, it is not found in a prokaryotic cell.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Given below are two statements: One is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): The primary function of the Golgi apparatus is to package the materials made by the endoplasmic reticulum and deliver it to intracellular targets and outside the cell.
Reason (R): Vesicles containing materials made by the endoplasmic reticulum fuse with the cis face of the Golgi apparatus, and they are modified and released from the trans face of the Golgi apparatus.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
questions.answer: Option (C): Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.solution: The Golgi apparatus principally performs the function of packaging materials, to be delivered either to the intra-cellular targets or secreted outside the cell. Materials to be packaged in the form of vesicles from the ER fuse with the cis face of the Golgi apparatus and move towards the maturing face. This explains, why the Golgi apparatus remains in close association with the endoplasmic reticulum.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which is the important site of formation of glycoproteins and glycolipids in eukaryotic cells?
questions.solution: Proteins and lipids are formed in the endoplasmic reticulum and some of them are modified to form glycoproteins and glycolipids in the Golgi apparatus.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The Golgi complex plays a major role
options: In trapping the light and transforming it into chemical energy
In post-translational modiﬁcation of proteins and glycosidation of lipid
questions.answer: Option (D): In post-translational modiﬁcation of proteins and glycosidation of lipid
questions.solution: The Golgi complex is involved in post-translational modiﬁcation of proteins and glycosidation of lipid and protein for the formation of glycolipid and glycoprotein, respectively.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following are not membrane-bound?
questions.solution: Ribosomes are non-membrane bound organelles found in all cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about inclusion bodies is incorrect?
options: They lie free in the cytoplasm
These represent reserve material in cytoplasm.
They are not bound by any membrane.
These are involved in ingestion of food particles.
questions.answer: Option (D): These are involved in ingestion of food particles.
questions.solution: Inclusions bodies are distinct granules that may occupy a substantial part of the cytoplasm. Inclusion, granules are usually reserved food material and not bound by any membrane. They are not involved in ingestion of food particles. So option (d) is incorrect.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match the columns and identify the correct option.
Column-IColumn-II
1. Thylakoids(i) Disc-shaped sacs in Golgi apparatus
2. Cristae(ii) Condensed structure of DNA
3. Cisternae(iii) Flat membranous sacs in stroma
4. Chromatin(iv) Infoldings in mitochondria
questions.solution:
1. Thylakoids are flat membranous sacs in stroma of chloroplasts.
2. Cristae are folds in the inner membrane of mitochondria.
3. Cisternae are disc-shaped sacs in Golgi apparatus.
4. Chromatin is a condensed structure of DNA.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Select the mismatch.
questions.answer: Option (A): Large central vacuoles- Animal cells
questions.solution: Plant cells have large central vacuoles while animal cells contain many small vacuoles. Protists are eukaryotic cells which have well defined nucleus and other cell organelles. Methanogens are prokaryotes which do not have well defined nuclei. Gas vacuoles are aggregates of hollow cylindrical structures called gas vesicles. They are the form of stored food materials in the cytoplasm of Blue-green algae, Purple photosynthetic bacteria, and Green photosynthetic bacteria.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List - I with List - II.
List – IList - II
A.CentromereI.Mitochondrion
B.CiliumII.Cell division
C.CristaeIII.Cell movement
D.Cell membraneIV.Phospholipid Bilayer

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Primary constriction or the centromere on the sides of which disc shaped structures called kinetochores are present. Centromere holds two chromatids of a chromosome. Centromere involved in the cell division during the splitting of sister chromatids. 
Cilia (sing.: cilium) and flagella (sing.: flagellum) are hair-like outgrowths of the cell membrane. Cilia are small structures which work like oars, causing the movement of either the cell or the surrounding fluid. 
The inner membrane forms a number of infoldings called the cristae (sing.: crista) towards the matrix. The cristae increase the surface area.
Cell Membrane - The major lipids are phospholipids that are arranged in a bilayer.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following pairs of organelles does not contain DNA?
questions.solution: Lysosomes and vacuoles do not have DNA. Inside the cell three organelles contain DNA i.e., mitochondria, chloroplast and nucleus.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The Golgi complex participates in
questions.solution:
Golgi complex, after modification of proteins, packs it and releases it in the form of secretory vesicles from their trans-face.
Mesosomes take part in the respiration of bacteria.
Fatty acid breakdown takes place in the cytoplasm.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding mitochondria is incorrect:
options: Enzymes of electron transport are embedded in outer membrane
Inner membrane is convoluted with infoldings
Mitochondrial matrix contains single circular DNA molecule and ribosomes
Outer membrane is permeable to monomers of carbohydrates, fats and proteins
questions.answer: Option (A): Enzymes of electron transport are embedded in outer membrane
questions.solution: In mitochondria, enzymes for electron transport are present in the inner membrane.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following cell organelles is enclosed by a single membrane?
questions.solution: Nucleus is the double membrane bound organelle of eukaryotic cells that serve to house genetic material. The two membranes together make the nuclear envelope. Mitochondrion is double membrane bound organelle, wherein the inner membrane is present as infolding and forms cristae. Cristae have respiratory enzymes and serve as a site for cellular respiration. Chloroplast is double membrane bound organelle in which the inner membrane surrounds the alkaline stroma and thylakoid system. Lysosomes are bound by a single layer of typical phospholipids.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match list I with list II.
List IList II
A. NucleolusI. Site of formation of glycolipid
B. CentrioleII. Organisation like the cartwheel
C. LeucoplastsIII. Site for active ribosomal RNA synthesis
D. Golgi apparatusIV. For storing nutrients

Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.solution:
- nucleolus is a site for active ribosomal RNA synthesis.
- The centrioles in a centrosome lie perpendicular to each other in which each has an organisation like the cartwheel.
- The leucoplasts are the colourless plastids of varied shapes and sizes with stored nutrients
- Golgi apparatus is the important site of formation of glycoproteins and glycolipids.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: When the centromere is situated in the middle of two equal arms of chromosomes, the chromosome is referred to as
questions.solution: Based on the position of the centromere, chromosomes are categorized as metacentric, submetacentric, acrocentric, and telocentric. The metacentric has a centromere in the middle of the chromosome with two equal arms of the chromosomes. Sub-metacentric has a sub-terminal centromere with one shorter arm and one longer arm. Acrocentric have centromere close to its end forming one extremely short and one very long arm. Telocentric have terminal centromere.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A major site for synthesis of lipids is
questions.solution: SER is the major site for lipid synthesis. Smooth endoplasmic reticulum (SER) lacks ribosomes and functions in lipid metabolism and biosynthesis, carbohydrate metabolism, etc., and is especially abundant in mammalian liver and gonad cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: How many different proteins does the ribosome consist of?

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following criteria does not pertain to facilitated transport?
questions.solution: Facilitated transport is a form of passive transport in which materials are moved across the plasma membrane with the help of transport protein down their concentration gradient. Uphill transport is a process in which diffusion of a component occurs from a less concentrated stream to a more concentrated stream. Thus, uphill transport does not pertain to facilitated transport.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List I with List II:
List IList II
A. AxonemeI. Centriole
B. Cartwheel patternII. Cilia and flagella
C. CristaIII. Chromosome
D. SatelliteIV. Mitochondria

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: AxonemeCilia and flagella Cartwheel patternCentrioleCristaMitochondria SatelliteChromosome

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Which of the following are characteristics of prokaryotic cells?
(a) Ribosomes are made of 50S and 30S subunits
(b) They can have plasmids
(c) They contain mesosome
(d) They have peroxisomes
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: The following are characteristics of prokaryotic cells: Ribosomes are made of 50S and 30S subunits (70S Ribosomes), They can have plasmids (Extra chromosomal DNA), They contain mesosome (Infoldings of plasma membrane). They do not possess membrane bound organelles such as peroxisomes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match the following and select the correct answer:
Column IColumn II
ACentriole(i)Infoldings in mitochondria
BChlorophyll(ii)Thylakoids
CCristae(iii)Nucleic acids
DRibozymes(iv)Basal body cilia or flagella
questions.solution: Basal bodies are modified centrioles that give rise to cilia and flagella. In the cell, apex is the basal body that is the anchoring site for a flagellum. Chlorophyll is found in high concentrations in chloroplasts of plant cells. Chlorophyll is vital for photosynthesis, which allows plants to absorb energy from light. Chlorophyll molecules are specifically arranged in and around photosystems that are embedded in the thylakoid membranes of chloroplasts. The inner membrane of the mitochondria folds inwards, forming the cristae. These folds allow a much greater amount of electron transport chain enzymes and ATP synthase to be packed into the mitochondrion. Ribozymes (ribonucleic acid enzymes), also termed RNA molecules are capable of catalyzing specific biochemical reactions, similar to the action of protein enzymes. RNA can be both genetic material (like DNA) and a biological catalyst lik…

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A specialised membranous structure in a prokaryotic cell which helps in cell wall formation, DNA replication and respiration is :
questions.solution: A specialised membranous structure in a prokaryotic cell which helps in cell wall formation, DNA replication and respiration is mesosome

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : Mitochondria and chloroplasts are both double membrane bound organelles.
Statement II : Inner membrane of Mitochondria is relatively less permeable, as compared to chloroplast.
In the light of the above statements. choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
questions.answer: Option (B): Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
questions.solution: Like mitochondria, the chloroplasts are also double membrane bound. Of the two, the inner chloroplast membrane is relatively less permeable.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Mitochondria and chloroplast are
(1) semi-autonomous organelles
(2) formed by division of pre-existing organelles and they contain DNA but lack protein synthesizing machinery
Which of the following options is correct?
questions.answer: Option (C): (1) is true but (2) is false
questions.solution: Mitochondria are considered as semi-autonomous cell organelle because they have their own DNA which can replicate independently. The mitochondrial DNA produces its own mRNA, tRNA and rRNA which acts as a protein synthesizing machinery. The organelles possess their own ribosomes, called mito ribosomes. The same applies to chloroplast as well.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following components provides a sticky character to the bacterial cell?
questions.solution: The bacterial cell consists of three components: glycocalyx, cell wall, and cell membrane. The sticky character of the bacterial wall is due to glycocalyx or slime layer. This layer is rich in glycoproteins.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Identify the types of cell junctions that help to stop the leakage of the substances across tissue and facilitation of communication with neighbouring cells via rapid transfer of ions and molecules.
options: Adhering junctions and Tight junctions, respectively
Adhering junctions and Gap junctions, respectively
Gap junctions and Adhering junctions, respectively
Tight junctions and Gap junctions, respectively
questions.answer: Option (D): Tight junctions and Gap junctions, respectively
questions.solution: Three types of junctions are found in tissues. Tight junctions stop leakage of substances from leaking across a tissue. Adhering junctions cement and keep neighboring cells together. Gap junctions or communication junctions facilitate communication between cells by connecting the cytoplasm of adjoining cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which structures perform the function of mitochondria in bacteria?
questions.solution: Mesosomes are the infolding of the bacterial cell membrane.These structures are thought to be analogous to the eukaryotic mitochondria. As mitochondria are the site of respiration, these mesosomes carry out respiration in the bacteria.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-IList-II
A. CristaeI. Flat membrane sacs in stroma of chloroplast
B. CisternaeII. Infoldings in mitochondria
C. ThylakoidsIII. Cell membrane
D. PhospholipidIV. Disc shaped sacs in the Golgi apparatus

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Following are the correct matches: Cristae → Infoldings in mitochondria, Cisternae → Disc shaped sacs in the Golgi apparatus, Thylakoids → Flat membrane sacs in stroma of chloroplast, Phospholipid → Cell membrane.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Endomembrane system includes
options: endoplasmic reticulum, chloroplast, peroxisomes and vacuole
Golgi complex, chloroplast, peroxisomes and vacuole
endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi complex, lysosomes and vacuole
questions.answer: Option (D): endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi complex, lysosomes and vacuole
questions.solution: Endomembrane system includes organelles whose functions are coordinated. It includes total four organelles, namely Endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi body, vacuole and lysosomes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements with respect to Endoplasmic Reticulum is incorrect?
options: RER has ribosomes attached to ER
In prokaryotes only RER are present
SER are the sites for lipid synthesis
questions.answer: Option (C): In prokaryotes only RER are present
questions.solution: Endoplasmic reticulum is not found in prokaryotes. Therefore, both RER and SER are absent in prokaryotic cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List - I with List - II. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
List - IList - II
(a) Metacentric chromosome(i)Centromere situated close to the end forming one extremely short and one long arms.
(b)Acrocentric chromosome(ii)Centromeres at the terminal end
(c)Sub-metacentric(iii)Centromere in the middle forming two equal arms of chromosomes
(d)Telocentric chromosome(iv)Centromere slightly away from the middle forming one shorter arm and one longer arm
questions.solution:
The metacentric chromosome has a middle centromere forming two equal arms of the chromosome.
- In the case of an acrocentric chromosome the centromere is situated close to its end forming one extremely short and one very long arm.
-The sub-metacentric chromosome has centromere slightly away from the middle of the chromosome resulting in one shorter arm and one longer arm.
-Telocentric chromosomes have a terminal centromere.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Cell theory was formulated by
questions.solution: Cell theory was formulated by Schleiden and Schwann.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is an incorrect statement?
options: The perinuclear space forms a barrier between the materials present inside the nucleus and that of the cytoplasm
Nuclear pores act as passages for proteins and RNA molecules in both directions between nucleus and cytoplasm
Mature sieve tube elements possess a conspicuous nucleus and usual cytoplasmic organelles
Microbodies are present both in plant and animal cells
questions.answer: Option (C): Mature sieve tube elements possess a conspicuous nucleus and usual cytoplasmic organelles
questions.solution:
The nuclear envelope consists of two lipid bilayer membranes: an inner nuclear membrane and an outer nuclear membrane. The space between the membranes is called the perinuclear space, which forms a barrier between the materials present inside the nucleus and that of the cytoplasm.At a number of places the nuclear envelope is interrupted by minute pores, which are formed by the fusion of its two membranes. These nuclear pores are the passages through which movement of RNA and protein molecules takes place in both directions between the nucleus and the cytoplasm.
Mature sieve tube elements are deep , tubular and do not contain nucleus in the cells with no secondary wall and terminal sieve plate. They lack nucleus at the maturity so that they are associated with companion cells for support.

Many membrane bound minute vesicles called microbodies that contain various enzymes, are present in …

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
From the statements given below choose the correct option :
A. The eukaryotic ribosomes are 80S and prokaryotic ribosomes are 70S.
B. Each ribosome has two sub-units.
C. The two sub-units of 80S ribosome are 60S and 40S while that of 70S are 50S and 30S.
D. The two sub-units of 80S ribosome are 60S and 20S and that of 70S are 50S and 20S.
E. The two sub-units of 80S are 60S and 30S and that of 70S are 50S and 30S.
questions.answer: Option (C): A. B, C are true
questions.solution: Ribosomes are non-membranous organelles involved in protein synthesis and are found in both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells. Statement A is correct because eukaryotic ribosomes are 80S, and prokaryotic ribosomes are 70S in size, where 'S' stands for Svedberg unit, indicating sedimentation rate during centrifugation. Statement B is also correct, as each ribosome is composed of two subunits. Statement C is correct because the 80S ribosome consists of a 60S (large) and 40S (small) subunit, and the 70S ribosome consists of a 50S (large) and 30S (small) subunit. Statements D and E are incorrect as they mention wrong subunit combinations that are not found in nature. Therefore, the correct combination of true statements is A, B, and C.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Non-membrane bound cell organelles found in both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells are ____.
questions.solution: Ribosome is a non-membrane bound cell organelle, found in both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Which of the following are NOT considered as the part of endomembrane system?
A. Mitochondria
B. Endoplasmic Reticulum
C. Chloroplasts
D. Golgi complex
E. Peroxisomes
Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
questions.answer: Option (A): A, C and E only
questions.solution: The endomembrane system include endoplasmic reticulum (ER), golgi complex, lysosomes and vacuoles. Since the functions of the mitochondria, chloroplast and peroxisomes are not coordinated with the above components, these are not considered as part of the endomembrane system.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Read the following statements and choose the set of correct statements:
(a) Euchromatin is loosely packed chromatin
(b) Heterochromatin is transcriptionally active
(c) Histone octamer is wrapped by negatively charged DNA in nucleosome
(d) Histones are rich in lysine and arginine.
(e) A typical nucleosome contains 400 bp of DNA helix
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Heterochromatin are regions of DNA that are tightly packed with histone proteins and are transcriptionally inactive, contrary to euchromatin. A nucleosome typically contains 200 bp of DNA helix.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following statements about Histones is wrong?
options: Histones are rich in amino acids - Lysine and Arginine
Histones carry positive charge in the side chain.
Histones are organized to form a unit of 8 molecules.
The pH of histones is slightly acidic
questions.answer: Option (D): The pH of histones is slightly acidic
questions.solution: Histones are rich in basic amino acids residue lysine and arginine with charged side chains. There are five types of histone proteins i.e., H1, H2A, H2B, H3, and H4. Four of them occur in pairs to produce a unit of 8 molecules (histone octamer). The pH of histones is basic.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The association of histone H1 with a nucleosome indicates
options: The DNA is condensed into a chromatin Fibre
The DNA double helix is exposed
questions.answer: Option (A): The DNA is condensed into a chromatin Fibre
questions.solution: The association of histone H1 protein indicates the complete formation of the nucleosome. Histone proteins are the proteins that coil around the DNA in the eukaryotes and forms a rigid structure known as nucleosomes. Therefore, the DNA is in condensed form.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Water soluble pigments found in plant cell vacuoles are:
questions.solution: Anthocyanins are water soluble pigments. These are present in the vacuoles. These appear in different colors like red, blue or purple depending on the pH. Xanthophylls are the typical yellow pigments of leaves. Chlorophyll is a term used for several closely related green pigments found in cyanobacteria and the chloroplasts of algae and plants. Carotenoids are plant pigments responsible for bright red, yellow and orange hues in many fruits and vegetables. These pigments play an important role in plant's health.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
          List-I                                  List-II
(a) Cristae                            (i)   Primary constriction in chromosome

(b) Thylakoids                      (ii)  Disc-shaped sacs in Golgi apparatus

(c) Centromere                    (iii) Infolding in mitochondria

(d) Cisternae                        (iv) Flattened membranous sacs in stroma of plastids
questions.solution: The inner membrane of mitochondria forms a number of infoldings called the cristae (sing.: crista) towards the matrix. The cristae increase the surface area. A number of organized flattened membranous sacs called the thylakoids are present in the stroma. Thylakoids are arranged in stacks like the piles of coins called grana (singular: granum) or the intergranal thylakoids. Every chromosome essentially has a primary constriction or the centromere on the sides of which disc-shaped structures called kinetochores are present. The golgi complex consists of many flat, disc-shaped sacs or cisternae of 0.5µm to 1.0µm diameter. These are stacked parallel to each other. A varied number of cisternae are present in a golgi complex.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The osmosis of a cell kept in water is chiefly regulated by
questions.solution: Vacuoles are the organelles that store all the extra water and salts that are the basis of creating osmotic pressure in the cell. The vacuole takes up a huge central place in the cell. The solution outside the cell is hypertonic, hypotonic, or isotonic with respect to the contents inside the vacuole. Plastids are the centers for photosynthesis. Ribosomes are small granule-like structures that help in protein synthesis whereas mitochondria generate energy for the cell by utilizing sugars.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Select the correct statement.
options: Insulin acts on pancreatic cells and adipocytes
questions.solution:
(a) Insulin acts mainly on hepatocytes and adipocytes (cells of adipose tissue), and enhances cellular glucose uptake and utilization.
(b) Glucagon acts mainly on the liver cells (hepatocytes) and stimulates glycogenolysis resulting in increased blood sugar (hyperglycemia).
(c) Glucocorticoids stimulate gluconeogenesis, lipolysis and proteolysis; and inhibit cellular uptake and utilization of amino acids.
(d) Insulin is associated with hypoglycemia.

questions.question: Identify the correct statement on ‘inhibin’.
options: Inhibits the secretion of LH, FSH and prolactin.
Is produced by granulosa cells in the ovary and inhibits the secretion of FSH.
Is produced by granulosa cells in the ovary and inhibits the secretion of LH.
Is produced by nurse cells is testes and inhibits the secretion of LH.
questions.answer: Option (B): Is produced by granulosa cells in the ovary and inhibits the secretion of FSH.
questions.solution: FSH and LH act on specific membrane receptors in granulosa cells and theca cells of the ovary, stimulating follicular growth and hormone synthesis. The peptide hormone inhibin is synthesized and secreted by granulosa cells and specifically inhibits FSH synthesis and secretion by the pituitary.

questions.answer: Option (A): α-cells of pancreas secrete insulin
questions.solution: The two main types of cells in the Islet of Langerhans are called α-cells and β-cells. The α-cells secrete a hormone called glucagon, while the β-cells secrete insulin. Glucagon stimulates glycogenolysis while insulin stimulates glycogenesis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Identify the hormone with its correct matching of source and function.
options: Melatonin – Pineal gland – regulates the normal rhythm of sleep-wake cycle
Progesterone – corpus callosum – secondary sex organs
Atrial natriuretic factor –ventricular wall – increases the blood pressure
Oxytocin – anterior pituitary – growth and maintenance of mammary glands
questions.answer: Option (A): Melatonin – Pineal gland – regulates the normal rhythm of sleep-wake cycle
questions.solution:
Oxytocin, produced by posterior pituitary gland functions in parturition.
Melatonin is a hormone from the pineal gland that helps regulate biological rhythms such as sleep and wake cycles. It directs the internal clock - the one that allows us to wake up about the same time every morning without an alarm clock. Progesterone secreted by the corpus luteum is a steroid hormone involved in the menstrual cycle, pregnancy and embryogenesis. Atrial natriuretic factor is a powerful vasodilator and a protein hormone, secreted by heart muscle cells.

questions.answer: Option (D): The anterior pituitary gland and stimulates the secretion of LH and FSH
questions.solution: Hypothalamus secretes GnRH which stimulates the anterior pituitary gland for the secretion of gonadotropins (FSH and LH). GnRH is a gonadotrophin hormone that is released by the hypothalamus. It acts on the anterior pituitary and stimulates the secretion of the LH and FSH which further helps in the development of gonads.

questions.solution: Hypothyroidism in the mother during pregnancy results in defective development and maturation of the growing foetus leading to stunted growth, mental retardation, low IQ and abnormal skin.

questions.solution:

• Excess secretion of growth hormone in adults especially in middle age can result in severe disfigurement (especially of the face) called Acromegaly, which may lead to serious complications, and premature death if unchecked.
• Cushing's syndrome: Cushing's syndrome is a disorder caused due to the body's long-term exposure to an excess level of the hormone cortisol.
• Exophthalmic goitre, also known as Graves disease, is an autoimmune disease. It is a disease related to the thyroid gland and it is caused due to hyperthyroidism. questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Which of the following are not the effects of Parathyroid hormone ?
a. Stimulates the process of bone resorption
b. Decreases Ca2+ level in blood
c. Stimulates reabsorption of Ca2+ by renal tubules
d. Decreases the absorption of Ca2+ from digested food
e. Increases metabolism of carbohydrates
Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
questions.solution: Parathyroid hormone increases the Ca2+ levels in the blood. PTH acts on bones and stimulates the process of bone resorption (dissolution/ demineralisation). PTH also stimulates reabsorption of Ca2+ by the renal tubules and increases Ca2+ absorption from the digested food. PTH is a hypercalcemic hormone and along with TCT (thyrocalcitonin), it plays a significant role in calcium balance in the body.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which hormones stimulate the production of pancreatic juice and bicarbonate?
questions.solution:
Cholecystokinin acts on both pancreas and gallbladder and stimulates the secretion of pancreatic and bile juice respectively. Secretin acts on the exocrine pancreas and stimulates secretion of bicarbonate ions.
So, the correct answer is 'Cholecystokinin and secretin'

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following pairs of hormones are not antagonistic (having opposite effects) to each other?
questions.solution: Relaxin is a protein hormone secreted by placenta. It dilates the cervix and aids in childbirth. Inhibin is secreted from ovaries and inhibits the release of FSH (Follicle stimulating hormone). Parathormone increases blood calcium level by increasing the reabsorption of calcium from the bones. Calcitonin acts on bone and kidneys to reduce blood calcium level. Insulin acts on hepatocytes and adipocytes and increases the uptake of cellular glucose and its utilisation. Thus, it decreases blood glucose level. Glucagon increases blood sugar level by stimulating glycogenolysis (i.e. breakdown of glucose) and gluconeogenesis (synthesis of glucose). Aldosterone maintains the electrolyte balance in the body by reducing the loss of sodium through urine and sweat. Atrial natriuretic factor stimulates excretion of sodium in kidneys.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Grave's disease is caused due to
questions.solution:
Oversecretion of thyroid hormones (hyperthyroidism) causes Graves’s disease which is characterized by the formation of the exophthalmic goiter. 
Addison’s disease is caused by the presence of ineffective ACTH which in turn leads to the deficiency of aldosterone and cortisol hormones of the adrenal cortex. Excessive ACTH secretion by anterior pituitary results in hyperproduction of cortisol causing Cushing’s disease. Myxedema is caused by hypothyroidism in adults and is characterized by lethargy, hair loss, weight gain, puffed skin, lowered body temperature and slowed pulse rate. Therefore, the correct answer is option a.

questions.solution: Estrogen promotes the activity of osteoblast and inhibits osteoclast. In aging female osteoporosis occurs due to deficiency of estrogen. Parathormone promotes the mobilisation of calcium from bone into the blood. Excessive activity of parathormone causes demineralisation leading to osteoporosis.

questions.solution:
Glucagon hormone from pancreas stimulates the liver to break down glycogen into glucose and breakdown of fat into glycerol and fatty acids in adipose tissues to serve as a substrate for glucose formation in liver cells.
Secretin is secreted by endocrine cells of the duodenal wall in response to the presence of hydrochloric acid in chyme and induces the release of pancreatic juice from the pancreas.
Insulin serves to lower the blood glucose level by stimulating the uptake of glucose by cells, specifically muscle cells, liver cells and adipose tissues cells. Liver and muscle cells store glucose as glycogen. Glucose serves as an energy source for muscle contraction and in adipose tissues, it supplies glycerol for the formation of fat. 
The enteroendocrine cells secrete gastrin which in turn promotes stomach churning and induces more release of gastric juices. 
Therefore, the correct answer …

a – iii; b – ii; c – i; d – iv
questions.answer: Option (A): a – iii; b – i; c – iv; d – ii
questions.solution: Antidiuretic hormone released by the pituitary gland stimulates reabsorption of water by the kidneys. The deficiency of this hormone causes increased urine production, a condition called diabetes insipidus. Graves disease is an immune system disorder that results in the overproduction of thyroid hormones. Addison's disease is caused by a deficiency of the hormones secreted by the adrenal cortex. Pancreas is a composite gland which functions as both an exocrine and endocrine gland. The deficiency of insulin, a hormone secreted by the pancreas, causes a complex disorder called diabetes mellitus which is associated with loss of glucose through urine and formation of harmful compounds known as ketone bodies.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct in relation to the endocrine system?
options: Adenohypophysis is under direct neural regulation of the hypothalamus
Organs in the body like gastrointestinal tract, heart, kidney and liver do not produce any hormones
Non-nutrient chemicals produced by the body in trace amount that act as intercellular messenger are hormones
Releasing and inhibitory hormones of hypothalamus are produced by the pituitary gland
questions.answer: Option (C): Non-nutrient chemicals produced by the body in trace amount that act as intercellular messenger are hormones
questions.solution:
Endocrine systems have non-nutrient intercellular messengers called hormones.
Adenohypophysis is under the control of hormonal secretions of the hypothalamus. The organs in the body like GI tract, kidney, etc. do produce hormones, e.g., gastrin by the gastrointestinal tract. 

Releasing and inhibitory hormones are produced by the hypothalamus.

 step (i) to be reversible, its equilibrium constant.

(Given: log 2 = 0.301)
questions.solution:
Rate constant k = 0.03 s–1
Initial concentration [A]0 = 7.2 mol L–1
Final concentration [A] = 0.9 mol L–1
log 2 = 0.301
For a first-order reaction, the integrated rate law is: 
ln [A] – ln [A]0 = –kt
\[{\text{t}} = \frac{1}{{\text{k}}} \times 2.303\log \frac{{{{\left[ {\text{A}} \right]}_0}}}{{\left[ {\text{A}} \right]}}\]
\[{\text{t}} = \frac{1}{{{\text{0}}{\text{.03}}}} \times 2.303\log \frac{{7.2}}{{{\text{0}}{\text{.9}}}}\]
\[{\text{t}} = \frac{1}{{{\text{0}}{\text{.03}}}} \times 2.303\log 8\]
\[{\text{t}} = \frac{1}{{{\text{0}}{\text{.03}}}} \times 2.303 \times \log 2\]
\[{\text{t}} = \frac{1}{{{\text{0}}{\text{.03}}}} \times 2.303 \times 0.3010 = 69.3\,{\text{s}}\]

questions.solution:
Magnetic moment \[\left( \mu \right) = \sqrt {n\left( {n + 2} \right)} {\text{BM}}\]
where 'n' is number of unpaired e-s
∴ 2.83 = \[\sqrt {n\left( {n + 2} \right)} \]
∴ n (n + 2) = (2.83)2 = 8
∴ n2 + 2n - 8 = 0
∴ (n + 4) (n - 2) = 0
∴ n = -4 or n = 2
∵ number of e-s can't be negative
∴ number of unpaired e-s = 2

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Across a metallic conductor of non-uniform cross section a constant potential difference is applied. The quantity which remains constant along the conductor is:
questions.solution:
Current is defined as charge flown per unit time, it should be remain same along any cross section as there is no accumulation of charge in conductor. Hence current will remain constant .
The resistance is given by $$R = \frac{{\rho L}}{A},$$ where $$\rho $$ is resistivity which is constant for given material. When the area of cross section of resistor varies its resistance will also vary.
Form Ohm's law $$V = IR$$ as the $$I$$ is constant and R varies, the potential difference varies along cross section and correspondingly electric field will also change in cross section. 
Drift velocity is given by $${v_d} = \frac{I}{{neA}}$$ which will also change ; as $$I$$ is constant and A is varying current density is given as $$J = \frac{I}{A},$$ which will also change ; as $$I$$ is constant and A is varying.
