questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: MALT constitutes about………… percent of the lymphoid tissue in the human body.
questions.solution: MALT is Mucosa Associated Lymphoid Tissue and it constitutes about 50 percent of the lymphoid tissue in the human body. It consists of T cells, B cells, and macrophages. It is distributed in association with mucosal tissue.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Select the incorrect statement :
options: FSH stimulates the sertoli cells which help in spermiogenesis
LH and FSH decrease gradually during the follicular phase
LH triggers secretion of androgens from the Leydig cells
questions.answer: Option (C): LH and FSH decrease gradually during the follicular phase
questions.solution: LH is a Luteinizing hormone produced by the gonadotropic cells in the anterior pituitary gland. It plays an important role in puberty, menstruation, and fertility. It triggers ovulation and development of the corpus luteum. In male, LH triggers the secretion of androgen called as testosterone from the Leydig cells. FSH is follicle-stimulating hormone produced by gonadotropic cells in the anterior pituitary gland. It helps in regulation of development, growth, pubertal maturation and reproductive processes of the body. It stimulates the Sertoli cells of the testicles and helps in spermatogenesis, production of sperm. During the follicular phase, the LH and FSH increase gradually. They stimulate follicular development and estrogen secretion by follicular cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The amnion of mammalian embryo is derived from
questions.solution:
The extraembryonic membranes are amnion, chorion, allantois, and Yolk sac. Amnion is formed from mesoderm on the outer side and ectoderm on the inner side.
Chorion is formed from trophectoderm and mesoderm whereas allantois and yolk sac membranes have mesoderm on the outer side and endoderm on the inner side.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is not a component of Fallopian tube?
questions.solution: The oviducts (fallopian tubes), uterus and vagina constitute the female accessory ducts. Each fallopian tube is about 10-12 cm long and extends from the periphery of each ovary to the uterus (Figure 3.3b), the part closer to the ovary is the funnel-shaped infundibulum. The edges of the infundibulum possess finger-like projections called fimbriae, which help in collection of the ovum after ovulation. The infundibulum leads to a wider part of the oviduct called ampulla. The last part of the oviduct, isthmus has a narrow lumen and it joins the uterus.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: At which stage of life the oogenesis process is initiated?
questions.solution: Oogenesis is the formation of the ova or the female sex gamete. It begins in the early fetus when primordial germ cells migrate from the yolk sac of the embryo to the genital ridge at 5–6 weeks of gestation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Capacitation occurs in
questions.solution: Capacitation is the phenomenon of sperm activation in mammals in which the sperm develops the ability to fertilise the ova. Capacitation occurs in the female reproductive tract. The secretion of the female reproductive tract removes the coating substances deposited on the acrosome, thereby, exposing the receptor sites and making the sperm active to penetrate the egg.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Twins are born to a family that lives next door to you. The twins are a boy and a girl. Which of the following must be true?
options: They were conceived through in vitro fertilization.
questions.solution: Fraternal twins, also known as dizygotic twins, occur when two separate eggs are fertilized by two different sperm. Since a boy and a girl are born, it indicates two separate eggs and sperm were involved, meaning they are fraternal twins. Monozygotic twins result from one fertilized egg splitting, leading to identical genetic content and the same sex. In vitro fertilization is a method of assisted reproduction but doesn't determine whether twins will be fraternal or identical.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The difference between spermiogenesis and spermiation is
options: In spermiogenesis spermatozoa from Sertoli cells are released into the cavity of seminiferous tubules, while in spermiation spermatozoa are formed
In spermiogenesis spermatozoa are formed, while in spermiation spermatids are formed
In spermiogenesis spermatids are formed, while in spermiation spermatozoa are formed
In spermiogenesis spermatozoa are formed, while in spermiation spermatozoa are released from Sertoli cells into the cavity of seminiferous tubules
questions.answer: Option (D): In spermiogenesis spermatozoa are formed, while in spermiation spermatozoa are released from Sertoli cells into the cavity of seminiferous tubules
questions.solution: Spermiogenesis is the transformation of spermatids into spermatozoa whereas spermiation is the release of sperms from Sertoli cells into the lumen of seminiferous tubules.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Ectopic pregnancies are referred to as:
options: Implantation of embryos at sites other than the uterus.
Implantation of defective embryos in the uterus.
Pregnancies terminated due to hormonal imbalance.
questions.answer: Option (B): Implantation of embryos at sites other than the uterus.
questions.solution: Ectopic pregnancies are referred to as implantation of embryos at sites other than uterus, either in the fallopian tubes, cervix or ovary.

questions.solution: Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Changes in GnRH pulse frequency in females is controlled by circulating levels of :
questions.solution: Gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) is produced by the hypothalamus. It stimulates the pituitary gland to produce luteinizing hormone (LH) and, to a lesser extent, follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH). However, with depletion of follicular number, estrogen levels decrease with subsequent loss of negative feedback and resultant increases in GnRH secretion. Progesterone also decreases GnRH secretion at the level of the hypothalamus.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The presence or absence of hymen is not a reliable indicator of virginity.
Statement II: The hymen is torn during the first coitus only.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both statement I and statement II are false
Statement I is true but statement II is false
Statement I is false but statement II is true
Both statement I and statement II are true
questions.answer: Option (B): Statement I is true but statement II is false
questions.solution: The opening of the vagina is often covered partially by a membrane called hymen. The hymen is often torn during the first coitus (intercourse). However, it can also be broken by a sudden fall or jolt, insertion of a vaginal tampon, active participation in some sports like horseback riding, cycling, etc. In some women the hymen persists even after coitus. In fact, the presence or absence of hymen is not a reliable indicator of virginity or sexual experience.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of these is not an important component of initiation of parturition in humans?
options: Increase in estrogen and progesterone ratio
questions.solution: At the end of gestation, the completely developed foetus is expelled out. This process is called parturition. Parturition is controlled by a complex neuroendocrine mechanism. The estrogen and progesterone ratio increases as estrogen levels rise significantly. Prostaglandins, which stimulate uterine contractions are also produced that act on the myometrium. Oxytocin, the main hormone, also called birth hormone is released by the maternal pituitary, which brings about strong uterine contractions. Prolactin is a lactation hormone that has no role in the initiation of parturition.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The covering of ovum at ovulation is
questions.solution: The Graafian follicle ruptures to release the secondary oocyte (ovum) from the ovary by the process called ovulation. The secondary oocyte forms a membrane called zona pellucida surrounding it.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following hormone levels will cause release of ovum (ovulation) from  the  graafian follicle ?
questions.solution: LH (Luteinizing hormone) is produced by the pituitary gland in the brain. It triggers ovulation & promotes the development of corpus luteum from ruptured graafian follicle. High concentration of estrogen is released by mature graafian follicle during ovulation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List I with List II related to embryonic development at various months of pregnancy:
List IList II
A.The foetus movement starts and hair appears on the head(I)24 weeks of pregnancy
B.The foetus develops limbs and digits(II)20 weeks of pregnancy
C.The foetus develops external genital organs(III)8 weeks of pregnancy
D.The foetus body is covered with fine hair; eyelids separate and eyelashes are formed(IV)12 weeks of pregnancy

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
- By the end of second month of pregnancy ( 8 weeks), the foetus develops limbs and digits
- By the end of 12 weeks (first trimester) of pregnancy, most of the major organ system are formed. The limbs and external genital organs are also well developed.
- During the fifth month ( 20 weeks) of pregnancy, the first movements of the foetus and appearance of hair on the head are usually observed.
- By the end of about 24 weeks (ends of second trimester) of pregnancy, the body is covered with fine hair, eye lids separate and eyelashes are formed.

So, the correct match is A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Spermatogonia undergo a series of cell divisions statements to produce sperms. Select the correct from the following :
A. Spermatogonia always undergo meiotic cell division.
B. Primary spermatocytes divide mitotically to produce secondary spermatocytes.
C. Secondary spermatocytes, through their second meiotic division, produce haploid spermatids.
D. Spermatids produce spermatozoa through mitosis.
E. Spermatids transform into spermatozoa by spermiogenesis.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
(A) Incorrect : Spermatogonia undergo mitotic differentiation.
(B) Incorrect : Primary spermatocytes undergo $1^{\text {st }}$ meiotic division to form secondary spermatocytes.
(C) Correct : Secondary spermatocytes undergo $2^{\text {nd }}$ meiotic division to form the haploid spermatids.
(D) Incorrect : Spermatids form spermatozoa through a differentiation process called spermiogenesis.
(E) Correct : Spermatids produce spermatozoa via spermiogenesis.

Thus, the correct statements are (C) and (E) only.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What is the correct sequence of sperm formation?
questions.solution: The correct sequence of spermatogenesis in human males is spermatogonia → spermatocyte → spermatid → spermatozoa.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Menstrual ﬂow occurs due to lack of
questions.solution: Progesterone functions in maintaining pregnancy. In the absence of progesterone, the endometrium along with blood is shed in the form of menstrual ﬂow.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following structure is not a part of the male reproductive system?
questions.solution: The male sex accessory ducts include rete testis, vasa efferentia, epididymis and vas deferens. Infundibulum is the part of oviduct (female accessory duct).

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is false.
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
questions.answer: Option (D): Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
questions.solution: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Extrusion of second polar body from egg nucleus occurs
options: Before entry of sperm into ovum
After entry of sperm but before fertilization
questions.answer: Option (D): After entry of sperm but before fertilization
questions.solution: Extrusion of the second polar body from the egg nucleus occurs after entry of sperm but before fertilization. The entry of sperm into the ovum induces completion of the meiotic division of the secondary oocyte. Entry of sperm causes breakdown of metaphase promoting factor (MPF) and turns on anaphase promoting complex (APC).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The first menstruation is called:
questions.solution: The first menstruation begins at puberty and is called as menarche.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Arrange the following cell layers/structures around the female gamete, from outer to inner side :
A. Zona pellucida
B. Perivitelline space
C. Corona radiata
D. Plasma membrane of ovum

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution: The cell layer/structure around the female gamete from outer to inner side is : Corona radiata → zona pellucida → perivitelline space → plasma membrane of ovum. So the correct answer is C, A, B, D.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The main function of mammalian corpus luteum is to produce
questions.solution: The corpus luteum is a temporary endocrine structure in human females that secretes a large amount of progesterone which is essential for the maintenance of endometrium of the uterus.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Find the correct statements:
A. In human pregnancy, the major organ systems are formed at the end of 12 weeks.
B. In human pregnancy, the major organ systems are formed at the end of 8 weeks.
C. In human pregnancy heart is formed after one month of gestation.
D. In human pregnancy, limbs and digits develop by the end of second month.
E. In human pregnancy the appearance of hair is usually observed in the fifth month.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: B, C, D and E only
A, C, D and E only
questions.answer: Option (B): A, C, D and E only
questions.solution: In human pregnancy, the major organ systems are formed at the end of 12 weeks, not 8, thus, statement B is incorrect. Statements A, C, D and E are correct.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding female reproductive cycle?
A. In non-primate mammals, cyclical changes during reproduction are called oestrus cycle.
B. First menstrual cycle begins at puberty and is called menopause.
C. Lack of menstruation may be indicative of pregnancy.
D. Cyclic menstruation extends between menarche and menopause.
Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
questions.answer: Option (C): A, C and D only
questions.solution: First menstrual cycle begins at puberty and is called menarche.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following secretes the hormone, relaxin, during the later phase of pregnancy?
questions.solution: The hormone relaxin is produced in the later phase of pregnancy. It is produced by the ovary. Graafian follicles are not formed when the woman is pregnant. Uterus and fetus do not produce relaxin. Relaxin is produced by the corpus luteum present in the ovary. A ruptured Graafian follicle is called the corpus luteum, which has an endocrine function.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following layers in an antral follicle is acellular?
questions.solution: During the development of antral follicle, a glycoprotein polymer capsule called the zona pellucida is acellular, which separates it from the surrounding granulosa cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Meiotic division of the secondary oocyte is completed
options: At the time of fusion of a sperm with an ovum
questions.answer: Option (B): At the time of fusion of a sperm with an ovum
questions.solution: When sperm nucleus enters into the secondary oocyte during fertilization, it provides the anaphase promoting factor that induces the completion of meiosis in the secondary oocyte.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Which of the following statements are true for spermatogenesis but do not hold true for Oogenesis?
(a) It results in the formation of haploid gametes
(b) Differentiation of gamete occurs after the completion of meiosis
(c) Meiosis occurs continuously in a mitotically dividing stem cell population
(d) It is controlled by the Luteinizing hormone (LH) and Follicle Stimulating Hormone (FSH) secreted by the anterior pituitary
(e) It is initiated at puberty
Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
- Oogenesis begins at the fetal stages and not at puberty. 
- Meiosis does not occur continuously in case of oogenesis since it is a discontinuous process in women. It starts dividing mitotically at the fetal stages to form a diploid primary oocyte. This primary oocyte enters meiosis but remains arrested at prophase I of meiosis up until puberty, after which it resumes division and completes Meiosis I. Meiosis II is completed only after fertilization.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following cannot be detected in a developing foetus by amniocentesis?
questions.solution: Amniocentesis is a test to determine the chromosomal pattern in the foetal cells within the amniotic ﬂuid surrounding the developing foetus. Jaundice is not a chromosomal disease and thus cannot be detected by amniocentesis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Which of the following statements are true with reference to the sex-determination in honeybees?
A. An offspring formed from the union of a sperm and an egg, develops as a female (queen or worker).
B. An unfertilized egg develops as a male by parthenogenesis.
C. A male has half the number of chromosomes than that of a female.
D. Males produce sperms by meiosis.
E. Honeybees have a haplodiploid sex-determination system.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: B, C, D and E only
A, B, C and D only
A, B, D and E only
A, B, C and E only
questions.answer: Option (D): A, B, C and E only
questions.solution: In case of honeybees, males have half the number of chromosomes than that of females. The females are diploid, having 32 chromosomes and males are haploid, i.e., having 16 chromosomes. This is called as haplodiploid sex-determination system and has special characteristic features, such as, the males produce sperms by mitosis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match the following columns and select the correct option
Column IColumn II
(a) Placenta(i) Androgens
(b) Zona pellucida(ii) Human Chorionic Gonadotropin (hCG)
(c) Bulbo-urethral glands(iii) Layer of the ovum
(d) Leydig cells(iv) Lubrication of the penis
options: a – iii; b – ii; c – iv; d - i
a – ii; b – iii; c – iv; d – i
a – iv; b – iii; c – i; d – ii
a – i; b – iv; c – ii; d – iii
questions.answer: Option (B): a – ii; b – iii; c – iv; d – i
questions.solution:
(a) Placenta also acts as an endocrine tissue and produces several hormones like human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG), human placental lactogen (hPL), estrogens, progestogens, etc.
(b) The secondary oocyte forms a new membrane called zona pellucida surrounding it.
(c) The male accessory glands include paired seminal vesicles, a prostate and paired bulbourethral glands. Secretions of these glands constitute the seminal plasma which is rich in fructose, calcium and certain enzymes. The secretions of bulbourethral glands also helps in the lubrication of the penis.
(d) The regions outside the seminiferous tubules called interstitial spaces, contain small blood vessels and interstitial cells or Leydig cells synthesise and secrete testicular hormones called androgens.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Several hormones like hCG, hPL, estrogen, progesterone are produced by
questions.solution: The placenta produces two steroid hormones, estrogen and progesterone along with a few proteinaceous hormones which include human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG), human placental lactogen (hPL), placental growth hormone, relaxin and kisspeptin. These hormones function to support pregnancy during the gestation period. So, the correct option is 'Placenta'.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Fertilization in human is practically feasible (possible) only if :
options: The sperms are transported into vagina just after the release of ovum in fallopian tube
The ovum and sperms are transported simultaneously to ampullary region of the fallopian tube
The ovum and sperms are transported simultaneously to ampullary-isthmic junction of the cervix
The sperms are transported into cervix within 48 hrs of release of ovum in uterus
questions.answer: Option (B): The ovum and sperms are transported simultaneously to ampullary region of the fallopian tube
questions.solution: The motile sperms swim rapidly, pass through the cervix, enter into the uterus and finally reach the ampullary region of the fallopian tube. The ovum released by the ovary is also transported to the ampullary region where fertilization takes place. Fertilization can only occur if the ovum and sperms are transported simultaneously to the ampullary region This is the reason why not all copulations lead to fertilization and pregnancy.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following hormone is not secreted by human placenta?
questions.solution: The placenta acts as a temporary endocrine gland during pregnancy, secreting several vital hormones. Several hormones produced by placenta are human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG), human placental lactogen (hPL), estrogen, progestogens, etc. Luteinizing hormone (LH) is secreted by anterior pituitary.

C. AcrosomeIII. Energy
D. TailIV. Genetic material

questions.solution: Head of the sperm contains the genetic material, DNA. Middle piece contains mitochondria, which is responsible for energy. Acrosome contains enzymes which help in dissolution of the membrane of the ovum, tail helps in providing motility to the sperm.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following depicts the CORRECT pathway of transport of sperms?
options: Rete testis → Epididymis → Efferent ductules → Vas deferens
Rete testis → Vas deferens → Efferent ductules → Epididymis
Efferent ductules → Rete testis → Vas deferens → Epididymis
Rete testis → Efferent ductules → Epididymis → Vas deferens
questions.answer: Option (D): Rete testis → Efferent ductules → Epididymis → Vas deferens
questions.solution:
In the male sex organ, accessory duct includes Rete testis, Vasa efferentia, Epididymis and Vas deferens. The sperm are produced in the Seminiferous tubules and Seminiferous tubules of the testis open into the Vasa efferentia through Rete testis and the Vasa efferentia leave the testis and open into epididymis located along the posterior surface of each testis and the epididymis leads to Vas deferens that ascends to the abdomen and loops over the urinary bladder and it receives a duct from seminal vesicle and opens into urethra as the ejaculatory duct. Hence, the correct pathway is:
Rete testis → Efferent ductules → Epididymis → Vas deferens

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In which of the following interactions both partners are adversely affected?
questions.solution:
Competition is a type of interaction in which both the partners are adversely affected by each other in search of food, shelter, and mate.Predation and Parasitism- In this, one organism gets the benefit and the other is harmed.

Mutualism- Both the organisms get the benefits.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Hormones secreted by the placenta to maintain pregnancy are
questions.solution: The placenta releases a human chorionic gonadotropic hormone (hCG) which stimulates the corpus luteum during pregnancy to release estrogen and progesterone and also rescues corpus luteum from regression. Human placental lactogen (hPL) is involved in the growth of the body of the mother and breast. Progesterone maintains pregnancy and helps in the development of the foetus, stimulates the growth of maternal breast tissue, prevents lactation, and strengthens the pelvic wall muscles for preparation of labour.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Ovulation is caused by LH surge leading to rupture of Graafian follicles.
Statement II: Graafian follicle remaining after ovulation transform into corpus luteum and secretes large amount of estrogen.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.answer: Option (B): Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
questions.solution: Rapid secretion of LH leading to its maximum level during the mid-cycle called LH surge induces rupture of Graafian follicle and thereby the release of ovum (ovulation). The remaining parts of the Graafian follicle transform as the corpus luteum, which secretes large amounts of progesterone.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Consider the following:
A. The reductive division for the human female gametogenesis starts earlier than that of the male gametogenesis.
B. The gap between the first meiotic division and the second meiotic division is much shorter for males compared to females.
C. The first polar body is associated with the formation of the primary oocyte.
D. Luteinizing Hormone (LH) surge leads to disintegration of the endometrium and onset of menstrual bleeding.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.answer: Option (C): A and B are true
questions.solution: Oogenesis starts before birth in females while spermatogenesis starts after puberty. In females, the first meiotic division occurs before birth, however is completed during each menstrual cycle followed by the second meiotic division which is again only completed after the entry of sperm but before fertilization. In males the first meiotic division is immediately followed by the second meiotic division.

questions.solution: In human females, meiosis II is not completed until fertilisation takes place when the ovum is released and the sperm cell contacts the plasma membrane of the oocyte.

questions.subject: Biology

questions.solution: In human male, urethra is the urinogenital duct which carries both urine and sperm. Hence, it is a shared terminal duct of the reproductive and urinary system in the human male.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.
Assertion A: Breast-feeding during initial period of infant growth is recommended by doctors for bringing a healthy baby.
Reason R: Colostrum Contains several antibodies absolutely essential to develop resistance for the new-born baby.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both A and R are correct, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is correct but R is not correct.
A is not correct but R is correct.
Both A and R are correct, and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.answer: Option (D): Both A and R are correct, and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.solution: The mammary glands of the female undergo differentiation during pregnancy and starts producing milk towards the end of pregnancy by the process called lactation. This helps the mother in feeding the newborn. The milk produced during the initial few days of lactation is called colostrum which contains several antibodies absolutely essential to develop resistance for the new-born babies. Breast-feeding during the initial period of infant growth is recommended by doctors for bringing up a healthy baby.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A container has two chambers of volumes ${V_1} = 2$ litres and ${V_2} = 3$ litres separated by a partition made of a thermal insulator. The chambers contains ${n_1} = 5$ and ${n_2} = 4$ moles of ideal gas at pressure ${p_1} = 1$ atm and ${p_2} = 2$atm, respectively. When the partition is removed, the mixture attains an equilibrium pressure of:
questions.solution:
${v_1} = 2Lt,{v_2} = 3Lt$
${n_1} = 5mol,{n_2} = 4mol$
${p_1} = 1atm,{p_2} = 2atm$
Chamber 1 ${P_1}{V_1} = {n_1}R{T_1}$
Chamber 2 ${P_2}{V_2} = {n_2}R{T_2}$
When partition is removed 
Gasses will mix without loss of energy 
From kinetic theory of gasses $PV = \frac{2}{3}n\left( {K.E} \right)$
For chamber 1 ${P_1}{V_2} = \frac{2}{2}{n_1}{E_1}$
For Chamber 2 ${P_2}{V_2} = \frac{2}{3}{n_2}{E_2}$
$\frac{3}{2}{P_1}{V_1} = {n_1}{E_1}$
$ \Rightarrow \left( {{n_1}{E_1} + {n_2}{E_2}} \right) = \frac{3}{2}\left( {{P_1}{V_1} + {P_2}{V_2}} \right)$
$\frac{3}{2}{P_2}{V_2} = {n_2}{E_2}$
We know $PV = \frac{2}{3}nE$
$P\left( {{V_1} + {V_2}} \right) = \left[ {{P_1}{V_1} + {P_2}{V_2}} \right]$
$P = \frac{{{P_1}{V_1} + {P_1}{V_2}}}{{{V_1} + {V_2}}} = \frac{{2 \times 1 + 2 \times 3}}{{2 + 3}}$
$P = \frac{{2 + 6}}{5} = \frac{8}{5} = 1.6$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: An ideal gas is made of polyatomic molecules. Each of the molecules has three translational, three rotational and $f$ number of vibrational modes. If the ratio of heat capacities $C_{P} / C_{V}$ of the gas is $8 / 7$, then the value of $f$ is:
questions.solution:
The total internal energy for one mole of gas, $U$
$$
\begin{aligned}
& =\left(\frac{3}{2} k_{B} T+\frac{3}{2} k_{B} T+f k_{B} T\right) N_{A} \\
& =(3+f) k_{B} T N_{A}=(3+f) R T \\
& \therefore \quad C_{V}=\frac{d U}{d T}=(3+f) R \\
& C_{P}=C_{V}+R=(4+f) R \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \frac{C_{P}}{C_{V}}=\frac{4+f}{3+f}=\frac{8}{7} \text { (given) } \\
& \Rightarrow \quad f=4
\end{aligned}
$$

\[\overrightarrow {{P_1}} + \overrightarrow {{P_2}} + \overrightarrow {{P_3}} = 0\]
Given that two of the masses of rock go off at right angles to each other.
Let \[\overrightarrow {{P_1}} \] and \[\overrightarrow {{P_2}} \] be the momentum of the rocks that go off at right angles to each other.
$${P_3} = \sqrt {{P_1}^2 + {P_2}^2} {\text{            }}(\because {V_1} \bot {V _2})$$
\[{m_3}{V _3} = \sqrt {{{({m_1}{V _1})}^2} + {{({m_2}{V _2})}^2}} \]
\[{m_3} \times 4 = \sqrt {{{(1)}^2} \times {{(12)}^2} + {{(2)}^2}{{(8)}^2}} \]
\[{m_3} \times 4 = 20\]
$$\therefore {m_3} = 5\,kg$$

Let the length of the plane inclined at angle θ be ‘2S’ and height be ‘h’. The work done is equal to the change in the kinetic energy which is equal to 0. Work done is equal to the work done by the gravitational force and by the frictional force. That is

\[\mu = \frac{h}{{S.\cos \theta }}\]………. (Equation 2)

questions.solution: Muscle contraction is initiated by a signal sent by the central nervous system (CNS) via a motor neuron. A motor neuron along with the muscle fibres connected to it constitute a motor unit. The junction between a motor neuron and the sarcolemma of the muscle fibre is called the neuromuscular junction or motor-end plate.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Lack of relaxation between successive stimuli in sustained muscle contraction is known as
questions.solution: Lack of relaxation between successive stimuli in sustained muscle contraction is known as tetanus. Tetanus is an acute, often-fatal disease of the nervous system that is caused by nerve toxins produced by the bacterium Clostridium tetani. The tetanus toxin amplifies the chemical signal from the nerve to the muscle, which causes the muscles to tighten up in a continuous ("tetanic" or "tonic") contraction or spasm. Tetanus often begins with mild spasms in the jaw muscles (lockjaw).

* 8th, 9th and 10th pairs of ribs do not articulate directly with the sternum but join the seventh ribs with the help of hyaline cartilage. These are vertebrochondral or false ribs.

* Only the first seven pairs of ribs are ventrally connected to the sternum.

questions.answer: Option (C): B, C and E only

(A) Incorrect : Human skull is dicondylic. The skull region articulates with the superior region of the vertebral column (Atlas) with the help of two occipital condyles.
(B) Correct : The joint present between the adjacent vertebrae of vertebral column is cartilaginous joints.

Calcium is the ion released into the sarcoplasm from sarcoplasmic reticulum during polarisation. Ca ion attaches to the Troponin-C. This brings a conformational change in the tropomyosin. As a result unmasking of active sites on actin for myosin takes place. Cross bridges are formed between actin and myosin. This results in muscle contraction.
Magnesium is used in phosphorylation reactions involving ATP.
Sodium and potassium help in maintaining the membrane potential.
So the correct option is d.

Statements A, B, D and E are correct while statement C is incorrect.
A neural signal reaching neuromuscular junction releases a neurotransmitter (Acetylcholine) which generates an action potential in the sarcolemma. This spreads through muscle fibre and causes the release of $\mathrm{Ca}^{++}$into the sarcoplasm. questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Calcium is important in skeletal muscle contraction because it
options: Activates the myosin ATPase by binding to it
Detaching the myosin head from the actin filament
Binds to troponin to remove the masking of active sites on actin for myosin
Prevents the formation of bonds between the myosin cross-bridges and the actin filament
questions.answer: Option (C): Binds to troponin to remove the masking of active sites on actin for myosin
questions.solution: During muscular contraction, the level of calcium ions gets increased in the sarcoplasm. Increased level of Ca++ now binds with a subunit of troponin (troponin “C”) which is masking the active site on actin filament and displaces the subunit of troponin. Once the active site is exposed, the head of the myosin attaches and initiates contraction by sliding the actin over the myosin.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
During the muscular contraction which of the following events occur?
(a) ‘H’ zone disappears
(b) ‘A’ band widens
(c) ‘I’ band reduces in width
(d) Myosin hydrolyzes ATP, releasing the ADP and Pi.
(e) Z-lines attached to actins are pulled inwards
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: (b), (c), (d), (e) only
(b), (d), (e), (a) only
(a), (c), (d), (e) only
(a), (b), (c), (d) only
questions.solution: The correct option is (c) because the length of the A-band is retained. During muscle contraction, the following events occur: (1) The globular head of myosin acts as ATPase and hydrolyses ATP molecule and eventually leads to the formation of cross-bridge. (2) This pulls the actin filament towards the center of the 'A-band'. (3) The Z-line attached to these actins are also pulled inwards thereby causing a shortening of the sarcomere. (4) The thin myofilaments move past the thick myofilaments due to which the H-zone narrows. This reduces the length of the I-band but retains the length of the A-band. (5) The myosin then releases ADP+Pi and goes back to its relaxed state.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is present between the adjacent bones of the vertebral column?
questions.solution: White fibrous cartilage is present between vertebrae to allow limited movement. This ensures proper structural rigidity and body balance and yet, allows for limited movement required.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following can be used as a biocontrol agent in the treatment of plant disease?
questions.solution: The natural method of eliminating and controlling the insects, pests and other disease-causing agents using their natural, biological enemies is called biocontrol or biological control. Fungus Trichoderma is a biological control agent being developed for use in the treatment of plant diseases.

questions.subject: Biology

questions.answer: Option (B): Removing clots from blood vessels

questions.subject: Biology

questions.solution: Streptokinase produced by the bacterium Streptococcus and modified by genetic engineering is used as a 'clot-buster' for removing clots from the blood vessels of patients who have undergone myocardial infarction.

The production of large amount of $\mathrm{CO}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{H}_{2}$ by Trichoderma polysporum
The production of large amount of $\mathrm{CO}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{H}_{2}$ by lactic acid bacteria called Lactobacillus

questions.solution: Cyclosporin is an effective immunosuppressant used in the treatment of autoimmune disorders (such as rheumatoid arthritis) and in organ transplantation to prevent rejection. questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Mycorrhizae are the example of
questions.solution: Mycorrhizae is a mutualistic association of fungi with roots of higher plants. Mutualism can be defined as the association in which both the involved organisms are benefited. In a mycorrhizal association, the fungi colonize the root system of the host plant providing increased water and mineral absorption capabilities. While the plant provides the fungus with carbohydrates formed from photosynthesis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In which of the following forms is iron absorbed by plants?
questions.solution: Iron is absorbed by plants in the form of ferric ions. However, plants in the acidic soil can absorb iron in ferrous (Fe2+) as well as ferric (Fe3+) form. Hence, ferric is the correct option. It is an important constituent of proteins involved in the transfer of electrons like ferredoxin and cytochromes.

questions.subject: Biology

questions.solution: Rhodospirillum is a facultative anaerobe, free-living nitrogen fixer. It is a nitrogen fixer that helps in the conversion of atmospheric nitrogen to ammonia. It is not associated with the roots of the vascular plant as mycorrhiza. Mycorrhiza is a symbiotic relationship between fungi and roots of higher plants.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The ﬁrst stable product of ﬁxation of atmospheric nitrogen in leguminous plants is
questions.solution: The ﬁrst stable product of atmospheric nitrogen ﬁxation in the root nodules of leguminous plants by Rhizobium is ammonia.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Deficiency symptoms of nitrogen and potassium are visible first in
questions.solution: The deficiency of potassium in plants is first visible in the leaves. They start turning yellow and brown scorches are also seen. Similarly, the first symptoms of nitrogen deficiency in plants are also observed in the yellowing of leaves. This is because plants are unable to make enough chlorophyll and hence start appearing pale green or yellow. The deficiency symptoms of nitrogen and potassium are characteristically seen in the old and senescent leaves of the plants. This is because plants generally move the nutrients from older parts to the younger leaves and hence deficiency symptoms are seen in senescent leaves first.

questions.subject: Biology

questions.solution: Mg++ is an activator for both ribulose bisphosphate carboxylase-oxygenase and phosphoenolpyruvate carboxylase, both of which are enzymes involved in the carbon fixation process of photosynthesis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following elements is responsible for maintaining turgor in cells?
questions.solution: Potassium is required for the maintenance of the turgidity of guard cells. In the guard cells, starch is converted into malic acid in the presence of light (during daytime). Protons formed are used by the guard cells for the uptake of K+ ions. In this way, the concentration of K+ ions increases in guard cells. The potassium combines with malate to form potassium malate.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In which of the following, all three are macronutrients?
questions.solution: In relatively large amounts, the soil supplies nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, calcium, magnesium, and sulfur; these are often called the macronutrients. In relatively small amounts, the soil supplies iron, manganese, boron, molybdenum, copper, zinc, chlorine, and cobalt, the so-called micronutrients. Nutrients must be available not only in sufficient amounts but also in appropriate ratios.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is required as inducer(s) for the expression of Lac operon?
questions.solution: The lac z, lac y, and lac a genes in lac operon are the structural genes that code for beta-galactosidase (converts lactose into glucose and galactose), beta-galactoside permease (transports lactose into the cell) and beta-galactoside transacetylase respectively. In the presence of lactose, allolactose; an isomer of lactose, binds to the repressor and causes an allosteric shift. The altered repressor cannot bind to the operator, allowing RNA polymerase to transcribe the lac genes. Thus lactose is required for expression of the lac operon.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The equivalent of a structural gene is
questions.solution: Structural genes are the continuous stretch of DNA that regulates a particular genetic trait. A cistron is defined as a unit of function that exhibits cis-trans test and is synonymous with the gene. Muton is the smallest unit in a chromosome that can be changed by mutations. The smallest unit capable of undergoing recombination is called recon. A cistron has multiple recons and mutons. An operon is a functioning unit of DNA containing a cluster of genes under the control of a single promoter. Therefore, the correct answer is option a.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: In the RNA world, RNA is considered the first genetic material evolved to carry out essential life processes, RNA acts as a genetic material and also as a catalyst for some important biochemical reactions in living systems. Being reactive, RNA is unstable.
Statement II: DNA evolved from RNA and is a more stable genetic material. Its double helical strands being complementary, resist changes by evolving repairing mechanism.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct
Both statement I and statement II are correct
Both statement I and statement II are incorrect
questions.answer: Option (C): Both statement I and statement II are correct
questions.solution: The first statement correctly explains RNA being the first genetic material as well as being unstable due to its single stranded nature. The second statement is correct as well as DNA evolved from RNA as a more stable double stranded genetic material.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following RNAs should be most abundant in animal cells?
questions.solution: Ribosomal RNA or rRNA is most abundant in animal cells. It constitutes 80% of the total RNA of the cell. It provides the site for protein synthesis. The rRNA is single-stranded and shows the presence of intra-chain hydrogen bonds.

This rRNA also serves as a structural component for a large subunit of bacterial ribosome. Therefore, the correct answer is option b.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: If the distance between two consecutive base pairs is 0.34 nm and the total number of base  pairs  of  a  DNA  double  helix  in  a  typical mammalian  cell is 6.6 × 10<sup>9</sup><sub> </sub>bp, then the length of the DNA is approximately.
questions.solution: A diploid cell of human genome contain 6.6 × 109 base pairs. The distance between two consecutive base pairs is 0.34 nm (0.34 × 10-9m), so the length of DNA double helix in a typical mammalian cell is around 6.6 × 109 bp × 0.34 × 10-9 m/bp = 2.2 metres.

questions.solution: RNA polymerase holoenzyme binds to the promoter, unwinds DNA (open complex) and forms phosphodiester bonds between the incoming nucleotides. DNA polymerase, DNA ligase & DNA helicase are involved in the process of replication and not in transcription.

questions.solution:
Nonsense mutation is a point mutation that results in a premature stop codon that terminates transcription.

questions.subject: Biology

options: DNA dependent DNA polymerase

questions.solution: In prokaryotes, the DNA-dependent RNA polymerase is a holoenzyme that is made of polypeptides. It is responsible for initiation, elongation, and termination during transcription. DNase degrades DNA. DNA-dependent DNA polymerase is involved in the replication of DNA. DNA ligase joins the discontinuously synthesized fragments of DNA.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: If the length of a DNA molecule is 1.1 metres, what will be the approximate number of base pairs?
questions.solution:
The length between two base pairs is 0.34nm.
Total length of double helix DNA = total number of base pairs * distance between two bp
Hence, total no. of base pairs = 
(Total length of double helix DNA) / (distance between two bp)
1.1m/0.34 nm
= (1.1 x 109 nm) / (0.34 nm)
= 3.235 x 109 base pairs
= 3.3 x 109 base pairs

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following is not applicable to RNA?
questions.solution: Chargaff's rule states that in the double-stranded DNA of an organism, the amount of adenine (A) is equal to that of thymine (T) and the amount of guanine (G) is equal to that of cytosine (C). Hence, Chargaff's rule is not applicable to RNA as it is single-stranded and this rule is applicable on double-stranded DNA molecules.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Transformation was discovered by:
questions.solution: Transformation is the genetic alteration of a cell resulting from the direct uptake and incorporation of exogenous genetic material from its surroundings and taken up through the cell membrane. Transformation was first demonstrated in 1928 by British bacteriologist Frederick Griffith.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A complex of ribosome attached to a single strand of RNA is known as
questions.solution: Large clusters of 10 to 100 ribosomes, actively translating protein synthesis are called polysomes. The ribosomes in a polysome are connected by a single molecule of mRNA that is being translated simultaneously by many closely spaced ribosomes. Polymers are large molecules composed of many monomer units. Polypeptide is a large linear polymer of amino acids bonded together by peptide linkage. questions.question: If Adenine makes 30% of the DNA molecule, what will be the percentage of Thymine, Guanine, and Cytosine in it?
options: T: 30; G: 20; C: 20
T: 20; G: 25; C: 25
T: 20; G: 30; C: 20
T: 20; G: 20; C: 30
questions.solution:
Erwin Chargaff proposed three rules which are termed Chargaff's rules. These rules played an important role in the discovery of the double-helix structure of DNA, they are
1. In any double-stranded DNA, the number of guanine units equals the number of cytosine units whereas the number of adenine units equals the number of thymine units (i.e no of A = no of T and no of C = no of G and vice versa ).
2. The sum of purines (A and G) equals that of pyrimidines (C and T). The composition of DNA varies from one species to another.
According to the question, the percentage of adenine is 30. Thus, the percentage of thymine will be 30 as per the first rule. The sum of A and T would be 60 %. The remaining % of bases is 40% which has to be divided equally between G and C since no of G= no of C. Thus G=C=20%.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In an E. coli strain the i gene gets mutated and its product can not bind the inducer molecule. If the growth medium is provided with lactose, what will be the outcome?
options: Only z gene will get transcribed
z, y, a genes will be transcribed
z, y, a genes will not be translated
RNA polymerase will bind the promoter region
questions.answer: Option (C): z, y, a genes will not be translated
questions.solution:
The i gene codes for the repressor of the lac operon. An inducer (allolactose or an analog) binds to the repressor and prevents its binding to the operator, thereby releasing the repression and allowing transcription of the lac operon. 
If the i gene is mutated in such a way that the repressor molecule is unable to bind with the inducer, the repressor which is now free from the inducer will now bind to the operator sequence. This will prevent the binding of RNA polymerase on the promoter sequence. Lactose in the medium, which is the inducer, cannot bind to the repressor because of the mutation.
Thus if the operator is blocked by the repressor, there will be no transcription and the structural genes z, y and a will not get transcribed and translated.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Ten E. coli cells with 15N- dsDNA are incubated in a medium containing 14N nucleotides. After 60 minutes, how many E. coli cells will have DNA totally free from 15N?
questions.solution:
The bacterium Escherichia coli can divide every 20 minutes. Therefore, in 60 minutes, 3 rounds of divisions will take place. 

First round of division:
20 daughter cells are formed from the 10 parent E. coli cells. All 20 cells have hybrid 15N-14N DNA.

Second round of division: 
Each DNA forms two daughter cells, one of which is a hybrid and the other is completely 14N-14N. Therefore, 20 cells form 40 daughter DNA molecules, out of which 20 are hybrids and 20 are free from 15N.

Third round of division: 
20 14N-14N cells from the previous generation give rise to 40 14N-14N cells
20 hybrid cells from the previous generation give rise to 20 hybrids + 20 14N-14N cells. 

Therefore, the total number of 14N-14N cells at the end of 3 rounds of division is 40+20 = 60.

questions.question: When the margins of sepals or petals overlap one another without any particular direction, the condition is termed as
questions.solution: Aestivation refers to the arrangement of the petals or sepals in a flower. When the margins of the sepals or petals overlap one another without any particular direction, it is called imbricate. Example Cassia. When the margins of the sepals or petals overlap one another regularly in a particular direction, it is called twisted, for example, China rose. When the margins of the sepals or petals do not overlap one another, it is called valvate, for example, Calotropis. When the petals are of different sizes and show a descending imbricate pattern, it is called vexillary, for example, pea.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The term ‘polyadelphous’ is related to
questions.solution:
If filaments of androecium are joined together to form more than two groups but their anthers are separated, it is called polyadelphous condition. E.g. Citrus
Therefore, the correct answer is option A.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The standard petal of a papilionaceous corolla is also called
questions.solution: Papilionaceous flowers are flowers with the characteristic irregular and butterfly-like corolla. The flowers have a bilateral symmetry with the corolla consisting of five petals. The largest known as vaxillum overlaps the two lateral petals (wings) which in turn overlap the two smallest anterior petals (keel); this type of aestivation is known as vexillary or papilionaceous.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Among mustard, brinjal, china rose, lupin, cucumber, sunn hemp, gram, guava, bean, chilli, plum, Petunia, tomato, rose, Ashwagandha, potato, aloe, and tulip, how many plants have hypogynous flowers?
questions.solution:
The plants with hypogynous flowers among the given options are:
Mustard

Brinjal

China rose

Lupin

Tomato

Rose

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Proximal end of the filament of stamen is attached to the
questions.solution: Thalamus is the basal thickened part of the stem to which all floral appendages are found attached. Petals are the colored structural unit of the corolla. The placenta is the region of the wall of the ovary to which ovules are found attached. A stamen consists of anther and filament. Anther is a broad knob part of the stamen that contains two long and cylindrical microsporangia in its lobes. The proximal ends of the filament are found attached to thalamus or petals while the distal end carries anther.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List I with List II :
List I (Placentation)List II (Example)
A.MarginalI.Mustard
B.AxileII.Pea
C.ParietalIII.Marigold
D.BasalIV.Lemon

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution: Marginal placentation is found in pea, axile placentation is found in lemon, parietal placentation is found in mustard and basal placentation is found in marigold.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The morphological nature of the edible part of the coconut is
questions.solution: The edible part of the coconut is the endosperm. The endosperm is the nutritive tissue that helps in the development of the embryo in angiosperms. Coconut has double endosperm with liquid nuclear endosperm and cellular endosperm. In mature coconut, the liquid endosperm becomes milky and is enclosed by the kernel.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Placenta and pericarp are both edible portions in:
questions.solution: The edible parts of tomato are the placenta and pericarp. Placenta is the connecting tissue which supplies nutrition to the embryo and pericarp is the remains of the ovular wall.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Non-albuminous seed is produced in
questions.solution: Non-albuminous seeds are seeds which have no residual endosperm as it is completely consumed during embryo development. Non-albuminous seed is produced in pea.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: An aggregate fruit is the one which develops from
questions.solution: When more than one carpel is present, they may be free and are called apocarpous. An aggregate fruit develops from multicarpellary apocarpous gynoecium and each ripened is called fruitlet or etaerio. The example is raspberry.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Ray florets have
questions.solution: Flower of compositae family contains two types of flower i.e., ray florets (located at peripheral) and disc florets (located at centre). Ray florets have inferior ovary and the reason is that the other parts of the flower are attached above the level of ovary. Example of such an ovary is ray florets of Sunflowers.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a zygomorphic flower?
questions.solution: Zygomorphic flowers are Pea, Beans, Cassia etc., Chilli, Petunia, Datura are all actinomorphic flowers.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Pneumatophores occur in
questions.solution: Halophytes like mangroves contain pneumatophores or respiratory roots. It is a modified tap root that emerges from the soil and absorbs oxygen from the air due to the unavailability of oxygen in the soil. It is an apogeotropic (-vely geotropic) root having lenticels called pneumathodes to uptake O2.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Radial symmetry is found in the flowers of
questions.solution: A flower which can be divided into two equal vertical halves by any vertical plane is said to be actinomorphic, e.g.: Datura, chilli, mustard. The bilaterally symmetrical flowers which are symmetrical in only one plane and can be cut into two equal halves through a single vertical plane only are said to be zygomorphic, e.g. Gulmohur and Cassia. Canna has asymmetric flowers.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Phyllotaxy is the pattern of arrangement of
questions.solution: Phyllotaxy is the pattern of arrangement of leaves on the stem.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In China rose the ﬂowers are
questions.answer: Option (A): Actinomorphic, hypogynous with twisted aestivation
questions.solution: China rose belongs to Family Malvaceae; ﬂowers of plants belonging to this family are actinomorphic showing radial symmetry, hypogynous ovary and with twisted aestivation of petals.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is not a stem modification?
questions.solution: The pitcher of Nepenthes is the modification of leaf lamina which takes the form of pitcher to trap insects. Thorns of citrus are modified stems which performs the function of climbing or defense. Thorns are present in the axil of leaves or apex of the stem. A tendril of cucumber is a modified stem which is formed by the modification of terminal bud into tendril because the stem is often weak in such plants. Flattened structure of Opuntia is also a stem modification.

Assertion A: A flower is defined as modified shoot wherein the shoot apical meristem changes to floral meristem.
Reason R: Internode of the shoot gets condensed to produce different floral appendages laterally at successive nodes instead of leaves.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

questions.solution: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Which of the following are characteristic features of Solanaceae family?
(a) Flowers are bisexual and actinomorphic
(b) Calyx have five sepals and are united
(c) Androecium have five stamens and are epipetalous
(d) Ovary is inferior
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: In Solanaceae family, flowers are bisexual and actinomorphic. Calyx include five sepals that are united. Androecium include five stamens and it is epipetalous. Ovary is superior.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Identify the correct set of statements:
(a) The leaflets are modified into pointed hard thorns in Citrus and Bougainvillea
(b) Axillary buds form slender and spirally coiled tendrils in cucumber and pumpkin
(c) Stem is flattened and fleshy on Opuntia and modified to perform the function of leaves
(d) Rhizophora shows vertically upward growing roots that help to get oxygen for respiration
(e) Subaerially growing stems in grasses and strawberry help in vegetative propagation
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
• Axillary buds of stems may also get modified into woody, straight and pointed thorns. Thorns are found in many plants such as Citrus and Bougainvillea. 
• Stem tendrils which develop from axillary buds, are slender and spirally coiled and help plants to climb such as in cucumber, pumpkins and watermelon etc. 
• Some plants of arid regions modify their stems into flattened structures such as Opuntia. They contain chlorophyll and carry out functions such as photosynthesis. 
• Rhizophora grows in swampy areas and many of their roots come out of the ground and grow vertically upwards. Such roots, also known as pneumatophores, help to get oxygen for respiration. 
• Underground stems of grass and strawberry, etc., spread to new niches and when older parts die new plants are formed (vegetative propagation).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Root hairs develop from the region of
questions.solution: Root has three prominent regions, i.e., a zone of cell division, a zone of elongation, and a zone of maturation and differentiation. In roots, the root hairs arise from the zone of maturation. This zone is a differentiated zone thus bearing root hairs.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The ovary is half inferior in _____.
questions.solution: Plum/peach belongs to the family Rosaceae and it shows half-inferior ovary. So the flowers are perigynous. Sunflowers have inferior ovary. Brinjal (Solanaceae) has a superior ovary. Mustards have superior ovaries.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The roots that originate from the base of the stem are
questions.solution: Roots that originate from the base of stem constitute the fibrous root system as seen in the monocots example is wheat plant.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Tricarpellary, syncarpous gynoecium is found in flowers of:
questions.solution: According to number of carpels, gynoecium is monocarpellary, bicarpellary, tricarpellary and multicarpellary. Ovary with united carpels is called a syncarpous ovary while that with distinct carpels is an apocarpous ovary. Solanaceae have bicarpellary, syncarpous, bilocular or tetralocular gynoecium with superior and obliquely placed ovary. Liliaceae have tricarpellary, syncarpous, trilocular gynoecium. Fabaceae has monocarpellary gynoecium.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: How many plants among Indigofera, Sesbania, Salvia, Allium, Aloe, mustard, groundnut, radish, gram and turnip have stamens with different lengths in their flowers?
questions.solution:
Families of the given plants :
Indigofera: Fabaceae 
Sesbania: Fabaceae
Salvia: Lamiaceae
Allium: Liliaceae
Aloe: Liliaceae 
Mustard: Brassicaceae
Groundnut: Fabaceae
Radish: Brassicaceae
Gram: Fabaceae
Turnip: Brassicaceae
The family having different length stamens in their flower is Brassicaceae and Lamiaceae. We are provided with four plants belonging to the above two mentioned families. So, Salvia (didynamous), mustard, radish and turnip (tetradynamous) will have an unequal length of stamens.
So, the correct answer is 'Four'.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Among china rose, mustard, brinjal, potato, guava, cucumber, petunia, and tulip, how many plants have a superior ovary?
questions.solution:
A superior ovary is an ovary attached to the receptacle above the attachment of other floral parts. 

Among china rose, mustard, brinjal, potato, guava, cucumber, petunia, and tulip 

have superior ovaries. Only guava and cucumber have inferior ovaries.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Perisperm diﬀers from endosperm in
options: Its formation by fusion of secondary nucleus with several sperms
questions.solution: The perisperm is the remains of the nucellus within the seed and is a diploid structure.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In Bougainvillea thorns are the modifications of
questions.solution: Stems sometimes get modified to perform some specialised functions. Thorns are hard, pointed straight structures for protection. The axillary bud of the stem is modified into thorns in Bougainvillea to protect them from their enemies.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
The flowers are Zygomorphic in:
(a) Mustard
(b) Gulmohar
(c) Cassia
(d) Datura
(e) Chilli
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Zygomorphic flowers are those which are only divided into two halves from one plane (bilaterally symmetrical). It includes pea, Gulmohar, Cassia, and beans.
Mustard, datura, and chilli are actinomorphic flowers as they can be divided into two halves from any plane (radially symmetrical) .

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Sweet potato is a modified
questions.solution:
Sweet potatoes (Ipomoea batatas) are modified adventitious roots. They are swollen and contain high amounts of starch. Other examples of modified adventitious roots include cassava, dahlia. Thus, the correct answer is option b.
A rhizome is a food storing underground modified stems.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following statements is correct?
options: A proteinaceous aleurone layer is present in maize grain
A sterile pistil is called a staminode
The seed in grasses is not endospermic
questions.answer: Option (B): A proteinaceous aleurone layer is present in maize grain
questions.solution: Mango is a seeded fruit. A sterile stamen is called a staminode. The seed in grasses is endospermic. However, in maize grain, the endosperm is surrounded by a proteinaceous aleurone layer.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Cotyledon of maize grain is called:
questions.solution: The embryo in maize grain consists of a single cotyledon called scutellum, a radicle and a plumule. The radicle lies towards the pointed side of the embryonic region of the seed. IT is covered by a protective sheath called coleorhiza. The plumule is located towards the upper side of the embryonic region opposite to radicle. It is also enclosed in a protective sheath known as coleoptile.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The coconut water from tender coconut represents :
questions.solution: The coconut water from tender coconut represents the free nuclear or liquid endosperm. During the development of nuclear type of endosperm, the primary endosperm mother cell divides by free nuclear divisions, and these divisions are not followed by cell wall formation. Thus, the free nuclei remain in the cytoplasm of the embryo sac.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Stems modified into flat green organs performing the functions of leaves are known as
questions.solution: Phylloclades is a flattened, photosynthetic branch or stem that resembles or performs the function of a leaf.

questions.question: An electron (mass $9 \times {10^{ - 31}}kg$ and charge $1.6 \times {10^{ - 19}}C$) moving with speed c/100 (c = speed of light) is injected into a magnetic field $\vec B$ of magnitude $9 \times {10^{ - 4}}T$perpendicular to its direction of motion. We wish to apply an uniform electric $\vec E$ together with the magnetic field so that the electron does not deflect from its path. Then (Speed of light $c = 3 \times {10^8}m{s^{ - 1}}$)
options: $\vec E$ is parallel to $\vec B$ and its magnitude is $27 \times {10^2}V{m^{ - 1}}$
$\vec E$ is parallel to $\vec B$ and its magnitude is $27 \times {10^4}V{m^{ - 1}}$
$\vec E$ is perpendicular to $\vec B$ and its magnitude is $27 \times {10^4}V{m^{ - 1}}$
$\vec E$ is perpendicular to $\vec B$ and its magnitude is $27 \times {10^2}V{m^{ - 1}}$
questions.answer: Option (D): $\vec E$ is perpendicular to $\vec B$ and its magnitude is $27 \times {10^2}V{m^{ - 1}}$
questions.solution:
V = velocity ${e^ - }$
$v = \frac{c}{{100}}$
$B = 9 \times {10^{ - 4}}T$ 
${F_B} = $ Force due to magnetic field 
${F_E} = $Force due to $\vec E$
${F_B} = {F_E}$
$qvB = qE$
$ \Rightarrow E = vB$
$ = \frac{c}{{100}} \times 9 \times {10^{ - 4}}$
$ = \frac{{3 \times {{10}^8}}}{{{{10}^2}}} \times 9 \times {10^{ - 4}}$
$ = 27 \times {10^6} \times {10^{ - 4}}$
$ = 27 \times {10^2}$
$ \to $direction should be perpendicular to $\vec B$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: When a proton (mass m) is released from rest in a room, it starts with an initial acceleration \[{a_0}\] towards west. When it is projected towards north with a speed \[{\nu _0}\] it moves with an initial acceleration \[3{a_0}\] toward west. The electric and magnetic fields in the room are
questions.solution:
Acceleration of charged particle, \[\vec a = \frac{{\left( {q\vec E + \vec v \times \vec B} \right)}}{m}\]
When released from rest, \[\vec a = {{\vec a}_0} = \frac{{e\vec E}}{m}\], so \[\vec E = \frac{{m{{\vec a}_0}}}{e},\,\,\vec E \propto {{\vec a}_0}\] (for positive charge)
Magnetic force $$ = {\text{ }}{F_m}\; = {\text{ }}3m{a_0}\;-{\text{ }}m{a_0}\; = {\text{ }}2m{a_0}$$ (in the west direction). \[\overrightarrow v \times \overrightarrow B \] is directed towards the west.
For positive charge,\[\overrightarrow v \] is directed towards the North and \[\overrightarrow B \] is directed vertically down.
\[\overrightarrow {{F_m}} = q\overrightarrow v \times \overrightarrow B \]
\[\therefore \,\,2m{\vec a_0}\; = \;e{\vec v_0}\; \times \;\vec B\]
\[B = \frac{{2m{a_0}}}{{e{v_0}}}\](in vertically downward direction)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A model for quantized motion of an electron in a uniform magnetic field B states that the flux passing through the orbit of the electron is $n\left( {\frac{h}{e}} \right)$ where n is an integer, $h$ is Planck’s constant and e is the magnitude of electron’s charge. According to the model, the magnetic moment of an electron in its lowest energy state will be (m is the mass of the eletron)
questions.solution:
$\boxed{\phi = \frac{{nh}}{e}}$
Given but $\phi = BA$
$\therefore \frac{\phi }{B} = A$
$\therefore A = \frac{\phi }{B} = \frac{{nh}}{{eB}}$
For n = 1 (lowest energy given)
$A = \frac{h}{{eB}}$
$\pi {r^2} = \frac{h}{{eB}}$
${r^2} = \frac{h}{{\pi eB}}$
We know, magnetic moment $\mu = \frac{{evr}}{2}$
We need velocity.
Centripetal force = Magnetic force 
$\frac{{m{v^2}}}{r} = evB$
$\mu = \frac{{eBr}}{m}$
$\therefore \mu = \frac{{evr}}{2}$
$ = \frac{e}{2}\frac{{eBr}}{m}r$
$ = \frac{{{e^2}B}}{{2m}}{r^2} = \frac{{{e^2}B}}{{2m}}\frac{h}{{\pi eB}}$
= $\frac{{he}}{{2\pi m}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A current carrying  loop in a magnetic field
options: Experiences a torque whether the field is uniform or non uniform in all orientations
Can be in equilibrium in one orientation
Can be in equilibrium in two orientations, both the equilibrium states are unstable
Can be in equilibrium in two orientations, one stable while the other is unstable
questions.answer: Option (D): Can be in equilibrium in two orientations, one stable while the other is unstable
questions.solution:
When a current loop is placed in a magnetic field it experiences a torque. It is given by
$\vec \tau = \vec M \times \vec B$ 
Where, vector M is the magnetic moment of the loop and vector B is the magnetic field.
Or $\tau = MB\sin \theta $ where $\theta $ is angle between $$\vec M$$ and $$\vec B$$ when vector M and vector B are parallel (i.e. $\theta = 0^\circ $) the equilibrium is stable and when they are antiparallel (i.e. $\theta = \pi $ ) the equilibrium is unstable.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two infinitely long parallel conducting wires $A$ and $B$ carry currents $I$ and $2 I$, respectively, in the same direction. The wire $A$ has uniform mass per unit length $\lambda$ and lies on an insulated floor. The wire $B$ is kept fixed at a height $h$ above the floor. The minimum magnitude of $h$ so that the wire $A$ does not rise from the floor is: [ $g$ is the acceleration due to gravity and $\mu_{0}$ is the permeability of free space.]
questions.solution:
Force per unit length on wire $A$ by wire $B$
$F=\frac{\mu_{0}}{4 \pi} \frac{2 l \cdot 2 l}{h}=\frac{\mu_{0}}{4 \pi} \frac{4 l^{2}}{h} l$
If $F_{n e t} \leq m g$, weight of wire $A$, then wire does not rise from the floor.
So, $F \leq m g$,
$\frac{\mu_{0}}{4 \pi} \frac{4 l^{2}}{h} \leq \lambda g$
$\therefore h \geq \frac{\mu_{0} l^{2}}{\pi \lambda g}$

questions.solution:
$\overrightarrow v  = 2\widehat i + 4\widehat j + 6\widehat k$
$\overrightarrow F  = 4\widehat i - 20\widehat j + 12\widehat k$

$ = \widehat i\left[ {4{B_0} - 6B} \right] - \widehat j\left[ {2{B_0} - 6B} \right] + \widehat k\left[ {2B - 4B} \right]$

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : The cerebral hemispheres are connected by nerve tract known as corpus callosum.
Statement II : The brain stem consists of the medulla oblongata, pons and cerebrum.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is Correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
questions.answer: Option (B): Statement I is Correct but Statement II is incorrect.
questions.solution:
Cerebrum forms the major part of the human brain. A deep cleft divides the cerebrum longitudinally into two halves, which are termed as the left and right cerebral hemispheres. The hemispheres are connected by a tract of nerve fibres called corpus callosum.
Three major regions make up the brainstem; midbrain, pons and medulla oblongata.

Cornea is convex, transparent layer which is highly vascularised
Cornea consists of a dense matrix of collagen and is the most sensitive portion of the eye

questions.answer: Option (C): Cornea consists of a dense matrix of collagen and is the most sensitive portion of the eye
questions.solution: Cornea consists of a dense matrix of collagen and corneal epithelium. It is the most sensitive part of the eye. The cornea's main function is to refract, or bend, light, so the light can meet and form an image of the object on the retina.

Column IColumn II

(b) Cochlea(ii) Coiled part of the labyrinth
(c) Eustachian tube(iii) Attached to the oval window
(d) Stapes(iv) Located on the basilar membrane

a – i; b – ii; c – iv; d - iii
a – ii; b – iii; c – i; d - iv
a – iii; b – i; c – iv; d - ii
questions.answer: Option (A): a – iv; b – ii; c – i; d - iii
questions.solution:

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Choose the CORRECT statement
options: Photoreceptors in the human eye are depolarized during darkness and become hyperpolarized in response to the light stimulus
Receptors do not produce graded potentials
Nociceptors respond to changes in pressure
questions.answer: Option (B): Photoreceptors in the human eye are depolarized during darkness and become hyperpolarized in response to the light stimulus
questions.solution: Photoreceptors in the human eye are depolarized during darkness and become hyperpolarized in response to the light stimulus. Meissner’s corpuscles are mechanoreceptors for touch sensitivity in skin. Taste cells and photoreceptors can produce graded potential. Nociceptors are pain receptors which produce threat response to stimuli like heat or chemicals.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Photosensitive compound in human eye is made up of
questions.solution: The photosensitive compound present in vision is called rhodopsin, also known as visual purple which consists of a large protein called opsin and retinal. Opsins are a group of light-sensitive proteins found in photoreceptor cells of the retina. Five classical groups of opsins are involved in vision, mediating the conversion of a photon of light into an electrochemical signal, the first step in the visual transduction cascade. Retinal allows certain microorganisms to convert light into metabolic energy.

questions.solution: The limbic system consists of a number of structures, including the fornix, hippocampus, cingulate gyrus, amygdala, parahippocampal gyrus, and parts of the thalamus. It deals with emotions and memory. It regulates autonomic or endocrine function in response to emotional stimuli and is also involved in reinforcing behaviour.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question:
Consider the following nuclear reaction
$$
{ }^{238} \mathrm{U} \longrightarrow{ }^{234} \mathrm{Th}+{ }^{4} \mathrm{He}
$$
Take masses of ${ }^{238} \mathrm{U},{ }^{234} \mathrm{Th}$ and ${ }^{4} \mathrm{He}$ as $238.050 \mathrm{u}, 234.043 \mathrm{u}$ and 4.003 u , respectively. The $Q$ value for the reaction, in keV , is:
[Given: $1 \mathrm{u}=931.5 \mathrm{MeV} \mathrm{c}^{-2}$ ]
questions.solution:
$Q$-value for the nuclear reaction is given by, $Q=\Delta m c^{2}$
${ }^{238} \mathrm{U} \longrightarrow{ }^{234} \mathrm{Th}+{ }^{4} \mathrm{He}$ has mass defect $\Delta m=m_{\text {reactants }}-m_{\text {products }}$
$\Rightarrow \quad \Delta m=238.050-(234.043+4.003)=0.004 \mathrm{u}$
$\therefore \quad Q=0.004 \times 931.5 \mathrm{MeV}=3.726 \mathrm{MeV}=3726 \mathrm{keV}$

${\left( {\frac{1}{2}} \right)^2} = {\left( {\frac{1}{2}} \right)^{\frac{t}{{{t_{1/2}}}}}}$
$t = 2{t_{1/2}} = 2 \times 10$
= 20 minutes

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question:
Four statements are given ( $A$ is mass number):
A. The volume of a nucleus is proportional to $A^{1 / 3}$.
B. The volume of a nucleus is proportional to $A$.
C. The difference in mass of an atom and its nucleus is called the mass defect.
D. The difference in mass of a nucleus and its constituents is called the mass defect.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: B and D are true, but A and C are false
$A$ and $D$ are true, but $B$ and $C$ are false
$A$ and $C$ are true, but $B$ and $D$ are false
B and C are true, but A and D are false
questions.answer: Option (A): B and D are true, but A and C are false
questions.solution:
As we know,
Size of nucleus, $r=r_{0}(A)^{\frac{1}{3}}$
$\Rightarrow \quad r^{3}=r_{0}^{3} \cdot A$
$\Rightarrow \quad V \propto A \quad\left(\because V=\frac{4}{3} \pi r^{3}\right)$
So, option $\mathrm{A} \rightarrow$ wrong and $\mathrm{B} \rightarrow$ correct
while the difference between the actual mass of nucleus and its constituents is called the mass defect.
$\therefore \quad$ option $\mathrm{C} \rightarrow$ wrong and $\mathrm{D} \rightarrow$ correct

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question:
An unknown nucleus has a nuclear density of $2.29 \times 10^{17} \mathrm{~kg} / \mathrm{m}^{3}$ and mass of $19.926 \times 10^{-27} \mathrm{~kg}$. Its mass number $A$ is approximately:
(Take $R_{0}=1.2 \times 10^{-15} \mathrm{~m}, 4 \pi=12.56$ )
questions.solution:
Given
$\rho=2.29 \times 10^{17} \mathrm{~kg} / \mathrm{m}^{3}$, mass $m=19.926 \times 10^{-27} \mathrm{~kg}$
$R_{0}=1.2 \times 10^{-15} \mathrm{~m}$ and $R=R_{0} A^{\frac{1}{3}}$
Now use volume $=\frac{\text { Mass }}{\text { Density }}$
$\Rightarrow \quad \frac{4}{3} \pi R^{3}=\frac{M}{\rho}$
$\Rightarrow \quad \frac{4}{3} \pi\left[R_{0}(A)^{1 / 3}\right]^{3}=\frac{M}{\rho}$
$\Rightarrow \quad \frac{4}{3} \pi R_{0}^{3} A=\frac{M}{\rho}$
$\Rightarrow A=\frac{M}{\rho} \times \frac{3}{4 \pi \times R_{0}^{3}}=\frac{19.926 \times 10^{-27} \times 3}{2.29 \times 10^{17} \times 12.56 \times\left(1.2 \times 10^{-15}\right)^{3}} \approx 12$

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
The equation of Verhulst-Pearl logistic growth is $\frac{{dN}}{{dt}} = rN\left[ {\frac{{K - N}}{K}} \right]$,
From this equation, K indicates.
questions.solution:
A population growing in a habitat with limited resources show initially a lag phase, followed by phases of acceleration and deceleration and finally an asymptote, when the population density reaches the carrying capacity. A plot of N in relation to time (t) results in a sigmoid curve. This type of population growth is called Verhulst-Pearl Logistic Growth and is described by the following equation:
$\frac{{dN}}{{dt}} = rN\left( {\frac{{K - N}}{K}} \right)$
Where,
N = Population density at time t
r = Intrinsic rate of natural increase
K = Carrying Capacity

questions.solution: The production of numerous small offspring followed by exponential population growth is the defining characteristic of r-selected species.
