questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: When does the growth rate of a population following the logistic model equal zero? The logistic model is given as DN/dt = rN(1 – N/K)
options: When N nears the carrying capacity of the habitat
When death rate is greater than birth rate
questions.answer: Option (A): When N/K is exactly one
questions.solution:
Logistic growth of a population size occurs when resources are limited. The formula we use to calculate logistic growth adds the carrying capacity as a moderating force in the growth rate. The logistic model is given as dN/dt = rN(1-N/K). When the value of N/K is one, then, dN/dt = rN(1-N/K) dN/dt = rN(1-1)
dN/dt = rN(0)
dN/dt = 0 (zero)
So, the growth rate of the population will be equal to zero, when the value of N/K is equal to one.

questions.question: Consider a population of 10 million cells. Given the per-capita birth rate of 0.002 (per unit time) and the per-capita death rate of 0.002 (per unit time), the expected number of cells after 10 generations is
questions.solution: The population dynamic equation is $\frac{dN}{dt} = (b-d)N$. Since $r = (b-d) = 0.002 - 0.002 = 0$, $\frac{dN}{dt} = 0$. So, the population remains constant at all times. Thus, even after 10 generations, the expected number of cells will be 10 million.

questions.question:
Given below are two statements:

Statement II: Fig wasp and fig tree exhibit mutual relationship as fig fruit and fig fruit gets pollinated by fig wasp.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct
Both statement I and statement II are correct
Both statement I and statement II are incorrect
questions.answer: Option (D): Both statement I and statement II are incorrect
questions.solution:
Statement I: Fig fruit is a non-vegetarian fruit as it has enclosed fig wasps in it.
This statement is partially misleading. While it is true that fig wasps often enter fig fruits to lay eggs and may die inside them, this does not make the fig fruit non-vegetarian in a biological or botanical sense. The term non-vegetarian is a cultural/culinary classification, not a botanical one.
Statement II: Fig wasp and fig tree exhibit mutual relationship as fig fruit gets pollinated by fig wasp is also incorrect because fruits can never be pollinated by any agents, only the flowers or inflorescence is pollinated. so this second statement also becomes incorrect.

questions.solution:
Commensalism refers to a relationship wherein one organism is benefited while the other remains unaffected and is denoted by + 0. 
Amensalism refers to association wherein one partner is inhibited while the other remains nearly unaffected and is denoted by - 0. 
Association of organisms which benefits one of the partners at the expense of others is called parasitism and is denoted by + -. 
Mutualism is the association of organisms wherein both are benefited and is denoted by + +.

Amensalism- In this, one organism is harmed and the other is unaffected. For example- Penicillin production from Penicillium notatum against Staphylococci bacteria.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Gause’s principle of competitive exclusion states that
options: More abundant species will exclude the less abundant species through competition
Competition for the same resources excludes species having different food preferences
No two species can occupy the same niche indefinitely for the same limiting resources
Larger organisms exclude smaller ones through competition
questions.answer: Option (C): No two species can occupy the same niche indefinitely for the same limiting resources
questions.solution: In ecology, the competitive exclusion principle, sometimes referred to as Gause's law of competitive exclusion or just Gause's law states that two species competing for the same resource cannot coexist at constant population values if other ecological factors remain constant. When two competing life forms attempt to occupy the same niche, only one outcome is possible that is one life form will drive out the other.

questions.subject: Biology

Which of the following interactions can be assigned (+) for one species and (-) for another species involved in the interaction?
questions.solution:
In case of predation, one organism is benefited while the other is harmed. Therefore predation can be denoted by (+/-). 
In amensalism, one organism is harmed while the other is neither benefited, nor harmed (unaffected). Hence, it can be denoted as (-/0).
In commensalism, one organism is benefited while the other organism is unaffected. Hence it is (+/0). 
In case of competition, both the organisms are harmed. Hence it is (-/-).

 \frac{{{n_1}}}{{{n_2}}} = \frac{{10}}{{11}} \\ 
\end{gathered} $
So, first meet insane phase will be after 11 oscillations of the shorter pendulum.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A particle is executing SHM along a straight line. Its velocities at distances $${x_1}$$ and $${x_2}$$, from the mean position are $${v_1}$$ and $${v_2}$$, respectively. Its time period is:
questions.solution:
\[{V_1} = \omega \sqrt {{A^2} - x_1^2} \,\therefore v_1^2 = {\omega ^2}\left( {{A^2} - x_1^2} \right)\]
\[{v_2} = \omega \sqrt {{A^2} - x_2^2} \,\,\therefore v_2^2 = {\omega ^2}\left( {{A^2} - x_2^2} \right)\]
$$\therefore v_1^2 - v_2^2 = {\omega ^2}\left( {x_2^2 - x_1^2} \right){\mkern 1mu} $$$$\therefore {\omega ^2} = \frac{{v_1^2 - v_2^2}}{{x_2^2 - x_1^2}}$$
\[\therefore \omega = \sqrt {\frac{{v_1^2 - v_2^2}}{{x_2^2 - x_1^2}}} \,\therefore T = \frac{{2\pi }}{\omega } = 2\pi \sqrt {\frac{{x_2^2 - x_1^2}}{{v_1^2 - v_2^2}}} \]

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: If $x = 5\sin \left( {\pi t + \frac{\pi }{3}} \right)m$ represents the motion of a particle executing simple harmonic motion, the amplitude and time period of motion, respectively, are:

$x = 5\sin \left( {\pi t + \frac{\pi }{3}} \right)m$
Amplitude = 5m

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two identical point masses P and Q, suspended from two separate massless springs of spring constant ${k_1}$ and ${k_2}$, respectively, oscillate vertically. If their maximum speeds are the same, the ratio $\left( {\frac{{{A_Q}}}{{{A_P}}}} \right)$ of the amplitude ${A_Q}$ of mass Q to the amplitude ${A_P}$ of mass P is:
questions.solution:
${A_1}{\omega _1} = {A_2}{\omega _2}$
${A_P}{\omega _P} = {A_Q}{\omega _Q}$
$\omega = \frac{{2\pi }}{T}$
$T = 2\pi \sqrt {\frac{m}{k}} $
\[ \Rightarrow \frac{{{A_P}}}{{{A_Q}}} = \frac{{{\omega _Q}}}{{{\omega _P}}}\]
$ = \frac{{{T_P}}}{{{T_Q}}}$
$ = \frac{{\sqrt {{k_Q}} }}{{\sqrt {{k_P}} }}$
$ = \sqrt {{k_2}:{k_1}} $
${A_Q}:{A_P} = \sqrt {{k_1}:{k_2}} $

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question:
The sum of kinetic energy and potential energy of a simple pendulum bob is 0.02 joule. The speed of the simple pendulum bob at equilibrium position is approximately:

At equilibrium position

$v=\sqrt{2}$
$v=1.41 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$

questions.question: The phase difference between the displacement and acceleration of a particle in a simple harmonic motion is:
questions.solution:
for SHM acceleration and displacement both must have opposite direction

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question:
The displacement of a particle executing simple harmonic motion is given by
$y = {A_0} + A\sin \omega t + B\cos \omega t.$
Then the amplitude of its oscillation is given by:
questions.solution:
\[y = {A_0} + A\sin \omega t + B\cos \omega t\] 
Equate SHM
\[y' = y - {A_0} = A\sin \omega t + B\cos \omega t\]
Resultant amplitude
 $R=\sqrt{A^2+B^2+2AB\cos90^o}=\sqrt{A^2+B^2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: When two displacements represented by y<sub>1</sub>= a sin (ωt) and y<sub>2</sub> = b cos (ωt) are superimposed the motion is:
questions.solution:
$${y_1} = a\sin \omega t$$
$$\& {y_2} = b\cos \omega t = b\sin \left( {\omega t + \frac{\pi }{2}} \right)$$
Since the frequencies for both SHM are same, resultant motion will be SHM. Now
Amplitude $$A = \sqrt {A_1^2 + A_2^2 + 2{A_1}{A_2}\cos \phi } $$
Here $${A_1} = a,{A_2} = b,\& \phi  = \frac{\pi }{2}$$
So $$A = \sqrt {{a^2} + {b^2}} $$

questions.question: A cylindrical cork of uniform density floats in a liquid of density $\rho_{1}$. If the cork is depressed slightly and released, it oscillates harmonically with time period $T$. If the same cork floats in another liquid of density $\rho_{2}$, then the similar oscillation has time period $2 T$. The value of $\rho_{2} / \rho_{1}$ is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A body of mass m is attached to the lower end of a spring whose upper end is fixed. The spring has negligible mass. When the mass m is slightly pulled down and released, it oscillates with a time period of 3s. When the mass m is increased by 1 kg, the time period of oscillations becomes 5s. The value of m in kg is
questions.solution:
$T = 2\pi \sqrt {\frac{m}{k}} $
$3 = 2\pi \sqrt {\frac{m}{k}} $ … (1)
$5 = 2\pi \sqrt {\frac{{m + 1}}{k}} $ … (2)
$\frac{{{{\left( 1 \right)}^2}}}{{{{\left( 2 \right)}^2}}} \Rightarrow \frac{9}{{25}} = \frac{m}{{m + 1}} \Rightarrow m = \frac{9}{{16}}$

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What is the role of large bundle sheath cells found around the vascular bundles in C<sub>4 </sub>plants?
options: To provide the site of photorespiratory pathway
To increase the number of chloroplast for the operation of Calvin cycle
To enable the plant to tolerate high temperature
To protect the vascular tissue from high light intensity
questions.answer: Option (B): To increase the number of chloroplast for the operation of Calvin cycle
questions.solution: The particularly large cells around the vascular bundles of the C4 plants are called bundle sheath cells, and the leaves which have such anatomy are said to have ‘Kranz’ anatomy. In C4 plants the bundle sheath cells may form several layers around the vascular bundles; they are characterised by having a large number of chloroplasts, thick walls impervious to gaseous exchange and no intercellular spaces. So, bundle sheath cells found around the vascular bundles of C4 plants increase the number of chloroplasts for the operation of the Calvin cycle.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A plant in your garden avoids photorespiratory losses, has improved water use efficiency, shows high rates of photosynthesis at high temperatures and has improved efficiency of nitrogen utilization. In which of the following physiological groups would you assign this plant?
questions.solution: This plant is a C4 plant. C4 plants are special as they have a special type of leaf anatomy called Kranz anatomy. They can tolerate higher temperatures, they show a response to high intensities of light, they lack a wasteful process called photorespiration and they have improved efficiency of nitrogen utilization. Most of the plants that are adapted to dry tropical regions have the C4 pathway and are known as C4 plants. In these plants, double fixation of carbon dioxide occurs.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Emerson’s enhancement effect and Red drop have been instrumental in the discovery of:
questions.solution: The Emerson effect is the increase in the rate of photosynthesis after chloroplasts are exposed to light of wavelength 670 nm (red light) and 700 nm (far red light). When simultaneously exposed to light of both wavelengths, the rate of photosynthesis is far higher than the sum of the red light and far red light photosynthesis rates. Wavelengths beyond 700nm are apparently of insufficient energy to drive any part of photosynthesis. So a huge drop in efficiency has been noticed at 700nm. This phenomenon is called the Red drop effect. In other words there is a sharp decrease in quantum yield at wavelengths greater than 680nm. This decrease in quantum yield takes place in the red part of the spectrum. The number of oxygen molecules released per light quanta absorbed is called the quantum yield of photosynthesis. This effect was first of all noticed by Robert Emerson.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Phosphoenolpyruvate (PEP) is the primary CO<sub>2</sub> acceptor in
questions.solution: PEP (Phosphoenolpyruvate) is a 3C compound that serves as the primary CO2 acceptor in the mesophyll cell of C4 plants like maize, sugarcane, sorghum, etc. In C3 plants ribulose biphosphate acts as a primary acceptor and gets converted into phosphoglycerate (PGA).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following combinations is required for chemiosmosis?
options: Membrane, proton pump, proton gradient, NADP synthase
Proton pump, electron gradient, ATP synthase
Proton pump, electron gradient, NADP synthase
Membrane, proton pump, proton gradient, ATP synthase
questions.answer: Option (D): Membrane, proton pump, proton gradient, ATP synthase
questions.solution: Membrane, proton pump, proton gradient, ATP synthase.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Water vapour comes out from the plant leaf through the stomatal opening. Through the same stomatal opening, carbon dioxide diffuses into the plant during photosynthesis. Reason out the above statements using one of following options:
options: Both processes can happen together because the diffusion coefficient of water and CO<sub>2</sub> is different.
The above processes happen only during night time.
One process occurs during day time and the other at night.
questions.answer: Option (B): Both processes can happen together because the diffusion coefficient of water and CO2 is different.
questions.solution:
When a plant is transpiring, its stomata are open, allowing gas exchange between the atmosphere and the leaf. Open stomata allow water vapor to leave the leaf but also allow carbon dioxide (CO2) to enter. Carbon dioxide is needed for photosynthesis to operate. Much more water leaves the leaf than CO2 enters for three reasons:
1. H2O molecules are smaller than CO2 molecules and so they move to their destination faster.
2. CO2 is only about 0.036% of the atmosphere so the gradient for its entry into the plant is much smaller than the gradient for H2O moving from a hydrated leaf into a dry atmosphere.
3. CO2 has a much longer distance to travel to reach its destination in the chloroplast from the atmosphere compared to H2O which only has to move from the leaf cell surface to the atmosphere.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Photorespiration reaction catalyzed by RuBisCo is shown below:
RuBP + O2 → 3-Phosphoglycerate + X.
Identify "X" from the given options:
questions.solution: During the process of photorespiration, RuBP binds with O2 and RuBP instead of being converted to 2 molecules of PGA, forms one molecule each of phosphoglycerate and phosphoglycolate. Hence, in the given reaction, the "X" is 2-phosphoglycolate.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: With reference to factors affecting the rate of photosynthesis, which of the following statements is not correct?
options: C<sub>3</sub> plants respond to higher temperatures with enhanced photosynthesis while C<sub>4</sub> plants have much lower temperature optimum
Tomato is a greenhouse crop that can be grown in CO<sub>2</sub> enriched atmosphere for higher yield
Light saturation for CO<sub>2</sub> fixation occurs at 10% of full sunlight
Increasing atmospheric CO<sub>2</sub> concentration up to 0.05% can enhance CO<sub>2</sub> fixation rate
questions.answer: Option (A): C3 plants respond to higher temperatures with enhanced photosynthesis while C4 plants have much lower temperature optimum
questions.solution: In C3 plants, photosynthesis is decreased at higher temperatures due to increased photorespiration. As a result, RuBisCO binds to oxygen instead of carbon dioxide. That's why C3 plants have a much lower temperature optimum as compared to C4 plants.C4 plants have a higher temperature optimum because of the presence of pyruvate phosphate dikinase enzyme, which is sensitive to lower temperatures. Hence, it shows a higher rate of photosynthesis at higher temperatures.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Given below are two statements.
Statement 1: in C3 plants, some O2 binds to RuBisCO, hence CO2 fixation is decreased.
Statement 2: In C4 plants, mesophyll cells show very little photorespiration while bundle sheath cells do not show photorespiration.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
questions.answer: Option (B): Statement I is true but Statement II is false
questions.solution:
In C3 plants some O2 does bind to RuBisCO, and hence CO2 fixation is decreased. Here the RuBP instead of being converted to 2 molecules of PGA binds with O2 to form one molecule of phosphoglycerate and phosphoglycolate (2 Carbon) in a pathway called photorespiration.
In C4 plants photorespiration does not occur. This is because they have a mechanism that increases the concentration of CO2 at the enzyme site. This takes place when the C4 acid from the mesophyll is broken down in the bundle sheath cells to release CO2 – this results in increasing the intracellular concentration of CO2. In turn, this ensures that the RuBisCO functions as a carboxylase minimising the oxygenase activity.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The reaction centre in PS II has an absorption maximum at
questions.solution: 680 nm

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I : The primary CO2 acceptor in C4 plants is phosphoenolpyruvate and is found in the mesophyll cells.
Statement II : Mesophyll cells of C4 plants lack RuBisCo enzyme.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.answer: Option (A): Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.solution:
PEP is the 3C compound and acts as the primary CO2 acceptor in the mesophyll cells of C4 plants, leading to the formation of OAA, a C4 acid.
Ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate carboxylase (RUBISCO) is an enzyme found in the mesophyll cells present within the C3 plants. In C4 plants, this enzyme is found in the bundle sheath cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The oxygen evolved during photosynthesis comes from water molecules. Which one of the following pairs of elements is involved in this reaction?
questions.solution: Photolysis of water takes place in the presence of manganese, calcium and chlorine ions.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Select the correct sequence of experiments that led to a gradual understanding of photosynthesis in green plants.
options: Role of air → release of oxygen → production of glucose → absorption spectra of chlorophyll a and b
Release of oxygen → production of glucose → absorption spectra of chlorophyll a and b → role of air
Production of glucose → role of air → release of oxygen → absorption spectra of chlorophyll a and b
Absorption spectra of chlorophyll a and b → production of glucose → release of oxygen → role of air
questions.answer: Option (A): Role of air → release of oxygen → production of glucose → absorption spectra of chlorophyll a and b
questions.solution: Following is the appropriate sequence of experiments: Role of air (Joseph Priestley's bell jar experiment) 1770 → Release of oxygen (Jan Ingenhousz's experiment using aquatic plant) → Production of Glucose (Julius Von Sach's experiment) 1854 → Absorption spectra of chlorophyll a and b (T.W. Engelmann's experiment).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A few normal seedlings of tomato were kept in a dark room. After a few days they were found to have become white-coloured lime albinos. Which of the following terms will you  use to describe them?
questions.solution: The process in which flowering plants are grown in partial or complete absence of light characterised by long and weak stems and smaller, sparse pale yellow colour of leaves is called etiolation. Hence, the white coloured tomato seedlings are etiolated.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Which of the following statements regarding photorespiration are correct?
(a) Do not occur in C3 plants
(b) CO2 is consumed and O2 is generated
(c) Phosphoglycolate is formed
(d) No synthesis of ATP and NADPH
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Photorespiration can occur in C3 plants. In photorespiration, O2 is consumed and CO2 is released. Phosphoglycolate is formed as the initial product. There is no synthesis of ATP and NADPH in photorespiration.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Find the incorrect statement(s) about photosynthesis from the following:
A. The water splitting complex is associated with PS I.
B. C4 plants use the C3 pathway of CO2 fixation as the main biosynthetic pathway.
C. In C4 plants, photorespiration does not occur.
D. C3 plants exhibit 'Kranz' anatomy.
E. ATP synthesis in chloroplast occurs through chemiosmosis.

Choose the answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
The water splitting complex is associated with PS-II. $\mathrm{C}_{3}$ pathway is the main biosynthetic pathway for $\mathrm{CO}_{2}$ fixation in both $\mathrm{C}_{3}$ and $\mathrm{C}_{4}$ plants.
$\mathrm{C}_{3}$ plants do not exhibit 'kranz' anatomy.
ATP synthesis in chloroplast (Photophosphorylation) occurs by chemiosmosis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The first stable product of CO2 fixation in sorghum is
questions.solution: Most of the plants that are adapted to dry tropical regions have the C4 pathway. These plants are called C4 plants. Sugarcane, maize, sorghum, etc. are examples of these plants. In C4 pathway, the primary CO2 acceptor is 3 carbon compound, phosphoenol pyruvate (PEP) which is present in mesophyll cells. PEP combines with CO2 to form 4 carbon compounds i.e., oxaloacetic acid (OAA) in the presence of enzyme PEP carboxylase. Hence, the first stable product of CO2 fixation in sorghum is oxaloacetic acid.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The enzyme required for carboxylation in the Calvin cycle is
questions.solution: RuBisCO (RuBP carboxylase -oxygenase) is the enzyme required for carboxylation in the Calvin cycle.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about RuBisCO is true?
options: It is an enzyme involved in the photolysis of water.
It catalyzes the carboxylation of RuBP.
It is active only in the dark.
It has higher affinity for oxygen than carbon dioxide.
questions.answer: Option (B): It catalyzes the carboxylation of RuBP.
questions.solution: Water Splitting Complex is involved in Photolysis. RuBisCO enzyme is involved in carboxylation of RuBP in C3 cycle. It is involved in dark reactions but can occur in dark and light conditions both. It has higher affinity for carbon dioxide than oxygen.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which pigment has absorption peak at 700 nm in the photosynthetic reaction centre PS I (P700)?
questions.solution: In PSI, the reaction centre chlorophyll a has an absorption peak at 700 nm and hence, is called P700.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which micronutrient is required for splitting of water molecule during photosynthesis?
questions.solution: Manganese

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: How many molecules of ATP and NADPH are required for every molecule of CO2 fixed in the Calvin cycle
options: 2 molecules of ATP and 2 molecules of NADPH
3 molecules of ATP and 3 molecules of NADPH
3 molecules of ATP and 2 molecules of NADPH
2 molecules of ATP and 3 molecules of NADPH
questions.answer: Option (C): 3 molecules of ATP and 2 molecules of NADPH
questions.solution: For every CO2 molecule entering the Calvin cycle, 3 molecules of ATP and 2 of NADPH are required.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: How many ATP and NADPH<sub>2</sub> are required for the synthesis of one molecule of glucose during Calvin cycle?
questions.solution: For every CO2 molecule entering the Calvin cycle, 3 molecules of ATP and 2 of NADPH are required. To make one molecule of glucose 6 turns of the cycle are required. Thus, 18 ATP and 12 NADPH2 are required for the synthesis of one molecule of glucose during Calvin cycle.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: How many ATP and NADPH molecules are required to make one molecule of glucose through the Calvin pathway?
questions.solution:
Each turn of Calvin pathway utilizes 3ATP and NADPH $+\mathrm{H}^{+}$molecules for fixation of $1 \mathrm{CO}_{2}$ molecule.
So for 1 Glucose 6 turns are required, hence 18 ATP and $12 \mathrm{NADPH}+\mathrm{H}^{+}$are required for glucose synthesis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In photosynthesis, the light-independent reactions take place at
questions.solution: The inside of the thylakoid membrane is called the lumen. The light-independent reactions take place outside the thylakoid membrane called the stroma. The light-independent reactions are also known as dark reactions in which carbon dioxide is utilized for the synthesis of sugar. These reactions are not light-driven but dependent upon products of the light reactions (ATP and NADPH).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is not a product of the light reaction of photosynthesis?
questions.solution: ATP, NADPH, and oxygen are products of light reaction, while NADH is a product of the respiration process. NADPH is produced at PS-I, ATP is formed by ATPase, and oxygen is released at PS-II.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: Grana lamellae have both PS I and PS II
Cyclic photophosphorylation involves both PS I and PS II.
Both ATP and NADPH<sup> </sup><sup>+</sup> H<sup>+</sup> are synthesized during non-cyclic photophosphorylation.
Stroma lamellae have PS I only and lack NADP reductase
questions.answer: Option (B): Cyclic photophosphorylation involves both PS I and PS II.
questions.solution: When the two photosystems work in a series, first PS II and then PS I, a process called non-cyclic photo-phosphorylation occurs. The two photosystems are connected through an electron transport chain, as seen earlier – in the Z scheme. Both ATP and NADPH + and H+ are synthesized by this kind of electron flow. When only PS I is functional, the electron is circulated within the photosystem and the phosphorylation occurs due to the cyclic flow of electrons is called cyclic photophosphorylation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In light reaction, plastoquinone facilitates the transfer of electrons from
questions.solution: In non-cyclic photophosphorylation, plastoquinone obtains electrons from PS-II and transfers them to cyt b6-f complex.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Which of the following are required for the dark reaction of photosynthesis? A. Light
B. Chlorophyll
C. CO2
D. ATP
E. NADPH
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.answer: Option (B): C, D and E only
questions.solution: The dark phase or biosynthetic phase of photosynthesis does not directly depend on the presence of light but is dependent on the products of the light reaction, i.e., ATP and NADPH, besides CO2 and H2O.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In a chloroplast, the highest number of protons are found in
questions.solution: The thylakoid lumen is a continuous aqueous phase, enclosed by the thylakoid membrane. It plays an important role for photophosphorylation during photosynthesis. During the light-dependent reaction, protons are pumped across the thylakoid membrane into the lumen making it acidic down to pH 4. The ATP synthase complex transports protons across the thylakoid from lumen to stroma. These protons flow down an electrochemical gradient and the energy released by that flow is trapped on the stroma side of the thylakoid membrane by ATP synthesis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The process which makes major difference between C3 and C4 plants is
questions.solution:
Photorespiration is a respiratory process in many higher plants by which they take up oxygen in the light and give out some carbon dioxide, contrary to the general pattern of photosynthesis. In this process, RuBisCO binds to oxygen, and RuBP is converted to produce one molecule of phosphoglycerate and one molecule of phosphoglycolate. Neither sugar nor ATP is synthesized in this pathway. It rather utilizes one ATP for the removal of carbon dioxide. Therefore, it is a wasteful process.Photorespiration is present in C3 but absent in C4 plants.
C4 plants have a mechanism to increase the intracellular concentration of carbon dioxide at the enzyme site. Hence, this ensures more carbon fixation and minimizes the oxygenase activity.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The oxygenation activity of RuBisCO enzyme in photorespiration leads to the formation of
options: 1 molecule of 4-C compound and 1 molecule of 2-C compound
1 molecule of 3-C compound and 1 molecule of 2-C compound
questions.answer: Option (D): 1 molecule of 3-C compound and 1 molecule of 2-C compound
questions.solution: Photorespiration is the light-dependent process in which RuBisCO enzymes perform oxygenation instead of fixing carbon dioxide (C3 cycle) and oxidizes ribulose 1, 5-bisphosphate to produce a 3-carbon phosphoglyceric acid and a 2-carbon phosphoglycolate. Hence, the (d) option is correct.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List I with List II:
List IList II
A.Chlorophyll aI.Yellow-green
B.Chlorophyll bII.Yellow
C.XanthophyllsIII.Blue-green
D.CarotenoidsIV.Yellow to Yellow-orange

Choose the option with all correct matches.
questions.solution: Chlorophyll a - Blue green, Chlorophyll b - Yellow green, Xanthophyll - yellow, Carotenoids - Yellow to yellow orange

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following is not true regarding the release of energy during ATP synthesis through chemiosmosis? It involves:
options: Movement of protons across the membrane to the stroma
Reduction of NADP to NADPH<sub>2</sub> on the stroma side of the membrane
questions.solution: Chemiosmotic hypothesis explains the mechanism of ATP synthesis in the thylakoids of chloroplast. In photosynthesis, the synthesis of ATP is linked to the development of a proton gradient across the cell membrane. No electron gradient is formed during generation of ATP.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: How many turns of Calvin cycle are required for the formation of three molecules of glucose?
questions.solution: To make one molecule of glucose 6 turns of the cycle are required. Therefore, for the formation of three molecules of glucose, 6 × 3 = 18 turns of Calvin cycle are required.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In tissue culture experiments, leaf mesophyll cells are put in a culture medium to form callus. This phenomenon may be called as:
questions.solution: The living differentiated cells, that by now have lost the capacity to divide can regain the capacity of division under certain conditions. This phenomenon is termed as dedifferentiation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The plant hormone used to destroy weeds in a field is
questions.solution: 2, 4-D (2, 4-Dichlorophenoxyacetic) is synthetic auxin. They are widely used to kill dicotyledonous weeds and do not affect mature monocotyledonous plants. It is used to prepare weed-free lawns by gardeners. Auxin also controls xylem differentiation and helps in cell division. IAA and IBA are natural auxins. NAA is a synthetic auxin.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The process of growth is maximum during
questions.solution: Growth curve consists of three phases i.e. lag phase (slow growth), log phase (fast growth) and steady state (no growth).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: You are given a tissue with its potential for differentiation in an artificial culture. Which of the following pairs of hormones would you add to the medium to secure shoots as well as roots?
questions.solution: Auxins help to initiate rooting in stem cuttings and thus promote the growth of stems and roots. Cytokinins are synthesised in regions where rapid cell division occurs, for example, root apices and developing shoot buds. Higher auxin and cytokinin ratio induces root formation whereas lower ratio induces formation of shoots.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Production of Cucumber has increased manifold in recent years. Application of which of the following phytohormones has resulted in this increased yield as the hormone is known to produce female flowers in the plants?
questions.solution: Ethylene is a simple gaseous plant growth regulator (PGR). It promotes Femaleness (feminising effect) in Pineapple (Bromeliaceae) and Cucumber. Application of Ethylene increases the number of female flowers in cucumber plants, thereby increasing the final yield. Hence, Ethylene can be applied by the farmer to increase the number of female flowers in the cucumber plants.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Heterophyllous development in response to environment is an example of which of the following phenomena?
questions.solution: Plants follow different pathways in response to environment or phases of life to form different kinds of structures. This ability is called plasticity, e.g., heterophylly in cotton, coriander and larkspur.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Spraying of which of the following phytohormone or juvenile conifers helps in hastening the maturity period, that leads to early seed production?
questions.solution: Gibberellic acid

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Length of the stem at time 0 is 20 cm. The arithmetic growth rate is 30 cm per day. What is the length of the stem at the end of the 7th day?
questions.solution: Arithmetic growth can be expressed as $L_{t} = L_{0} + rt$ (where $L_{t}$ = length at time 't', $L_{0}$ = Length at time 'zero', $r$ = growth rate). $L_{7th~day} = 20 + 30 \times 7 = 20 + 210 = 230$ cm.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What is the site of perception of photoperiod necessary for induction of flowering in plants?
questions.solution: Photoperiodism is the phenomenon in which formation of flowers in plants depends on the relative length of dark or light periods. Photoperiodic stimulus is perceived by the leaf. Flowering plants use phytochrome as a photoreceptor.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Dr.F. Went noted that if coleoptile tips were removed and placed on agar for one hour, the agar would produce a bending when placed on one side of freshly cut coleoptile stumps. Of what significance is this experiment?
options: It is the basis for quantitative determination of small amounts of growth promoting substances
It supports the hypothesis that IAA is auxin
It demonstrated polar movement of auxins
It made possible the isolation and exact identification of auxin
questions.answer: Option (A): It is the basis for quantitative determination of small amounts of growth promoting substances
questions.solution: It is the basis for quantitative determination of small amounts of growth promoting substances. The Avena coleoptile test is a bioassay firstly done by F. W. Went. It is for IAA (indole-3-acetic acid). It measures the angle of the curvature of a decapitated coleoptile after placing an agar block containing auxin on one side. It is seen that when coleoptile tips are placed on agar, agar produced bending when placed on one side of freshly cut coleoptile stumps.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: During seed germination, its stored food is mobilized by
questions.solution: Gibberellin functions in breaking seed dormancy by inducing the aleurone cells to secrete enzymes which break stored food in the seed.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following is not a characteristic of plant cells in the phase of elongation?
questions.solution: Phase of elongation is characterised by new cell wall deposition, increased vacuolation and enlargement of cell. Presence of large conspicuous nuclei is a feature of cells in the meristematic phase.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Name the plant growth regulators which upon spraying on sugarcane crop, increases the length of stem, thus increasing the yield of sugarcane crop.
questions.solution: Gibberellin hormone causes the plant growth in length and elongation of stem. It is able to promote the internode elongation because of which the size of sugarcane plant increases.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which hormone promotes internode/petiole elongation in deep water rice?
questions.solution: Ethylene

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Auxin can be bioassayed by
questions.solution: Avena coleoptile curvature is an auxin bioassay quantitative test that measures the concentration of auxin to produce the effect and its amount.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Plants follow different pathways in response to the environment or phases of life to form different kinds of structures. This ability is called
questions.solution: Plants follow different pathways in response to the environment or phases of life to form different kinds of structures. This ability is called plasticity, e.g., heterophylly in cotton, coriander, and larkspur. In such plants, the leaves of the juvenile plant are different in shape from those in mature plants. On the other hand, differences in the shapes of leaves produced in air and those produced in water in buttercup also represent the heterophyllous development due to the environment. This phenomenon of heterophylly is an example of plasticity.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Spraying sugarcane crop with which of the following plant growth regulators, increases the length of stem, thus, increasing the yield?
questions.solution: Sugarcane stores carbohydrate as sugar in their stems. Spraying sugarcane crop with gibberellins increases the length of the stem, thus increasing the yield by as much as 20 tonnes per acre

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Fruit and leaf drop at early stages can be prevented by the application of
questions.solution:
Auxins prevent premature leaf and fruit fall. It promotes the abscission of older mature leaves and fruits. Hence, the (a) option is correct.Whereas cytokinin helps in the delay of leaf senescence, overcome apical dominance, etc.
Gibberellin help in seed germination.
Ethylene help in fruit ripening, triple response etc.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The site of perception of light in plants during photoperiodism is
questions.solution: The site of perception of light in plants during photoperiodism is the leaf. The site of perception of low-temperature stimulus during vernalization is shoot apex and embryo. Axillary buds are not sites of perception of photoperiod.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following plants does not show plasticity?
questions.solution: Plasticity is the ability of the plant to adjust to a particular environment by altering the rate of growth, development, and metabolism. For example, heterophylly in cotton, coriander, larkspur and buttercup. Maize does not show plasticity.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Read the following statements on plant growth and development.
A. Parthenocarpy can be induced by auxins.
B. Plant growth regulators can be involved in promotion as well as inhibition of growth.
C. Dedifferentiation is a pre-requisite for re-differentiation.
D. Abscisic acid is a plant growth promoter.
E. Apical dominance promotes the growth of lateral buds.
Choose the option with all correct statements.
questions.solution: Abscisic acid is a plant growth inhibitor, not a promoter. Apical dominance prevents the growth of lateral buds, it doesn't promote it. Thus, statements D and E are incorrect and statements A, B and C are correct.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is not an inhibitory substance governing seed dormancy?
questions.solution: Gibberellins are involved in the natural process of breaking dormancy and other aspects of germination. Gibberellic acid, one of the gibberellins, stimulates the cells of germinating seeds to produce mRNA molecules that code for hydrolytic enzymes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following phytohormones promotes nutrient mobilization which helps in the delay of leaf senescence in plants?
questions.solution: Cytokinin promote nutrient mobilisation which helps in the delay of leaf senescence.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Auxin is used by gardeners to prepare weed-free lawns. But no damage is caused to grass as auxin
options: promotes abscission of mature leaves only
does not affect mature monocotyledon plants
can help in cell division in grasses, to produce growth
questions.answer: Option (B): does not affect mature monocotyledon plants
questions.solution: Auxins are widely used as herbicides. 2, 4-D, widely used to kill dicotyledonous weeds, does not affect mature monocotyledonous plants. It is used to prepare weed-free lawns by gardeners.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Formation of interfascicular cambium from fully developed parenchyma cells is an example for
questions.solution: The living differentiated cells, that by now have lost the capacity to divide can regain the capacity of division under certain conditions. This phenomenon is termed as dedifferentiation. For example, formation of meristems – interfascicular cambium and cork cambium from fully differentiated parenchyma cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: It takes a very long time for pineapple plants to produce flowers. Which combination of hormones can be applied to artificially induce flowering in pineapple plants throughout the year to increase yield?
questions.solution: Plant hormone auxin induces flowering in pineapple. Ethylene also helps in synchronization of flowering and fruit set up in pineapple.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following plant growth regulators is used as herbicide?
questions.solution: 2, 4-D is an artificial auxin, which is widely used as herbicide.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following growth regulators is known as ‘stress hormone’?
questions.solution: Abscisic acid stimulates the closure of stomata in the epidermis during water stress conditions and increases the tolerance of plants to various kinds of stresses. Therefore, it is also called the stress hormone.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following flowers only once in its life-time?
questions.solution:
Bamboo species are monocarpic i.e., produce flowers only once in their life after 50-100 years depending on the species.
Jackfruit, papaya, and mango are polycarpic i.e., produce flowers and fruits many times in their life.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following plant growth regulators promotes internode elongation prior to flowering in cabbage?
questions.solution: Gibberellin promotes internode elongation prior to flowering in cabbage.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The Avena curvature is used for bioassay of:
questions.solution: The Avena geo-curvature test is a bioassay for auxin-type growth regulators. Etiolated oat coleoptiles are used and the test is conducted in special perspex trays under diffuse daylight. The lowest IAA concentration which can be determined is around 30 to 60 μg/l IAA. The concentration response curves follow a logarithmic course up to 1,000 μg/l.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The gaseous plant growth regulator is used in plants to:
options: Promote root growth and root hair formation to increase the absorption surface
Kill dicotyledonous weeds in the fields
questions.answer: Option (B): Promote root growth and root hair formation to increase the absorption surface
questions.solution:
Ethylene is a gaseous phytohormone that regulates both growth, and senescence.
• It is produced in large amounts by tissues undergoing senescence and ripening fruits.
• It promotes or inhibits growth and senescence processes in the plants.
• Ethylene inhibits lateral buds and causes apical dominance.
• Ethylene promotes femaleness in Pineapple and Cucumber.
• It increases the number of female flowers in cucumber plants, thereby increasing the final yield.
• The hormone also increases the absorption surface area of the root as it promotes root growth and root hair formation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Select the correct statement:
options: Gymnosperms are both homosporous and heterosporous
Sequoia is one of the tallest trees
The leaves of gymnosperms are not well adapted to extremes of climate
questions.answer: Option (C): Sequoia is one of the tallest trees
questions.solution: Sequoia is one of the tallest trees. It is also known as the redwood tree. Leaves of gymnosperms are well adapted to the extreme of climate. Gymnosperms are heterosporous. Salvinia is a pteridophyte whereas Ginkgo and Pinus are gymnosperms.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In bryophytes and pteridophytes, transport of male gametes requires
questions.solution: In bryophytes and pteridophytes, transport of male gametes requires water. The male gametes, produced by reproductive structures called antheridia, are free-swimming sperm cells that need water to transport them to the female gametes, which are enclosed within structures called archegonia. Because of the need for water, bryophytes are especially common in wet habitats such as bogs, streambanks, and in moist forests.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Hydrocolloid carrageen is obtained from
questions.solution: Red algae and brown algae can be employed to produce hydrocolloids as thickening and gelling agents. Carrageen is one such hydrocolloid which is produced by red algae (Rhodophyceae).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
The correct sequence of events in the life cycle of bryophytes is
A. Fusion of antherozoid with egg.
B. Attachment of gametophyte to substratum.
C. Reduction division, to produce haploid spores.
D. Formation of sporophyte.
E. Release of antherozoids into water.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.answer: Option (A): B, E, A, D, C
questions.solution:
1. The plant body of bryophytes is thallus-like and prostrate or erect, and attached to the substratum by unicellular or multicellular rhizoids. 
2. The male sex organ is called antheridium. They produce biflagellate antherozoids. The antherozoids are released into water where they come in contact with archegonium. 
3. An antherozoid fuses with the egg to produce the zygote.
4. Zygotes do not undergo reduction division immediately. They produce a multicellular body called a sporophyte.
5. Some cells of the sporophyte undergo reduction division (meiosis) to produce haploid spores. These spores germinate to produce gametophyte.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Male gametophyte with least number of cells is present in:
questions.solution: In angiosperms, male gametophyte is reduced to about 2-3 cells and is called pollen grain. Lilium is an angiosperm which possesses the male gametophyte with least number of cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Read the following statements and choose the set of correct statements:
In the members of Phacophyceae,
A. Asexual reproduction occurs usually by biflagellate zoospores.
B. Sexual reproduction is in oogamous method only.
C. Stored food is in the form of carbohydrates which is either mannitol or laminarin.
D. The major pigments found are chlorophyll a, c and carotenoids and xanthophyll.
E. Vegetative cells have a cellulosic wall, usually covered on the outside by gelatinous coating of algin.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: B, C, D and E only
A, C, D and E only
A, B, C and E only
A, B, C and D only
questions.answer: Option (B): A, C, D and E only
questions.solution:
A. Asexual reproduction in most Phaeophyceae (brown algae) is by biflagellate zoospores that are pear-shaped and have two unequal laterally attached flagella. 
B. Sexual reproduction may be isogamous, anisogamous or oogamous.
C. Food is stored as complex carbohydrates, which may be in the form of laminarin or mannitol
D. The members of phaeophyceae possess chlorophyll a, c, carotenoids and xanthophylls.
E. The vegetative cells have a cellulosic wall usually covered on the outside by a gelatinous coating of algin

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: In gymnosperms, the male and female gametophytes remain within the sporangia.
Statement II: In gymnosperms, seeds are not covered.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.answer: Option (D): Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.solution: In gymnosperms, the male and female gametophytes do not have an independent free-living existence. They remain within sporangia, retained on the sporophyte. In gymnosperms the ovules are not enclosed by any ovary wall and remain exposed, both before and after fertilisation. The seeds that develop post fertilisation are not covered, i.e., naked.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is responsible for peat formation?
questions.solution: Species of Sphagnum, a moss, provide peat that has been used as fuel and packaging material because of its water holding capacity.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Identify the pair of heterosporous pteridophytes among the following:
questions.solution: Genera like Selaginella and Salvinia produce two kinds of spores, macro (large) and micro (small) spores, are known as heterosporous.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following algae produce Carrageen?
questions.solution: Red algae produce carrageen. Carrageen is a common name given to polysaccharides extracted from certain seaweeds like red edible seaweeds. It is used as a gelling, thickening, and stabilizing agent. The cell wall of red algae is composed of agar, carrageen, and funori along with cellulose. In brown algae, the cell wall contains algin while in green algae it is composed of cellulose and pectin. In blue-green algae, the cell wall is composed of mucopeptides.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List I with List II.
List IList II
A. PteridophyteI. Salvia
B. BryophyteII. Ginkgo
C. AngiospermIII. Polytrichum
D. GymnospermIV. Salvinia

Choose the option with all correct matches.
questions.solution: Salvinia is a pteridophyte, Polytrichum is a Bryophyte, Salvia is a Angiosperms, Ginkgo is a gymnosperms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Conifers are adapted to tolerate extreme environmental conditions because of
questions.solution: Conifers are gymnosperms and lack vessels. Needle-shaped leaves of gymnosperms are adapted not to accumulate much snow, the presence of thick waxy cuticle and sclerenchyma protect the underlying mesophyll cells, tightly packed tissues protect the central vein containing vascular tissues. Thus, these leaves are well adapted to withstand the harsh and cold climate. They have sunken stomata to preserve water loss during physiological drought conditions. So, the correct answer is 'Thick cuticle'.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Select the mismatch.
questions.solution:
Pinus is a monoecious plant having both male and female cones on the same plant.
Cycas possess either male or female reproductive parts, Equisetum produces the same type of spore (homosporous) and Salvinia produces different types of spores (heterosporous).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Monoecious plant of Chara shows occurrence of
options: Antheridiophore and archegoniophore on the same plant
Stamen and carpel and on the same plant
Upper antheridium and lower oogonium on the same plant
Upper oogonium and lower antheridium on the same plant
questions.answer: Option (D): Upper oogonium and lower antheridium on the same plant
questions.solution: Chara is a monoecious green alga that shows the presence of an upper oogonium and lower antheridium on the same plant.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following algae contains mannitol as reserve food material?
questions.solution: Ectocarpus is a member of Phaeophyceae or brown algae that are found primarily in marine habitats. They possess chlorophyll a, c, carotenoids, and xanthophylls. They vary in colour from olive green to various shades of brown depending upon the amount of the xanthophyll pigment, fucoxanthin present in them. Food is stored as complex carbohydrates, which may be in the form of laminarin or mannitol.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Given below are two statements: One is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R:
Assertion A: The first stage of gametophyte in the life cycle of moss is protonema stage.
Reason R: Protonema develops directly from spores produced in capsule.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both A and R are correct, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is correct, but R is not correct.
A is not correct, but R is correct.
Both A and R are correct, and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.answer: Option (D): Both A and R are correct, and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.solution: Both A and R are correct, and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Genera like Selaginella and Salvinia produce two kinds of spores. Such plants are known as
questions.solution: Genera like Selaginella and Salvinia which produce two kinds of spores, macro (large) and micro (small) spores, are known as heterosporous. The megaspores and microspores germinate and give rise to female and male gametophytes, respectively. The female gametophytes in these plants are retained on the parent sporophytes for variable periods. The development of the zygotes into young embryos takes place within the female gametophytes. This event is a precursor to the seed habit and it is considered an important step in evolution.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one is a wrong statement?
options: Archegonia are found in Bryophyta, Pteridophyta and Gymnosperms.
Haploid endosperm is a typical feature of gymnosperms.
Brown algae have chlorophyll a and c, and fucoxanthin.
questions.solution: Mucor has non-motile and non-flagellated gametes. It belongs to the kingdom Fungi.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one is wrongly matched?
questions.solution: Polysiphonia is a genus of red algae, where asexual spores and gametes are non-motile or non-flagellated.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following is wrong about Chara?
options: Globule and nucule present on the same plant
Globule is the male reproductive structure
Upper oogonium and lower round antheridium
questions.answer: Option (B): Upper antheridium and lower oogonium
questions.solution: Chara is a multicellular green alga. Sexual reproduction in Chara is oogamous. The male sex organ is a spherical structure which is yellow in color and is called antheridium or globule. The female sex organ is oval shaped green colored structure and is called oogonium or nucule. Most species of Chara are monoecious i.e. globule and nucule are present on the same plant. Globule and nucule are present at the nodes with globule present below the nucule i.e. oogonium are present at upper portion and antheridium is present at a lower portion.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following is the characteristic feature of gymnosperms?
questions.solution: The gymnosperms (gymnos : naked, sperma : seeds) are plants in which the ovules are not enclosed by any ovary wall and remain exposed, both before and after fertilisation. The seeds that develop post-fertilisation, are not covered, i.e., are naked.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which among these is an edible alga?
questions.solution: Chlorella is a genus of single-cell green algae belonging to the phylum Chlorophyta. It is a potential food source because it is high in protein and other essential nutrients; when dried, it is about 45% protein, 20% fat, 20% carbohydrate, 5% fibre, and 10% minerals and vitamins. It is also abundant in calories and vitamins.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Given below are the stages in the life cycle of pteridophytes. Arrange the following stages in the correct sequence.
A. Prothallus stage
B. Meiosis in spore mother cells
C. Fertilisation
D. Formation of archegonia and antheridia in gametophyte.
E. Transfer of antherozoids to the archegonia in presence of water.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.answer: Option (C): B, A, D, E, C
questions.solution:
Let’s go step-by-step through the life cycle of pteridophytes:
B. Meiosis in spore mother cells occurs in the sporangia of the sporophyte to produce haploid spores.
A. Prothallus stage: These spores germinate to form the gametophyte called prothallus.
D. Formation of archegonia and antheridia in gametophyte
The mature prothallus develops sex organs: antheridia (male) and archegonia (female).
E. Transfer of antherozoids to the archegonia in presence of water
Water is necessary for the motile antherozoids (sperm) to swim to the archegonia.
C. Fertilisation occurs when the antherozoid fuses with the egg in the archegonium, forming a diploid zygote, which develops into a new sporophyte.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Gemmae are present in
questions.solution: Gemmae are green, multicellular asexual buds that are produced by some liverworts like Marchantia. Mosses reproduce vegetatively by fragmentation and budding of protonema. Pteridophytes and gymnosperms normally do not reproduce asexually.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Sphenopsida class belongs to
questions.solution: Sphenopsida class belongs to pteridophytes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following statements is WRONG?
options: Algin is obtained from red algae and carrageen from brown algae
Algae increases the level of dissolved oxygen in the immediate environment.
questions.answer: Option (A): Algin is obtained from red algae and carrageen from brown algae
questions.solution: Algin is obtained from brown algae and carrageenan from red algae.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following shows isogamy with non-flagellated gametes?
questions.solution: In Spirogyra, sexual reproduction takes place through non-flagellated and similar sized gametes, and hence called isogamous. Isogamy involves the fusion of gametes that are morphologically and physiologically similar.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Read the following statements [A-E] and answer the question which follows them
(A) In liverworts, mosses, and ferns gametophytes are free-living
(B) Gymnosperms and some ferns are heterosporous
(C) Sexual reproduction in Fucus, Volvox and Albugo is oogamous
(D) The sporophyte in liverworts is more elaborate than that in mosses
(E) Both Pinus and Marchantia are dioecious
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
(a) In liverworts, mosses, and ferns gametophytes are free-living.
(b) Gymnosperms and some ferns produce two kinds of spores, macro (large) and micro (small) spores,and are known as heterosporous.
(c) Sexual reproduction in Fucus, Volvox and Albugo Is oogamous which refers to the fusion between one large, non-motile (static) female gamete and a smaller, motile male gamete. 
(d) The sporophyte in mosses is more elaborate than that in liverworts.
(e) Pinus is monoecious, having the male and female cones on the same tree whereas Marchantia is a dioecious species having male and female organs on different thalli.Hence, statements a, b and c are correct whereas statements d and e are not correct.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In bryophytes, the gemmae help in which one of the following?
questions.solution: Asexual reproduction in liverworts takes place by fragmentation of thalli, or by the formation of specialised structures called gemmae (sing. gemma). Gemmae are green, multicellular, asexual buds, which develop in small receptacles called gemma cups located on the thalli. The gemmae become detached from the parent body and germinate to form new individuals.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: From evolutionary point of view, retention of the female gametophyte with developing young embryo on the parent sporophyte for some time, is first observed in
questions.solution: In pteridophytes, megaspore is retained for some time in female gametophyte, however, permanent retention is required for seed formation, such as in gymnosperms and angiosperm. That's why pteridophytes are the first plant that retains female gametophyte on the parent sporophyte for some time.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following plants is monoecious?
questions.solution: When male and female sex organs are present on the same plant body, such plants are said to be monoecious. Chara is monoecious as both male and female reproductive structures are in the same plant body. Cycas circinalis, Carica papaya, and Marchantia polymorpha are dioecious.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Strobili or cones are found in:
questions.solution: Strobilus is a structure present on many land plant species such as gymnosperms, club moss, horsetail, etc. It consists of sporangia bearing structure densely aggregated along a stem. Equisetum produces strobili.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In which one of the following, the ovules are not enclosed by an ovary wall and remain exposed?
questions.solution:
The gymnosperms are plants in which the ovules are not enclosed by any ovary wall and remain exposed, both before and after fertilisation.
Pinus is a gymnosperm.
Funaria is a moss.
Selaginella is a pteridophyte.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
options: Ovules are not enclosed by ovary wall in gymnosperms.
Stems are usually unbranched in both Cycas and Cedrus.
questions.answer: Option (C): Ovules are not enclosed by ovary wall in gymnosperms.
questions.solution:
Gymnosperms have a naked ovule hence ovule is not enclosed by the ovary wall.
Selaginella and Salvinia both are heterosporous.
Sequoia is a gymnosperm
Stems are usually unbranched in Cycas and branched in Cedrus.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Select the wrong statement:
options: Isogametes are similar in structure, function and behaviour
Anisogametes diﬀer either in structure, function or behaviour
In Oogamy, female gamete is smaller and motile, while male gamete is larger and nonmotile
Chlamydomonas exhibits both isogamy and anisogamy and Fucus shows oogamy
questions.answer: Option (C): In Oogamy, female gamete is smaller and motile, while male gamete is larger and nonmotile
questions.solution: Oogamy is the type of sexual reproduction in which male gamete is small and vigorously motile while female gamete is large and either non-motile or movement is less. This is found in all the higher plants as well as animals.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Winged pollen grains are present in
questions.solution: In pinus, winged pollen grains are present. It is extended outer exine on two lateral sides to form the wings of pollen. It is the characteristic feature of Pinus. The wings of the pollen rise upwards and float in the air during pollination.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Select the correct match
options: Sickle cell anaemia  -  Autosomal recessive trait, chromosome – 11
questions.answer: Option (A): Sickle cell anaemia - Autosomal recessive trait, chromosome – 11
questions.solution:
Sickle cell anaemia is an autosome linked recessive trait that can be transmitted from parents to the offspring when both the partners are carriers for the gene (or heterozygous). The disease is controlled by a single pair of allele, HbA and HbS on chromosome -11. The defect is caused by the substitution of Glutamic acid (Glu) by Valine (Val) at the sixth position of the beta globin chain of the haemoglobin molecule. The substitution of amino acid in the globin protein results due to the single base substitution at the sixth codon of the beta globin gene from GAG to GUG. 
Thalassemia is caused by mutations in the DNA of cells that make hemoglobin — the substance in red blood cells that carries oxygen throughout the body. This is an autosomal inheritance. 
Hemophilia is caused by a mutation or change, in one of the genes, that provides instructions for making the clotting factor needed to…

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In a plant, black seed color (BB/bb) is dominant, over white seed color (bb). In order to find out the genotype of the black seed plant, which of the following genotype will you cross it?
questions.solution: By simply looking at the phenotype of a dominant trait (BB/Bb), it is not possible to know the genotypic composition. That is, for example, whether a tall plant from F1 or F2 has BB or Bb composition, cannot be predicted. Therefore, to determine the genotype of a tall plant at F2, Mendel crossed the tall plant from F2 with a dwarf (bb) plant. This he called a test cross. In a typical test cross an organism (black seed color plants here) showing a dominant phenotype (and whose genotype is to be determined) is crossed with the recessive parent (bb) instead of self-crossing.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The phenomenon of pleiotropism refers to
options: Presence of two alleles, each of the two genes controlling a single trait
A single gene affecting multiple phenotypic expression
More than two genes affecting a single character
Presence of several alleles of a single gene controlling a single crossover

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A pink flowered Snapdragon plant was crossed with a red flowered Snapdragon plant. What type of phenotype/s is/are expected in the progeny ? ( I ) (2) (3).
options: Red flowered as well as pink flowered plants
Red, Pink as well as white flowered plants
questions.answer: Option (A): Red flowered as well as pink flowered plants
questions.solution:
The inheritance of flower colour in the dog flower (snapdragon or Antirrhinum sp.) is a good example to understand incomplete dominance. In a cross between true-breeding red-flowered (RR) and true breeding white-flowered plants (rr), the F1 (Rr) was pink. When the F1 was self-pollinated the F2 resulted in the following ratio 1 (RR) Red: 2 (Rr) Pink: 1 (rr) White.
So in a cross between red and pink flowers, the phenotypes expected in the progeny will be 1 Red (RR): 1 Pink (Rr), only red and pink flowers will be obtained.

Linkage group refers to number of types of chromosome present in species. Humans have 22 autosomal linkage groups, one X and one Y linkage group. Inversion and duplication cause rearrangement of genes on the same chromosome.There is a change in the order of genes within the same linkage group. 
Crossing over results in exchange of genes between two homologous chromosomes. A process that occurs during Meiosis I resulting in recombination.
Therefore, the correct answer is option b.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): Mendel’s law of Independent assortment does not hold goods for the genes that are located closely on the same chromosome.
Reason (R): Closely located genes assort independently.
Answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and  (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.answer: Option (C): (A) is correct but (R) is not correct
questions.solution: Mendel’s law of Independent assortment states that the alleles of two different genes get sorted into gametes independently of one another. However, after Morgan’s experiment, it was found that if the genes are grouped on the same chromosome, some genes were very tightly linked (showed very low recombination) while others were loosely linked (showed very high recombination). Due to the process of crossover or recombination, there is a chance for two genes on the same chromosome to behave independently or as if it is linked. Two different genes situated close together on the same chromosome tend to be inherited together, hence the law of Independent assortment does not hold goods for the genes that are located closely on the same chromosome. The isolation of alleles into gametes can be under the influence of linkage. The assertion statement is correct but the reason is false.

options: The two genes are located on two different chromosomes.
Chromosomes failed to separate during meiosis.
The two genes are linked and present on the same chromosome.
Both of the characters are controlled by more than one gene.
questions.answer: Option (C): The two genes are linked and present on the same chromosome.
questions.solution: The linkage is the tendency of closely placed genes on a chromosome to stay together during inheritance (no crossover and independent assortment). Completely linked genes do not show crossover and independent assortment; thereby produce only parental combinations. Linked genes are the genes which are closely located on the same chromosome. Option A is incorrect as genes present on different chromosomes exhibit crossing over to make more recombinant offspring; not linkage. Option B is incorrect as a failure of chromosomes to separate during meiosis results in chromosomal abnormalities. Option D is incorrect as the production of recombinant and parental offspring is determined by presence or absence of crossing over; not by type of inheritance.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: If a colour blind female marries a man whose mother was also colour blind, what are the chances of her progeny having colour blindness ?
questions.solution:
Colour blindness is a sex-linked recessive disorder due to defect in either red or green cone of eye resulting in failure to discriminate between red and green colour. This defect is due to mutation in certain genes present in the X chromosome. The female is colour blind which means she is homozygous (XCXC) for the disorder. The man she is marrying is also colorblind (XCY). Males have only one X chromosome and females have two. The XC in male is coming from his mother’s side. 
If a female (XCXC) marries a man (XCY), the chances of her progeny having color blindness is 100% . If they have girls, all of them will be getting diseased X chromosomes (one from mother and one from father). If they have boys, all of them will be getting the diseased X chromosome from their mother.

questions.solution: A plant having either dominant or recessive allele of a gene is said to be pure breeding or homozygous for that gene or trait. Due to the presence of both similar types of allele, pure-breeding plants produce progeny of their own kind. A cross pollination of two unrelated plants produces heterozygous plants having one dominant and one recessive allele for a gene. Pure breeding plants are obtained by self-pollination only. questions.solution: The frequency of recombination between gene pairs on the same chromosome can be used to measure the distance between genes. The distance between two genes is equal to this recombination frequency. If genes are located on the same chromosome, some genes can be very tightly linked hence showed very low recombination and low recombination frequency. If genes are loosely linked, they show higher recombination (high recombination frequency). As the recombination frequency is smallest in case of a and c, it means they are closely located to each other (linked genes). Recombination frequency of a and c is slightly higher but they can also be linked. The recombination frequency of a and d is highest hence the chances are more for these two genes to be located far apart. The correct sequence will be a-c-b-d.

questions.solution: Hemophilia A and hemophilia B are inherited in an X-linked recessive pattern. The genes associated with these conditions are located on the X chromosome, which is one of the two sex chromosomes. Aneuploidy refers to a condition when there is an abnormal number of chromosomes. Down syndrome, also known as trisomy 21, is a genetic disorder caused by the presence of all or part of a third copy of chromosome 21. PKU is an autosomal recessive disorder, caused by mutations in both alleles of the gene for phenylalanine hydroxylase (PAH), found on chromosome 12. Sickle cell anemia is inherited as an autosomal (meaning that the gene is not linked to a sex chromosome) recessive condition. This means that the gene can be passed on from a parent carrying it to male and female children.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Fruit colour in squash is an example of
questions.solution: Fruit colour in squash is an example of dominant epistasis in which the dominant/epistatic gene masks the effect of recessive gene giving it a white colour appearance. In summer squash, the fruit colour may be white, yellow or green. White fruits are produced by a domain epistatic allele 'W'. At another locus, Y for yellow fruits is dominant to its allele y for green fruits. Dominant white hides the effect of yellow or green. A consequence of this dominant epistasis is that the hybrid ratio is modified into 12 white: 3 yellow: 1 green. So, dominant epistasis suppresses the expression of a non-allelic gene (dominant or recessive).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Experimental verification of the Chromosomal theory of inheritance was done by:
questions.solution: Thomas Hunt Morgan, who studied on fruit flies, provided the first strong confirmation of the chromosomal theory. Morgan discovered a mutation that affected fly eye color. The chromosomal theory of inheritance states that genes are found at specific locations on chromosomes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which Mendelian idea is depicted by a cross in which the F1 generation resembles both the parents?
questions.solution: In codominance, the alleles from both parents are expressed in the F1 generation. Therefore, it resembles both parents. Individuals receive one version of a gene, called an allele, from each parent. If the alleles are different, the dominant allele usually will be expressed, while the effect of the other allele, called recessive, is masked (Law of dominance). In incomplete dominance, progeny does not resemble either of the two parents. The dominant allele does not completely mask the effects of recessive allele.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The frequency of recombination between gene pairs on the same chromosome as a measure of the distance between genes was explained by:
questions.solution: Alfred Sturtevant explained chromosomal mapping on the basis of recombination frequency which is directly proportional to distance between two genes on the same chromosome. its unit is centimorgan or map unit.

questions.question: A plano-convex lens fits exactly into a plano concave lens. This plane surface are parallel to each other. If lenses are made of different materials of refractive indices μ1 and μ2 and R is the radius of curvature of the curved surface of the lenses, then the focal length of the combination is
questions.solution:
For a plano-convex lens, the formula is given as 
\[\frac{1}{{{f_1}}} = \left( {{\mu _1} - 1} \right)\left( {\frac{1}{\infty } - \frac{1}{{ - R}}} \right)\]
\[ = \frac{{{\mu _1} - 1}}{R}\]………(Equation 1) 
For a plano-concave lens, the formula is given as
\[\frac{1}{{{f_2}}} = \left( {{\mu _2} - 1} \right)\left( { - \frac{1}{R} - \frac{1}{\infty }} \right)\]
\[\frac{1}{{{f_2}}} = \frac{{ - ({\mu _2} - 1)}}{R}\]……..(Equation 2)
From equation (1) and (2), the net focal length of combination is given as
\[\frac{1}{f} = \frac{1}{{{f_1}}} + \frac{1}{{{f_2}}}\]
\[ = \frac{{{\mu _1} - 1}}{R} - \frac{{{\mu _2} - 1}}{R}\]
\[ = \frac{{{\mu _1} - {\mu _2}}}{R}\]
\[\therefore f = \frac{R}{{{\mu _1} - {\mu _2}}}\]
