questions.question:
Consider the given data :
(a) \[HCl\left( g \right) + 10{H_2}O\left( l \right) \to HCl.10{H_2}O\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\Delta H = - 69.01\,kJ\,mo{l^{ - 1}}\]
(b) \[HCl\left( g \right) + 40{H_2}O\left( l \right) \to HCl.40{H_2}O\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\Delta H = - 72.79\,kJ\,mo{l^{ - 1}}\]
Choose the correct statement :
options: Dissolution of gas in water is an endothermic process
The heat of solution depends on the amount of solvent.
The heat of dilution for the HCl (HCl.10H<sub>2</sub>O to HCl.40H<sub>2</sub>O) is 3.78 kJ mol<sup>–1</sup>.
The heat of formation of HCl solution is represented by both (a) and (b)
questions.answer: Option (B): The heat of solution depends on the amount of solvent.
questions.solution:
From the given information
\[\Delta \]H is negative so it means dissolution of gas HCl(g) is exothermic.
\[HCl\left( g \right) + 10{H_2}O\left( l \right) \to HCl.10{H_2}O\,\,\,\,\,....\left( 1 \right)\]
\[\Delta {H_1} = - 69.01\,\frac{{kJ}}{{mol}}\]
\[HCl\left( g \right) + 40{H_2}O \to HCl.40{H_2}O\,\,\,\,....\left( 2 \right)\]
\[\Delta {H_2} = - 72.79\,\frac{{kJ}}{{mol}}\]
Hence heat of solution depends upon amount of solvent
By equation…..(2) – equation ….(1)
\[HCl.10{H_2}O + 30{H_2}O\left( \ell \right) \to HCl.40{H_2}O\]
So Heat of dilution = \[ - 72.79 - \left( { - 69.01} \right)\]
\[ = - 3.78\frac{{kJ}}{{mol}}\]
Hence option (3) is incorrect.
For heat of formation reactant should be in elemental form hence option (4) is incorrect

questions.question: \[If\;\int {\left( {\frac{1}{x} + \frac{1}{{{x^3}}}} \right)\left( {\sqrt[{23}]{{3{x^{ - 24}} + {x^{ - 26}}}}} \right)\;dx =  - \frac{\alpha }{{3\left( {\alpha  + 1} \right)}}{{\left( {3{x^\beta } + {x^\gamma }} \right)}^{\frac{{\alpha  + 1}}{\alpha }}} + C,\;x > 0,} \]\[\left( {\alpha ,\beta ,\gamma  \in Z} \right),\]where C is the constant of integration, then α + β + γ is equal to_____.
questions.solution:
\[\int {\left( {\frac{1}{{{x^2}}} + \frac{1}{{{x^4}}}} \right){{\left( {\frac{3}{x} + \frac{1}{{{x^3}}}} \right)}^{\frac{1}{{23}}}}dx} \]

 \Rightarrow \;\alpha = 23\;\beta = - 1\;\gamma = - 3 \\

x1, x2, x3, x4 \[ \to \] G.P.

(1,1), (2,2), (3,3), (1, 2) \[ \in R\]
Remaining elements are
(2,1), (2,3), (1,3), (3,1), (3,2)

questions.question:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: When an electric discharge is passed through gaseous hydrogen, the hydrogen molecules dissociate and the energetically excited hydrogen atoms produce electromagnetic radiation of discrete frequencies.
Statement II: The frequency of second line of Balmer series obtained from $\mathrm{He}^{+}$is equal to that of first line of Lyman series obtained from hydrogen atom.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
questions.answer: Option (A): Both Statement I and Statement II are true
questions.solution:
$\frac{1}{\lambda}=R Z^{2}\left(\frac{1}{n_{1}^{2}}-\frac{1}{n_{2}^{2}}\right)$
For Ist line of lyman series in H -atom
$\frac{1}{\lambda}=\mathrm{R}(1)^{2}\left(\frac{1}{1^{2}}-\frac{1}{2^{2}}\right)$
$\frac{1}{\lambda}=\frac{3 R}{4}$
for $2^{\text {nd }}$ line of Balmer series of $\mathrm{He}^{+}$
$\frac{1}{\lambda^{\prime}}=R(2)^{2}\left(\frac{1}{2^{2}}-\frac{1}{4^{2}}\right)$
$\frac{1}{\lambda^{\prime}}=\frac{3 \mathrm{R}}{4}$
As $\lambda$ and $\lambda^{\prime}$ is equal so frequency of these lines will be also equal.

$=[\mathrm{HX}] \cdot \frac{\Lambda_{\mathrm{m}}}{\Lambda_{\mathrm{m}}^{\infty}}$
$\Lambda_{\mathrm{m}}=\frac{\mathrm{k} \times 1000}{[\mathrm{HX}]}$
$\mathrm{K}=\mathrm{G} . \mathrm{G}^{*}=4 \times 10^{-5} \times \frac{15}{1}=6 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~S} . \mathrm{cm}^{-1}$
$\left[\mathrm{H}^{+}\right]=10^{-5}=[\mathrm{HX}] \times \frac{6 \times 10^{-4} \times 1000}{\Lambda_{\mathrm{m}}^{\infty} \times[\mathrm{HX}]}$
$\Lambda_{\mathrm{m}}^{\infty}=60000 \mathrm{S.cm}^{2} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$
$\Lambda_{\mathrm{m}}^{\infty}=6 \mathrm{~S} . \mathrm{m}^{2} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$

questions.question:
Let f be a twice differentiable non-negative function such that
$(\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x}))^{2}=25+\int_{0}^{\mathrm{x}}\left((\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{t}))^{2}+\left(\mathrm{f}^{\prime}(\mathrm{t})\right)^{2}\right) \mathrm{dt}$. Then the mean of $f\left(\log _{e}(1)\right), f\left(\log _{e}(2)\right), \ldots . ., f\left(\log _{e}(625)\right)$ is equal to $\_\_\_\_$‚
questions.solution:
$2 f(x) f^{\prime}(x)=f^{2}(x)+\left(f^{\prime}(x)\right)^{2}$
$\Rightarrow\left(\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})-\mathrm{f}^{\prime}(\mathrm{x})\right)^{2}=0$
$\Rightarrow \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=\mathrm{f}^{\prime}(\mathrm{x})$
$\Rightarrow \ell \mathrm{n}(\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x}))=\mathrm{x}+\mathrm{c} \Rightarrow \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=\mathrm{c}^{\prime} \mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{x}}$
$\mathrm{f}(0)=5 \Rightarrow \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=5 \mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{x}}$
Mean $=\frac{\mathrm{f}(\ell \mathrm{n} 1)+\mathrm{f}(\ell \mathrm{n} 2)+\ldots \ldots \ldots .+\mathrm{f}(\ell \mathrm{n} 625)}{625}$
$=\frac{5[1+2+\ldots \ldots \ldots \ldots+625]}{625}=1565$

questions.question: Let f(x) be a positive function and ${I_1} = \int\limits_{ - \frac{1}{2}}^1 {2xf\left( {2x\left( {1 - 2x} \right)} \right)dx} $ and ${I_2} = \int\limits_{ - 1}^2 {f\left( {x\left( {1 - x} \right)} \right)dx} $. questions.solution:
${I_1} = \int\limits_{ - \frac{1}{2}}^1 {2xf\left( {2x\left( {1 - 2x} \right)} \right)} dx$
$ \Rightarrow 2x = t \Rightarrow 2dx = dt \Rightarrow {I_1} = \frac{1}{2}\int\limits_{ - 1}^2 {tf\left( {t\left( {1 - t} \right)} \right)dt} $
$ \Rightarrow 2{I_1} = \int\limits_{ - 1}^2 {\left( {1 - t} \right)f\left( {1 - t} \right)} \left( {1 - \left( {1 - t} \right)} \right)dt$
$ \Rightarrow 2{I_1} = \int\limits_{ - 1}^2 {f\left( {t\left( {1 - t} \right)} \right)dt} - \int\limits_{ - 1}^2 {tf\left( {t\left( {1 - t} \right)} \right)dt} $
$ \Rightarrow 2{{\text{I}}_1} = {{\text{I}}_2} - 2{{\text{I}}_1}$
 $ \Rightarrow 4{{\text{I}}_1} = {{\text{I}}_2}$
$ \Rightarrow \frac{{{{\text{I}}_2}}}{{{{\text{I}}_1}}} = 4$

\[\frac{{dy}}{{dx}} = \left( {{e^{ - 2\sqrt x }}g\left( {f\left( {f\left( x \right)} \right)} \right) - \frac{y}{{\sqrt x }}} \right),y(0) = 0,\,then\,y(1)\] is
questions.solution:
f(x) = x – 1 
f(f(x)) = f(x) – 1 = x – 1 – 1 = x – 2 
g(f(f(x))) = ex–2
\[\therefore \,\,\frac{{dy}}{{dx}} + \frac{1}{{\sqrt x }}y = {e^{x - 2\sqrt x - 2}}\] which is L.D.E
I.F. = \[{e^{\int {\frac{{dy}}{{\sqrt x }}} }} = {e^{2\sqrt x }}\]
Its solution is 
\[y \times {e^{2\sqrt x }} = \int {{e^{2\sqrt x }} \times {e^{x - 2\sqrt x - 2}}} dx + c\]
\[y \times {e^{2\sqrt x }} = {e^{x - 2}} + c\]
Given x = 0, y = 0 ⇒ 0 = e–2 + c ; c = – e–2
∴ \[y \times {e^{2\sqrt x }} = {e^{x - 2}} + {e^{ - 2}}\]
\[when\,\,x = 1,\,\,y \times {e^2} = {e^{ - 1}} - {e^{ - 2}}\]
\[y = \frac{{{e^{ - 1}} - {e^{ - 2}}}}{{{e^2}}} = \frac{{\frac{1}{e} - \frac{1}{{{e^2}}}}}{{{e^2}}} = \frac{{{e^2} - e}}{{{e^5}}} = \frac{{e - 1}}{{{e^4}}}\]
Option (1) is correct

questions.question:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : Net dipole moment of a polar linear isotropic dielectric substance is not zero even in the absence of an external electric field.
Reason (R) : In absence of an external electric field, the different permanent dipoles of a polar dielectric substance are oriented in random directions.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.answer: Option (D): (A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:

R : If \[\vec E\] is absent, polar dielectric remain polar & are randomly oriented.

questions.question:
In a moving coil galvanometer, two moving coils M1 and M2 have the following particulars:
\[{R_1} = 5\Omega ,{{\rm N}_1} = 15,{A_1} = 3.6 \times {10^{ - 3}}{m^2},{B_1} = 0.25T\]
\[{R_2} = 7\Omega ,{{\rm N}_2} = 21,{A_2} = 1.8 \times {10^{ - 3}}{m^2},{B_2} = 0.50T\]
Assuming that torsional constant of the springs are same for both coils, what will be the ratio of voltage sensitivity M1 and M2 ?
questions.solution:
Voltage sensitivity = \[\frac{\theta }{V} = \frac{{NAB}}{{cR}}\]
\[Ratio = \left( {\frac{{{N_1}{A_1}{B_1}}}{{{N_2}{A_2}{B_2}}}} \right)\frac{{{R_2}}}{{{R_1}}} = \frac{{15 \times 3.6 \times 0.25}}{{21 \times 1.8 \times 0.5}} \times \frac{7}{5} = \frac{1}{1}\]

questions.question: A light wave is propagating with plane wave fronts of the type x + y + z = constant. The angle made by the direction of wave propagation with the x-axis is :
questions.solution:
The direction of propagation of light is perpendicular to the wave front and is symmetric about x, y and z axis.
∴ Angle made by the light with x, y & z axis is same.
∴ cosα = cosβ = cosγ (α , β & γ are angle made by light with x, y & z axis respectively)
Also cos2α + cos2β + cos2γ = 1 [Sum of direction cosines]
∴ α = cos-1 \[\frac{1}{{\sqrt 3 }}\]

questions.question: Let the solution curve of the differential equation $x d y-y d x=\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}} d x, x>0, y(1)=0$, be $y= y(x)$. Then $y(3)$ is equal to
questions.solution:
$\frac{x d y-y d x}{x^{2}}=\frac{\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}}{x^{2}} d x$
$\mathrm{d}\left(\frac{\mathrm{y}}{\mathrm{x}}\right)=\sqrt{1+\frac{\mathrm{y}^{2}}{\mathrm{x}^{2}}} \cdot \frac{1}{\mathrm{x}} \mathrm{dx}$
$\int \frac{\mathrm{d}\left(\frac{\mathrm{y}}{\mathrm{x}}\right)}{\sqrt{1+\left(\frac{\mathrm{y}}{\mathrm{x}}\right)^{2}}}=\int \frac{1}{\mathrm{x}} \mathrm{dx}$
$\Rightarrow \ln \left(\frac{\mathrm{y}}{\mathrm{x}}+\sqrt{1+\frac{\mathrm{y}^{2}}{\mathrm{x}^{2}}}\right)=\ln \mathrm{x}+\ln \mathrm{k}=\ln \mathrm{kx}$
$\Rightarrow \mathrm{y}+\sqrt{\mathrm{x}^{2}+\mathrm{y}^{2}}=\mathrm{k} \mathrm{x}^{2}$
$0+1=\mathrm{k}$
$\Rightarrow \mathrm{y}+\sqrt{\mathrm{x}^{2}+\mathrm{y}^{2}}=\mathrm{x}^{2}$
$y+\sqrt{9+y^{2}}=9$
$y=4$

questions.question: If the sum of the first four terms of an A.P. is 6 and the sum of its first six terms is 4 , then the sum of its first twelve terms is
questions.solution:

$$

$$

$$

& S_{12}=\frac{12}{2}\left\{2 \times \frac{11}{4}+(12-1)\left(-\frac{5}{6}\right)\right\}
\end{aligned}
$$
$$
S_{12}=6\left(-\frac{22}{6}\right)=-22
$$

in equilibrium
\[{F_{ext}} + {F_w} = {F_\ell }\]
\[ \Rightarrow {F_{ext}} = {F_\ell } - {F_w}\]
\[ = \left( {{P_0} + {\rho _\ell }gh} \right)A - ({P_0} + {\rho _w}gh)A\]
\[ = ({\rho _\ell } - {p_w})ghA\]
\[ = (1500 - 1000) \times 10 \times 3 \times (100 \times {10^{ - 4}})\]
\[ = 150\,m\]

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question:
Two charges $7 \mu \mathrm{C}$ and $-2 \mu \mathrm{C}$ are placed at $(-9,0,0) \mathrm{cm}$ and $(9,0,0) \mathrm{cm}$ respectively in an external field $E=\frac{\mathrm{A}}{\mathrm{r}^{2}} \hat{\mathrm{r}}$, where $A=9 \times 10^{5} \mathrm{~N} / \mathrm{C} . \mathrm{m}^{2}$.
Considering the potential at infinity is 0 , the electrostatic energy of the configuration is $\_\_\_\_$ J.
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{dV}=-\overrightarrow{\mathrm{E}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathrm{dr}}$
$\int_{0}^{\mathrm{v}} \mathrm{dV}=-\int_{\infty}^{\mathrm{r}} \frac{\mathrm{A}}{\mathrm{r}^{2}} \mathrm{dr}$
$\mathrm{V}=-\left[\frac{-\mathrm{A}}{\mathrm{r}^{2}}\right]_{\infty}^{\mathrm{r}} \Rightarrow \mathrm{V}=\frac{\mathrm{A}}{\mathrm{r}}$
$\mathrm{U}=\mathrm{U}_{\text {self }}+\mathrm{U}_{\text {interaction }}$
$=\mathrm{q}_{1} \mathrm{v}_{1}=\mathrm{q}_{2} \mathrm{v}_{2}+\frac{\mathrm{kq}_{1} \mathrm{q}_{2}}{2 \mathrm{r}}$
$=7 \times 10^{-6} \frac{\mathrm{~A}}{9 \times 10^{-2}}-2 \times 10^{-6} \frac{\mathrm{~A}}{9 \times 10^{-2}}$
$-\frac{9 \times 10^{9} \times 14 \times 10^{-12}}{2 \times 9 \times 10^{-2}}$
$=\frac{5 \times 10^{-6} \times 9 \times 10^{5}}{9 \times 10^{-2}}-7 \times 10^{-1}$
$=50-0.7$
$=49.3 \mathrm{~J}$

questions.question: A parallel plate capacitor with plate separation 5 mm is charged by a battery. On introducing a mica sheet of 2 mm and maintaining the connections of the plates with the terminals of the battery, it is found that it draws $25 \%$ more charge from the battery. The dielectric constant of mica is $\_\_\_\_$ .
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{C}=\frac{\in_{0} \mathrm{~A}}{\mathrm{~d}}$
$\mathrm{Q}_{1}=\mathrm{CV}$
 
$\mathrm{Q}_{2}=\left(\mathrm{c}_{\mathrm{eq}}\right) \mathrm{v}$
$\mathrm{Q}_{2}=1.25 \mathrm{cv}$
 
$c_{\text {eq }}=\frac{C_{1} C_{2}}{C_{1}+C_{2}}=\frac{\frac{\epsilon_{0} A}{3} \times \frac{K \epsilon_{0} A}{2}}{\frac{\epsilon_{0} A}{3}+\frac{K \epsilon_{0} A}{2}}$
$c_{e q}=\frac{\left(\epsilon_{0} A\right)^{2}\left(\frac{K}{6}\right)}{\epsilon_{0} A\left(\frac{2+3 K}{6}\right)} \Rightarrow C_{e q}=\frac{K \epsilon_{0} A}{2+3 K}$
$1.25 \times \frac{\in_{0} \mathrm{~A}}{5}=\frac{\mathrm{K} \in_{0} \mathrm{~A}}{2+3 \mathrm{~K}} \Rightarrow 0.25(2+3 \mathrm{~K})=\mathrm{K}$
$$
2+3 \mathrm{~K}=4 \mathrm{~K} \Rightarrow \mathrm{~K}=2
$$

$\frac{\left(\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{atm}}+\rho \mathrm{gh}\right) 2.9 \mathrm{~cm}^{3}}{290 \mathrm{~K}}=\frac{\left(\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{atm}}\right) \mathrm{V}_{2}}{300}$
$\mathrm{V}_{2}=4.5 \mathrm{~cm}^{3}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: To compare EMF of two cells using potentiometer the balancing lengths obtained are 200 cm and 150 cm . The least count of scale is 1 cm . The percentage error in the ratio of EMFs is $\_\_\_\_$
questions.solution:
$\in=\lambda \ell$
Potential gradient
$$
\begin{aligned}
& \epsilon_{1}=\lambda \ell_{1} \\
& \epsilon_{2}=\lambda \ell_{2} \\
& \mathrm{y}=\frac{\epsilon_{1}}{\epsilon_{2}}=\frac{\ell_{1}}{\ell_{2}} \\
& \frac{\Delta \mathrm{y}}{\mathrm{y}}=\frac{\Delta \ell_{1}}{\ell_{1}}+\frac{\Delta \ell_{2}}{\ell_{2}} \\
& \begin{aligned}
\frac{\Delta \mathrm{y}}{\mathrm{y}} & =\frac{1}{200}+\frac{1}{150} \\
& \frac{\Delta \mathrm{y}}{\mathrm{y}} \times 100\left(\frac{1}{200}+\frac{1}{150}\right) \times 100 \\
& =\left(\frac{3+4}{600}\right) \times 100 \Rightarrow \frac{7}{6}=1.16 \%
\end{aligned}
\end{aligned}
$$
No options matching

questions.question: Three identical spheres of mass m, are placed at the vertices of an equilateral triangle of length a. When released, they interact only through gravitational force and collide after a time T = 4 seconds. If the sides of the triangle are increased to length 2a and also the masses of the spheres are made 2m, then they will collide after _____
questions.solution:
\[{\text{T}} \propto {{\text{m}}^{\text{x}}}{{\text{G}}^{\text{y}}}{{\text{a}}^{\text{z}}}\]
\[{\text{T}} \propto {{\text{M}}^{\text{x}}}{\left[ {{{\text{M}}^{ - 1}}{{\text{L}}^3}{{\text{T}}^{ - 2}}} \right]^{\text{y}}}{\left[ {\text{L}} \right]^{\text{z}}}\]
\[{\text{T}} \propto {{\text{M}}^{{\text{x}} - {\text{y}}}}{{\text{L}}^{3{\text{y}} + {\text{z}}}}{{\text{T}}^{ - 2{\text{y}}}}\]
x – y = 0 ⇒ x = y
\[ - 2{\text{y}} = 1 \Rightarrow y = - \frac{1}{2},{\text{x = }} - \frac{1}{2}\]
⇒ 3y + z = 0
\[{\text{z}} = - 3{\text{y}} = \frac{3}{2}\]
Hence 
\[{\text{T}} \propto {{\text{m}}^{ - 1/2}}{{\text{G}}^{ - 1/2}}{{\text{a}}^{3/2}}\]
\[{\text{T}} \propto {\left( {\frac{{{{\text{a}}^3}}}{{\text{m}}}} \right)^{1/2}}\]
\[{\text{T}} = 4 \times {\left( {\frac{{{{\text{2}}^3}}}{{\text{2}}}} \right)^{1/2}} = 8{\text{s}}\]

questions.question: If the solution curve $y=f(x)$ of the differential equation $\left(x^{2}-4\right) y^{\prime}-2 x y+2 x\left(4-x^{2}\right)^{2}=0, x>2$, passes through the point $(3,15)$, then the local maximum value of $f$ is
questions.solution:
$\left(x^{2}-4\right) y^{1}-2 x y=-2 x\left(x^{2}-4\right)^{2}$
$\mathrm{d}\left(\frac{\mathrm{y}}{\mathrm{x}^{2}-4}\right)=-2 \mathrm{x}$
$\mathrm{y}=\left(-\mathrm{x}^{2}+\mathrm{C}\right)\left(\mathrm{x}^{2}-4\right)$
for $x=3 y=15 \Rightarrow C=12$
$\mathrm{y}=\left(-\mathrm{x}^{2}+12\right)\left(\mathrm{x}^{2}-4\right)$
$y^{1}=0 \Rightarrow x=2 \sqrt{2}$
$y_{\text {local maxi . }}=\left((2 \sqrt{2})^{2}-4\right)\left(-(2 \sqrt{2})^{2}+12\right)$
$=16$

If $\vec{v} \cdot \vec{c}=11$ and the length of the projection of $\vec{b}$ on $\vec{c}$ is $p$, then $9 p^{2}$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
$\vec{a}=\hat{i}-2 \hat{j}+3 \hat{k}, \vec{b}=2 \hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k}, \vec{c}=\lambda \hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}$, and $\vec{v}=\vec{a} \times \vec{b}$. If $\vec{v} \cdot \vec{c}=11$
$\vec{v}=(\vec{a} \times \vec{b})=(-\hat{i}+7 \hat{j}+5 \hat{k})$
$\vec{v} \cdot \vec{c}=11=(-\hat{i}+7 \hat{j}+5 \hat{k}) \cdot(\lambda \hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k})=11$
$\Rightarrow-\lambda+7+5=11$
$\Rightarrow \lambda=1$
Length of projection of $\vec{b}$ on $\vec{c}=\vec{b} \cdot \hat{c}$
$\Rightarrow\left|(2 \hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k}) \cdot \frac{(\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k})}{\sqrt{3}}\right|=\frac{2+1-1}{\sqrt{3}}=P=\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}$
$\Rightarrow 9 \mathrm{p}^{2}=9\left(\frac{4}{3}\right)=12$

questions.question: The sum of all the real solutions of the equation $\log _{(x+3)}\left(6 x^{2}+28 x+30\right)=5-2 \log _{(6 x+10)}\left(x^{2}+6 x+9\right)$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
$\log _{x+3}[(x+3)(6 x+10)]=5-2 \log _{6 x+10}(x+3)^{2}$
$1+\log _{\mathrm{x}+3}(6 \mathrm{x}+10)=5-4 \log _{6 \mathrm{x}+10}(\mathrm{x}+3)$
Let $\log _{(x+3)}(6 \mathrm{x}+10)=\mathrm{A}$
$\Rightarrow A+\frac{4}{A}=4$ or $A=2$
$\Rightarrow \log _{(\mathrm{x}+3)}(6 \mathrm{x}+10)=2$
$\Rightarrow 6 \mathrm{x}+10=(\mathrm{x}+3)^{2}$
$\Rightarrow 6 \mathrm{x}+10=\mathrm{x}^{2}+9+6 \mathrm{x}$
$\Rightarrow \mathrm{x}^{2}=1, \mathrm{x}= \pm 1$
So sum of roots $=0$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
For the following gas phase equilibrium reaction at constant temperature,
$\mathrm{NH}_{3}(\mathrm{~g}) \rightleftharpoons \frac{1}{2} \mathrm{~N}_{2}(\mathrm{~g})+\frac{3}{2} \mathrm{H}_{2}(\mathrm{~g})$
If the total pressure is $\sqrt{3} \mathrm{~atm}$ and the pressure equilibrium constant $\left(\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{p}}\right)$ is 9 atm , then the degree of dissociation is given as $\left(\mathrm{x} \times 10^{-2}\right)^{-1 / 2}$.
The value of $x$ is ________ (Nearest integer)
questions.solution:
$
\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{P}}=\frac{\left(\frac{\alpha}{2}\right)^{1 / 2}\left(\frac{3 \alpha}{2}\right)^{3 / 2}}{(1-\alpha)}\left[\frac{\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{T}}}{1+\alpha}\right]^{1} \quad\left[\because \mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{T}}=\sqrt{3} \mathrm{~atm}\right] \\
& 9=\frac{\left(\frac{\alpha}{2}\right)^{1 / 2}\left(\frac{3 \alpha}{2}\right)^{3 / 2}}{(1-\alpha)} \times \frac{(3)^{1 / 2}}{1+\alpha} \\
& 9=\frac{9\left(\frac{\alpha}{2}\right)^{2}}{1-\alpha^{2}} \\
& 1-\alpha^{2}=\frac{\alpha^{2}}{4} \\
& \frac{5 \alpha^{2}}{4}=1 \\
& \alpha^{2}=0.8 \\
& \alpha=(0.8)^{1 / 2} \\
& \alpha=\left[\frac{1}{0.8}\right]^{-1 / 2} \\
& \alpha=\left[125 \times 10^{-2}\right]^{-1 / 2} \\
& \mathrm{x}=125 .
\end{aligned}
$$

questions.question:
Observe the following reactions at $\mathrm{T}(\mathrm{K})$
I. A → products.
II. $5 \mathrm{Br}^{-}(\mathrm{aq})+\mathrm{BrO}_{3}^{-}(\mathrm{aq})+6 \mathrm{H}^{+}(\mathrm{aq}) \rightarrow 3 \mathrm{Br}_{2}(\mathrm{aq})+ 3 \mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}(\mathrm{l})$
Both the reactions are started at 10.00 am . The rates of these reactions at 10.10 am are same. The value of $-\frac{\Delta\left[\mathrm{Br}^{-}\right]}{\Delta \mathrm{t}}$ at 10.10 am is $2 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~mol} \mathrm{~L}^{-1} \mathrm{Min}^{-1}$. The concentration of A at 10.10 am is $10^{-2} \mathrm{~mol} \mathrm{~L}^{-1}$. What is the first order rate constant (in $\mathrm{min}^{-1}$ ) of reaction I?
questions.solution:
At $\mathrm{t}=10$ minutes
Rate of reaction $=-\frac{1}{5} \frac{\Delta\left[\mathrm{Br}^{-}\right]}{\Delta \mathrm{t}}=\frac{1}{5} \times\left(2 \times 10^{-4}\right) =4 \times 10^{-5}$
For reaction $\mathrm{A} \rightarrow \mathrm{P}$
at $\mathrm{t}=10$ minutes
Rate of reaction $=4 \times 10^{-5}=\mathrm{k}[\mathrm{A}]$
$\mathrm{k}=4 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~min}^{-1}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The work functions of two metals ( $\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{A}}$ and $\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{B}}$ ) are in the $1: 2$ ratio. When these metals are exposed to photons of energy 6 eV , the kinetic energy of liberated electrons of $M_{A}: M_{B}$ is in the ratio of 2.642 : 1. The work functions (in eV ) of $\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{A}}$ and $\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{B}}$ are respectively.
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{KE}_{\text {max }}=\mathrm{E}-\phi$
\[{\left( {{\text{K}}{{\text{E}}_{\max }}} \right)_1} = 6 - {\phi _1}\] …. (1)
\[{\left( {{\text{K}}{{\text{E}}_{\max }}} \right)_2} = 6 - {\phi _2}\] …. (2)
By eq. (1) divide eq. (2)
$\frac{\left(\mathrm{KE}_{\text {max }}\right)_{1}}{\left(\mathrm{KE}_{\text {max }}\right)_{2}}=\frac{2.642}{1}=\frac{6-\phi_{1}}{6-\phi_{2}}$
$\frac{2.642}{1}=\frac{6-\phi_{1}}{6-2 \phi_{1}}$
$\phi_{1}=2.3 \mathrm{eV}$
$\phi_{2}=4.6 \mathrm{eV}$.

questions.question:
$\mathrm{X}_{2}(\mathrm{~g})+\mathrm{Y}_{2}(\mathrm{~g}) \rightleftharpoons 2 \mathrm{Z}(\mathrm{g})$
$\mathrm{X}_{2}(\mathrm{~g})$ and $\mathrm{Y}_{2}(\mathrm{~g})$ are added to a 1 L flask and it is found that the system attains the above equilibrium at $\mathrm{T}(\mathrm{K})$ with the number of moles of $\mathrm{X}_{2}(\mathrm{~g}), \mathrm{Y}_{2}(\mathrm{~g})$ and $\mathrm{Z}(\mathrm{g})$ being 3, 3 and 9 mol respectively (equilibrium moles). Under this conditions of equilibrium, 10 mol of $\mathrm{Z}(\mathrm{g})$ is added to the flask and the temperature is maintained at $\mathrm{T}(\mathrm{K})$. Then the number of moles of $\mathrm{Z}(\mathrm{g})$ in the flask when the new equilibrium is established is $\_\_\_\_$ . (Nearest integer).
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{X}_{2}(\mathrm{~g})+\mathrm{Y}_{2}(\mathrm{~g}) \rightleftharpoons 2 \mathrm{Z}(\mathrm{g})$
$\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{C}}=\frac{(9)^{2}}{3 \times 3}=9$
Now 10 moles of $Z$ are added then reaction will move in backward direction.
$\mathrm{X}_{2}(\mathrm{~g})+\mathrm{Y}_{2}(\mathrm{~g}) \rightleftharpoons 2 \mathrm{Z}(\mathrm{g})$
$3+\mathrm{X} \quad 3+\mathrm{X} \quad 19-2 \mathrm{X}$
$\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{C}}=\frac{(19-2 \mathrm{X})^{2}}{(3+\mathrm{X})(3+\mathrm{X})}=9$
$\frac{19-2 X}{3+X}=3$
$19-2 X=9+3 X$
$10=5 \mathrm{X}$
$\mathrm{X}=2$
At equilibrium ⇒ moles of $\mathrm{Z}=19-2 \times 2$

$$
=15 \text { moles }
$$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question:
A point charge of $10^{-8} \mathrm{C}$ is placed at origin. The work done in moving a point charge $2 \mu \mathrm{C}$ from point $\mathrm{A}(4,4,2) \mathrm{m}$ to $\mathrm{B}(2,2,1) \mathrm{m}$ is $\_\_\_\_$ J.
( $\frac{1}{4 \pi \epsilon_{0}}=9 \times 10^{9}$ in SI units)
questions.solution:
Work done by external agent :
$\mathrm{W}_{\mathrm{ext}}=\Delta \mathrm{U} ;$
$\Delta \mathrm{U} \rightarrow$ Change in potential energy in taking the charge from initial to final configuration
$\Rightarrow \mathrm{W}_{\text {ext }}=\frac{1}{4 \pi \epsilon_{0}} \frac{\mathrm{q}_{1} \mathrm{q}_{2}}{\mathrm{r}_{\mathrm{f}}}-\frac{1}{4 \pi \epsilon_{0}} \frac{\mathrm{q}_{1} \mathrm{q}_{2}}{\mathrm{r}_{\mathrm{i}}}$
Now, $r_{f}=\sqrt{(2-0)^{2}+(2-0)^{2}+(1-0)^{2}}=3 \mathrm{~m}$
$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{r}_{\mathrm{i}} & =\sqrt{(4-0)^{2}+(4-0)^{2}+(2-0)^{2}}=6 \mathrm{~m} \\
\therefore \quad \mathrm{~W}_{\mathrm{ext}} & =\left(9 \times 10^{9}\right) \times\left(10^{-8} \times 2 \times 10^{-6}\right)\left[\frac{1}{3}-\frac{1}{6}\right] \\
& =3 \times 10^{-5} \\
& =30 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{~J}
\end{aligned}
$$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A conducting circular loop of area $1.0 \mathrm{~m}^{2}$ is placed perpendicular to a magnetic field which varies as $\mathrm{B}=\sin (100 \mathrm{t})$ Tesla. If the resistance of the loop is $100 \Omega$, then the average thermal energy dissipated in the loop in one period is $\_\_\_\_$ J.
questions.solution:
Area of the loop $=1 \mathrm{~m}^{2}$
$\mathrm{B}=\sin (100 \mathrm{t})$
$\therefore \quad \phi=\mathrm{BA}=\sin (100 \mathrm{t})$
$\therefore \quad \frac{\mathrm{d} \phi}{\mathrm{dt}}=100 \cos (100 \mathrm{t})$
$\therefore \quad \mathrm{P}=\frac{\mathrm{V}^{2}}{\mathrm{R}}=\frac{10^{4} \cos ^{2}(100 \mathrm{t})}{100}$
$\therefore \quad$ Thermal energy dissipated in 1 time period
$$
\begin{aligned}
& =\int_{0}^{\mathrm{T}} \mathrm{Pdt}=\int_{0}^{\mathrm{T}} 100 \cos ^{2}(100 \mathrm{t}) \mathrm{dt} \\
& \mathrm{~T}=\frac{2 \pi}{100}=\frac{\pi}{50} \mathrm{sec} \\
& \therefore \quad \mathrm{Q}=100 \int_{0}^{\pi / 50} \cos ^{2}(100 \mathrm{t}) \mathrm{dt} \\
& \quad=100 \int_{0}^{\pi / 50} \frac{1+\cos 200 \mathrm{t}}{2} \mathrm{dt} \\
& =100\left[\frac{\pi}{100}\right]=\pi
\end{aligned}
$$
Correct option (c)

questions.question: Two strings (A, B) having linear densities $\mu_{\mathrm{A}}=2 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~kg} / \mathrm{m}$ and $\mu_{\mathrm{B}}=4 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~kg} / \mathrm{m}$ and lengths $\mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{A}}=2.5 \mathrm{~m}$ and $\mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{B}}=1.5 \mathrm{~m}$ respectively are joined. Free ends of A and B are tied to two rigid supports C and D , respectively creating a tension of 500 N in the wire. Two identical pulses, sent from C and D ends, take time $\mathrm{t}_{1}$ and $\mathrm{t}_{2}$, respectively, to reach the joint. The ratio $\mathrm{t}_{1} / \mathrm{t}_{2}$ is :
questions.solution:
Given $\mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{A}}=2.5 \mathrm{~m}$,
$$
\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{B}}=1.5 \mathrm{~m}, \\
& \mathrm{~T}=500 \mathrm{~N} \\
& \mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{A}}=\sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{T}}{\mu_{\mathrm{A}}}}=\sqrt{\frac{500}{2 \times 10^{-4}}}=5 \sqrt{10} \times 10^{2} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s} \\
& \mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{B}}=\sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{T}}{\mu_{\mathrm{B}}}}=\sqrt{\frac{500}{4 \times 10^{-4}}}=5 \sqrt{5} \times 10^{2} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s} \\
& \mathrm{t}_{1}=\frac{\mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{A}}}{\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{A}}}=\frac{2.5}{5 \sqrt{10}} \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{~s} \\
& \mathrm{t}_{2}=\frac{\mathrm{L}_{B}}{\mathrm{v}_{B}}=\frac{1.5}{5 \sqrt{5}} \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{~s} \\
& \therefore \quad \frac{\mathrm{t}_{1}}{\mathrm{t}_{2}}=\frac{2.5}{5 \sqrt{10}} \times \frac{5 \sqrt{5}}{1.5}=\frac{5}{3} \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}=\frac{1.66}{1.41}=1.18
\end{aligned}
$$

questions.question:
The electric field a plane electromagnetic wave is given by :
$\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{y}}=69 \sin \left[0.6 \times 10^{3} \mathrm{x}-1.8 \times 10^{11} \mathrm{t}\right] \mathrm{V} / \mathrm{m}$.

questions.solution:
$\hat{B}=\hat{c} \times \hat{E}$
$\Rightarrow \quad \hat{\mathrm{c}}=\hat{\mathrm{i}}$ because phase of electric field is function of x .
$$
\begin{aligned}
\Rightarrow \quad & \hat{\mathrm{E}}=\hat{\mathrm{j}} \text { (given) } \\
\Rightarrow \quad & \hat{\mathrm{B}}=\hat{\mathrm{i}} \times \hat{\mathrm{j}}=\hat{\mathrm{k}} \\
& |\mathrm{~B}|=\frac{|\mathrm{E}|}{\mathrm{c}}=\frac{69 \times 0.6 \times 10^{3}}{1.8 \times 10^{11}}=\frac{69}{3 \times 10^{8}} \\
& |\mathrm{~B}|=2.3 \times 10^{-7} \\
& \overrightarrow{\mathrm{~B}}_{2}=2.3 \times 10^{-7} \sin \left(0.6 \times 10^{3} \mathrm{x}-1.8 \times 10^{11} \mathrm{t}\right)
\end{aligned}
$$
(phase is same as that of electric field)

questions.question: 80 mL of a hydrocarbon on mixing with 264 mL of oxygen in a closed U-tube undergoes complete combustion. The residual gases after cooling to 273 K occupy 224 mL . When the system is treated with KOH solution, the volume decreases to 64 mL . The formula of the hydrocarbon is :
questions.solution:
$$
\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{x}} \mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{y}(\mathrm{~g})}+\left(\mathrm{x}+\frac{\mathrm{y}}{4}\right) \mathrm{O}_{2(\mathrm{~g})} \longrightarrow \mathrm{xCO}_{2(\mathrm{~g})}+\frac{\mathrm{y}}{2} \mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{(\ell)}
$$
$\begin{array}{llccl}\mathrm{t}=0 & 80 & 264 & 0 & - \\ \mathrm{t}=\mathrm{t}_{\text {final }} & - & 264-80\left(\mathrm{x}+\frac{\mathrm{y}}{4}\right) & 80 \mathrm{x} & -\end{array}$
$264-80\left(\mathrm{x}+\frac{\mathrm{y}}{4}\right)+80 \mathrm{x}=224$
$264-\frac{80 \mathrm{y}}{4}=224$
$40=\frac{80 \mathrm{y}}{4} \Rightarrow \mathrm{y}=2$
$264-80\left(\mathrm{x}+\frac{\mathrm{y}}{4}\right)=64$
$264-80\left(\mathrm{x}+\frac{1}{2}\right)=64$
$264-80 \mathrm{x}-40=64$
$\mathrm{x}=2$

questions.question:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Pressure of fluid is exerted only on a solid surface in contact as the fluid-pressure does not exist everywhere in a still fluid.
Statement II: Excess potential energy of the molecules on the surface of a liquid, when compared to interior, results in surface tension.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.answer: Option (D): Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.solution:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Three identical coils $\mathrm{C}_{1}, \mathrm{C}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{C}_{3}$ are closely placed such that they share a common axis. $\mathrm{C}_{2}$ is exactly midway. $\mathrm{C}_{1}$ carries current $I$ in anti-clockwise direction while $\mathrm{C}_{3}$ carries current $I$ in clockwise direction. An induced current flows through $\mathrm{C}_{2}$ will be in clockwise direction when
options: $\mathrm{C}_{1}$ and $\mathrm{C}_{3}$ move with equal speeds away from $\mathrm{C}_{2}$
$\mathrm{C}_{1}$ moves towards $\mathrm{C}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{C}_{3}$ moves away from $\mathrm{C}_{2}$
$\mathrm{C}_{1}$ moves away from $\mathrm{C}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{C}_{3}$ moves towards $\mathrm{C}_{2}$
$C_{1}$ and $C_{3}$ move with equal speeds towards $C_{2}$
questions.answer: Option (B): $\mathrm{C}_{1}$ moves towards $\mathrm{C}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{C}_{3}$ moves away from $\mathrm{C}_{2}$
questions.solution:
Magnetic field through the coil is
$$
\begin{aligned}
\overrightarrow{\mathrm{B}} & =\left(\mathrm{B}_{\mathrm{C}_{2}}-\mathrm{B}_{\mathrm{C}_{1}}\right) \hat{\mathrm{i}} \\
\phi & =\left(\mathrm{B}_{\mathrm{C}_{2}}-\mathrm{B}_{\mathrm{C}_{1}}\right) \mathrm{A} \\
\varepsilon & =\frac{-\mathrm{d} \phi}{\mathrm{dt}}
\end{aligned}
$$
Find the direction according to Lenz's law
If coil move away then magnetic field decreases & vice versa
Correct Ans. (2)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The escape velocity from a spherical planet A is 10 $\mathrm{km} / \mathrm{s}$. The escape velocity from another planet B whose density and radius are $10 \%$ of those of planet A, is $\_\_\_\_$ $\mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}$.
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{e}}=\sqrt{\frac{2 \mathrm{GM}}{\mathrm{R}}}=\sqrt{\frac{2 \mathrm{G} \times \rho \times \frac{4 \pi \mathrm{R}^{3}}{3}}{\mathrm{R}}} \Rightarrow \mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{e}} \propto \sqrt{\rho} \times \mathrm{R}$
$\frac{\left(\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{e}}\right)_{\mathrm{B}}}{\left(\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{e}}\right)_{\mathrm{A}}}=\sqrt{\frac{\rho_{\mathrm{B}}}{\rho_{\mathrm{A}}}} \times \frac{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{B}}}{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{A}}}=\sqrt{\frac{0.1 \rho_{\mathrm{A}}}{\rho_{\mathrm{A}}}} \times\left(\frac{0.1 \mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{A}}}{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{A}}}\right)$
$\frac{\left(\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{e}}\right)_{\mathrm{B}}}{\left(\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{e}}\right)_{\mathrm{A}}}=\frac{1}{10} \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}$
$\left(V_{e}\right)_{B}=\frac{10 \times 1000}{10 \sqrt{10}}=100 \sqrt{10} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{sec}$

$\mathrm{V}=150 \mathrm{~cm}$
$\mathrm{x} \rightarrow$ measure from center
$\mathrm{x}=\mathrm{V}-\mathrm{R}$
$=150-50=100 \mathrm{~cm}$

questions.question: Electric field in a region is given by $\vec{E}=A x \hat{i}+B y \hat{j}$, where $A=10 \mathrm{~V} / \mathrm{m}^{2}$ and $B=5 \mathrm{~V} / \mathrm{m}^{2}$. If the electric potential at a point $(10,20)$ is 500 V , then the electric potential at origin is $\_\_\_\_$ V.
questions.solution:
$\overrightarrow{\mathrm{E}}=10 x \hat{\mathrm{i}}+5 y \hat{\mathrm{j}}$
$$
\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{at}(10,20)}=500 \mathrm{~V} \\
& \Delta \mathrm{~V}-\int \overrightarrow{\mathrm{E}} \cdot \mathrm{~d} \overrightarrow{\mathrm{r}}
\end{aligned}
$$
$500-V_{0}=-\int_{(0,0)}^{(10,20)}(10 x \hat{i}+5 y \hat{j}) \cdot(d x \hat{i}+d y \hat{j})$
$500-V_{0}=-\left[5 x^{2}+\frac{5 y^{2}}{2}\right]_{(0,0)}^{(10,20)}$
$\mathrm{V}_{0}-500=\left(500+5 \times \frac{400}{2}\right)-(0-0)$
$\mathrm{V}_{0}-500=500+1000$
$\mathrm{V}_{0}=2000 \mathrm{~V}$

questions.question:
$7.9 \mathrm{MeV} \alpha$-particle scatters from a target material of atomic number 79. From the given data the estimated diameter of nuclei of the target material is (approximately) $\_\_\_\_$ m.
$\left[\frac{1}{4 \pi \epsilon_{\mathrm{o}}}=9 \times 10^{9} \mathrm{Nm}^{2} / \mathrm{C}^{2}\right.$ and electron charge $\left.=1.6 \times 10^{-19} \mathrm{C}\right]$
questions.solution:
By mechanical energy conservation
 
$(\mathrm{Me})_{\mathrm{i}}=(\mathrm{Me})_{\mathrm{f}}$
$\mathrm{PE}_{\mathrm{i}}+\mathrm{KE}_{\mathrm{i}}=\mathrm{PE}_{\mathrm{f}}+\mathrm{KE}_{\mathrm{f}}$
$0+7.9 \times 10^{6} \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19}=\frac{\mathrm{k}(2 \mathrm{e})(\mathrm{Ze})}{\mathrm{r}}+0$
$\mathrm{r}=\frac{9 \times 10^{9} \times 2 \times\left(1.6 \times 10^{-19}\right)^{2} \times 79}{7.9 \times 10^{6} \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19}}=2.88 \times 10^{-14} \mathrm{~m}$
For diameter ⇒ D = $2 \mathrm{r}=5.76 \times 10^{-14} \mathrm{~m}$

If $2 \sum_{n=1}^{40}\left(P_{n}\right)^{\frac{1}{n}}=\frac{3^{\alpha}-1}{3^{\beta}}$ and $\operatorname{gcd}(\alpha, \beta)=1$, then $\alpha+\beta$ is equal to
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{n}}=729.81 .9 \ldots \ldots$. ( n terms)
$$
\begin{aligned}
& =3^{6} \cdot 3^{4} \cdot 3^{2} \ldots \ldots \cdot 3^{-2 n+8} \\
& P_{n}=3^{6+4+2+\ldots \ldots+(-2 n+8)}=3^{n(7-n)} \\
& P_{n}^{1 / n}=3^{7-n}
\end{aligned}
$$
$$
\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow \sum_{n=1}^{40}\left(P_{n}\right)^{\frac{1}{n}}=3^{6}+3^{5}+\ldots . .+(40 \text { terms }) \\
& =3^{6}\left[\frac{1-\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^{40}}{1-\frac{1}{3}}\right] \\
& =\frac{3^{6}\left[3^{40}-1\right] \times 3^{1}}{3^{40} \times 2} \\
& \sum\left(P_{n}\right)^{\frac{1}{n}}=\frac{\left(3^{40}-1\right)}{2 \times 3^{33}}, \quad \alpha=40 \\
& \alpha+\beta=73
\end{aligned}
$$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The largest value of n , for which $40^{\mathrm{n}}$ divides 60 !, is
questions.solution:
$40^{\mathrm{n}}=2^{3 \mathrm{n}} \times 5^{\mathrm{n}}$
$$
\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{E}_{2}(60!)=\left[\frac{60}{2}\right]+\left[\frac{60}{2^{2}}\right]+\left[\frac{60}{2^{3}}\right]+\left[\frac{60}{2^{4}}\right]+\left[\frac{60}{2^{5}}\right] \\
& =30+15+7+3+1=56 \\
& \mathrm{E}_{5}(60!)=\left[\frac{60}{5}\right]+\left[\frac{60}{5^{2}}\right] \\
& =12+2=14 \\
& 40^{\mathrm{n}}=\left(2^{3}\right)^{\mathrm{n}} \times 5^{\mathrm{n}}=\left(2^{3} \times 5\right)^{\mathrm{n}} \\
& 60!=2^{56} \times 5^{14} \ldots=2^{14} \cdot\left(2^{3} \cdot 5\right)^{14}
\end{aligned}
$$
$\therefore $ Maximum value of n is 14 .

questions.solution:
$\sqrt{2}=\frac{\left|\begin{array}{ccc}-1 & 1 & 3 \\ \alpha & -1 & -\alpha \\ \alpha & 2 & 2 \alpha\end{array}\right|}{\left|\begin{array}{ccc}\hat{i} & j & k \\ \alpha & -1 & -\alpha \\ \alpha & 2 & 2 \alpha\end{array}\right|}$
$$
\begin{aligned}
\sqrt{2}= & \frac{-1(-2 \alpha+2 \alpha)-1\left(2 \alpha^{2}+\alpha^{2}\right)+3(2 \alpha+\alpha)}{\left|\hat{\mathrm{i}}(-2 \alpha+2 \alpha)-\hat{\mathrm{j}}\left(2 \alpha^{2}+\alpha^{2}\right)+\hat{\mathrm{k}}(2 \alpha+\alpha)\right|} \\
& \sqrt{2}=\frac{-3 \alpha^{2}+9 \alpha}{\sqrt{9 \alpha^{4}+9 \alpha^{2}}} \\
& \sqrt{2}=\frac{-\alpha+3}{\sqrt{\alpha^{2}+1}} \\
& \Rightarrow 2 \alpha^{2}+2=\alpha^{2}+9-6 \alpha \\
& \alpha^{2}+6 \alpha-7=0 \\
& (\alpha+7)(\alpha-1)=0 \\
& \alpha=-7,1 \\
& \text { sum }=-7+1=-6
\end{aligned}
$$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: An insulated cylinder of volume $60 \mathrm{~cm}^{3}$ is filled with a gas at $27^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ and 2 atmospheric pressure. Then the gas is compressed making the final volume as $20 \mathrm{~cm}^{3}$ while allowing the temperature to rise to $77^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. The final pressure is $\_\_\_\_$ atmospheric pressure.
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{PV}=\mathrm{nRT}$
$\frac{\mathrm{P}_{1} \mathrm{~V}_{1}}{\mathrm{RT}_{1}}=\frac{\mathrm{P}_{2} \mathrm{~V}_{2}}{\mathrm{RT}_{2}}$
$\frac{2 \times 10^{5} \times 60}{300}=\frac{\mathrm{P}_{2} \times 20}{350}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Three small identical bubbles of water having same charge on each coalesce to form a bigger bubble. Then the ratio of the potentials on one initial bubble and that on the resultant bigger bubble is :
questions.solution:
Using volume conservation
$$
\begin{aligned}
& 3\left(\frac{4}{3} \pi r^{3}\right)=\left(\frac{4}{3} \pi R^{3}\right) \\
& R=3^{1 / 3} r
\end{aligned}
$$
$\frac{\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{i}}}{\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{f}}}=\frac{\frac{\mathrm{kq}}{\mathrm{r}}}{\frac{\mathrm{k} 3 \mathrm{q}}{\mathrm{R}}}=\frac{\mathrm{R}}{3 \mathrm{r}}=\frac{3^{1 / 3} \mathrm{r}}{3 \mathrm{r}}=\frac{1}{3^{2 / 3}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A cylindrical conductor of length 2 m and area of cross-section $0.2 \mathrm{~mm}^{2}$ carries an electric current of 1.6 A when its ends are connected to a 2 V battery. Mobility of electrons in the conductor is $\alpha \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~m}^{2} / \mathrm{V}$.s. The value of $\alpha$ is : (electron concentration $=5 \times 10^{28} / \mathrm{m}^{3}$ and electron charge $=1.6 \times 10^{-19} \mathrm{C}$ )
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{V}_{\ell}=\mu \mathrm{E}=\mu \times \frac{\mathrm{V}}{\ell}$
$\mathrm{I}=\mathrm{neAV}_{\mathrm{d}}$
$\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{d}}=\frac{\mathrm{I}}{\mathrm{neA}}$
$\mu=\frac{\mathrm{I} \ell}{\text { NneA }}$
$\mu=\frac{1.6 \times 3}{2 \times 5 \times 10^{26} \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \times 2 \times 10^{-7}}$
$\mu=1 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~m}^{2} / \mathrm{v} \cdot \mathrm{s}$
$\alpha=1$

questions.question: A capacitor $P$ with capacitance $10 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{~F}$ is fully charged with a potential difference of 6.0 V and disconnected from the battery. $\mathrm{V}=2$ volt

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question:
Consider two boxes containing ideal gases A and B such that their temperatures, pressures and number densities are same. The molecular size of A is half of that of B and mass of molecule A is four times that of B . If the collision frequency in gas B is $32 \times 10^{18}$ /s then collision frequency in gas A is
$\_\_\_\_$ /s.
questions.solution:
Collision frequency $(z)=\sqrt{2} \pi d^{2} N \sqrt{\frac{8 R T}{\pi M}}$
Temp, N are same
$\mathrm{Z} \propto \frac{\mathrm{d}^{2}}{\sqrt{\mathrm{M}}}$
$\mathrm{d}_{\mathrm{A}}=\frac{\mathrm{d}_{\mathrm{B}}}{2}$
$\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{A}}=4 \mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{B}}$
$\frac{\mathrm{Z}_{\mathrm{A}}}{\mathrm{Z}_{\mathrm{B}}}=\frac{\mathrm{d}_{\mathrm{A}}^{2}}{\sqrt{\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{A}}}} \times \frac{\sqrt{\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{B}}}}{\mathrm{d}_{\mathrm{B}}^{2}}=\left(\sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{B}}}{\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{A}}}}\right)\left(\frac{\mathrm{d}_{\mathrm{A}}}{\mathrm{d}_{\mathrm{B}}}\right)^{2}$
$=\left(\sqrt{\frac{1}{4}}\right)\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{2}$
$\frac{\mathrm{Z}_{\mathrm{A}}}{\mathrm{Z}_{\mathrm{B}}}=\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{4}=\frac{1}{8}$
$\Rightarrow \mathrm{Z}_{\mathrm{A}}=\frac{32 \times 10^{8}}{8}=4 \times 10^{8} / \mathrm{s}$

questions.question:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I: For a mechanical system of many particles total kinetic energy is the sum of kinetic energies of all the particles.
Statement II : The total kinetic energy can be the sum of kinetic energy of the center of mass w.r.t. to the origin and the kinetic energy of all the particles w.r.t. the center of mass as the reference.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
questions.answer: Option (A): Both Statement I and Statement II are true
questions.solution:
$\quad K E=\frac{1}{2} m_{1} v_{1}^{2}+\frac{1}{2} m_{2} v_{2}^{2}$
$\mathrm{KE}=\frac{1}{2}\left(\mathrm{~m}_{1}+\mathrm{m}_{2}\right) \mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{cm}}^{2}+\frac{1}{2} \frac{\mathrm{~m}_{1} \mathrm{~m}_{2}}{\mathrm{~m}_{1}+\mathrm{m}_{2}}\left|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}_{1}-\overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}_{2}\right|^{2}$

$\phi=\mathrm{h} v$
$v=\frac{\phi}{\mathrm{h}}$
$\omega=2 \pi \nu=\frac{2 \pi \phi}{\mathrm{~h}}=\frac{2 \times 3.14 \times 110 \times 10^{-2}}{6.63 \times 10^{-34}}$

questions.question: A laser beam has intensity of $4.0 \times 10^{14} \mathrm{~W} / \mathrm{m}^{2}$. The amplitude of magnetic field associated with beam is $\_\_\_\_$ T. questions.solution:
$\mathrm{I}=\frac{1}{2} \in_{0} \mathrm{E}_{0}^{2} \cdot \mathrm{C}$
$\therefore \mathrm{E}_{0}=\sqrt{\frac{2 \mathrm{I}}{\epsilon_{0} \mathrm{C}}}$
$\& \frac{\mathrm{E}_{0}}{\mathrm{~B}_{0}}=\mathrm{C}$

$\mathrm{B}_{0}=\frac{10}{3} \sqrt{\frac{8}{8.85 \times 3}}$
$\mathrm{B}_{0}=1.83 \mathrm{~T}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The wavelength of light, while it is passing through water is 540 nm . The refractive index of water is $\frac{4}{3}$. The wavelength of the same light when it is passing through a transparent medium having refractive index of $\frac{3}{2}$ is $\_\_\_\_$ nm .

$\lambda=480 \mathrm{~nm}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I: A satellite is moving around earth in the orbit very close to the earth surface. The time period of revolution of satellite depends upon the density of earth.
Statement II : The time period of revolution of the satellite is $T=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{R_{e}}{g}}$ (for satellite very close to the earth surface), where $R_{e}$ radius of earth and $g$ acceleration due to gravity.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.answer: Option (B): Both Statement I and Statement II are true
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{T}=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{R}^{3}}{\mathrm{GM}}}$
$\because \mathrm{M}=\rho \cdot \frac{4}{3} \pi \mathrm{R}^{3}$
$\therefore \mathrm{T}=2 \mathrm{gp} \sqrt{\frac{1}{\mathrm{Gp} \frac{4}{3} \pi}}$
Statement I is correct.
And $\therefore \frac{\mathrm{GM}}{\mathrm{R}^{2}}=\mathrm{g}$
$\therefore \mathrm{T}=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{R}}{\mathrm{g}}}$
Statement II is correct

$\frac{\Delta \mathrm{h}}{\mathrm{h}}=+1 \%$

questions.question:
Let $f$ and g be functions satisfying
$f(\mathrm{x}+\mathrm{y})=f(\mathrm{x}) f(\mathrm{y}), \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{l})=7$ and $\mathrm{g}(\mathrm{x}+\mathrm{y})=\mathrm{g}(\mathrm{xy})$,
$\mathrm{g}(\mathrm{l})=1$, for all $\mathrm{x}, \mathrm{y} \in \mathbb{N} . \sum_{\mathrm{x}=1}^{\mathrm{n}}\left(\frac{\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})}{\mathrm{g}(\mathrm{x})}\right)=19607$, then n is equal to :
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x}+\mathrm{y})=\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x}) \cdot \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{y}) \Rightarrow \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=\mathrm{a}^{\mathrm{x}}$
$\left(\because f(1)=7 \Rightarrow a^{1}=7\right)$
So $\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=7^{\mathrm{x}}$
Now
$g(x+y)=g(x y) \quad($ put $y=1)$
$\Rightarrow \mathrm{g}(\mathrm{x}+1)=\mathrm{g}(\mathrm{x})$
so $\mathrm{g}(1)=\mathrm{g}(2)=\mathrm{g}(3)=\ldots=\mathrm{g}(\mathrm{n})=1$
Given $\sum_{\mathrm{x}=1}^{\mathrm{n}} \frac{\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})}{\mathrm{g}(\mathrm{x})}=19607$
$\sum_{x=1}^{n} \frac{7^{x}}{1}=19607$
$\Rightarrow 7\left(\frac{7^{\mathrm{n}}-1}{7-1}\right)=19607$
$7^{\mathrm{n}}-1=\frac{6}{7} \times 19607$
$7^{\mathrm{n}}=16807 \Rightarrow \mathrm{n}=5$

questions.question: The speed of a longitudinal wave in a metallic bar is $400 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$. $$
\begin{aligned}
& \vec{b}=8 \hat{i}+7 \hat{j}-3 \hat{k} \\
& \vec{c}=c_{1} \hat{i}+c_{2} \hat{j}+c_{3} \hat{k} \\
& \vec{a} \times \vec{c}=\vec{b} \Rightarrow\left(2 c_{3}-2 c_{2}\right) \hat{i}+\left(c_{3}+2 c_{1}\right) \hat{j}- \\
& \left(c_{2}+2 c_{1}\right) \hat{k}=8 \hat{i}+7 \hat{j}-3 \hat{k} \\
& 2 c_{3}-2 c_{2}=8, c_{3}+2 c_{1}=7, c_{2}+2 c_{1}=3 \\
& \left(c_{1} \hat{i}+c_{2} \hat{j}+c_{3} \hat{k}\right) \cdot(\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k})=4 \\
& \Rightarrow c_{1}+c_{2}+c_{3}=4, c_{1}=2, c_{2}=-1, c_{3}=3 \\
& |\vec{a}+\vec{c}|^{2}=|\hat{i}+\hat{j}+5 \hat{k}|^{2}=27
\end{aligned}
$$

Put $x=t^{6} \Rightarrow d x=6 t^{5} d t$
$=\int \frac{6 t^{5} d t}{t^{4}+2 t^{3}}=6 \int \frac{\left(t^{2}-4\right)+4}{t+2} d t$
$=6\left[\int(\mathrm{t}-2) \mathrm{dt}+4 \int \frac{1}{\mathrm{t}+2} \mathrm{dt}\right]$
$=6\left[\frac{t^{2}}{2}-2 t+4 \ell n(t+2)\right]+C$
$=3 \mathrm{x}^{1 / 3}-12 \mathrm{x}^{1 / 6}+24 \ell \mathrm{n}\left(\mathrm{x}^{1 / 6}+2\right)+\mathrm{C}$
$\mathrm{f}(0)=24 \ell \mathrm{n} 2+\mathrm{C}=-26+24 \ell \mathrm{n} 2$ (given)
$\Rightarrow \mathrm{C}=-26$
Now
$\mathrm{f}(1)=-35+24 \ell \mathrm{n} 3=\mathrm{a}+\mathrm{b} \ell \mathrm{n} 3$ (as given in ques.)
$\Rightarrow \mathrm{a}=-35 \& \mathrm{~b}=24$
$\Rightarrow \mathrm{a}+\mathrm{b}=-11$

questions.question:
Let f be a differentiable function satisfying
$\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=1-2 \mathrm{x}+\int_{0}^{\mathrm{x}} \mathrm{e}^{(\mathrm{x}-\mathrm{t})} \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{t}) \mathrm{dt}, \mathrm{x} \in \mathbf{R}$ and let
$g(x)=\int_{0}^{x}(f(t)+2)^{15}(t-4)^{6}(t+12)^{17} d t, x \in \mathbf{R}$.
If p and q are respectively the points of local minima and local maxima of g , then the value of $|\mathrm{p}+\mathrm{q}|$ is equal to $\_\_\_\_$。
questions.solution:
$f(x)=1-2 x+e^{x} \int_{0}^{x} e^{-t} f(t) d t$
$e^{-x} f(x)=(1-2 x) e^{-x}+\int_{0}^{x} e^{-t} f(t) d t$
$e^{-x} f^{\prime}(x)-e^{-x} f(x)=-2 e^{-x}+(1-2 x) e^{-x}(-1)+e^{-x} f(x)$
$\mathrm{f}^{\prime}(\mathrm{x})-2 \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=2 \mathrm{x}-3$
$\frac{d y}{d x}-2 y=2 x-3$
$\Rightarrow \mathrm{y} . \mathrm{e}^{-2 \mathrm{x}}=\int \mathrm{e}^{-2 \mathrm{x}}(2 \mathrm{x}-3) \mathrm{dx}$
On solving we get
$\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=1-\mathrm{x}$
$g(x)=\int_{0}^{x}(3-t)^{15}(t-4)^{6}(t+12)^{17} d t$
$g^{\prime}(x)=(3-x)^{15}(x-4)^{6}(x+12)^{17}$
$=-(x-3)^{15}(x-4)^{6}(x+12)^{17}$
 
Local maxima $\Rightarrow \mathrm{q}=3$
Local minima $\Rightarrow \mathrm{p}=-12=|\mathrm{p}+\mathrm{q}|=9$

$\mathrm{I}=\int_{-\frac{\pi}{2}}^{-1} \frac{12(1) \mathrm{dx}}{2}+\int_{-1}^{0} \frac{12(2) \mathrm{dx}}{2}+\int_{0}^{1} \frac{12(3) \mathrm{dx}}{3}+\int_{1}^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \frac{12(4) \mathrm{dx}}{3}$
$\mathrm{I}=6\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-1\right)+12(0+1)+12(1-0)+16\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-1\right)$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Let the circle $x^{2}+y^{2}=4$ intersect $x$-axis at the points $\mathrm{A}(\mathrm{a}, 0), \mathrm{a}>0$ and $\mathrm{B}(\mathrm{b}, 0)$. Let $\mathrm{P}(2 \cos \alpha$, $2 \sin \alpha), 0<\alpha<\frac{\pi}{2}$ and $\mathrm{Q}(2 \cos \beta, 2 \sin \beta)$ be two points such that $(\alpha-\beta)=\frac{\pi}{2}$. Then the point of intersection of AQ and BP lies on :
questions.solution:
Let point of intersection $\mathrm{R}(\mathrm{h}, \mathrm{k})$
$$
\begin{aligned}
& m_{B R}=m_{B P} \Rightarrow \frac{k}{h+2}=\frac{2 \sin \alpha}{2 \cos \alpha+2} \Rightarrow \frac{k}{h+2}=\tan \frac{\alpha}{2} \\
& m_{A R}=m_{A Q} \Rightarrow \frac{k}{h-2}=\frac{2 \sin \beta}{2 \cos \beta-2}=\frac{\sin \beta}{\cos \beta-1}=-\cot \frac{\beta}{2} \\
& \frac{\alpha}{2}-\frac{\beta}{2}=\frac{\pi}{4} \\
& \tan \left(\frac{\alpha}{2}-\frac{\beta}{2}\right)=\tan \frac{\pi}{4}=1 \\
& \frac{\tan \frac{\alpha}{2}-\tan \frac{\beta}{2}}{1+\tan \frac{\alpha}{2} \tan \frac{\beta}{2}}=1 \\
& \frac{\frac{k}{h+2}+\frac{h-2}{k}}{1+\left(\frac{k}{h+2}\right)\left(\frac{2-h}{k}\right)}=1 \Rightarrow \frac{k^{2}+h^{2}-4}{\frac{k(h+2)}{4}}{(h+2)}=1 \\
& \frac{h^{2}+k^{2}-4}{4 k}=1 \\
& x^{2}+y^{2}-4 y-4=0
\end{aligned}
$$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question:
Let $\mathrm{y}=\mathrm{y}(\mathrm{x})$ be the solution of the differential equation $x \frac{d y}{d x}-y=x^{2} \cot x, x \in(0, \pi)$.
If $y\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)=\frac{\pi}{2}$, then $6 y\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)-8 y\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
$x d y-y d x=x^{2} \cot x d x$
$x^{2} d\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)=x^{2} \cot x d x$
$\mathrm{d}\left(\frac{\mathrm{y}}{\mathrm{x}}\right)=\cot \mathrm{x} \mathrm{dx}$
$\int d\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)=\int \cot x d x$
$\frac{\mathrm{y}}{\mathrm{x}}=\log _{\mathrm{e}} \sin \mathrm{x}+\mathrm{C}$
given $\mathrm{y}\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)=\frac{\pi}{2}$
$\Rightarrow \mathrm{c}=1$
$\mathrm{y}=\mathrm{x}\left(\log _{\mathrm{e}} \sin \mathrm{x}+1\right)$
$y\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)=\frac{\pi}{6}\left[-\log _{e} 2+1\right]$
$\mathrm{y}\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=\frac{\pi}{4}\left[-\frac{1}{2} \log _{\mathrm{e}} 2+1\right]$
$6 y\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)-8 y\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)$
$=\pi\left[\left(-\log _{\mathrm{e}} 2+1\right)+2\left(\frac{1}{2} \log _{\mathrm{e}} 2-1\right)\right]$
$=\pi[1-2]=-\pi$

questions.question: In the potentiometer, when the cell in the secondary circuit is shunted with $4 \Omega$ resistance, the balance is obtained at the length 120 cm of wire. Now when the same cell in shunted with $12 \Omega$ resistance, the balance is shifted to a length of 180 cm . The internal resistance of cell is $\_\_\_\_$ $\Omega$.
questions.solution:
Let E is emf and r is internal resistance of cell.

questions.question:
Given below are two statements :
Statement-I : A plane wave after passing through prism remains as plane wave but passing through small pin hole may become spherical wave.
Statement-II : The curvature of a spherical wave emerging from a slit will increase for increasing slit width.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are false.
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are true.
Statement-I is true but Statement-II is false.
Statement-I is false but Statement-II is true.
questions.answer: Option (C): Statement-I is true but Statement-II is false.
questions.solution: Increasing the slit width 'a' decreases the diffraction angle ( $\theta=\lambda / a$ ) and reduces the spreading of the wave. A narrower slit produces a more pronounced spherical wave (high curvature) while a wider slit leads to a flatter, less curved wave.

Two numbers are chosen from $\{1,2,3, \mathrm{x}-4, \mathrm{y}, 5\}$ one after another without replacement, then the probability, that the smaller number among the two chosen numbers is less than 4 , is:

Mean $(\overline{\mathrm{x}})=8$ (Given)

$\Rightarrow x+y=14 \ldots .(1) \ldots$.
Variance $\left(\sigma^{2}\right)=16$ (Given)

$\Rightarrow \mathrm{x}^{2}+\mathrm{y}^{2}=100 \quad \ldots \ldots(2) \ldots$.
$\because(x+y)^{2}=x^{2}+y^{2}+2 x y$
$\Rightarrow \mathrm{xy}=48$ (sum is 14 product is 48 )
Since problem states $x>y$
$\therefore \mathrm{x}=8$ and $\mathrm{y}=6$
Now set $X=\{1,2,3,4,6,5\}$
Now we choose two numbers one after other without replacement total outcomes $=6 \times 5=30$

We want the prob. That the smaller number among the two is less than 4
$\mathrm{P}($ smaller $<4)=1-\mathrm{P}($ smaller $\geq 4)$
$$
=1-\frac{6}{30}=\frac{4}{5}
$$

questions.question: The value of $\int_{-\pi / 6}^{\pi / 6}\left(\frac{\pi+4 x^{11}}{1-\sin (|x|+\pi / 6)}\right) d x$ is equal to
questions.solution:
$=2 \pi \int_{0}^{\pi / 6} \frac{1}{1-\sin \left(x+\frac{\pi}{6}\right)} d x$ let $x+\frac{x}{6}=t, d x=d t$
$=2 \pi \int_{\pi / 6}^{\pi / 3} \frac{\mathrm{dt}}{1-\sin \mathrm{t}}=2 \pi \int_{\pi / 6}^{\pi / 3} \frac{1+\sin \mathrm{t}}{\cos ^{2} \mathrm{t}} \mathrm{dt}$
$=2 \pi\left[\int_{\pi / 6}^{\pi / 3} \sec ^{2} \mathrm{tdt}+\int_{\pi / 6}^{\pi / 3} \sec \mathrm{t} \tan \mathrm{tdt}\right]$
$=2 \pi\left[(\tan \mathrm{t})_{\pi / 6}^{\pi / 3}+(\sec \mathrm{t})_{\pi / 6}^{\pi / 3}\right]$
$=2 \pi\left[\left(\sqrt{3}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)+\left(2-\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\right)\right]$
$=2 \pi[\sqrt{3}+2-\sqrt{3}]=4 \pi$

questions.question:
Let the maximum value of $\left(\sin ^{-1} \mathrm{x}\right)^{2}+\left(\cos ^{-1} \mathrm{x}\right)^{2}$ for $x \in\left[-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}, \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right]$ be $\frac{m}{n} \pi^{2}$, where $\operatorname{gcd}(m, n)=1$.
Then $\mathrm{m}+\mathrm{n}$ is equal to $\_\_\_\_$ .
questions.solution:
$\left(\sin ^{-1} \mathrm{x}\right)^{2}+\left(\cos ^{-1} \mathrm{x}\right)^{2}$
$=\left(\sin ^{-1} \mathrm{x}+\cos ^{-1} \mathrm{x}\right)^{2}-2 \sin ^{-1} \mathrm{x} \cos ^{-1} \mathrm{x}$
$=\frac{\pi^{2}}{4}-2\left(\sin ^{-1} \mathrm{x}\right)\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-\sin ^{-1} \mathrm{x}\right)$
$=2\left(\sin ^{-1} \mathrm{x}-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)^{2}+\frac{\pi^{2}}{8} \quad$ where $\sin ^{-1} \mathrm{x} \in\left[\frac{-\pi}{3}, \frac{\pi}{4}\right]$
Then max value occurs at $\sin ^{-1} \mathrm{x}=\frac{-\pi}{3}$
Which is $2\left(\frac{\pi}{3}+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)^{2}+\frac{\pi^{2}}{8}=\frac{29 \pi^{2}}{36}$
$\Rightarrow \mathrm{m}=29$ and $\mathrm{n}=36$
$\therefore \mathrm{m}+\mathrm{n}=65$

questions.question:
The positive integer n , for which the solutions of the equation
$\mathrm{x}(\mathrm{x}+2)+(\mathrm{x}+2)(\mathrm{x}+4)+\ldots .+(\mathrm{x}+2 \mathrm{n}-2)(\mathrm{x}+2 \mathrm{n})$
$=\frac{8 n}{3}$
are two consecutive even integers, is :-
questions.solution:
$x(x+2)+(x+2)(x+4)+\ldots .+(x+2 n-2)(x+2 n)=\frac{8 n}{3}$
$\Rightarrow \sum_{\mathrm{r}=1}^{\mathrm{n}}(\mathrm{x}+2 \mathrm{r}-2)(\mathrm{x}+2 \mathrm{r})=\frac{8 \mathrm{n}}{3}$
$n x^{2}+2 x \sum_{r=1}^{n}(2 r-1)+4 \sum_{r=1}^{n} r(r-1)=\frac{8 n}{3}$
$n x^{2}+2 x \cdot n^{2}+\frac{4 n\left(n^{2}-1\right)}{3}-\frac{8 n}{3}=0$
$x^{2}+2 n x+\frac{4\left(n^{2}-1\right)}{3}-\frac{8}{3}=0<_{\beta}^{\alpha}$
$\because|\alpha-\beta|=2 \Rightarrow \frac{\sqrt{\mathrm{D}}}{|\mathrm{a}|}=2 \Rightarrow \mathrm{D}=4$
$\Rightarrow 4 \mathrm{n}^{2}-4\left(4 \frac{\left(\mathrm{n}^{2}-1\right)}{3}-\frac{8}{3}\right)=4$
$\Rightarrow \mathrm{n}^{2}-\frac{4 \mathrm{n}^{2}}{3}=-3$
$\Rightarrow \mathrm{n}^{2}=9$
$\Rightarrow \mathrm{n}=3$

questions.answer: Option (A): Catalyst does not alter the Gibbs energy change of a reaction.

questions.solution:
$A^{T}=-A$

$\mathrm{B}^{\mathrm{T}}=\left((\mathrm{I}-\mathrm{A})^{-1}\right)^{\mathrm{T}}(\mathrm{I}+\mathrm{A})^{\mathrm{T}}$

$\mathrm{B}^{\mathrm{T}} \mathrm{B}=(\mathrm{I}+\mathrm{A})^{-1}(\mathrm{I}-\mathrm{A})(\mathrm{I}+\mathrm{A})(\mathrm{I}-\mathrm{A})^{-1}$
$=(\mathrm{I}+\mathrm{A})^{-1}(\mathrm{I}+\mathrm{A})(\mathrm{I}-\mathrm{A})(\mathrm{I}-\mathrm{A})^{-1}$
$=\mathrm{I}$
$\operatorname{tr}\left(\mathrm{B}^{\mathrm{T}} \mathrm{B}\right)=3$

questions.question: Let A be the set of all functions f : Z →  Z and R be a relation on A such that R = {(f, g) : f (0) = g(1) and f (1) = g(0)}. Then R is:
options: Symmetric and transitive but not reflective
Symmetric but neither reflective nor transitive
Reflexive but neither symmetric nor transitive
Transitive but neither reflexive nor symmetric
questions.answer: Option (B): Symmetric but neither reflective nor transitive
questions.solution:
R = {(f, g) : f(0) = g(1) and f(1) = g(0)} Reflexive: (f, f) ∈ R
= f(0) = f(1) and f(1) = f(0) → must hold
⇒ but this is not true for all function so not reflexive
Symmetric: If (f, g) ∈ R ⇒ (g, f) ∈ R
Now, g(0) = f(1) and g(1) = f(0) → true
∴ symmetric
Transitive : If(f, g) ∈ R and (g, h) ∈ R 
⇒ (f, h) ∈ R
Now (f, g) ∈ R ⇒ f(0) = g(1) and f(1) = g(0)
(g, h) ∈ R ⇒ g(0) = h(1) and g(1) = h(0)
For (f, h) ∈ R we need f(0) = h(1) and f(1) = h(0)
Now f(0) = g(1) = h(0) and f(1) = g(0) = h(1)
Hence not transitive

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The sum $\frac{1^{3}}{1}+\frac{1^{3}+2^{3}}{1+3}+\frac{1^{3}+2^{3}+3^{3}}{1+3+5}+\ldots$ up to 8 terms, is :
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{r}}=\frac{1^{3}+2^{3}+3^{3}+\ldots \ldots \mathrm{r}^{3}}{1+3+5+\ldots . .+(2 \mathrm{r}-1)}=\frac{\left(\frac{\mathrm{r}(\mathrm{r}+1)}{2}\right)^{2}}{\mathrm{r}^{2}}$
$=\frac{\mathrm{r}^{2}+2 \mathrm{r}+1}{4}$
$\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{n}}=\sum_{\mathrm{r}=1}^{\mathrm{n}} \mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{r}}$
$\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{n}}=\frac{1}{4} \sum\left(\mathrm{r}^{2}+2 \mathrm{r}+1\right)$
$=\frac{1}{4}\left[\frac{\mathrm{n}(\mathrm{n}+1)(2 \mathrm{n}+1)}{6}+2 \frac{\mathrm{n}(\mathrm{n}+1)}{2}+\mathrm{n}\right]$
$\mathrm{S}_{8}=\frac{1}{4}\left[\frac{8 \times 9 \times 17}{6}+8 \times 9+8\right]$
$=\frac{1}{4}[204+72+8]=71$

questions.question: Let a circle pass through the origin and its centre be the point of intersection of two mutually perpendicular lines $\mathrm{x}+(\mathrm{k}-1) \mathrm{y}+3=0$ and $2 \mathrm{x}+ \mathrm{k}^{2} \mathrm{y}-4=0$. If the line $\mathrm{x}-\mathrm{y}+2=0$ intersects the circle at the points A and B , then $(\mathrm{AB})^{2}$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
$x+(k-1) y+3=0$
$2 \mathrm{x}+\mathrm{k}^{2} \mathrm{y}-4=0$
$\left(\frac{1}{1-\mathrm{k}}\right)\left(\frac{2}{\mathrm{k}^{2}}\right)=1$
$2=\mathrm{k}^{2}-\mathrm{k}^{3}$
$\mathrm{k}^{3}-\mathrm{k}^{2}+2=0$
$\mathrm{k}=-1$
Solving :
$2(\mathrm{x}-2 \mathrm{y}+3)=0$
$2 \mathrm{x}+\mathrm{y}-4=0$
$-5 y+10=0$
$\mathrm{y}=2$
 
$\mathrm{x}=1$
Centre $(1,2)$
$\mathrm{r}=\sqrt{5}$
So circle is $(x-1)^{2}+(y-2)^{2}=5$
Chord $\mathrm{x}-\mathrm{y}+2=0$
$\mathrm{p}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$
$\ell=\sqrt{5-\frac{1}{2}}=\frac{3}{\sqrt{2}}$
$\mathrm{AB}=\frac{6}{\sqrt{2}} \quad \therefore \mathrm{AB}^{2}=18$

questions.question: A man throws a fair coin repeatedly. He gets 10 points for each head he throws and 5 points for each tail he throws. If the probability that he gets exactly 30 points is $\frac{\mathrm{m}}{\mathrm{n}}, \operatorname{gcd}(\mathrm{m}, \mathrm{n})=1$, then $\mathrm{m}+\mathrm{n}$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{P}=(6$ tail $)+(4$ tail +1 head $)+(2$ tail +2 head $)+(3$ head $)$
$\mathrm{P}=\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{6}+\frac{5!}{1!4!}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{5}+\frac{4!}{2!2!}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{4}+\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{3}$
$\mathrm{P}=\frac{1}{64}+\frac{5}{32}+\frac{3}{8}+\frac{1}{8}$
$\mathrm{P}=\frac{1+10+24+8}{64}=\frac{43}{64}=\frac{\mathrm{m}}{\mathrm{n}}$
$\mathrm{m}+\mathrm{n}=107$

\Rightarrow \mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{n}}^{2}=80 \mathrm{n}-496 \tag{2}
\end{equation*}
$$

$\Rightarrow 4 \mathrm{n}^{2}-28 \mathrm{n}-25 \mathrm{n}+175=0$
$\Rightarrow 4 \mathrm{n}(\mathrm{n}-7)-…

questions.question: Let the parabola $\mathrm{y}=\mathrm{x}^{2}+\mathrm{px}+\mathrm{q}$ passing through the point $(1,-1)$ be such that the distance between its vertex and the x -axis is minimum. Then the value of $p^{2}+q^{2}$ is :
questions.solution:
parabola passes through $(1,-1)$ so
$-1=1+\mathrm{p}+\mathrm{q}$
$\mathrm{p}+\mathrm{q}=-2$
$$
\begin{equation*}
\mathrm{q}=-2-\mathrm{p} \tag{1}
\end{equation*}
$$

Distance from x -axis
$\frac{-\mathrm{D}}{4 \mathrm{a}}=\frac{-\left(\mathrm{p}^{2}-4 \mathrm{q}\right)}{4(1)}=\frac{4 \mathrm{q}-\mathrm{p}^{2}}{4}$
$=\frac{4(-2-\mathrm{p})-\mathrm{p}^{2}}{4} \quad$ from (1)
$=\frac{-8-4 \mathrm{p}-\mathrm{p}^{2}}{4}=\frac{-\left(\mathrm{p}^{2}+4 \mathrm{p}+8\right)}{4}=\frac{-\left((\mathrm{p}+2)^{2}+4\right)}{4}$
Minimum at $\mathrm{p}=-2 \Rightarrow \mathrm{q}=0$
$\mathrm{p}^{2}+\mathrm{q}^{2}=4+0=4$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question:
Let $P=\left\{\theta \in[0,4 \pi]: \tan ^{2} \theta \neq 1\right\}$ and
$S=\left\{a \in Z: 2\left(\cos ^{8} \theta-\sin ^{8} \theta\right) \sec 2 \theta=a^{2}, \theta \in P\right\}$. Then $\mathrm{n}(\mathrm{S})$ is :
questions.solution:
$2\left(\cos ^{8} \theta-\sin ^{8} \theta\right) \sec 2 \theta=\mathrm{a}^{2}$
$$
\begin{aligned}
& 2\left(\cos ^{4} \theta+\sin ^{4} \theta\right)\left(\cos ^{2} \theta+\sin ^{2} \theta\right)\left(\cos ^{2} \theta-\sin ^{2} \theta\right) \sec 2 \theta=\mathrm{a}^{2} \\
& 2\left(\cos ^{4} \theta+\sin ^{4} \theta\right)=\mathrm{a}^{2} \\
& 2\left(1-2 \sin ^{2} \theta \cos ^{2} \theta\right)=\mathrm{a}^{2} \\
& 2\left(1-\frac{\sin ^{2} 2 \theta}{2}\right)=\mathrm{a}^{2}, \mathrm{a} \in \mathrm{Z} \\
& \mathrm{a}^{2}=2-\sin ^{2} 2 \theta \in[1,2] \\
& \mathrm{a}^{2}=1 \text { at } \sin ^{2} 2 \theta=1 \\
& 2 \theta=(2 \mathrm{n}+1) \frac{\pi}{2} \\
& \theta=(2 \mathrm{n}+1) \frac{\pi}{4} \notin \mathrm{P} \\
& \mathrm{n}(\mathrm{~S})=0
\end{aligned}
$$

questions.question: Let the point A be the foot of perpendicular drawn from the point $\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{a}, \mathrm{b}, 0)$ on the line $\frac{x-1}{2}=\frac{y-2}{1}=\frac{z-\alpha}{3}$. If the midpoint of the line segment PA is $\left(0, \frac{3}{4}, \frac{-1}{4}\right)$, then the value of $\mathrm{a}^{2}+\mathrm{b}^{2} +\alpha^{2}$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
$\frac{2 \mathrm{r}+1+\mathrm{a}}{2}=0 \Rightarrow 2 \mathrm{r}+\mathrm{a}=-1$
$\frac{\mathrm{r}+2+\mathrm{b}}{2}=\frac{3}{4} \Rightarrow \mathrm{r}+\mathrm{b}=-\frac{1}{2}$
 
$\frac{3 r+\alpha}{2}=\frac{-1}{4} \Rightarrow 3 r+\alpha=\frac{-1}{2}$
$2 \cdot a+1 \cdot(b-3 / 4)+3 \cdot \frac{1}{4}=0 \Rightarrow a+b=0$
$\Rightarrow 2(-1-2 \mathrm{r})+(-\mathrm{r}-1 / 2)=0$
$\Rightarrow-3 / 2=3 \mathrm{r}=1 \Rightarrow \mathrm{r}=-1 / 2, \mathrm{a}=0, \mathrm{~b}=0, \alpha=1$
$\therefore \mathrm{a}^{2}+\mathrm{b}^{2}+\alpha^{2}=1$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Two adjacent sides of a parallelogram PQRS are given by $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{PQ}}=\hat{\mathrm{j}}+\hat{\mathrm{k}}$ and $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{PS}}=\hat{\mathrm{i}}-\hat{\mathrm{j}}$. If the side PS is rotated about the point P by an acute angle $\alpha$ in the plane of the parallelogram so that it becomes perpendicular to the side PQ , then $\sin ^{2}\left(\frac{5 \alpha}{2}\right)-\sin ^{2}\left(\frac{\alpha}{2}\right)$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
Let angle between $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{PQ}}$ \& $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{PS}}$ is $\theta$
$\cos \theta=\frac{\overrightarrow{\mathrm{PQ}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathrm{PS}}}{|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{PQ}}||\overrightarrow{\mathrm{PS}}|}$
$\cos \theta=\frac{0-1+0}{\sqrt{2} \sqrt{2}}$
$\cos \theta=\frac{-1}{2}$
$\theta=\frac{2 \pi}{3}$
$\alpha=\frac{2 \pi}{3}-\frac{\pi}{2}$ So $\alpha=\frac{\pi}{6}$
$\sin ^{2} \frac{5 \alpha}{2}-\sin ^{2} \frac{\alpha}{2}=\sin \left(\frac{5 \alpha}{2}+\frac{\alpha}{2}\right) \sin \left(\frac{5 \alpha}{2}-\frac{\alpha}{2}\right)$
$=\sin \frac{6 \alpha}{2} \times \sin \frac{4 \alpha}{2}$
$=\sin 3 \alpha \times \sin 2 \alpha$
$=\sin \frac{\pi}{2} \times \sin \frac{\pi}{3}$
$=1 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$

questions.question: A uniform wire of length $l$ of weight w is suspended from the roof with a weight of W at the other end. The stress in the wire at $\frac{l}{3}$ distance from the top is $\left(\frac{\mathrm{W}}{\mathrm{A}}+\frac{2}{\gamma} \frac{\mathrm{w}}{\mathrm{A}}\right)$, where, A is the cross sectional area of the wire. $\Rightarrow \sigma=\frac{\mathrm{W}}{\mathrm{A}}+\frac{2}{6} \frac{\mathrm{~W}}{\mathrm{~A}}$
$\therefore \gamma=6$

$=10^{-6}[\hat{\mathrm{i}}+11 \hat{\mathrm{j}}+7 \hat{\mathrm{k}}]$
$\Rightarrow \overrightarrow{\mathrm{F}}=\sqrt{171} \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{~N}$
$\therefore \alpha=171$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two charged conducting spheres $\mathrm{S}_{1}$ and $\mathrm{S}_{2}$ of radii 8 cm and 18 cm are connected to each other by a wire. After equilibrium is established, the ratio of electric fields on $\mathrm{S}_{1}$ and $\mathrm{S}_{2}$ spheres are $\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{S} 1}$ and $\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{S} 2}$ respectively. The value of $\frac{\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{S} 1}}{\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{S} 2}}$ is $\_\_\_\_$ .
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{V}_{1}=\mathrm{V}_{2}$
$\frac{\mathrm{kQ}_{1}}{8}=\frac{\mathrm{kQ}_{2}}{18} \quad\left\{\mathrm{v}_{\text {surface }}=\frac{\mathrm{kQ}}{\mathrm{R}}\right\}$
$\frac{\mathrm{Q}_{1}}{\mathrm{Q}_{2}}=\frac{4}{9}$
$\frac{\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{S}_{1}}}{\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{S}_{2}}}=\frac{\mathrm{kQ}_{1}}{\mathrm{r}_{1}^{2}} \frac{\mathrm{r}_{2}^{2}}{\mathrm{kQ}_{2}}\left\{\mathrm{E}_{\text {surface }}=\frac{\mathrm{kQ}}{\mathrm{R}^{2}}\right\}$
$=\frac{\mathrm{Q}_{1}}{\mathrm{Q}_{2}}\left(\frac{\mathrm{r}_{2}}{\mathrm{r}_{1}}\right)^{2}=\frac{4}{9} \times\left(\frac{9}{4}\right)^{2}=\frac{9}{4}$

questions.question:
The diameter of a wire measured by a screw gauge of least count 0.001 cm is 0.08 cm . The length measured by a scale of least count 0.1 cm is 150 cm . When a weight of 100 N is applied to the wire, the extension in length is 0.5 cm , measured by a micrometer of least count 0.001 cm . The error in the measured Young's modulus is $\alpha \times 10^{9} \mathrm{~N} / \mathrm{m}^{2}$. The value of $\alpha$ is $\_\_\_\_$ .
(Ignore the contribution of the load to Young's modulus error calculation)
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{Y}=\frac{\mathrm{F} \ell}{\mathrm{A} \Delta \ell}$
$\therefore \frac{\Delta \mathrm{Y}}{\mathrm{Y}}=\frac{\Delta \mathrm{F}}{\mathrm{F}}+\frac{\Delta \ell}{\ell}+2 \frac{\Delta \mathrm{~d}}{\mathrm{~d}}+\frac{\Delta(\Delta \ell)}{\Delta \ell}$
$\left[\mathrm{A}=\pi \frac{\mathrm{d}^{2}}{4} \Rightarrow \frac{\Delta \mathrm{~A}}{\mathrm{~A}}=\frac{2 \Delta \mathrm{~d}}{\mathrm{~d}}\right]$
Since F is known exactly $\Rightarrow \Delta \mathrm{F}=0$
$\frac{\Delta Y}{Y}=\frac{0.1}{150}+\frac{2 \times 0.001}{0.08}+\frac{0.001}{0.5}=0.0277$
$\therefore \Delta \mathrm{Y}=0.0277 \mathrm{Y}$
$\mathrm{Y}=\frac{100 \times 1.5}{\frac{\pi}{4}\left(\frac{0.08}{100}\right)^{2} \times 0.5 \times 10^{-2}}=5.97 \times 10^{10} \mathrm{~N} / \mathrm{m}^{2}$
$\therefore \Delta \mathrm{Y}=0.0277 \times 5.97 \times 10^{10} \mathrm{~N} / \mathrm{m}^{2}=1.65 \times 10^{9} \mathrm{~N} / \mathrm{m}^{2}$

$\frac{1}{2} \in_{0} \mathrm{E}^{2}=$ Energy density

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A liquid drop of diameter 2 mm breaks into 512 droplets. The change in surface energy is $\alpha \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{~J}$. The value of $\alpha$ is $\_\_\_\_$ . (Take surface tension of liquid $=0.08 \mathrm{~N} / \mathrm{m}$ )
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{V}_{1}=\mathrm{V}_{2}$
$$
\begin{aligned}
& \frac{4}{3} \pi \mathrm{R}^{3}=512\left(\frac{4}{3} \pi \mathrm{r}^{3}\right) \\
& \mathrm{R}=(512)^{1 / 3} \mathrm{r} \\
& 1=8 \mathrm{r} \\
& \mathrm{r}=\frac{1}{8} \mathrm{~mm} \\
& \Delta \mathrm{SE}=\mathrm{SE}_{2}-\mathrm{SE}_{1} \\
& =512\left[\mathrm{~T} \times 4 \pi \mathrm{r}^{2}\right]-\left[\mathrm{T} \times 4 \pi \mathrm{R}^{2}\right] \\
& =4 \pi \mathrm{~T}\left[512 \mathrm{r}^{2}-\mathrm{R}^{2}\right] \\
& =4 \pi(0.08)\left[512\left(\frac{1}{8}\right)^{2}-1^{2}\right] \times 10^{-6} \approx 7 \times 10^{-6} \\
& \alpha=7
\end{aligned}
$$

questions.question:
The velocity of a particle is given as
$\overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}=-x \hat{\mathrm{i}}+2 y \hat{\mathrm{j}}-z \hat{\mathrm{k}} \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}$. The magnitude of acceleration at point $(1,2,4)$ is $\_\_\_\_$ $\mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}^{2}$.
questions.solution:
$\vec{v}=-x \hat{i}+2 y \hat{j}-z \hat{k}$
$\vec{a}=\frac{d \vec{v}}{d t}=-\frac{d x}{d t} \hat{i}+2 \frac{d y}{d t} \hat{j}-\frac{d z}{d t} \hat{k}$
$=-(-x) \hat{i}+2(2 y) \hat{j}-(-z) \hat{k}=x \hat{i}+4 y \hat{j}+z \hat{k}$
$\therefore \overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}$ at $(1,2,4)=\hat{\mathrm{i}}+8 \hat{\mathrm{j}}+4 \hat{\mathrm{k}}$
$\therefore|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}|=9 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^{2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A particle is rotating in a circular path and at any instant its motion can be described as $\theta=\frac{5 t^{4}}{40}-\frac{t^{3}}{3}$. The angular acceleration of the particle after 10 seconds is $\_\_\_\_$ $\mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}^{2}$.
questions.solution:
$\theta=\frac{5 t^{4}}{40}-\frac{t^{3}}{3}$
$\frac{\mathrm{d} \theta}{\mathrm{dt}}=\frac{5}{40}\left(4 \mathrm{t}^{3}\right)-\frac{3 \mathrm{t}^{2}}{3}=\frac{\mathrm{t}^{3}}{2}-\mathrm{t}^{2}$
$\alpha=\frac{\mathrm{d}^{2} \theta}{\mathrm{dt}^{2}}=\frac{3 \mathrm{t}^{2}}{2}-2 \mathrm{t}$
at $\mathrm{t}=10$
$\alpha=\frac{3}{2}(10)^{2}-2 \times 10=130 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{sec}^{2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A planet ( $\mathrm{P}_{1}$ ) is moving around the star of mass 2M in the orbit of radius R . Another planet ( $\mathrm{P}_{2}$ ) is moving around another star of mass 4M in a orbit of radius $2 R$. Ratio of time periods of revolution of $P_{2}$ and $P_{1}$ is $\_\_\_\_$ .
questions.solution:
From Kepler's law,
$$
\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{T}^{2}=\frac{4 \pi^{2}}{\mathrm{GM}_{\mathrm{S}}} \mathrm{r}^{3} \\
& \therefore \mathrm{~T}_{\mathrm{P}_{1}}=\frac{2 \pi}{\sqrt{\mathrm{G}(2 \mathrm{M})}} \mathrm{R}^{3 / 2} \\
& \mathrm{~T}_{\mathrm{P}_{2}}=\frac{2 \pi}{\sqrt{\mathrm{G}(4 \mathrm{M})}}(2 \mathrm{R})^{3 / 2} \\
& \therefore \frac{\mathrm{~T}_{\mathrm{P}_{2}}}{\mathrm{~T}_{\mathrm{P}_{1}}}=\frac{(2)^{3 / 2}}{\sqrt{4}} \times \frac{\sqrt{2}}{1}=\frac{2 \sqrt{2} \times \sqrt{2}}{2}=2
\end{aligned}
$$

If a body of mass 1 kg falls on the earth from infinity, it attains velocity (v) and kinetic energy (k) on reaching the surface of earth. The values of v and k respectively are $\_\_\_\_$ .
(Take radius of earth to be 6400 km and $\mathrm{g}=9.8 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^{2}$ )
questions.solution:
M.E.C
$\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{i}}+\mathrm{U}_{\mathrm{i}}=\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{f}}+\mathrm{U}_{\mathrm{f}}$
$\Rightarrow \mathrm{O}-\frac{\mathrm{GM}_{\mathrm{e}} \mathrm{m}}{\infty}=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{mv}^{2}-\frac{\mathrm{GMm}}{\mathrm{Re}}$
$\mathrm{V}=\sqrt{\frac{2 \mathrm{GM}}{\mathrm{Re}}}=\sqrt{2 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{Re}}=\sqrt{2 \times 9.8 \times 6400 \times 1000}$
$=11.2 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{s}$
Kinetic energy $=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{mv}^{2}$
$=6.27 \times 10^{7} \mathrm{~J}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Using Bohr's model, calculate the ratio of the magnetic fields generated due to the motion of the electrons in the $2^{\text {nd }}$ and $4^{\text {th }}$ orbits of hydrogen atom $\_\_\_\_$ .
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{B}=\frac{\mu_{0} \mathrm{I}}{2 \pi \mathrm{r}}$
$\mathrm{I}=\frac{\mathrm{ev}}{2 \pi \mathrm{r}}$
$\mathrm{B} \propto \frac{\mathrm{V}}{\mathrm{r}^{2}}$
$\mathrm{V} \propto \frac{\mathrm{Z}}{\mathrm{n}}$
$\mathrm{r} \propto \frac{\mathrm{n}^{\mathrm{n}}}{\mathrm{Z}}$
$\mathrm{B} \propto \frac{\left(\frac{\mathrm{Z}}{\mathrm{n}}\right)}{\left(\frac{\mathrm{n}^{2}}{\mathrm{Z}}\right)^{2}}$
$\mathrm{B} \propto \frac{\mathrm{Z}^{3}}{\mathrm{n}^{5}}$
$\frac{\mathrm{B}_{1}}{\mathrm{~B}_{2}}=\frac{\mathrm{n}_{2}^{5}}{\mathrm{n}_{1}^{5}}=\frac{4^{5}}{2^{5}}=64$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The surface tension of a soap bubble is $0.03 \mathrm{~N} / \mathrm{m}$. The work done in increasing the diameter of bubble from 2 cm to 6 cm is $\alpha \pi \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~J}$. The value of $\alpha$ is $\_\_\_\_$ . (Take $\pi=3.14$ )
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{W}=\Delta \mathrm{U}=2 \mathrm{~T}\left[4 \pi \mathrm{R}_{2}{ }^{2}-4 \pi \mathrm{R}_{1}{ }^{2}\right]$
$$
\begin{aligned}
& W=2 \times 3 \times 10^{-2} \times 4 \pi\left[9 \times 10^{-4}-1 \times 10^{-4}\right] \\
& W=1.92 \pi \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~J} \\
& \alpha=1.92
\end{aligned}
$$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: If sunlight is focused on a paper using convex lens, it starts burning the paper in shortest time when the lens is kept at 30 cm above the paper. If the radius of curvature of the lens is 60 cm then the refractive index of the lens material is $\frac{\alpha}{10}$. The value of $\alpha$ is $\_\_\_\_$。
questions.solution:
To burn in minimum time distance of paper must be at focus.
So $\mathrm{f}=30 \mathrm{~cm}$
$\frac{1}{30}=(\mu-1)\left(\frac{1}{60}-\frac{1}{-60}\right)$
$\frac{1}{30}=\frac{\mu-1}{30}$
$\mu=2$
$\alpha=20$

questions.question: In a screw gauge the zero of main scale reference line coincides with the fifth division of the circular scale when two studs are in contact. When diameter of a sphere is measured, the reading of main scale is 5 mm and $50^{\text {th }}$ division of circular scale coincides with the reference line of main scale. The diameter of sphere is $\_\_\_\_$ mm.

Reading $=$ MSD $+($ CSD $) \times$ LC - zero error
$=5 \mathrm{~mm}+50 \times 0.001-5 \times 0.001=5.045 \mathrm{~mm}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: If an air bubble of diameter 2 mm rises steadily through a liquid of density $2000 \mathrm{~kg} / \mathrm{m}^{3}$ at a rate of $0.5 \mathrm{~cm} / \mathrm{s}$, then the coefficient of viscosity of liquid is $\_\_\_\_$ Poise. (Take $\mathrm{g}=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^{2}$ )
questions.solution:
For constant speed
$\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{B}}=\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{V}}$
$\Rightarrow \rho_{\ell} \frac{4}{3} \pi \mathrm{R}^{3} \mathrm{~g}=6 \pi \eta \mathrm{Rv}$
$\frac{2}{9} \frac{\rho_{\ell} R^{2} g}{V}=\eta$
$\Rightarrow \frac{2}{9} \times \frac{2000 \times 10^{-6} \times 10}{5 \times 10^{-3}}=\eta$
$\Rightarrow \eta=\frac{8}{9} \times 10$
$\Rightarrow \eta=\frac{80}{9}$ Poise $=8.88$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: An electromagnetic wave travels in free space along the $x$-direction. At a particular point in space and time, $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{B}}=2 \times 10^{-7} \hat{\mathrm{j}} \mathrm{T}$ is associated with this wave. The value of corresponding electric field $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{E}}$ at this point is $\_\_\_\_$ $\mathrm{V} / \mathrm{m}$.
questions.solution:
$\overrightarrow{\mathrm{E}}=\overrightarrow{\mathrm{B}} \times \overrightarrow{\mathrm{C}}$
$=2 \times 10^{-7} \hat{\mathrm{j}} \times 3 \times 10^{8} \hat{\mathrm{i}}$
$\overrightarrow{\mathrm{E}}=-60 \hat{\mathrm{k}} \mathrm{V} / \mathrm{m}$

questions.question: A spherical ball of mass 2 kg falls from a height of 10 m and is brought to rest after penetrating 10 cm into sand. The average force exerted by sand on the ball is $\_\_\_\_$ N.
questions.solution:

$$
\begin{aligned}
& 2 \times 10 \times\left(10+\frac{10}{100}\right)-\mathrm{F}_{\text {sand }} \times\left(\frac{10}{100}\right)=0 \\

$$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question:
Two metal plates ( $\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}$ ) are kept horizontally with separation of $\left(\frac{12}{\pi}\right) \mathrm{cm}$, with plate A on the top. An atomizer jet sprays oil (density $1.5 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{cm}^{3}$ ) droplets of radius 1 mm horizontally. All oil droplets carry a charge 5 nC . The potentials $\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{A}}$ and $\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{B}}$ are required on plates A and B respectively in order to ensure the droplets do not descend. The values of $\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{A}}$ and $\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{B}}$ are $\_\_\_\_$ .
(Neglect the air resistance to the droplets and take $\mathrm{g}=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^{2}$ )
questions.solution:
$\frac{\Delta \mathrm{V}}{(12 / \pi) \times 10^{-2}} \times 5 \times 10^{-9}=\frac{4}{3} \pi\left(\mathrm{r}^{3}\right) \rho(\mathrm{g})$
$\Delta \mathrm{V} \times 5 \times 10^{-7}=16\left(\mathrm{r}^{3}\right) \rho(\mathrm{g})$
$\Delta \mathrm{V}=480, \mathrm{~V}_{\mathrm{A}}<\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{B}}$
Plate A will be lower potential.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two resistors of $200 \Omega$ and $400 \Omega$ are connected in series with a battery of 100 V . A bulb rated at $200 \mathrm{~V}, 100 \mathrm{~W}$ is connected across the $400 \Omega$ resistance. The potential drop across the bulb is $\_\_\_\_$ V.
questions.solution:
For resistance of bulb
$\mathrm{R}=\frac{\mathrm{V}^{2}}{\mathrm{P}}=\frac{200 \times 200}{100}=400 \Omega$
Now circuit will look like this
 
$\mathrm{V}_{1} \& \mathrm{~V}_{2}$ will be same as resistances are same
$\mathrm{V}_{1}=\mathrm{V}_{2}=50 \mathrm{~V}$
$\mathrm{V}_{\text {bulb }}=\mathrm{V}_{2}=50 \mathrm{~V}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two point charges $8 \mu \mathrm{C}$ and $-2 \mu \mathrm{C}$ are located at $\mathrm{x}=2 \mathrm{~cm}$ and $\mathrm{x}=4 \mathrm{~cm}$, respectively on the x -axis. The ratio of electric flux due to these charges through two spheres of radii 3 cm and 5 cm with their centers at the origin is $\_\_\_\_$ .
questions.solution:
For sphere with radius 3 cm and center origin
$\phi_{1}=\frac{\mathrm{q}_{\mathrm{en}}}{\varepsilon_{0}}=\frac{8 \mu \mathrm{C}}{\varepsilon_{0}}$
for sphere of radius 5 cm
$\phi_{2}=\frac{\mathrm{q}_{\mathrm{en}}}{\varepsilon_{0}}=\frac{(8-2) \mu \mathrm{C}}{\varepsilon_{0}}=\frac{6 \mu \mathrm{C}}{\varepsilon_{0}}$
$\frac{\phi_{1}}{\phi_{2}}=\frac{8}{6}=\frac{4}{3}=1.33$
$\frac{\phi_{1}}{\phi_{2}}=1.33$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A 0.5 kg mass is in contact against the inner wall of a cylindrical drum of radius 4 m rotating about its vertical axis. The minimum rotational speed of the drum to enable the mass to remain stuck to the wall (without falling) is 5 $ \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}$. The coefficient of friction between the drum's inner wall surface and mass is $\_\_\_\_$ . (Take $\mathrm{g}=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^{2}$ )
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{N}=\mathrm{m} \omega^{2} \mathrm{R}$
$\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{s}}=\mathrm{mg}$
$\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{s}} \leq \mathrm{f}_{\ell}$
$\mathrm{mg} \leq \mu \mathrm{N}$
$\mathrm{mg} \leq \mu \mathrm{m} \omega^{2} \mathrm{R}$
$\mu \geq \frac{\mathrm{g}}{\omega^{2} \mathrm{R}}$
$\mu_{\text {min }}=\frac{\mathrm{g}}{\omega^{2} \mathrm{R}}=\frac{10}{10^{2} \times 1}=0.1$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A circular current loop of radius R is placed inside square loop of side length $L(L \gg R)$ such that they are co-planar and their centers coincide. The permeability of free space is $\mu_{0}$. The mutual inductance between circular loop and square loop is $\_\_\_\_$ .
questions.solution:
Magnetic field due to square
$B=4 \times \frac{\mu_{0} I}{4 \pi \frac{L}{2}}\left\{2 \sin 45^{\circ}\right\}$
$=\frac{4 \mu_{0} \mathrm{I}}{\pi \mathrm{L}} \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}=\frac{2 \sqrt{2} \mu_{0} \mathrm{I}}{\pi \mathrm{L}}$
$\mathrm{Q}=\mathrm{B} \times \mathrm{A}_{\text {circle }}$
$Q=\frac{2 \sqrt{2} \mu_{0} I}{\pi L} \times \pi R^{2}$
$\mathrm{Q}=\frac{2 \sqrt{2} \mu_{0} \mathrm{R}^{2}}{\mathrm{~L}} \mathrm{I}$

Inductance $=\frac{2 \sqrt{2} \mu_{0} R^{2}}{L}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Dimensions of universal gravitational constant (G) in terms of Planck's constant ( $h$ ), distance ( $L$ ), mass ( $M$ ) and time ( $T$ ) are $\_\_\_\_$ .
questions.solution:
Energy $=\frac{\mathrm{hc}}{\lambda}=\frac{\mathrm{GM}_{1} \mathrm{M}_{2}}{\mathrm{r}}$
$\left[\mathrm{ML}^{2} \mathrm{~T}^{-2}\right]=[\mathrm{h}]\left[\mathrm{T}^{-1}\right]=[\mathrm{G}]\left[\mathrm{M}^{2} \mathrm{~L}^{-1}\right]$
