questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In a Young's double slit experiment, the intensity at some point on the screen is found to be $\frac{3}{4}$ times of the maximum of the interference pattern. The path difference between the interfering waves at this point is $\frac{\lambda}{\mathrm{x}}$ where $\lambda$ is wavelength of the incident light. The value of x is $\_\_\_\_$ .
questions.solution:
$I_{r}=I_{\text {max }} \cos ^{2} \frac{\phi}{2}$
$\frac{3 \mathrm{I}_{\text {max }}}{4}=\mathrm{I}_{\text {max }} \cos ^{2} \frac{\phi}{2}$
$\cos \frac{\phi}{2}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$
$\frac{\phi}{2}=30^{\circ}=\frac{\pi}{6}$
$\left(\phi=\frac{\pi}{3}\right)$

Path difference $\Delta \mathrm{x}=\frac{\phi}{2 \pi} \times \lambda$
$\Rightarrow \frac{\pi}{3 \times 2 \pi} \times \lambda$
$\Delta \mathrm{x}=\frac{\lambda}{6}$
$\mathrm{x}=6$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A particle having charge $10^{-9} \mathrm{C}$ moving in $x-y$ plane in fields of $0.4 \hat{\mathrm{j}} \mathrm{N} / \mathrm{C}$ and $4 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{k} \mathrm{T}$ experiences a force of $(4 \hat{i}+2 \hat{j}) \times 10^{-10} \mathrm{~N}$. The velocity of the particle at that instant is $\_\_\_\_$ $\mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}$.
questions.solution:
$\overrightarrow{\mathrm{F}}=\mathrm{q} \overrightarrow{\mathrm{E}}+\mathrm{q}(\overrightarrow{\mathrm{V}} \times \overrightarrow{\mathrm{B}})$
$$
\begin{aligned}
& (4 \hat{i}+2 \hat{j}) \times 10^{-10} \\
& =10^{-9}\left[0.4 \hat{j}+\left(v_{x} \hat{i}+v_{y} \hat{j}\right) \times\left(4 \times 10^{-3}\right) \hat{k}\right] \\
& (4 \hat{i}+2 \hat{j}) \times 10^{-10} \\
& =10^{-9}\left(0.4 \hat{j}-4 \times 10^{-3} v_{x} \hat{j}+4 \times 10^{-3} v_{y} \hat{i}\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

On comparing
$\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{y}}=100, \mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{x}}=50$
$\overrightarrow{\mathrm{V}}=50 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+100 \hat{\mathrm{j}}$

Phase of the motion of particle is as follows :

questions.question:
An electrochemical cell is constructed using half cells in the direction of spontaneous change
$\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{OH})_{2}(\mathrm{~s})+2 \mathrm{e}^{-} \rightarrow \mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{s})+2 \mathrm{OH}(\mathrm{aq}) \quad \mathrm{E}^{0}=-0.88 \mathrm{~V}$
and $\operatorname{AgBr}(\mathrm{s})+\mathrm{e}^{-} \rightarrow \operatorname{Ag}(\mathrm{s})+\operatorname{Br}^{-}(\mathrm{aq}) \mathrm{E}^{0}=+0.07 \mathrm{~V}$
Which of the following option is correct?
options: Fe is reduced in the electrochemical cell
questions.solution:
Overall reaction
$\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{s})+2 \mathrm{OH}^{-}(\mathrm{aq})+2 \mathrm{AgBr}(\mathrm{s}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{OH})_{2}(\mathrm{~s})+ 2 \mathrm{Ag}(\mathrm{s})+2 \mathrm{Br}^{-}(\mathrm{aq})$
$\mathrm{E}_{\text {cell }}^{o}=\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{R}(\text { cathode })}^{o}-\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{R}(\text { anode })}^{o}$
$=0.07-(-0.88)=0.95 \mathrm{~V}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
The solubility product constants of $\mathrm{Ag}_{2} \mathrm{CrO}_{4}$ and AgBr are 32x and 4y respectively at 298 K .
The value of $\left(\frac{\text { molarity of } \mathrm{Ag}_{2} \mathrm{CrO}_{4}}{\text { molarity of } \mathrm{AgBr}}\right)$ can be expressed as :
questions.solution:
For $\mathrm{Ag}_{2} \mathrm{Cr}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{4}$
$4 \mathrm{~S}_{1}{ }^{3}=32 \mathrm{x}$
$\Rightarrow \mathrm{S}_{1}=2 \mathrm{x}^{1 / 3}$
For AgBr
$\mathrm{S}_{2}{ }^{2}=4 \mathrm{y}$
$\Rightarrow \mathrm{S}_{2}=2 \mathrm{y}^{1 / 2}$
Ratio $\left(\frac{S_{1}}{S_{2}}\right)=\frac{\sqrt[3]{x}}{\sqrt{y}}$

(ii) Among B, Ca, Al, Fe

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Consider the following data
(i) $2 \mathrm{Al}(\mathrm{s})+6 \mathrm{HCl}(\mathrm{aq}) \rightarrow \mathrm{Al}_{2} \mathrm{Cl}_{6}(\mathrm{aq})+3 \mathrm{H}_{2}(\mathrm{~g})+ 1200 \mathrm{~kJ} / \mathrm{mol}$.
(ii) $\mathrm{H}_{2}(\mathrm{~g})+\mathrm{Cl}_{2}(\mathrm{~g}) \rightarrow 2 \mathrm{HCl}(\mathrm{g})+164 \mathrm{~kJ} / \mathrm{mol}$.
(iii) $\mathrm{HCl}(\mathrm{g})+\mathrm{aq} \rightarrow \mathrm{HCl}(\mathrm{aq})+83 \mathrm{~kJ} / \mathrm{mol}$.
(iv) $\mathrm{Al}_{2} \mathrm{Cl}_{6}(\mathrm{~s})+\mathrm{aq} \rightarrow \mathrm{Al}_{2} \mathrm{Cl}_{6}(\mathrm{aq})+663 \mathrm{~kJ} / \mathrm{mol}$.

The enthalpy of formation of anhydrous solid $\mathrm{Al}_{2} \mathrm{Cl}_{6}$ is :
questions.solution:
$2 \mathrm{Al}(\mathrm{s})+6 \mathrm{HCl}(\mathrm{aq}) \rightarrow \mathrm{Al}_{2} \mathrm{Cl}_{6}(\mathrm{aq})+3 \mathrm{H}_{2}(\mathrm{~g})$

questions.question: Gas 'A' undergoes change from state ' X ' to state ' Y '. In this process, the heat absorbed and work done by the gas is 10 J and 18 J respectively. Now gas is brought back to state ' X ' by another process during which 6 J of heat is evolved. In the reverse process of ' Y ' to ' X ',
options: 18 J of the work is done by the gas ' A '.
2 J of the work is done by the gas ' A '.
12 J of the work is done on the gas ' A ' by the surrounding.
14 J of the work is done on the gas ' A ' by the surrounding.
questions.answer: Option (D): 14 J of the work is done on the gas ' A ' by the surrounding.
questions.solution:
For process $\mathrm{X} \rightarrow \mathrm{Y}$
$\mathrm{w}=-18 \mathrm{~J}$
$\mathrm{q}=+10 \mathrm{~J}$
$\Delta \mathrm{U}=\mathrm{q}+\mathrm{w}$
$\Delta \mathrm{U}_{\mathrm{X} \rightarrow \mathrm{Y}}=10+(-18)=-8 \mathrm{~J}$
For reverse process :
$\Delta \mathrm{U}_{\mathrm{Y} \rightarrow \mathrm{X}}=8 \mathrm{~J}$
$\mathrm{q}=-6 \mathrm{~J}$
$\Delta \mathrm{U}=\mathrm{q}+\mathrm{w}$
$8=-6+w$
$\mathrm{w}=14 \mathrm{~J}$

questions.question:
The time taken by a block of mass $m$ to slide down from the highest point to the lowest point on a rough inclined plane is $50 \%$ more compared to the time taken by the same block on identical inclined smooth plane. Both inclined planes are at $45^{\circ}$ with the horizontal. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the rough inclined surface and block is
$\_\_\_\_$ .
questions.solution:
For Rough incline plane
$\mathrm{a}=\mathrm{g}(\sin \theta-\mu \cos \theta)$
$\mathrm{t}_{1}=\sqrt{\frac{2 \ell}{\mathrm{~g}(\sin \theta-\mu \cos \theta)}}$
For smooth incline plane
$\mathrm{t}_{2}=\sqrt{\frac{2 \ell}{\mathrm{~g} \sin \theta}} \& \mathrm{t}_{1}=1.5 \mathrm{t}_{2}$
$\sqrt{\frac{2 \ell}{g(\sin \theta-\mu \cos \theta)}}=\frac{3}{2} \times \sqrt{\frac{2 \ell}{g \sin \theta}}$
$(\sin \theta-\mu \cos \theta)=\frac{4}{9} \sin \theta$
$\frac{5}{9} \sin \theta=\mu \cos \theta \Rightarrow \frac{5}{9} \tan \theta$
$\mu=\frac{5}{9} \tan 45^{\circ}=\frac{5}{9}$

$\mathrm{V}=\overrightarrow{\mathrm{V}}_{\mathrm{SB}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question:
The temperature of a metal strip having coefficient of linear expansion $\alpha$ is increased from $\mathrm{T}_{1}$ to $\mathrm{T}_{2}$ resulting in increase of its length by $\Delta \mathrm{L}_{1}$. The temperature is further increased from $\mathrm{T}_{2}$ to $\mathrm{T}_{3}$ such that the increase in its length is $\Delta \mathrm{L}_{2}$.
Given $\mathrm{T}_{3}+\mathrm{T}_{1}=2 \mathrm{~T}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{T}_{2}-\mathrm{T}_{1}=\Delta \mathrm{T}$, the value of $\Delta \mathrm{L}_{2}$ is $\_\_\_\_$ .
questions.solution:
$\Delta \mathrm{L}_{1}=\mathrm{L}_{0} \alpha\left(\mathrm{~T}_{2}-\mathrm{T}_{1}\right)$
So final length at $\mathrm{T}_{2}=\mathrm{L}_{0}+\Delta \mathrm{L}_{1}$
$\Delta \mathrm{L}_{2}=\left(\mathrm{L}_{0}+\Delta \mathrm{L}_{1}\right) \alpha\left(\mathrm{T}_{3}-\mathrm{T}_{2}\right)$ and $\mathrm{T}_{3}-\mathrm{T}_{2}=\mathrm{T}_{2}-\mathrm{T}_{1}=\Delta \mathrm{T}$
$\Delta \mathrm{L}_{2}=\mathrm{L}_{0} \alpha \Delta \mathrm{~T}+\Delta \mathrm{L}_{1} \alpha \Delta \mathrm{~T}$
$=\Delta \mathrm{L}_{1}+\Delta \mathrm{L}_{1} \alpha \Delta \mathrm{~T}$
$=\Delta \mathrm{L}_{1}(1+\alpha \Delta \mathrm{T})$

questions.question:
If $\mathrm{f}: \mathrm{N} \rightarrow \mathrm{Z}$ is defined by
$f(n)=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}n & -1 & -5 \\ -2 n^{2} & 3(2 k+1) & 2 k+1 \\ -3 n^{3} & 3 k(2 k+1) & 3 k(k+2)+1\end{array}\right|, k \in N$, and $\sum_{n=1}^{k} f(n)=98$, then $k$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
$f(n)=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}n & -1 & -5 \\ -2 n^{2} & 3(2 k+1) & 2 k+1 \\ -3 n^{3} & 3 k(2 k+1) & 3 k(k+2)+1\end{array}\right|$
$\sum_{n=1}^{k} f(n)=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}\frac{k(k+1)}{2} & -1 & -5 \\ -2 \frac{k(k+1)(2 k+1)}{6} & 3(2 k+1) & 2 k+1 \\ -3 \frac{k^{2}(k+1)^{2}}{4} & 3 k(2 k+1) & 3 k(k+2)+1\end{array}\right|=98$
$\Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{k}(\mathrm{k}+1)(2 \mathrm{k}+1)}{2} \cdot \frac{7}{3}=98$
$\Rightarrow \mathrm{k}(\mathrm{k}+1)(2 \mathrm{k}+1)=84$
$\Rightarrow \mathrm{k}=3$

questions.question: Let $\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})$ and $\mathrm{g}(\mathrm{x})$ be twice differentiable functions satisfying $\mathrm{f}^{\prime \prime}(\mathrm{x})=\mathrm{g}^{\prime \prime}(\mathrm{x})$ for all $\mathrm{x} \in \mathrm{R}$, $\mathrm{f}^{\prime}(1)=2 \mathrm{~g}^{\prime}(1)=4$ and $\mathrm{g}(2)=3 \mathrm{f}(2)=9$. Then $\mathrm{f}(25)-\mathrm{g}(25)$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{f}^{\prime \prime}(\mathrm{x})=\mathrm{g}^{\prime \prime}(\mathrm{x})$
Integrate
$\mathrm{f}^{\prime}(\mathrm{x})=\mathrm{g}^{\prime}(\mathrm{x})+\mathrm{C}_{1}$
Put $\mathrm{x}=1$
$\mathrm{f}^{\prime}(1)=\mathrm{g}^{\prime}(1)+\mathrm{C}_{1}$
$4=2+\mathrm{C}_{1}$
$\mathrm{C}_{1}=2$
$\Rightarrow \mathrm{f}^{\prime}(\mathrm{x})=\mathrm{g}^{\prime}(\mathrm{x})+2$
$\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=\mathrm{g}(\mathrm{x})+2 \mathrm{x}+\mathrm{C}_{2}$
Put $\mathrm{x}=2$
$\mathrm{f}(2)=\mathrm{g}(2)+4+\mathrm{C}_{2}$
$3=9+4+\mathrm{C}_{2}$
$\mathrm{C}_{2}=-10$
$\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=\mathrm{g}(\mathrm{x})+2 \mathrm{x}-10$
Put $x=25$
$\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})-\mathrm{g}(25)=40$

$=5+29$
$=34$

questions.question: Let $\alpha, \beta$ be the roots of the equation $\mathrm{x}^{2}-\mathrm{x}+\mathrm{p}=0$ and $\gamma, \delta$ be the roots the equation $\mathrm{x}^{2}-4 \mathrm{x}+\mathrm{q}=0$; $\mathrm{p}, \mathrm{q} \in \mathrm{Z}$. If $\alpha, \beta, \gamma, \delta$ are in G.P., then $|\mathrm{p}+\mathrm{q}|$ equals:
questions.solution:
Let $\alpha=\mathrm{a}, \beta=\mathrm{ar}, \gamma=\mathrm{ar}^{2}, \delta=\mathrm{ar}^{3}$
$$
\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{a}+\mathrm{ar}=1 \\
& \mathrm{ar}^{2}+\mathrm{ar}^{3}=4 \\
& \Rightarrow \mathrm{ar}^{2}(1+\mathrm{r})=4 \\
& \left.\Rightarrow \mathrm{r}=2, \mathrm{a}=\frac{1}{3} \text { (reject as } \mathrm{p} \in \mathrm{z}\right) \\
& \text { or } \mathrm{r}=-2, \mathrm{a}=-1 \\
& \text { Now }|\mathrm{P}+\mathrm{q}|=\left|\mathrm{a}(\mathrm{ar})+\mathrm{ar}^{2}-\mathrm{ar}^{3}\right| \\
& =\left|\mathrm{a}^{2} \mathrm{r}\left(1+\mathrm{r}^{4}\right)\right| \\
& |1 \times-2 \times 17|=34
\end{aligned}
$$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Correct statements from the following are
A. Potassium dichromate is an oxidising agent and it oxidises $\mathrm{FeSO}_{4}$ to $\mathrm{Fe}_{2}\left(\mathrm{SO}_{4}\right)_{3}$ in acidic medium.
B. Sodium dichromate can be used as primary standard in volumetric estimation.
C. $\mathrm{CrO}_{4}^{2-}$ and $\mathrm{Cr}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{7}^{2-}$ are interconvertible in aqueous solution by varying the pH of the solution.
D. $\mathrm{Cr}-\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{Cr}$ bond angle in $\mathrm{Cr}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{7}^{2-}$ is $126^{\circ}$.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.answer: Option (B): A, C and D only
questions.solution:
(A) $\mathrm{MnO}_{4}^{-}+\mathrm{Fe}^{+2}+\mathrm{H}^{+} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Fe}^{+3}+\mathrm{Mn}^{+2}+\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}$
(B) $\mathrm{Na}_{2} \mathrm{Cr}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{7}$ generally not used as a primary standard in volumetric analysis because it is deliquescent.
(C) In acidic medium $\mathrm{Cr}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{7}^{2-}$ exists and it get converted into $\mathrm{CrO}_{4}^{2-}$ in basic medium.
$2 \mathrm{CrO}_{4}^{2-}+2 \mathrm{H}^{+} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Cr}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{7}^{2-}+\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}$
$\mathrm{Cr}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{7}^{2-}+2 \mathrm{OH}^{-} \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{CrO}_{4}^{2-}+\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}$
(D) $\mathrm{K}_{2} \mathrm{Cr}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{7}$ is a good oxidising agent and bond angle of $\mathrm{Cr}-\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{Cr}$ bond in $\mathrm{Cr}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{7}^{2-}$ is $126^{\circ}$

constant volume $\mathrm{w}=0$

$\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{v}}=$ Heat capacity at constant volume.

questions.question:
A monochromatic source of light operating at 15 kW emits $2.5 \times 10^{22}$ photons/s. The region of an electromagnetic spectrum to which the emitted electromagnetic radiation belongs to $\_\_\_\_$ .
(Take $\mathrm{h}=6.6 \times 10^{-34} \mathrm{~J}$.s and $\mathrm{c}=3 \times 10^{8} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ ).
questions.solution:
$\frac{h \mathrm{C}}{\lambda}=\frac{15 \times 10^{3}}{2.5 \times 10^{22}}$
$\therefore \lambda=\frac{6.6 \times 10^{-34} \times 3 \times 10^{8} \times 2.5 \times 10^{22}}{15 \times 10^{3}}$
$\lambda=3.3 \times 10^{-7}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For a spring, $\mathrm{k} \ell=$ constant
$\mathrm{k}_{1} \ell=\mathrm{k}_{2} \frac{\ell}{2} \Rightarrow \mathrm{k}_{2}=2 \mathrm{k}_{1}$
$\mathrm{f}=\frac{1}{2 \pi} \sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{k}}{\mathrm{m}}}$
$\Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{f}_{1}}{\mathrm{f}_{2}}=\sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{k}_{1}}{\mathrm{k}_{2}}}$
$\Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{f}_{1}}{\mathrm{f}_{2}}=\sqrt{\frac{1}{2}} \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{f}_{2}}{\mathrm{f}_{1}}=\sqrt{2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A 30 cm long solenoid has 10 turns per cm and area of $5 \mathrm{~cm}^{2}$. The current through the solenoid coil varies from 2 A to 4 A is 3.14 s . The e.m.f. induced in the coil is $\alpha \times 10^{-5} \mathrm{~V}$. The value $\alpha$ is $\_\_\_\_$ .
questions.solution:
$\varepsilon=-\frac{\mathrm{Ldi}}{\mathrm{dt}}=-\mu_{0} \mathrm{n}^{2} \mathrm{~A} \ell \frac{\mathrm{di}}{\mathrm{dt}}$
$=-4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \times 10^{6} \times 5 \times 10^{-4} \times 0.3 \times \frac{2}{\pi}$
$\Rightarrow-12 \times 10^{-5}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A current carrying circular loop of radius 2 cm with unit normal $\hat{\mathrm{n}}=\frac{\hat{\mathrm{k}}+\hat{\mathrm{i}}}{\sqrt{2}}$ is placed in a magnetic field, $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{B}}=\mathrm{B}_{0}(3 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+2 \hat{\mathrm{k}})$. If $\mathrm{B}_{0}=4 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~T}$ and current $\mathrm{I}=100 \sqrt{2} \mathrm{~A}$, the torque experienced by the loop is $\_\_\_\_$ Wb.A. $(\pi=3.14)$
questions.solution:
$\vec{\tau}=\overrightarrow{\mathrm{M}} \times \overrightarrow{\mathrm{B}}$
$\Rightarrow 100 \sqrt{2} \times 3.14 \times 4 \times 10^{-4}\left[\left(\frac{\hat{\mathrm{k}}+\hat{\mathrm{i}}}{\sqrt{2}}\right) \times(3 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+2 \hat{\mathrm{k}})\right] \mathrm{B}_{0}$
$\Rightarrow 16 \times 3.14 \times[+3 \hat{\mathrm{j}}-2 \hat{\mathrm{j}}] \times 10^{-5}$
$\Rightarrow 50.24 \times 10^{-5} \hat{\mathrm{j}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A spherical liquid drop of radius R acquires the terminal velocity $\mathrm{v}_{1}$ when falls through a gas of viscosity $\eta$. Now the drop is broken into 64 identical droplets and each droplet acquires terminal velocity $\mathrm{v}_{2}$ falling through the same gas. The ratio of terminal velocities $\mathrm{v}_{1} / \mathrm{v}_{2}$ is $\_\_\_\_$ .
questions.solution:
Using volume conservation,
$\frac{4}{3} \pi R_{1}^{3}=64 \times \frac{4}{3} \pi R_{2}^{3} \Rightarrow R_{2}=\frac{R_{1}}{4}$
Terminal velocity $\mathrm{v} \propto \mathrm{R}^{2}$
$\frac{\mathrm{v}_{1}}{\mathrm{v}_{2}} \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{R}_{1}^{2}}{\mathrm{R}_{2}^{2}} \Rightarrow(4)^{2}=16$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two masses of 3.4 kg and 2.5 kg are accelerated from an initial speed of $5 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ and $12 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$, respectively. The distances traversed by the masses in the $5^{\text {th }}$ second are 104 m and 129 m , respectively. The ratio of their momenta after 10 s is $\frac{x}{8}$. The value of $x$ is $\_\_\_\_$ .
questions.solution: $\mathrm{S}=\mathrm{u}+\frac{\mathrm{a}}{2}(2 \mathrm{n}-1) \Rightarrow 104=5+\frac{\mathrm{a}}{2}(9) \Rightarrow \mathrm{a}=22 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^{2} ; 129=12+\frac{\mathrm{a}}{2} \times 9 \Rightarrow \mathrm{a}=26 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^{2}$$\frac{\mathrm{p}_{1}}{\mathrm{p}_{2}}=\frac{(5+22 \times 10) 3.4}{(12+26 \times 10)(2.5)}=\frac{225 \times(3.4)}{272 \times 2.5}=\frac{9}{8}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Initial pressure and volume of a monoatomic ideal gas are P and V. The change in internal energy of this gas in adiabatic expansion to volume $\mathrm{V}_{\text {final }}=27 \mathrm{~V}$ is $\_\_\_\_$ J.
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{P}_{1} \mathrm{~V}_{1}^{\gamma}=\mathrm{P}_{2} \mathrm{~V}_{2}^{\gamma}$
$\gamma=\frac{5}{3}$
$\mathrm{PV}^{5 / 3}=\mathrm{P}_{2} \times(27 \mathrm{~V})^{5 / 3}$
$\mathrm{P}_{2}=\frac{\mathrm{P}}{(27)^{5 / 3}}=\frac{\mathrm{P}}{3^{5}}$
$\Delta \mathrm{U} \Rightarrow \mathrm{nC}_{\mathrm{v}} \Delta \mathrm{T}=\frac{\mathrm{nR} \Delta \mathrm{T}}{(\gamma-1)}$
$=\frac{P_{2} V_{2}-P_{1} V_{1}}{(\gamma-1)}$
$\Rightarrow \frac{\frac{\mathrm{P}}{3^{5}} \times 3^{3} . \mathrm{V}-\mathrm{PV}}{\frac{5}{3}-1} \Rightarrow \frac{-\mathrm{PV}\left\{1-\frac{1}{9}\right\}}{\frac{2}{3}}$
$=-\mathrm{PV} \times \frac{8}{9} \times \frac{3}{2}$
$\Rightarrow-\frac{4}{3} \mathrm{PV}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question:
A liquid of density $600 \mathrm{~kg} / \mathrm{m}^{3}$ flowing steadily in a tube of varying cross-section. The cross-section at a point A is $1.0 \mathrm{~cm}^{2}$ and that at B is $20 \mathrm{~mm}^{2}$. Both the points A and B are in same horizontal plane, the speed of the liquid at A is $10 \mathrm{~cm} / \mathrm{s}$. The difference is pressures at A and B points is
$\_\_\_\_$ Pa.
questions.solution:
Using continuity equation,
$$
\begin{aligned}
& A_{1} V_{1}=A_{2} V_{2} \\
& 1 \times 10=\frac{1}{5} \times V_{2} \\
& \Rightarrow V_{2}=50 \mathrm{~cm} / \mathrm{s}
\end{aligned}
$$
Using Bernoulli's theorem,
$P_{1}+\frac{1}{2} \rho V_{1}^{2}=P_{2}+\frac{1}{2} \rho V_{2}^{2}$
$P_{1}-P_{2}=\frac{1}{2} \rho\left[V_{2}^{2}-V_{1}^{2}\right]$
$=\frac{1}{2} \times 600\left[(50)^{2}-(10)^{2}\right] \times 10^{-4}=72 \mathrm{~Pa}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A thin biconvex lens is prepared from the glass ( $\mu=1.5$ ) both curved surfaces of which have equal radii of 20 cm each. Left side surface of the lens is silvered from outside to make it reflecting. To have the position of image and object at the same place, the object should be placed, from the lens at a distance of $\_\_\_\_$ cm.
questions.solution:
Combination of lens + mirror
$\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{m}}=\frac{\mathrm{R}}{2}=-10 \mathrm{~cm} ; \mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{L}}=\frac{\mathrm{R}}{2(\mu-1)}=20 \mathrm{~cm}$
$\frac{1}{\mathrm{f}}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{m}}}-\frac{2}{\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{L}}}$
$\frac{1}{\mathrm{f}}=\frac{-1}{10}-\frac{2}{20}=-\frac{1}{5}$
$\mathrm{f}=-5 \mathrm{~cm}$
To form image at the position of object, it should be placed at center of curvature of mirror + lens combination.
$\therefore \mathrm{u}=2 \mathrm{f}=2 \times 5=10 \mathrm{~cm}$

It has a capacitance of $1 \mu \mathrm{~F}$ when the space between the plates is filled with an insulating material of resistivity $1 \times 10^{13} \Omega \mathrm{~m}$ and resistance $17.7 \times 10^{14} \Omega$. Relative permittivity of the insulating material is $\alpha \times 10^{7}$. The value of $\alpha$ is $\_\_\_\_$ .

$\mathrm{RC}=\rho \mathrm{K} \in_{0}$
$\mathrm{K}=\frac{\mathrm{RC}}{\rho \varepsilon_{0}}=\frac{17.7 \times 10^{14} \times 10^{-6}}{10^{13} \times 8.85 \times 10^{-12}}=2 \times 10^{7}$

questions.question:
A gas balloon is going up with a constant velocity of $10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$. When this balloon reached a height of 75 m , a stone is dropped from it and balloon keeps moving up with the same velocity. The height of the balloon when the stone hits the ground is
$\_\_\_\_$ m . (Take $\mathrm{g}=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^{2}$ )
questions.solution:
$-75=10 \times \mathrm{t}-\frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times \mathrm{t}^{2}$
$\mathrm{t}^{2}-2 \mathrm{t}-15=0$
$(\mathrm{t}-5)(\mathrm{t}+3)=0 \Rightarrow \mathrm{t}=5$
Height $=75+10 \times 5=125 \mathrm{~m}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two identical bodies, projected with the same speed at two different angles cover the same horizontal range R . If the time of flight of these bodies are 5 s and 10 s , respectively, then the value of $R$ is $\_\_\_\_$ m. (Take $\mathrm{g}=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^{2}$ )
questions.solution:
For range to be same, angle of projection must be complementary angles.
$\mathrm{T}_{1}=\frac{2 \mathrm{u} \sin \theta}{\mathrm{g}}=10, \mathrm{~T}_{2}=\frac{2 \mathrm{u} \cos \theta}{\mathrm{g}}=5$
Range $=\frac{2(\mathrm{u} \sin \theta)(\mathrm{u} \cos \theta)}{\mathrm{g}}$
$=\frac{2(50)(25)}{10} \mathrm{~m}=250 \mathrm{~m}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Consider $|\mathrm{x}|$ is the difference in oxidation states of Mn in highest manganese fluoride and highest manganese oxide. The ions with $|x|$ number of unpaired electrons from the following are:
A. $\mathrm{Sc}^{3+}$
B. $\mathrm{Zn}^{2+}$
C. $\mathrm{V}^{2+}$
D. $\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}$
E. $\mathrm{Co}^{2+}$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Oxide of Mn in its highest O.S. $=\mathrm{Mn}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{7}\left[\mathrm{Mn}^{+7}\right]$ Fluoride of Mn in its highest O.S. $=\mathrm{MnF}_{4}\left[\mathrm{Mn}^{+4}\right]$
⇒ Difference in O.S. $=|\mathrm{x}|=3$
$\mathrm{Sc}^{+3} \Rightarrow[\mathrm{Ar}] ; 0$ unpaired $\mathrm{e}^{-}$
$\mathrm{Zn}^{2+} \Rightarrow[\mathrm{Ar}] 3 \mathrm{~d}^{10} ; 0$ unpaired electrons
$\mathrm{Fe}^{+2} \Rightarrow[\mathrm{Ar}] 3 \mathrm{~d}^{6} ; 4$ unpaired electrons

questions.question:
An electrochemical cell. consist of the following two redox couples,
$\mathrm{M}^{\times+}(\mathrm{aq}) / \mathrm{M}(\mathrm{s})\left[\mathrm{E}_{\text {red }}^{\ominus}=+0.15 \mathrm{~V}\right]$ and
$\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}(\mathrm{aq}) / \mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{s})\left[\mathrm{E}_{\text {red }}^{\ominus}=-0.036 \mathrm{~V}\right]$
The cell EMF ( $\left.\mathrm{E}_{\text {cell }}\right)$ is recorded to be 0.2057 V .
If the reaction quotient of the electrochemical reaction is found to be $10^{-2}$, then the value of x is
$\_\_\_\_$ (Nearest integer)
[Given : M is a p-block metal and
$$
\left.\frac{2.303 \mathrm{RT}}{\mathrm{~F}}=0.059 \mathrm{~V}\right]
$$
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{E}_{\text {cell }}=\mathrm{E}_{\text {cell }}^{\mathrm{o}}-\frac{0.059}{3 \mathrm{x}} \log 10^{-2}$
$0.2057=0.186-\frac{0.059}{3 \mathrm{x}}(-2)$

questions.question: A wheel initially at rest is subjected to a uniform angular acceleration about its axis. In the first 2 s it rotates through an angle $\theta_{1}$ and in the next 2 s it rotates through an angle $\theta_{2}$. The ratio $\frac{\theta_{2}}{\theta_{1}}$ is $\_\_\_\_$ .
questions.solution:
Let $\alpha$ be angular acceleration
In first 2 sec
$\theta_{1}=\frac{1}{2} \cdot \alpha(2)^{2}=2 \alpha$
Angular covered in 4 sec
$\theta^{\prime}=\frac{1}{2}(\alpha)(4)^{2}=8 \alpha$
Angle in next 2 sec
$\theta_{2}=\theta^{\prime}-\theta_{1}=8 \alpha-2 \alpha$
$\theta_{2}=6 \alpha$
$\frac{\theta_{2}}{\theta_{1}}=\frac{6 \alpha}{2 \alpha}=3$

questions.question: Eight mercury drops, each of radius $r$, coalesce to form a bigger drop. The surface energy released in this process is $\_\_\_\_$ . ( S is the surface tension of mercury).

Volume conservation
(8) $\left[\frac{4}{3} \pi r^{3}\right]=\frac{4}{3} \pi R^{3}$
$\mathrm{R}=2 \mathrm{r}$
$\mathrm{U}_{\mathrm{i}}=(8)\left(4 \pi \mathrm{r}^{2}\right)(\mathrm{s}) ; \mathrm{s}=$ surface tension
$\mathrm{U}_{\mathrm{i}}=32 \pi \mathrm{r}^{2} \mathrm{~s}$
$\mathrm{U}_{\mathrm{f}}=\left(4 \pi \mathrm{R}^{2}\right)(\mathrm{s})$

questions.solution:
$\mathrm{U}_{1}=\frac{-\mathrm{GMm}}{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{e}}}$
$\mathrm{U}_{2}=\frac{-\mathrm{GMm}}{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{e}}+2 \mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{e}}}=-\frac{\mathrm{GMm}}{3 \mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{e}}}$
$\Delta \mathrm{U}=\mathrm{U}_{2}-\mathrm{U}_{1}=\frac{-\mathrm{GMm}}{3 \mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{e}}}+\frac{\mathrm{GMm}}{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{e}}}$
$\Delta \mathrm{U}=\frac{2}{3} \frac{\mathrm{GMm}}{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{e}}}=\frac{2}{3}\left[\frac{\mathrm{GM}}{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{e}}^{2}}\right]\left(\mathrm{mR}_{\mathrm{e}}\right)$
$\Delta \mathrm{U}=\frac{2}{3} \mathrm{mgR}_{\mathrm{e}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A metal rod of length $L$ rotates about on end at origin with a uniform angular velocity $\omega$. The magnetic field radially falls off as $B(\mathrm{r})=\mathrm{B}_{\mathrm{o}} \mathrm{e}^{-\lambda \mathrm{r}}$; $\lambda$ being a positive constant. The emf induced (neglecting the centripetal force on electrons in the rod) is:
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{e}=\int_{0}^{\mathrm{L}} \mathrm{B}(\omega \mathrm{r}) \mathrm{dr}=\mathrm{B}_{0} \omega \int_{0}^{\mathrm{L}} \mathrm{e}^{-\lambda \mathrm{r}} \cdot \mathrm{rdr}$
$=\mathrm{B}_{0} \omega\left[\mathrm{r} \int \mathrm{e}^{-\lambda \mathrm{r}} \mathrm{dr}-\int 1 \cdot \frac{\mathrm{e}^{-\lambda \mathrm{r}}}{-\lambda} \mathrm{dr}\right]_{0}^{\mathrm{L}}$
$=\mathrm{B}_{0} \omega\left[\frac{\mathrm{re}^{-\lambda \mathrm{r}}}{-\lambda}-\frac{\mathrm{e}^{-\lambda \mathrm{r}}}{\lambda^{2}}\right]_{0}^{\mathrm{L}}$
$=\mathrm{B}_{0} \omega\left[\left(0+\frac{1}{\lambda^{2}}\right)-\left(\frac{\mathrm{Le}^{-\lambda \mathrm{L}}}{\lambda}+\frac{\mathrm{e}^{-\lambda \mathrm{L}}}{\lambda^{2}}\right)\right]$

$$
\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{a}_{1}=\mathrm{g} \sin \theta-\mu \mathrm{g} \\
& \ell=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{a} \cdot \mathrm{t}^{2}
\end{aligned}
$$
for frictionless surface $\mathrm{a}_{2}=\mathrm{g} \sin \theta$
$\ell=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{a}_{2} \frac{\mathrm{t}^{2}}{4}$
$\mathrm{a}, \mathrm{t}^{2}=\mathrm{a}_{2} \frac{\mathrm{t}^{2}}{4}$
$g\left(\sin 45-\mu \cos 45^{\circ}\right)=\frac{g \sin 45}{4}$
$1-\mu=\frac{1}{4}$
$\mu=\frac{3}{4}=\frac{\alpha}{100}$
$\alpha=75$

$$

Statement II : The oxidation state of oxygen in $\mathrm{OF}_{2}$ is +2 and in $\mathrm{Na}_{2} \mathrm{O}$ is -2 .
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.answer: Option (A): Both Statement I and Statement II are true
questions.solution:
Statement-I
$$
\left.\begin{array}{l}
(\mathrm{EN})_{\mathrm{F}}=4.0 \\
(\mathrm{EN})_{\mathrm{O}}=3.5 \\
(\mathrm{EN})_{\mathrm{N}}=3.0
\end{array}\right\} \text { on pauling scale }
$$
Statement-II
Oxidation state of oxygen in $\mathrm{OF}_{2}$
$$
\begin{gathered}
\mathrm{OF}_{2} \Rightarrow \mathrm{x}-1 \times 2=0 \\
\mathrm{x}=+2
\end{gathered}
$$
Oxidation state of oxygen in $\mathrm{Na}_{2} \mathrm{O}$
$$

& \mathrm{x}=-2

$$
Both the statement I and statement II are correct.

questions.question:
Identify the correct statements from the following:
(A) $\left[\mathrm{Fe}\left(\mathrm{C}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{4}\right)_{3}\right]^{3-}$ is the most stable complex among $\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{OH})_{6}\right]^{3-},\left[\mathrm{Fe}\left(\mathrm{C}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{4}\right)_{3}\right]^{3-}$ and $\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{SCN})_{6}\right]^{3-}$
(B) The stability of $\left[\mathrm{Cu}\left(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\right)_{4}\right]^{2+}$ is greater than that of $\left[\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{en})_{2}\right]^{2+}$
(C) The hybridization of Fe in $\mathrm{K}_{4}\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}\right]$ is $\mathrm{d}^{2} \mathrm{sp}^{3}$
(D) $\left[\mathrm{Fe}\left(\mathrm{NO}_{2}\right)_{3} \mathrm{Cl}_{3}\right]^{3-}$ exhibits linkage isomerism
(E) $\mathrm{NO}_{2}^{-}$and $\mathrm{SCN}^{-}$ligands are NOT ambidentate ligands

options: A, B, C, D and E
questions.answer: Option (C): A, C and D only
questions.solution:
(A) $\left[\mathrm{Fe}\left(\mathrm{C}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{4}\right)_{3}\right]^{3-}$ has oxalate ion as ligand which leads to chelation thus maximum stability among given complexes.
(B) Stability : $\left[\mathrm{Cu}\left(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\right)_{4}\right]^{2+}<\left[\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{en})_{2}\right]^{2+}$; due to higher CFSE and chelation.
(C) $\mathrm{K}_{4}\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}\right]$
$\Rightarrow \mathrm{Fe}^{2+}=[\mathrm{Ar}] 3 \mathrm{~d}^{6}$
In presence of SFL the electronic configuration of $\mathrm{Fe}^{+2}\left[\mathrm{t}_{2 \mathrm{~g}}^{6}, \mathrm{e}_{\mathrm{g}}^{0}\right]$, thus $\mathrm{d}^{2} \mathrm{sp}^{3}$ hybridized.
(D) $\left[\mathrm{Fe}\left(\mathrm{NO}_{2}\right)_{3} \mathrm{Cl}_{3}\right]^{3-}$ has $\mathrm{NO}_{2}^{-}$as ambidentate ligand thus can show linakge isomerism.
(E) $\mathrm{NO}_{2}^{-}$and SCN both are ambidentate ligands.

Put $\mathrm{x}=0$ in eq.(1)
$\Rightarrow \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{y})=-1+2 \mathrm{y}^{2}+\mathrm{y}$
Now put $\mathrm{x}=\mathrm{y}=1$ in eq. (1)
$\Rightarrow \mathrm{f}(2)=\mathrm{f}(1)+3+\alpha$
$\Rightarrow 9=2+3+\alpha \Rightarrow \alpha=4$
Now $\sum_{n=1}^{5}(\alpha+f(n))=\sum_{n=1}^{5}\left(2 y^{2}+y+3\right)$
$=\frac{2 \times 5 \times 6 \times 11}{6}+\frac{5 \times 6}{2}+3 \times 5=140$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question:
In interference experiment the path difference between two interfering waves at a point A on the screen is $\lambda / 3$, where $\lambda$ is the wavelength of these waves, and at another point B the path difference is $\lambda / 6$. The ratio of intensities at points A and B is
$\_\_\_\_$。
questions.solution:
$\quad \Delta \phi_{\mathrm{A}}=\frac{2 \pi}{\lambda} \times \frac{\lambda}{3}=\frac{2 \pi}{3}$
$\therefore I_{A}=I+I+2 \sqrt{I} \cdot \sqrt{I} \cdot \cos \left(\frac{2 \pi}{3}\right)=I$
$\Delta \phi_{\mathrm{B}}=\frac{2 \pi}{\lambda} \times \frac{\lambda}{6}=\frac{\pi}{3}$
$\therefore \mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{B}}=\mathrm{I}+\mathrm{I}+2 \sqrt{\mathrm{I}} \cdot \sqrt{\mathrm{I}} \cdot \cos \left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)=3 \mathrm{I}$
$\frac{\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{A}}}{\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{B}}}=\frac{\mathrm{I}}{3 \mathrm{I}}=\frac{1}{3}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question:
The energy released when $\frac{7}{17.13} \mathrm{~kg}$ of ${ }_{3}^{7} \mathrm{Li}$ is converted into ${ }_{2}^{4} \mathrm{He}$ by proton bombardment is $\alpha \times 10^{32} \mathrm{eV}$. The value of $\alpha$ is $\_\_\_\_$ . (Nearest integer)
(Mass of ${ }_{3}^{7} \mathrm{Li}=7.0183 \mathrm{u}$, mass of ${ }_{2}^{4} \mathrm{He}=4.004 \mathrm{u}$,
mass of proton $=1.008 \mathrm{u}$ and $1 \mathrm{u}=931 \mathrm{MeV} / \mathrm{c}^{2}$ and Avogadro number $=6.0 \times 10^{23}$ )
questions.solution:
$\quad{ }_{3}^{7} \mathrm{Li}+{ }_{1}^{1} \mathrm{P} \rightarrow 2{ }_{2}^{4} \mathrm{He}$
$\Delta \mathrm{m}=(7.018+1.008)-2(4.004)=0.0183 \mathrm{u}$
Energy released per reaction $\mathrm{E}=\Delta \mathrm{mc}^{2}$
Number of moles of $\mathrm{Li}=\frac{7}{17.13} \times \frac{10^{3}}{7}=\frac{10^{3}}{17.13}$
Number of molecules $=\frac{10^{3}}{17.13} \times 6 \times 10^{23}$
Total energy released
$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{E}_{\text {Total }} & =0.0183 \times 931 \times \frac{6}{17.13} \times 10^{32} \\
& \simeq 6 \times 10^{32}
\end{aligned}
$$
$\alpha=6$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A solid sphere of radius 4 cm and mass 5 kg is rotating (rotation axis is passing through the centre of the sphere) with an angular velocity of 1200 rpm . It is brought to rest in 10 s by applying a constant torque. The torque applied and the number of rotations it made before it comes to rest are $\_\_\_\_$ and $\_\_\_\_$ respectively.
questions.solution:
$\quad \omega_{\mathrm{i}}=1200 \mathrm{rpm}=1200 \times \frac{2 \pi}{60}=40 \pi \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{sec}$
$\rightarrow \omega_{\mathrm{f}}=\omega_{\mathrm{i}}+\alpha \mathrm{t} \Rightarrow 0=40 \mathrm{p}+\alpha(10)$
$\alpha=-4 \pi \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{sec}^{2}$
$\rightarrow \mathrm{I}=\frac{2}{5} \mathrm{MR}^{2}=\frac{2}{5}(5)(0.04)^{2}=2 \times 0.0016$
$\mathrm{I}=0.0032 \mathrm{Kg}-\mathrm{m}^{2}$
$\rightarrow \tau=\mathrm{I} \alpha=0.0032 \times 4 \pi$
$\tau=0.0128 \pi \mathrm{~N}-\mathrm{m}$
$\rightarrow \omega_{\mathrm{f}}^{2}=\omega_{\mathrm{i}}^{2}+2 \alpha \theta$
$0=(40 \pi)^{2}+2(4 \pi) \theta$
$\theta=\frac{1600 \pi^{2}}{8 \pi}=200 \pi$
No. of revolution $=\frac{\theta}{2 \pi}=\frac{200 \pi}{2 \pi}$
No. of revolution $=100$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: An unpolarized light of intensity $\mathrm{I}_{0}$ passes through polarizer and then through a certain optically active solution and finally it goes to analyser. If the angle between analyser and polariser is $0^{\circ}$ and intensity of light emerged from analyser is $\frac{3}{8} \mathrm{I}_{0}$, the angle of rotation of the light by the solution with respect to analyser is $\_\_\_\_$ degrees.

$\frac{3 \mathrm{I}_{0}}{8}=\frac{\mathrm{I}_{0}}{2} \cos ^{2} \theta$
$\cos \theta=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$
$\theta=30^{\circ}$

questions.question: A small cube of side 1 mm is placed at the centre of a circular loop of radius 10 cm carrying a current of 2 A . Magnetic field at centre $B=\left(\frac{\mu_{0}}{4 \pi}\right) \frac{2 \pi i}{R}$
 
$=\frac{10^{-7} \times 2 \times \pi \times 2}{10 \times 10^{-2}}$
So energy stored

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The ratio of momentum of the photons of the $1^{\text {st }}$ and $2^{\text {nd }}$ line of Balmer series of Hydrogen atoms is $\alpha / \beta$. The possible values of $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are :-
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{p}=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\lambda}$
$\frac{1}{\lambda_{1}}=\mathrm{R}\left(\frac{1}{2^{2}}-\frac{1}{3^{2}}\right)=\mathrm{R}\left(\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{9}\right)$
$\frac{1}{\lambda_{1}}=\mathrm{R} \frac{5}{36}$

$\frac{1}{\lambda_{2}}=\frac{3 \mathrm{R}}{16}$
$\frac{\mathrm{p}_{1}}{\mathrm{p}_{2}}=\frac{\lambda_{2}}{\lambda_{1}}=\frac{\frac{16}{3 \mathrm{R}}}{\frac{36}{5 \mathrm{R}}}=\frac{20}{27}$
$\alpha=20 \& \beta=27$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Given below are two statements :
Given : Molar mass of $\mathrm{C}, \mathrm{H}, \mathrm{O}, \mathrm{Cl}$ are 12, 1, 16 and $35.5 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$, respectively.
Statement I: In $30 \%(\mathrm{w} / \mathrm{w})$ solution of methanol in $\mathrm{CCl}_{4}$ (at T K ), the mole fraction of $\mathrm{CCl}_{4}$ is equal to 0.33 .
Statement II : Mixture of methanol and $\mathrm{CCl}_{4}$ shows positive deviation deviation from Raoult's law.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the option given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are ture
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II are ture
questions.answer: Option (A): Both Statement I and Statement II are ture
questions.solution:
(i) Let wt of solution $=100 \mathrm{~g}$
wt of methanol $=30 \mathrm{~g}$
wt of $\mathrm{CCl}_{4}=100-30=70 \mathrm{~g}$
mole fraction of $\mathrm{CCl}_{4}=\frac{\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{CCl}_{4}}}{\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{CCl}_{4}}+\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{CH}_{3} \mathrm{OH}}}=\frac{\frac{70}{154}}{\frac{70}{154}+\frac{30}{32}} =0.3267 \approx 0.33$
(ii) $\mathrm{CCl}_{4} \&$ methanol is mixture of positive deviation from Raoult's law.
So, statement (I) & statement (II) are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Consider the equilibrium
\[CO({\text{g}}) + 3{{\text{H}}_2}({\text{g}}) \rightleftharpoons C{H_4}({\text{g}}) + {{\text{H}}_2}{\text{O}}({\text{g}})\]
If the pressure applied over the system increases by two fold at constant temperature then
(A) Concentration of reactants and products increases.
(B) Equilibrium will shift in forward direction.
(C) Equilibrium concentration of products increases.
(D) Equilibrium constant remains unchanged as concentration of reactants and products remain same.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Increasing the pressure on a gaseous equilibrium system at constant temperature will cause the equilibrium to shift in the direction that reduces the number of gas molecules. In this reaction, there are 4 moles of gas on the reactant side (1 CO + 3 H2) and 2 moles of gas on the product side (1 CH4 + 1 H2O).
Le Chatelier's principle states that if a change of condition is applied to a system in equilibrium, the system will shift in a direction that relieves the stress. The stress here is the increased pressure. The system will shift to the side with fewer gas molecules to reduce the pressure.
Therefore, the equilibrium will shift to the right (forward direction), increasing the concentration of products (CH4 and H2O) and decreasing the concentration of reactants (CO and H2). However, the total number of moles decreases, leading to an increase in the overall concentration of both reactants…

Let \[y = y\left( x \right)\] be the solution of the differential equation \[2\cos x\frac{{dy}}{{dx}} = \sin 2x-4y\sin x,x \in \left( {0,\frac{\pi }{2}} \right).\]
If \[y\left( {\frac{\pi }{3}} \right) = 0,\] then \[y'\left( {\frac{\pi }{4}} \right) + y\left( {\frac{\pi }{4}} \right)\] is equal to _______.
questions.solution:
\[\frac{{dy}}{{dx}} + 2y\tan x = \sin x\]
I.F. \[ = {e^{x\int {\tan xdx} }} = {\sec ^2}x\]
\[y{\sec ^2}x = \int {\frac{{\sin x}}{{{{\cos }^2}x}}dx} \]
\[ = \int {\tan x\sec xdx} \]
\[ = \sec x + C\]
\[C = -2\]
\[y = \cos x-2{\cos ^2}x\]
\[y\left( {\frac{\pi }{4}} \right) = \frac{1}{{\sqrt 2 }}-1\]
\[y' = -\sin x + 4\cos x\sin x\]
\[y'\left( {\frac{\pi }{4}} \right) = -\frac{1}{{\sqrt 2 }} + 2\]
\[y'\left( {\frac{\pi }{4}} \right) + y\left( {\frac{\pi }{4}} \right) = 1\]

\[\left( {\lambda + 1} \right)x + \left( {\lambda + 2} \right)y - \left( {\lambda + 2} \right)z = 9\]

questions.solution:
\[\left( {\lambda - 1} \right)x + \left( {\lambda - 4} \right)y + \lambda z = 5\]
\[\lambda x + \left( {\lambda - 1} \right)y + \left( {\lambda - 4} \right)z = 7\]
\[\left( {\lambda + 1} \right)x + \left( {\lambda + 2} \right)y - \left( {\lambda + 2} \right)z = 9\]
For infinitely many solutions
\[D = \left| {\begin{array}{*{20}{c}}
 {\lambda - 1}&{\lambda - 4}&\lambda \\ 
 \lambda &{\lambda - 1}&{\lambda - 4} \\ 
 {\lambda + 1}&{\lambda + 2}&{ - \left( {\lambda + 2} \right)} 
\end{array}} \right| = 0\]
\[\left( {\lambda - 3} \right)\left( {2\lambda + 1} \right) = 0\]
\[{D_x} = \left| {\begin{array}{*{20}{c}}
 5&{\lambda - 4}&\lambda \\ 
 7&{\lambda - 1}&{\lambda - 4} \\ 
 9&{\lambda + 2}&{ - \left( {\lambda + 2} \right)} 
\end{array}} \right| = 0\]
\[2\left( {3 - \lambda } \right)\left( {23 - 2\lambda } \right) = 0\]
\[\lambda = 3\]
\[\therefore {\lambda ^2} + \lambda = 9 + 3 = 12\]

Let \[E:\frac{{{x^2}}}{{{a^2}}} + \frac{{{y^2}}}{{{b^2}}} = 1,\,\,a > b\,\,and\,H = \frac{{{x^2}}}{{{A^2}}} - \frac{{{y^2}}}{{{B^2}}} = 1\]
Let the distance between the foci of E and the foci of H be \[2\sqrt 3 .\] If a – A = 2, and the ratio of the eccentricities of E and H is \[\frac{1}{3},\] then the sum of the lengths of their latus rectums is equal to :
questions.solution:
\[\frac{{{x^2}}}{{{a^2}}} + \frac{{{y^2}}}{{{b^2}}} = 1\,\]foci are (ae, 0) and (− ae, 0)
\[\frac{{{x^2}}}{{{A^2}}} + \frac{{{y^2}}}{{{B^2}}} = 1\,\]foci are (Ae′ , 0) and (Ae′ , 0)
\[ \Rightarrow 2ae = 2\sqrt 3 \Rightarrow ae = \sqrt 3 \,\]
\[and\,\,2Ae' = 2\sqrt 3 \Rightarrow Ae' = \sqrt 3 \]
\[ \Rightarrow ae = Ae' \Rightarrow \frac{e}{{e'}} = \frac{A}{a}\]
\[ \Rightarrow \frac{1}{3} = \frac{A}{a} \Rightarrow a = 3A\]
\[Now\,\,a - A = 2 \Rightarrow a - \frac{a}{3} - 2 \Rightarrow a = 3\,and\,A = 1\]
\[Ae = \sqrt 3 \Rightarrow e = \frac{1}{{\sqrt 3 }}\,and\,e' = \sqrt 3 \]
\[{b^2} = {a^2}(1 - {e^2})\]
\[{b^2} = 6\]
\[and\,\,{B^2} = {A^2}\left( {{{\left( {e'} \right)}^2} - 1} \right) = (2) \Rightarrow {B^2} = 2\]
\[sum\,\,of\,\,LR\,\, = \frac{{2{b^2}}}{a} + \frac{{2{B^2}}}{A} = 8\]

questions.question: Let \[f:R \to R\] be a twice differentiable function such that f(2) = 1. If F(x) = xƒ(x) for all x\[ \in \]R, \[\int_0^2 {xF'\left( x \right)dx = 6} \] and \[\int_0^2 {{x^2}F''\left( x \right)dx = 40} \], then \[F'\left( 2 \right) + \int_0^2 {F\left( x \right)dx} \] is equal to:
questions.solution:
\[\int\limits_0^2 {xF'\left( x \right)dx = 6} \]
\[ = \left. {xF\left( x \right)} \right|_0^2 - \int\limits_0^2 {f\left( x \right)dx} = 6\]
\[ = 2F\left( 2 \right) - \int\limits_0^2 {xF\left( x \right)dx} = 6\,\,\left[ {\therefore f\left( 2 \right) = 2F\left( 2 \right) = 2} \right]\]
\[\int\limits_0^2 {xF\left( x \right)dx} = - 2\,\,\,\,...\left( 1 \right)\]
\[ \Rightarrow \int\limits_0^2 {F\left( x \right)dx} = - 2\,\,\,\,...\left( 2 \right)\]
Also
\[\int\limits_0^2 {{x^2}F''\left( x \right)dx} = \left. {{x^2}F'\left( x \right)} \right|_0^2 - 2\int\limits_0^2 {xF'\left( x \right)dx} = 40\]
\[ = 4F'\left( 2 \right) - 2 \times 6 = 40\]
\[F'\left( 2 \right) = 13\]
\[\therefore \,F'\left( 2 \right) + \int\limits_0^2 {F\left( x \right)} = 13 - 2 = 11\]

questions.solution:
All the three points A, B, C lie on the circle x2 + y2 = 100 so circumcentre is (0, 0)
 
\[\frac{{a + 0}}{3} = h \Rightarrow a = 3h\,and\,\frac{{9 + 3}}{3} = k \Rightarrow k = 3\]
also centroid \[\frac{{6 + 10\cos \alpha - 10\sin \alpha }}{3} = h\]
\[ \Rightarrow 10(\cos \alpha - \sin \alpha ) = 3h - 6\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,......(i)\]
\[and\,\,\frac{{8 + 10\cos \alpha - 10\sin \alpha }}{3} = k\]
\[ \Rightarrow 10\left( {\cos \alpha - \sin \alpha } \right) = 3k - 8 = 9 - 8 = 1\,\,\,\,\,\,\,......(ii)\]
\[on\,\,squaring\,\,100(1 - \sin 2\alpha ) = 1\]
\[ \Rightarrow 100\sin 2\alpha = 99\]
From equation (i) and (ii) we get $h = \frac{7}{3}$
Now 5a – 3h + 6k + 100 sin2α 
= 15h – 3h + 6k + 100 sin2α 
\[ = 12 \times \frac{7}{3} + 18 + 99\]
= 145

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The amount of work done to break a big water drop of radius 'R' into 27 small drops of equal radius is 10 J. The work done required to break the same big drop into 64 small drops of equal radius will be :-
questions.solution:
\[W = \Delta U = S\Delta A\]
One drop to n drop
\[\frac{4}{3}\lambda {R^3} = n\frac{4}{3}\lambda {r^3}\]
\[r = \frac{R}{{{n^{\frac{1}{3}}}}}\]
\[So\,\,\,W = S\left( {n4\pi {r^2} - 4\pi {R^2}} \right)\]
\[ = S4\pi {R^2}\left( {{n^{\frac{1}{3}}} - 1} \right)\]
For one drop to 27 drops
\[W = S4\pi {R^2}\left( {{{27}^{\frac{1}{3}}} - 1} \right) = 10\,\,......(i)\]
For one drop to 64 drops
\[W' = S4\pi {R^2}\left( {{{64}^{\frac{1}{3}}} - 1} \right)\,\,......(ii)\]
\[\begin{gathered}
  (ii)/(i) \\
  \frac{{W'}}{W} = \frac{{4 - 1}}{{3 - 1}} = \frac{3}{2} \\ 
\end{gathered} \]
\[W' = \frac{3}{2}W = 15J\]

questions.question:
Let \[A = \left[ {\begin{array}{*{20}{c}}
  {\frac{1}{{\sqrt 2 }}}&{ - 2} \\
  0&1
\end{array}} \right]\] and \[P = \left[ {\begin{array}{*{20}{c}}
  {\cos \theta }&{ - \sin \theta } \\
  {\sin \theta }&{\cos \theta }
\end{array}} \right],\theta > 0\]. If \[B = PA{P^T},C = {P^T}{B^{10}}P\] and the sum of the diagonal elements of C is \[\frac{m}{n}\], where \[\gcd \left( {m,n} \right) = 1\], then m+n is:
questions.solution:
\[P = \left[ {\begin{array}{*{20}{c}}
 {\cos \theta }&{ - \sin \theta } \\ 
 {\sin \theta }&{\cos \theta } 
\end{array}} \right]\]
\[\because \,{P^T}P = I\]
\[B = PAPT\]
Pre multiply by PT ( Given)
PTB = PTP APT = APT
Now post multiply by P
PTBP = APTP = A
So 
\[{A^2} = {P^T}{B^2}P\]
Similarly \[{A^{10}} = {P^T}{B^{10}}P = C\]
\[A = \left[ {\begin{array}{*{20}{c}}
 {\frac{1}{{\sqrt 2 }}}&{ - 2} \\ 
 0&1 
\end{array}} \right]\left( {{\text{Given}}} \right)\]
\[ \Rightarrow {A^2} = \left[ {\begin{array}{*{20}{c}}
 {\frac{1}{2}}&{ - \sqrt 2 - 2} \\ 
 0&1 
\end{array}} \right]\]
Similarly check A3 and so on since C = A10
\[ \Rightarrow \] Sum of diagonal elements of C is \[{\left( {\frac{1}{{\sqrt 2 }}} \right)^{10}} + 1\]
\[ = \frac{1}{{32}} + 1 = \frac{{33}}{{32}} = \frac{m}{n}\]
\[\gcd \left( {m,n} \right) = 1\left( {{\text{Given}}} \right)\]
\[ \Rightarrow m + n = 65\]

questions.question:
Drug X becomes ineffective after 50% decomposition. The original concentration of drug in a bottle was 16 mg/mL which becomes 4 mg/mL in 12 months. The expiry time of the drug in months is _____.
Assume that the decomposition of the drug follows first order kinetics.
questions.solution:
C0 = 16 mg/mL
Ct = 4 mg/mL
t = 12 monthsUsing the first-order kinetics equation: ln(Ct) = ln(C0) - kt
ln(4) = ln(16) - k(12)

k(12) = ln(16) - ln(4) = ln(16/4) = ln(4)

k = ln(4)/12 ≈ 0.2888 months-1
 t1/2 = 0.693/k
t1/2 = 0.693 / (ln(4)/12) = (0.693 * 12) / ln(4) ≈ 6 months

\[5{x^2} + 5{y^2} + 22y + 8 = 0\]
\[{x^2} + {y^2} + \frac{{22}}{5}y + \frac{8}{5} = 0\]
\[{\text{centre}} \Rightarrow \left( {0, - \frac{{11}}{5}} \right)\]

 \alpha &0&1

\[ \Rightarrow \mathop {\lim }\limits_{x \to {0^ + }} \frac{1}{x}\ln \left( {1 + \frac{{\left( {{k_1} - {k_2}} \right)x}}{{2 + {k_2}x}}} \right) = 2\]
\[ \Rightarrow \frac{{{k_1} - {k_2}}}{2} = 2\]
\[ \Rightarrow {k_1} - {k_2} = 4\]

\[k_1^2 + k_2^2 = 9 + 1 = 10\]

Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.answer: Option (A): Statement I is true but Statement II is false
questions.solution:
Due to resonance bond length is identical in ozone. Because of resonance, both the O-O bond lengths have partial double bond character. In other words, both the O-O bond lengths are equal (128 pm) and lie in between those O = O double bond length of 121 pm and O-O single bond length of 148 pm.
Therefore statement I is true and statement II is false.

Let \[f\left( x \right) = \mathop {\lim }\limits_{n \to \infty } \sum\limits_{r = 0}^n {\left( {\frac{{\tan \left( {x/{2^{r + 1}}} \right) + {{\tan }^3}\left( {x/{2^{r + 1}}} \right)}}{{1 - {{\tan }^2}\left( {x/{2^{r + 1}}} \right)}}} \right)} \].
Then \[\mathop {\lim }\limits_{x \to 0} \frac{{{e^x} - {e^{f\left( x \right)}}}}{{\left( {x - f\left( x \right)} \right)}}\] is equal to _______.
questions.solution:
\[f\left( x \right) = \mathop {\lim }\limits_{n \to \infty } \sum\limits_{r = 0}^n {\left( {\tan \frac{x}{{{2^r}}} - \tan \frac{x}{{{2^{r + 1}}}}} \right)} = \tan x\]
\[\mathop {\lim }\limits_{x \to 0} \left( {\frac{{{e^x} - {e^{\tan x}}}}{{x - \tan x}}} \right) = \mathop {\lim }\limits_{x \to 0} {e^{\tan x}}\frac{{\left( {{e^{x - \tan x}} - 1} \right)}}{{\left( {x - \tan x} \right)}} = 1\]

\[ \Rightarrow 48 = 4a.4\]
\[4a = 12\]
\[ \Rightarrow {y^2} = 12x\] is equation of parabola 
Now, parameter of P is \[{t_1} = \frac{2}{{\sqrt 3 }} \Rightarrow Parameters\,of\,Q\] 
\[{t_1} = \frac{2}{{\sqrt 3 }} \Rightarrow Parameters\,of\,Q\,is\,{t_2} = - \frac{{\sqrt 3 }}{2} \Rightarrow Q\left( {\frac{9}{4}, - 3\sqrt 3 } \right)\]
Area of trapezium PQNM
\[ = \frac{1}{2}MN.\left( {PM + QN} \right)\] 
\[ = \frac{1}{2}MN.\left( {PS + QS} \right)\]
\[ = \frac{1}{2}MN.\,PQ\]
\[ = \frac{1}{2}7\sqrt 3 .\frac{{49}}{4} = \left( {343} \right)\frac{{\sqrt 3 }}{8} \]

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question:
Consider following statements:
A. Surface tension arises due to extra energy of the molecules at the interior as compared to the molecules at the surface, of a liquid.
B. As the temperature of liquid rises, the coefficient of viscosity increases.
C. As the temperature of gas increases, the coefficient of viscosity increases.
D. The onset of turbulence is determined by Reynold’s number.
E. In a steady flow two stream lines never intersect.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution: Surface tension arises due to extra energy of the molecules at the molecules at the surface as compared at the interior of a liquid. The coefficient of viscosity for a liquid decreases with rise in temperature where as it increases for gases with increase in temperature. The flow is turbulent for a Reynold’s number greater than 2000. Stream lines never intersect in a steady flow.

questions.question: Define a relation R on the interval \[\left[ {0,\frac{\pi }{2}} \right)\] by x R y if and only if sec<sup>2</sup>x – tan<sup>2</sup>y = 1. Then R is :
options: both reflexive and transitive but not symmetric
both reflexive and symmetric but not transitive
reflexive but neither symmetric not transitive
questions.solution:
\[{\sec ^2}x-{\tan ^2}x = 1\] (on replacing y with x)
\[ \Rightarrow \] Reflexive
\[{\sec ^2}x-{\tan ^2}y = 1\]
\[ \Rightarrow 1 + {\tan ^2}x + 1-{\sec ^2}y = 1\]
\[ \Rightarrow {\sec ^2}y-{\tan ^2}x = 1\]
\[ \Rightarrow \] symmetric 
\[{\sec ^2}x-{\tan ^2}y = 1,\]
\[{\sec ^2}y-{\tan ^2}z = 1\]
Adding both
\[ \Rightarrow {\sec ^2}x-{\tan ^2}y + {\sec ^2}y-{\tan ^2}z = 1 + 1\]
\[{\sec ^2}x + 1-{\tan ^2}z = 2\]
\[{\sec ^2}x-{\tan ^2}z = 1\]
\[ \Rightarrow \] Transitive
Hence equivalence relation

\[ \Rightarrow \pi \]

(1 + x)7

is coeff. of middle term

Total valence electrons = 5 + 12 + 1 = 18 electrons.Drawing the Lewis structureThe central atom is nitrogen. Connect each oxygen atom to the nitrogen atom with a single bond. This uses 4 electrons (2 bonds × 2 electrons/bond).

In the sulphur estimation, 0.20 g of a pure organic compound gave 0.40 g of barium sulphate. The percentage of sulphur in the compound is ____ × 10–1 %.
(Molar mass : O = 16, S = 32, Ba = 137 in g mol–1)
questions.solution:
Step 1: Calculating the moles of barium sulfateThe molar mass of barium sulfate (BaSO₄) is: 137 (Ba) + 32 (S) + 4 * 16 (O) = 233 g/mol
Moles of BaSO₄ = mass of BaSO₄ / molar mass of BaSO₄ = 0.40 g / 233 g/mol = 0.001717 mol
Step 2: Calculating the moles of sulfurFrom the chemical formula BaSO₄, we know that 1 mole of BaSO₄ contains 1 mole of sulfur (S). Therefore, the moles of sulfur are equal to the moles of barium sulfate.
Moles of S = 0.001717 mol
Step 3: Calculating the mass of sulfurMass of S = moles of S * molar mass of S = 0.001717 mol * 32 g/mol = 0.054944 g
Step 4: Calculating the percentage of sulfur in the compoundPercentage of S = (mass of S / mass of compound) * 100% = (0.054944 g / 0.20 g) * 100% = 27.472%

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding a charged particle in a magnetic field. Which of the statements are true? (a) Starting with zero velocity, it accelerates in a direction perpendicular to the magnetic field (b) Charge particle will not move if we place it stationary in Magnetic Field (c) While deflecting in magnetic field its energy gradually increases (d) Direction of deflection force on the moving charged particle is perpendicular to its velocity
questions.solution: (a) FALSE: Lorentz force requires motion; if starting from rest, no force acts initially. (b) TRUE: A stationary charged particle experiences no magnetic force. (c) FALSE: Magnetic force is always perpendicular to velocity, so it does no work and energy doesn't change. (d) TRUE: Lorentz force F = q(v × B) is perpendicular to both v and B, hence perpendicular to velocity.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which one of the following processes involve chemical reactions?
questions.answer: Heating copper wire in presence of air at high temperature
options: Storing of oxygen gas under pressure in a gas cylinder
Keeping petrol in a China dish in the open
Heating copper wire in presence of air at high temperature
questions.solution: Heating copper wire in air causes oxidation (2Cu + O₂ → 2CuO), which is a chemical reaction producing a new substance (black copper oxide). Other options are physical changes: compression, liquefaction, and evaporation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Baking soda on thermal decomposition produces:
questions.answer: Sodium carbonate, carbon dioxide gas and water
options: Sodium carbonate, carbon dioxide gas and water
Sodium oxide, carbon dioxide gas and water
Baking soda does not undergo thermal decomposition
questions.solution: 2NaHCO₃ → Na₂CO₃ + CO₂↑ + H₂O. Baking soda decomposes into sodium carbonate, carbon dioxide gas, and water when heated.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Electrolytes when dissolved in water dissociate into their constituent ions. The degree of dissociation of an electrolyte increases with:
options: Presence of a substance yielding a common ion
questions.solution: Ostwald's dilution law states that degree of dissociation increases when the solution is diluted (concentration decreases). More dilute solutions have higher ionization because ions are farther apart, reducing recombination.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Molten sodium chloride conducts electricity due to the presence of:
questions.solution: In molten NaCl, the ionic compound is in liquid state where ions (Na⁺ and Cl⁻) are free to move. These mobile ions carry electric current. Free electrons are not present in ionic compounds.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Lewis acid:
options: Presence of H atom is necessary
questions.solution: According to Lewis definition, an acid is an electron pair acceptor (not just H⁺ donor). A base is an electron pair donor. This definition is broader than Brønsted-Lowry definition.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The compound whose 0.1 M solution is basic is:
questions.solution: Sodium acetate (CH₃COONa) is a salt of weak acid (acetic acid) and strong base (NaOH). It undergoes hydrolysis: CH₃COO⁻ + H₂O ⇌ CH₃COOH + OH⁻, producing OH⁻ ions, making the solution basic. Ammonium salts produce acidic solutions.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A hydrated solid X on heating initially gives a monohydrated compound Y. Y upon heating above 373 K leads to an anhydrous white powder Z. X and Z, respectively, are:
options: Baking soda and dead burnt plaster
Washing soda and dead burnt plaster
questions.solution: X = Washing soda (Na₂CO₃·10H₂O) → heating → Y = Monohydrated (Na₂CO₃·H₂O) → heating above 373K → Z = Soda ash (Na₂CO₃). Soda ash is the anhydrous white powder.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Matrix is defined as:
questions.answer: The unwanted foreign material present in the ore
options: The unwanted foreign material present in the ore
The flux added to remove the unwanted impurities from the ore
The slag formed as a result of the reaction of flux with gangue
The material used in the reduction of metal oxide to metal
questions.solution: In ore processing, matrix (also called gangue) refers to the unwanted rock and foreign material associated with the ore mineral. Flux is added to react with gangue to form slag.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In the electrolysis of alumina to obtain aluminum metal, cryolite is added to:
questions.answer: Lower the melting point of alumina
options: Lower the melting point of alumina
questions.solution: Cryolite (Na₃AlF₆) acts as a solvent and flux for alumina (Al₂O₃). It lowers the melting point from 2327°C to about 900°C, making the industrial process economically feasible. This mixture is called the 'Hall-Heroult cell'.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Choose the correct statement(s) among the following: (A) In the Aluminothermite process, aluminium acts as reducing agent. (B) 'Slag' formed during smelting in the extraction of copper is FeSiO₃. (C) In the extractive metallurgy of zinc, partial fusion of ZnO with coke is called sintering, and reduction of ore to the molten metal is called smelting. (D) Extractive metallurgy of silver from its ore argentine involves complex formation and displacement by more electropositive metal.
questions.solution: (A) TRUE: 2Al + Fe₂O₃ → 2Fe + Al₂O₃ (highly exothermic). (B) TRUE: In copper extraction, iron silicate (FeSiO₃) forms as slag. (C) TRUE: Both are correct definitions for zinc extraction. (D) FALSE: Silver extraction uses cyanide leaching and displacement by zinc, not complex formation alone.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which among the following statements is incorrect?
questions.answer: In parasitic mode of nutrition, the organisms feed by ingesting solid organic matter which is then digested and absorbed into their bodies
options: Green plants are photoautotrophs as they prepare their food through photosynthesis
In heterotrophic nutrition, the organism depends on other organisms for its food
In parasitic mode of nutrition, the organisms feed by ingesting solid organic matter which is then digested and absorbed into their bodies
Saprophytes obtain their food from dead and decaying organic matter
questions.solution: Statement (c) is incorrect. Parasites do NOT ingest solid food. They absorb pre-digested nutrient solutions from the host organism. Saprophytes ingest solid organic matter (like fungi and bacteria on dead matter). All other statements are correct.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What type of nutrition is shown in amoeba?
questions.solution: Amoeba shows holozoic nutrition because it ingests solid organic matter (small organisms, food particles) through its pseudopodia. The food is then digested in food vacuoles.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which type of teeth do humans possess?
questions.solution: Humans have Heterodont teeth (different types: incisors, canines, premolars, molars) and Diphyodont teeth (two sets in lifetime: deciduous and permanent).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What is the dental formula of the teeth in a 5-year-old child?
questions.solution: At 5 years old, the child has deciduous (milk) teeth. Dental formula = 2 incisors, 1 canine, 2 molars per half = 2123/2123. Permanent teeth (adult) = 2123/2123.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Transpiration is very important for plants because it helps in:
options: The absorption of water from soil
The cooling of leaves at high temperature
The movement of water and minerals absorbed by roots to various parts of the plant
questions.solution: Transpiration is important for: (1) Creating water potential gradient that pulls water up from roots, (2) Cooling leaves through evaporative cooling, (3) Transporting water and minerals throughout the plant.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Transport of sucrose in phloem is by:
questions.solution: Sucrose is transported in phloem through active transport (requires ATP and carrier proteins). Sucrose moves from photosynthetic cells (source) to non-photosynthetic cells (sink) against concentration gradient.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Stomata of a plant open due to:
questions.solution: Stomata open due to influx (entry) of potassium ions (K⁺) into guard cells. This increases osmotic potential, causing water influx and turgor pressure, which opens the stomatal pore.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect about transpiration?
questions.answer: Higher temperature of the surrounding decreases transpiration
options: Higher temperature of the surrounding decreases transpiration
Higher the velocity of wind, more is the transpiration
The transpiration is inversely proportional to humidity
Strong light stimulates the opening and closing of stomata and thus increases the transpiration
questions.solution: Statement (a) is incorrect. Higher temperature INCREASES transpiration (not decreases). Temperature increases evaporation rate from leaves. All other statements are correct.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Nerve impulse travels as:
questions.solution: Nerve impulse travels as an electrical impulse due to movement of ions (Na⁺ and K⁺) across the axon membrane. This creates a change in membrane potential that propagates along the neuron.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Energy transformation during nerve conduction is:
questions.solution: During nerve conduction, chemical energy (from ATP) is converted to electrical energy. ATP is used to maintain the Na⁺/K⁺ pump, creating the resting potential that drives electrical impulses.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The junction between the axon of one neuron and the dendrite of the next is called:
questions.solution: A synapse is the junction between the axon terminal of one neuron (presynaptic) and the membrane of the receiving neuron (postsynaptic). It consists of synaptic vesicles, synaptic cleft, and receptors.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The binding of the neurotransmitter with the receptors opens ion channels allowing the entry of ions which can generate a new potential in the:
questions.solution: Neurotransmitters bind to receptors on the postsynaptic membrane (receiving neuron). This opens ion channels, allowing ion influx and generation of new electrical potential in the receiving neuron.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The first link in any food chain is usually green plants. Which of the following statements gives the correct explanation?
questions.answer: Only green plants have the capacity to synthesize food using sunlight
options: Only green plants have the capacity to synthesize food using sunlight
There are more herbivores than carnivores in a food chain
Green plants are the only ones fixed at one place in the soil and do not show movement
questions.solution: Green plants are the first trophic level because they are PRODUCERS - they convert solar energy into chemical energy through photosynthesis. All other organisms depend on this energy.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following results when there is an increase in the population of sharks? Plankton→Fish→Seal→Shark
questions.answer: A decrease in the population of fish
options: A decrease in the population of seals
A decrease in the population of fish
An increase in the population of seals
An increase in the population of plankton
questions.solution: When shark population increases, more fish are eaten (fish are primary food of sharks). This reduces fish population. Eventually, seal population decreases due to less food, but the immediate effect is fish population decrease.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What will happen if deer gets extinct in the food chain: Grass → Deer → Tiger?
questions.answer: The population of tiger decreases and the population of grass increases
options: The tiger will start eating grass
The population of tiger decreases and the population of grass increases
questions.solution: If deer (primary consumer) becomes extinct: (1) Tigers lose their food source, so tiger population decreases. (2) Grass has no herbivore to eat it, so grass population increases. This demonstrates interdependence in ecosystems.
